items.statement: Malaysia quarry capacity expansion from 4,000 MT to 8,000 MT expected by FY29; plant commencement by FY30
items.quote: On the Malaysia project, it is already ongoing. We are working on the quarry part, raising capacity from 4,000 MT to 8,000 MT, which we expect to achieve by FY29, and by FY30 the plant should also commence.

items.statement: 9 MW captive solar plant (5.5 MW Rajasthan, 3.5 MW Gujarat) targeting Q4 FY27 commissioning; to meet ~40% power needs
items.quote: We are building 9 MW of captive solar capacity across two plants – 5.5 MW in Rajasthan and 3.5 MW in Gujarat. The total investment is about ₹29 crores and we are targeting commissioning in the fourth quarter of this financial year. Once running, solar should meet about 40% of our power needs.

items.statement: Captive talc mine in Andhra Pradesh and quartz/feldspar mine in Rajasthan to start production from December 2026
items.quote: Our new talc mine in Andhra Pradesh and our quartz and feldspar mine in Rajasthan are expected to begin production from December 2026.

items.statement: Solar project estimated to deliver ~₹8 crore annual EBITDA benefit (~80 bps margin) from FY29 at grid tariff ₹3.45-3.5/kWh net of O&M
items.quote: We reduce the tariff to around ₹3.45–3.5 [as heard]. That is how the economics will work, and based on that we expect a benefit of around ₹8 crores per year from FY29

items.statement: Furnace oil cost rose 33% (₹42 to ₹56/kg) impacting ₹1.34 crore; gas cost rose 77% (₹69 to ₹122/kg) impacting ₹0.62 crore; freight/MT rose 11% (₹2,108 to ₹2,346) impacting ₹2.92 crore in Q2 FY27
items.quote: In Q1, the furnace oil rate was around ₹42 per kg, and it has risen to ₹56 per kg – a rise of about 33%, an impact of ₹1.34 crores. Gas has risen from ₹69 to ₹122 per kg, around 77%, an impact of ₹0.62 crores. Freight per metric tonne has gone from ₹2,108 to ₹2,346, an 11% rise, an impact of around ₹2.92 crores.

items.statement: Functional additives (250+ specialised grades) contribute ~25% of revenue; non-paints markets (polymers, cables, rubber, inks, ceramics, agrochemicals, construction chemicals) now >50% of sales
items.quote: Functional additives – more than 250 specialised grades that we already carry in our portfolio – contribute about one quarter of our revenue. They are priced on the performance they deliver, not per tonne. Paints remains our largest market, but the market beyond paints – led by polymers, cables, rubber, inks, ceramics, agrochemicals and construction chemicals – now accounts for more than half of w

items.statement: Specialty products already contributing to margins; 20 Microns Nano grew double-digit with higher profitability in Q2 FY27
items.quote: The specialty products have already started to contribute to margins. You have to look at 20 Microns on a consolidated basis – if you look at 20 Microns Nano as an individual company, it has grown in double digits this quarter and its profitability has also increased.

items.statement: Bid placed in Government of India PLI scheme for rare-earth permanent magnets (REPM); awaiting results in next couple of months
items.quote: 20 Microns has placed its bid in the PLI scheme launched by the Government of India for rare-earth permanent magnets (REPM), in which 20 bidders participated. This is a very crucial product used across all these sectors. We await the results of the bidding, hopefully in the next couple of months, as to whether we

items.statement: EBITDA margins consistently between 12-14% for over a decade despite pandemic, supply-chain disruptions and energy/freight cost swings
items.quote: Through a pandemic, supply-chain disruptions and sharp swings in energy and freight costs, our EBITDA margins have stayed between 12% and 14% year after year for over a decade.

items.statement: Q3/Q4 margins hard to predict due to supply-chain disruptions, wars and upcoming midterm elections; wait-and-watch approach
items.quote: For Q3 and Q4, as I mentioned, it is very hard to predict – not only for us but for all industries – given the ongoing supply-chain disruptions, the wars and the upcoming midterm elections. We don't know what's ahead, so it's a wait-and-watch situation; we hope things don't get worse.

items.statement: Customer relationships span 10-25 years; new grades take 3-10 years from brief to commercial supply; leading FMCG company moving to commercial supply after nearly 10 years of trials
items.quote: A new grade typically takes anywhere from three to ten years to move from the first brief to commercial supply. A leading FMCG company is only now moving into commercial supply after nearly ten years of trials with us. Once approved, a grade is rarely replaced, because changing it means re-qualifying the customer's own products. That is why many of our relationships with India's largest paints, po

items.statement: Inventory normalising and cash flow catching up with profits expected over coming months as mines start December 2026 and solar commissions Q4 FY27
items.quote: Several of the actions I described should start to show in the numbers over the coming months: inventory normalising and cash flow catching up with profits. With both mines starting production from December and the solar plants commissioning in Q4, the full-year benefit will come from FY28.

items.statement: Employee costs increased in Q2 FY27 as teams strengthened in preparation for planned capacity expansion
items.quote: The quarter's operating performance was impacted by higher power and fuel costs, export freight expenses and some increase in employee costs as we strengthen our teams in preparation for our planned capacity.

items.statement: Power demand grew 11.1% YoY in Q2 FY27, with September up 11.3% and October month-to-date up 21.2%; management sees structural drivers supporting 5-6% long-term CAGR.
items.quote: Power demand in Q2 FY27 grew about 11.1% year -on-year, building on 8.3% growth in Q1. September alone grew about 11.3%, with peak demand touching 270 GW in Q2FY27. The momentum strengthened further into October, with month-to-date demand growth of 21.2%.

items.statement: Planned capex for FY27 is around ₹20,000 crore to support the 3 GW commissioning target and 1 GWh of energy storage projects.
items.quote: The pipeline is substantially de-risked, and we are confident of achieving our 3 GW commissioning target for FY27, supported by planned capex of around ₹20,000 crore. Further, on our energy storage pursuits, we expect to commission about 1 GWh of projects in FY27.

items.statement: Installed capacity exceeded 15.1 GW with renewables at ~61%; 1.4 GW organic renewable capacity commissioned since April (513 MW in Q2), plus 300 MW Maruti thermal acquisition.
items.quote: Since April, we have commissioned 1.4 GW of organic renewable capacity as compared to last full year’s approximately 1.2 GW. This is also nearly half of our FY27 target of 3 GW. In Q2, we added 513 MW, comprising 301 MW of solar and 212 MW of hybrid capacity. Including the 300 MW Maruti thermal acquisition, total capacity additions since April stand at 1.7 GW, taking our installed capacity above 1

items.statement: Utkal thermal plant EBITDA more than tripled YoY to ₹368 crore in Q2 FY27, driven by better plant performance and PPA realisations well above DAM prices.
items.quote: Utkal had an exceptional quarter, now that it operates under long -term PPAs. Plant EBITDA more than tripled year -on-year to ₹368 crore in Q2 FY27, and grew over 60% YoY in H1 FY27. This was driven by significantly better plant performance and by PPA realisations well above the DAM prices at which the plant's power was sold a year ago.

items.statement: Merchant realisation averaged ₹6.9/kWh in Q2 FY27, ~20% above DAM average of ₹5.7/kWh; Q3 fully booked at similar or better pricing.
items.quote: Day-Ahead Market prices averaged ₹5.7 per unit in Q2 FY27. Our merchant realisation, however, stood around ₹6.9 per unit which was around 20% higher than the DAM average, driven by the strategic bilateral contracts we have entered into.

items.statement: API4 imported coal prices averaged ~US$115/t in Q2 FY27, up 28% YoY; shift to domestic coal and job-work arrangements insulated fuel costs.
items.quote: API4 benchmark coal prices averaged close to US$115 per tonne in Q2 FY27, up around 28% year-on-year from US$90 per tonne. Despite this increase, our transition to domestic coal and the implementation of job -work arrangements at imported -coal plants, which shield us from fuel-price volatility, have enabled us to effectively mitigate the impact and maintain cost competitiveness.

items.statement: Net Debt/TTM EBITDA (ex-CWIP) improved to 4.94x from 5.2x in FY26; cash & equivalents ~₹15,700 crore; debt cost fell 51 bps YoY to 8.28%; 25% of term debt fixed for 5-6 years, 90% of floating linked to MCLR.
items.quote: Excluding debt tied to capital work-in-progress, our Net Debt to TTM EBITDA stands at about 4.94 times, down from about 5.2 times in FY26. We hold cash and cash equivalents of about ₹15,700 crore, and our cash return on net worth, adjusted for our JSW Steel shareholding, stands at about 15%.

items.statement: ₹10,150 crore capital unlocked in calendar year via fundraising and JSW Steel share sale; ICRA and India Ratings affirmed AA/Stable rating.
items.quote: ICRA and India Ratings have affirmed JSW Energy's long-term credit rating at AA with a Stable outlook. This recognises our larger and more diversified operating base, our high share of contracted capacity, and the d eleveraging we delivered through the ₹10,150 crore capital unlocking in this calendar year

items.statement: Acquired Maruti Clean Coal & Power in August at EV ₹1,410 crore; EBITDA/PAT accretive from day one, generated ₹45 crore EBITDA in 55 days; 195 MW under long-term PPA, 64 MW merchant.
items.quote: We completed the acquisition of Maruti Clean Coal & Power in August at an enterprise value of ₹1,410 crore. It is EBITDA and PAT accretive from day one and lowers our net leverage. About 195 MW (net) is tied up under a long-term PPA with Rajasthan discoms with around 14 years of residual life, while about 64 MW gives us merchant exposure at a time of strong prices.

items.statement: Salboni thermal: turbine orders for all four 800 MW units placed (3,200 MW total); Phase I first unit expected by 2030. KSK Mahanadi: 600 MW unit 4 on track for FY28, balance 1,200 MW by FY29; capex 25-30% below industry benchmark.
items.quote: At Salboni, Turbine Generator orders for all four 800 MW units, totalling 3,200 MW, are now in place, with the Phase II turbines ordered from Toshiba JSW in September. Site work on Phase I is progressing well, and the first unit is expected by 2030. At KSK, the 600 MW fourth unit remains on track for FY28, and the balance 1,200 MW by

items.statement: Renewables at ~61% of portfolio; C&I/group captive 3.7 GW (25% of operating capacity); thermal provides firm power complementing renewables.
items.quote: Since April, we have commissioned 1.4 GW of organic renewable capacity as compared to last full year's approximately 1.2 GW. This is also nearly half of our FY27 target of 3 GW. In Q2, we added 513 MW, comprising 301 MW of solar and 212 MW of hybrid capacity. Including the 300 MW Maruti thermal acquisition, total capacity additions since April stand at 1.7 GW, taking our installed capacity above 1

items.statement: Group captive demand expected to more than double to ~7 GW by 2032 as JSW Steel targets 80 MTPA; 2 GW of group MoUs under advanced discussion.
items.quote: With JSW Steel plan ning to expand capacity to up to 80 MTPA, and other Group businesses scaling rapidly, the Group’s RTC power requirement is expected to more than double to around 7 GW by 2032. A substantial share of this will be met through green energy, in line with the Group’s decarbonisation ambitions

items.statement: Curtailment at 4.8% of generation in H1 (national 5.4%); Q2 curtailed ~225 MUs, revenue impact ₹59 crore; 60% of curtailed capacity on temporary GNA to move to permanent GNA by end Q3 FY27.
items.quote: Curtailment across our portfolio stood at about 4.8% of total generation in H1, below the national level curtailment of about 5.4%. In Q2, our curtailed units stood at ~225 MUs with a Revenue impact of Rupees 59 Crores. Further, about 60% of our curtailed capacity currently on temporary GNA will move to permanent GNA by the end of Q3 FY27, which should reduce our exposure meaningfully.

items.statement: NCLT sanctioned scheme to acquire GE Power India's boiler business including Durgapur facility on Oct 1; boiler order for entire Salboni project placed with Durgapur facility.
items.quote: The scheme to acquire GE Power India's boiler business, including its Durgapur manufacturing facility, received NCLT sanction on October 1st, and the transaction should close soon. We have placed the boiler order for the entire Salboni project with the Durgapur facility, which sits in the same state as the project.

items.statement: Merchant exposure limited to ~4% of capacity (7% of energy); Q3 fully booked at similar or better rates; evening peak opportunity may keep part of Mahanadi capacity merchant.
items.quote: Yes. Definitely, third quarter is fully booked. And maybe I'll not comment on the pricing, but the pricing discovered may be either same or better than this, not lower than these for quarter 3. And now the discussions are on for quarter 4. Normally, it is 2-2.5 months back before this planning start. There are discussions going on even for quarter 4, but quarter 3 is fully booked.

items.statement: Annual renewable addition guidance of 2.5-3 GW/year maintained; BESS pipeline 3.2 GWh plus additional solar+BESS for evening peak arbitrage; 1 GWh BESS commissioning targeted in FY27.
items.quote: Yes, 3 GW current year and next year, we have given the guidance that maybe 2.5 GW- 3 GW every year, that is on track. And our capacity addition beyond current year, say, for FY28 or beyond is basically we have divided our planned addition into three categories. One is that the off -grid, which is the group captive requirement under the C&I, wherein my dependence on the grid or the grid curtailmen

items.statement: KSK Mahanadi 1.8 GW expansion capex 25-30% below industry benchmark per MW due to ready balance-of-plant infrastructure for 3.6 GW.
items.quote: See, as we have said that the balance of plant in KSK has been ready. And in the last earnings call also, I have mentioned about this that the capex per MW for the capacity addition of 1.8 GW at Mahanadi plant will be significantly lower than the industry benchmark. So when we say that the investment in Mahanadi expansion, doubling the capacity will be at least 25% to 30% lower cost per MW capex a

items.statement: 30 GW target by 2030 underwritten by locked-in pipeline; growth beyond 2030 driven by Salboni thermal, 920 MW Punatsangchhu-III hydro (Bhutan), pumped storage 26.4 GWh, thermal & C&I opportunities.
items.quote: Looking further ahead, our locked -in pipeline gives us clear line of sight to our 30 GW target for 2030, and our growth runway extends well beyond it. Multiple drivers support our growth beyond 2030: the Salboni thermal project; the 920 MW Punatsangchhu -III hydro project, our first cross-border generation venture, being developed in partnership with Druk Green Power Corporation, Bhutan's state-o

items.statement: States awarded ~17 GW long-term thermal at ₹5.4-6.3/kWh in FY26; further 18 GW thermal tenders under bidding; renewables and thermal seen as complementary for firm power.
items.quote: States awarded around 17 GW of long-term thermal capacity at tariffs of about ₹5.4 to ₹6.3 per unit in FY26, and a further 18 GW of thermal tenders are currently under bidding. To us, the conclusion is simple. Renewables and thermal are not competing; they are complementary. Renewables deliver the cheapest energy, while thermal and storage keep the lights on through the evening peak.

items.statement: Punatsangchhu-III 920 MW hydro project in Bhutan with Druk Green Power Corp is first cross-border venture; DPR stage, JV finalisation and DPR expected by June 2027.
items.quote: We are working. It is at a DPR stage. We have already signed the agreement with the Bhutan government. We are in the process of finalizing the joint venture company and the DPR work is on. Once all the details are ready, which is expected by June 27, then only we will be in a better position to speak on the numbers.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; IR head Bikash Choudhury present on call.
items.quote: We have with us today from the management, Mr. Sharad Mahendra, Joint MD and CEO; Mr. Chandrasekaran Prabhakaran, CFO; and Mr. Bikash Choudhury, Head of Investor Relations and ERM.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton guidance maintained at INR9,000-12,000 for foreseeable future
items.quote: Our guidance remains INR9,000 to INR12,000 as EBITDA per ton.

items.statement: Full-year sales volume target revised to ~260,000 tons
items.quote: So, we expect sales of about 260,000 tons now for the year. Budget was about 260,000 tons.

items.statement: New steel plant cost to exceed INR2,000 crore; forging plant capex lower than budgeted INR475 crore
items.quote: But suffice it to say at this point in time that the project cost will be higher than the INR2,000 crores that we had envisaged.

items.statement: Existing plant capex ~INR150 crore per year; brownfield expansion to 360KTPA needs ~INR100-115 crore
items.quote: It will be about INR150 crores for the existing plant. And for the steel plant, as I said, we are still considering the final figures that will be investing.

items.statement: New steel plant on track for completion by Sep 2029, stabilization by Mar 2030; target 500K-700K tons
items.quote: We are on track as of now to complete the project by September of '29 and stabilization by March of '30.

items.statement: Forging plant expected by Mar 2028; initial capacity 15,000 tons/year
items.quote: The forging plant is expected to come up by March of '28. And then, of course, it will take some time to fill up the capacity.

items.statement: Environmental approval sought to raise melting capacity from 300K to 360KTPA; decision awaited
items.quote: We have applied for increasing the capacity to 360,000 tons. We seem to have got a recommendation. Maybe this may happen.

items.statement: Strong demand driven by auto (2W, SUV, PV) and non-auto; tractors showing slight slowdown
items.quote: Demand was strong. And pa rtly demand has been strong because of the GST cuts, which happened last year on 2-wheelers as well as the smaller vehicles as well as SUV sales have been good

items.statement: Price increase letters of INR3,500-4,000/ton sent for Q3; Q2 settlements ongoing
items.quote: The other companies have sent out letters for price increases, which are ranging between INR3,500 to INR4,000 a ton.

items.statement: Seeding non-auto segments (tool & die, oil & gas, railways, bearings) via ingot casting from Nov 2026
items.quote: So, we are starting with ingot casting, which is the route to make specialized stee ls. This is something that we will start in the end of November, it will

items.statement: Major import substitution win with domestic OEM; high-end quality; mass manufacturing started
items.quote: Also, on a major import substitution of domestic major, which is a large quantity and it was a highly very high-end quality. We have successfully got approval and mass manufacturing for that too has started.

items.statement: Receivables up due to higher sales in Aug-Sep; debtor days increased 4-5 days
items.quote: In number of days, it has increased by 4 to 5 days only because of some sales to customers who are having a high credit period.

items.statement: Debt-equity for new plant revised from 0.75:1 to 1:1; rights issue in H2 CY2027
items.quote: We are now coming around with a conclusion, we are diluting a bit more than required. And therefore, we may look at a 1:1 debt equity.

items.statement: Board to consider suspending dividend for 3-4 years to fund expansion; decision in Apr 2027
items.quote: The other thing we are examining, of course, the decision will be taken by the Board, is also to look at examini ng, suspending the dividend for 3 -4 years.

items.statement: Solar expansion of 22.5 MW (20 MW for current plant, 2.5 MW for forging NDT line)
items.quote: And we are now expanding the solar plant by another 22.5 megawatts. 20 -megawatt for this will be for the current plant and 2.5 -megawatt will be for the NDT line.

items.statement: Environmental clearance application for new steel plant melting shop by Dec 2026
items.quote: EC will be applied within this year because EC for the steel, for the melting part takes a longer period. So that will be applied within this year. By December we would have applied for the EC.

items.statement: Project implementation risk cited as biggest risk; no new competitor capacity expected for 2-3 years
items.quote: There are several risks. One, there's a project implementation risk. Two, I think that's the biggest risk that we have.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton at high end of INR9,000-12,000 range in Q2; not sustainable
items.quote: Currently, we are at the higher end of the EBITDA range.

items.statement: Kocks Block & reheating furnace raised capacity to 300KTPA, improved yields, cut job work, boosted margin
items.quote: So, with the combination of Kocks Block and reheating furnace, we have been able to increase our capacity to 300,000 tons. And we can actually increase this capacity even beyond this.

items.statement: Exports steady at 6-7% direct and 6-7% indirect via ASC
items.quote: It is almost in the same ratio as was there in the last year. So, 6% to 7% is direct and another 6% to 7% is indirect through ASC.

items.statement: Aichi Steel (JV partner) dispatched senior executive as President of forging business
items.quote: Aichi, the Japanese, will be driving this business.

items.statement: Strong order book visibility from major customers driving tower and tenancy growth
items.quote: we do have a visibility of a strong order book. And I think we will keep executing based on that order book. So yo u'll continue to see our delivery in the line with what the orders we have

items.statement: 5G subscriber base grew 36 million in Q1 to exceed 463 million, driving sustained operator investment
items.quote: According to the recent TRAI data, India's 5G subscriber base grew by 36 million in the first quarter, exceeding 463 million subscribers.

items.statement: Industry added ~30,000 5G BTS in Q2, total installed base ~593,000; focus shifting to densification
items.quote: With the industry adding approximately 30,000 5G BTS s during the second quarter, taking the total installed base to around 593,000.

items.statement: Total data volume up 30% YoY in Q1; 5G usage up 79% YoY, now 44% of total consumption
items.quote: In Q1, total data volume increased by 30% year -on-year, supported by an 18% rise in average monthly usage per subscriber. Notably, 5G networks are accelerating this trend, with 5G usage alone growing 79% year-on-year, representing 44% of total data consumption, up from 32% in the prior year.

items.statement: Added ~2,900 macro towers and 7,900 co-locations in Q2; tower base ~270,500, co-location base ~440,200
items.quote: We added approximately 2,900 macro towers and robust co-locations of 7,900, marking year -on-year growth of 5.6% in towers and 5.9% in co-locations. Our total macro tower and co-location base reached approximately 270,500 and 440,200, respectively.

items.statement: Tenancy ratio improved from 1.62 to 1.63 driven by sharing of existing towers
items.quote: Our industry -leading tenancy ratio has also improved from 1.62 to 1.63, driven by substantial rollout through sharing of our existing towers.

items.statement: Reported EBITDA grew 2.5% QoQ to INR46.3bn; EBITDA margin improved 80bps QoQ to 54.4%
items.quote: Reported EBITDA increased by 2.5% quarter-on-quarter and stands at INR46.3 billion for the quarter. Our EBITDA margin also improved by 80 basis points quarter-on-quarter and stands at 54.4% for the quarter.

items.statement: Energy margin improved to -3.6% in Q2 from -4.6% in Q1 and -4.8% YoY; diesel consumption down 11% YoY
items.quote: Our energy margin was negative 3.6% in Q2 compared to negative of 4.6% in Q1 and negative 4.8% in the corresponding quarter of last year, reflecting a significant improvement during the reported quarter. Our structured energy efficiency measures are yielding positive results, and diesel consumption is further reduced by 11% year-on-year.

items.statement: Growth capex increase reflected in CWIP rising ~INR250 cr QoQ due to healthy order book; capex includes towers, tenancies, 5G upgrades, solar
items.quote: If you follow our balance sheet, there is an increase of around INR250-odd crores on the CWIP value quarter-on-quarter, which is a reflection of what Prachur was alluding on the very healthy order book what we have.

items.statement: Africa tower deployments commenced in Zambia and Uganda in Q2; Nigeria deployment starting in Q3; early capex per tower within plan
items.quote: We have successfully deployed towers in Zambia and Uganda in Q2 and also started generating revenue. In line with our phased rollout plan, we are set to begin deployment in Nigeria during the current quarter and our early capex performance per tower remains within the plan, validating our cost model during the initial phases.

items.statement: Government support for smart meter deployment on telecom towers; ~140,000 sites deployed over 3 years
items.quote: Government support for smart meter deployment on telecom towers has further reinforced telecom infrastructure as a priority consumer category. Over the last three years, we have deployed smart meters on approximately 140,000 sites.

items.statement: IBS deployments gaining market share for two consecutive years; provided solutions for India Mobile Congress and Vizag Airport
items.quote: Supported by a specialized team focused on design and execution, the company has led incremental market share gains in new IBS deployments for two consecutive years and remains focused on expanding its presence in this segment while enhancing the end user connectivity experience.

items.statement: Network uptime improved sequentially from 99.955% to 99.97% despite seasonal weather
items.quote: Our determination to deliver superior service delivery resulted in sequential improvement in our network uptime from 99.955% to 99.97% despite challenging seasonal weather.

items.statement: Revenue grew 1% QoQ to INR85.2bn; core rental revenue up 1.3% QoQ to INR54.5bn; YoY revenue up 4%, core revenue up 3.9%
items.quote: Revenue for the company grew at 1% quarter -on-quarter and the revenue absolute value stands at INR85.2 billion. Core revenue for the rental is up by 1.3% quarter-on-quarter, stands at INR54.5 billion, driven by steady co-location addition and asset loading.

items.statement: Airtel remains primary anchor customer in Africa; no agreements signed with other telcos yet
items.quote: No, I think Airtel remains our primary anchor customer in Africa.

items.statement: Annual rental escalation covers majority of inflation impact on opex; capex rates revised per MSA where flexibility exists
items.quote: I think first is the escalation that we have that takes care of the inflation impact when it comes to opex. As far as capex is concerned, based on our MSA, whichever rates are to be revised on capex, wherever we have that flexibility, that is accordingly adjusted for the customers.

items.statement: Frontline teams in Northeast, Bihar & Jharkhand, UP East demonstrated exceptional resilience during severe floods
items.quote: During the quarter, our teams across Northeast, Bihar & Jharkhand and UP East, once again demonstrated exceptional resilience in the face of severe floods that disrupted network operations, restricted site access and caused prolonged power outages.

items.statement: Africa expansion at early stage; meaningful metrics to be shared in subsequent quarters as portfolio reaches representative scale
items.quote: As the portfolio reaches to a more representative scale, we intend to share more detail on operational and financial metrics in subsequent quarters.

items.statement: CRISIL ESG rating improved from 57 to 63; recognized at Mahatma Awards and Business World Sustainable World Awards
items.quote: We are pleased to report that our CRISIL ESG rating improved from 57 to 63, complemented by recognition at Mahatma Awards and Business World Sustainable World Awards.

items.statement: CSR initiatives Saksham and Pragati impacted over 11 million lives in Q2; supported disaster-affected communities in Assam, Arunachal Pradesh
items.quote: Through our flagship CSR initiatives, Saksham and Pragati, we positively impacted over 11 million lives this quarter, while actively supporting communities affected by natural disasters and humanitarian challenges in Assam, Arunachal Pradesh and

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance revised to early 20s percent for FY27 from prior mid-teens to high teens
items.quote: I had said mid-teens to high teens. I think now I think early 20s is a good estimate of where we think we'll end the year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin long-term guidance anchored at 31-31.5% while funding growth investments
items.quote: I would say a long- term guidance of about 31%, 31.5%, where we are funding all these investments for growth is what I would anchor on, right, and not above that.

items.statement: Specialty diagnostics target 10-15% of revenue in 3-5 year horizon
items.quote: As I said, in a 3 to 5-year horizon, specialty should be at least around 10% to 15% of our revenue, and we'll hold to that.

items.statement: Franchisee additions expected at 1,500-2,000 per year, targeting 20,000-25,000 in 5 years
items.quote: We expect to maintain the 1,500 to 2,000 additions every year, right? So if you take a 5-year out view, a simple mathematics will be between 20,000 and 25,000 franchisees in 5 years.

items.statement: API Group ex-Thyrocare profitability target by Q4 FY27 before any corporate action discussion
items.quote: I have guided to API Group ex-Thyrocare turning profitable by Q4 FY27. It is only by then that I think even any kind of corporate action would be in the realm of discussion.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex of INR30 crores for 8 new labs and capacity; similar capex expected in H2
items.quote: During H1 FY27, a capex of INR30 crores has been invested on account of new lab expansion, 5 in this quarter and 3 in quarter 1 and capacity capex to support 27% volume growth. In balance part of the financial year, we are expecting a similar capex investm ent for the growth of the business

items.statement: Lab network expanded to 49 labs (48 India + 1 Tanzania) with 5 new labs added in Q2 FY27
items.quote: We now operate 48 labs in India and 1 in Tanzania. This quarter, we added 5 new labs, 4 regional processing labs at Asansol, Nashik, Madurai, and Jabalpur, and 1 hybrid lab partnership at Jamshedpur.

items.statement: Active franchisee base reached 12,911 with record 1,180 net additions in Q2 FY27
items.quote: We added about 1,180 franchises in the quarter, our highest quarterly addition in 3 years, taking the active base of franchise to a record of 12,911.

items.statement: Pathology business grew 27% YoY in Q2 FY27; test volumes up 27%, patients up 13%, tests per patient up 12%
items.quote: Continuing the growth momentum of over 20% achieved in each of the past 2 years, our pathology business grew even faster in Q2 FY27, delivering 27% growth.

items.statement: Specialty diagnostics launched (allergy, genomics) contributing ~4% of pathology revenue; pregnancy test kit launched at INR60 MRP with Beta hCG confirmation at INR399

items.statement: Operating cash flow of INR133 crores generated in H1 FY27
