items.statement: MOU with RDSO for joint wagon design development; design patent protection via MOU; RDSO cannot share design without permission
items.quote: No, basically the thing which is the MOU which we talked about, that talks of the patent. Without our permission, RDSO cannot give this design to anybody else.

items.statement: Wagon design enables 5.4 TEUs per wagon vs 3 TEUs charged; potential 30-40% unit cost reduction; train capacity 264 TEUs vs 180 TEUs
items.quote: So basically, as we have been telling that these wagons can carry 42-foot containers on the chassis. If you double-stack two 42-foot containers, so this wagon will be equivalent to volume-wise 5.4 TEUs per wagon.

items.statement: Key risks: orders may not meet expectations; targeted PAT/EBITDA may not materialize; mitigating via zero-debt capex and revenue-capex alignment
items.quote: When you are into the industry, and specially expanding industry, there can be lot of risks. One is that order don't come as per your expectations. Secondly, that whatever the PAT or whatever the EBITDA you are targeting may not come.

items.statement: Options open: debt (HDFC sanctioned), preferential shares, rights issue; no anchor customer equity interest
items.quote: We have got options. Either we go through that, bank is supporting us. We may raise some funds through preferential shares at some point of time.

items.statement: Continuous hiring from relevant fields; MD handles stakeholder communication personally
items.quote: We keep on hiring the people from the relevant field. Yogesh Khatri: Okay, sir. Naresh Kumar: But talking to stakeholders like you is my prerogative. I would like to explain what we are doing and what we are going in future

items.statement: INR4.67 crores receivable from Briskworld Ventures; payments now being received
items.quote: Okay, okay, okay. That is a company, yes, fine. We are receiving the payment now.

items.statement: Long-term vision: INR4,000-5,000 crores revenue in 7-8 years driven by wagons (INR1,000+ crores at 2,000 units), containers, ICD, rail terminal
items.quote: And we have promised that within 7 years to 8 years, we will be touching that margin.

items.statement: Container manufacturing low-tech; large companies unlikely due to margin constraints and high overheads; competitive advantage from low overheads and strategic location
items.quote: Brother, a container is a very low-tech item, baba. No big company will come here, they're not sure of the margins. We are able to generate margins because our overheads are very less.

items.statement: Strategic location near Mundra, Kandla, Tuna ports; rail and highway connectivity; ICD permission granted Sept 10, 2026; warehousing foundation laid Sept 14, 2026
items.quote: And a happy thing is that we have got on 10th of September 2026 permission to construct and operate Inland Container Depot. So, it will be total logistic platform, integrated platform at one place in around 144 acres.

items.statement: Stainless steel salt container carries 33.5t; special railway rates granted; open-roof 20ft container loads 33t wheat (27% more); 40ft super high-cube carries 200 cotton bales (34t)
items.quote: And Indian Railways, on our request, has given very special rates for the movement of salt in these containers. So, we may expect good orders from various people for this particular container because we have only made this container till now.

items.statement: Half-yearly results pending; H1 performance not as expected due to geopolitical uncertainties and supply chain disruptions; catch-up expected in H2
items.quote: But the second half is going to – the first half number may not be so great, but we are sure we will catch up into the second half.

items.statement: Zero-EMI company currently; INR100 crore HDFC sanction unused; capex funded via internal accruals and promoter warrants
items.quote: So till now, we didn't use any debt. We have been able to manage through our equity funding, and the margins available with us, surplus available with us from our normal operations.

items.statement: Wagon manufacturing: Stage 1 design approval cleared; Stage 2 docs ready; G-105 factory audit application submitted; final approval hoped by 2027
items.quote: So, we have been given notification regarding our own design. So, new wagon design, the RDSO has cleared our stage one. items.statement: Refrigerated container technology agreement with Japanese company; production timeline delayed due to other priorities
items.quote: With regards to the refrigerated container manufacturing, we have already got the technology sharing agreement with a Japanese company specialized refrigerated container manufacturing facility.

items.statement: Quarterly results not yet decided; will follow statutory requirements upon main board listing
items.quote: Right now we have not yet decided. We will go by the statutory requirement. When we come to the main board, then we have to follow that.

items.statement: Industry capital, approvals, pipeline and AI adoption are all turning positive simultaneously, creating compounding demand for Indegene's services
items.quote: For the first time in several years, the major signals are pointing the same way at the same time. Capital is back. Approvals are at a record pace. The pipeline is large and later stage. And AI has moved on to the operating agenda of almost every large bio pharmaceutical company.

items.statement: Q2 revenue INR11,223 million, up 39.5% YoY and 5.6% QoQ; fifth consecutive quarter of >5% sequential INR growth
items.quote: Revenues came in at INR11,223 million, up 39.5% year -on-year and 5.6% sequentially. That makes 5 consecutive quarters in which we have grown more than 5% quarter-on-quarter in INR terms.

items.statement: Revenue per employee (TTM) rose to US$79,600 from ~US$69,000 a year ago, driven by GenAI platforms and output-based pricing
items.quote: Revenue per employee on a trailing 12 -month basis is US$79,600. This is up from around US$69,000 a year ago. We are growing revenue faster than headcount because most of our delivery now runs on our GenAI-enabled platforms and more of the work is priced on output and outcomes rather than on time spent.

items.statement: 9 deal wins with ACV ~$1M+, including 3 large deals: one $5M+, two $3-5M range; Tectonic expanded to Canada (3rd market in 3 quarters)
items.quote: We had a good quarter in terms of deal wins . 9 deal wins with annual contract values about $1 million, including 3 large deals, one in the $5 million-plus range and 2 in the $3 million to $5 million range.

items.statement: No formal guidance; organic growth target better than FY26 with balanced client growth; quarterly EBITDA margin back in historical range by Q4 FY27

items.statement: DSO net of unearned/unbilled 69 days (+2 days QoQ); cash and investments INR13,896M; unbilled revenue rise partly seasonal, partly milestone-based billing

items.statement: Amortization charge to reduce in Q3 and beyond; investment portfolio shifting to higher held-to-maturity allocation to reduce yield volatility
items.quote: Amortization charge will reduce in quarter 3 and beyond. We anticipate yields to increase with the higher interest rates prevailing combined with a conscious shift in the investment portfolio towards a higher allocation to held -to-maturity instruments, which reduce volatility.

items.statement: ~60%+ revenue outcome-aligned; most Q2 wins output/outcome-based; actively converting FTE contracts to hybrid at renewals

And we are also making focused effort to convert our pure FTE contracts into a hybrid contract with a mix of outcome -based as we head into the renewal cycles for these contracts.

items.statement: Do not see IT services firms (e.g., TCS) competing in same deals; compete with agencies and CROs; selling to CMOs/Chief Medical Officers, not CIOs

items.statement: Tectonic ramp-up slower than scope expansion due to client change management dynamics between central and local brand teams; not worried, seen similar patterns before

Getting those organizational dynamics right in these very, very large companies takes time.

items.statement: Tectonic run-rate grew from ~$1M/quarter to $1.7M this quarter; contracted run-rate >$2M/quarter looking ahead
items.quote: Tectonic has grown from a run rate of about $1 million a quarter to $1.7 million this quarter. And the contracts, as we mentioned, have actually crossed a level of more than $2 million a quarter as we look ahead.

items.statement: $10M ACV outcome-based deal: small revenue recognized in Q2; bulk expected in H2; true-up in Q4 (Feb-Mar) upon calendar year outcome confirmation
items.quote: We believe that our quarter 4 is when any true-up on this contract would show up given that it's a full year threshold that we have to meet and beat on the outcomes to be certain on the full revenue recognition. items.statement: Margin walk: Q1-Q2 productivity +85 bps, favorable FX; 75% of 2-quarter ahead forex exposure hedged; workforce transformation and operating leverage to continue; Q4 uplift from $10M outcome deal

items.quote: We believe this year should be organically a stronger year than last year, and H2 would be stronger than H1. So we are fairly confident of H2 given where we sit today.

items.quote: The relationship started with our Tectonic offering and evolved into Agentic Agency of Record. I highlight this because it shows our content engagements can now start anywhere in the value chain, strategy, studio, production and then move upstream or downstream.

items.quote: Tandem brought us over 20 years of proprietary data on how physicians respond to promotions spanning more than 300 million exposure events and 15 million engagements. items.statement: Revenue: North America 74%, Europe 23%, RoW 3%; USD revenue $117.5M (+27.5% YoY, +4.4% QoQ); favorable FX offset wage hike impact
items.quote: Revenue for the second quarter was INR11,223 million or US$117.5 million. In dollar terms, that is a strong growth of 27.5% year -on-year and 4.4% sequentially.

items.statement: Interest income down 44% QoQ (INR237M to INR134M) due to mutual fund NAV markdown from rate hike; invested funds largely constant; PBT impact ~90 bps, PAT ~70 bps
items.quote: Interest income was down 44% sequentially from INR237 million to INR134 million. items.statement: Frontier AI labs (e.g., Anthropic) partnering with pharma for drug discovery not seen as threat; Indegene partnering with multiple tech players; domain workflow redesign is the differentiator
items.quote: We don't see that as a threat to our model of working. items.statement: Reaffirmed FY28 outlook of $400 million revenue and $160 million EBITDA
items.quote: we are also reaffirming our FY28 outlook, which we have given of $400 million revenue and $160 million EBITDA.

items.statement: Expect second half FY27 to be stronger than first half

items.statement: Second DDC cartridge line running commercial batches since September, doubling sterile production days

items.statement: Softgel capacity utilization visibility 80%+, greenfield site planned for high potent softgels
items.quote: we already have a visibility of -- as I said, visibility of 80% plus from a capacity utilization point of view. That's why because we can't increase the capacity at this site, we are going in for a new greenfield.

items.statement: Semaglutide demand robust across markets; India volumes grew from 20k-25k to 200k+ units/month; Canada market growing from 12M to 16-17M units
items.quote: if you see how sema from February, which was before the patent expiry of anywhere between 20,000-25,000 units a month is now looking at more than 200,000 units a month as of And this is when typically, India takes -- for a chronic therapy like this, it takes 3 years to stabilize. So there is still a very strong growth path available there. As we see in markets like Canada, which is obviously the l

items.statement: Multiple new biologics project wins: 2 end-to-end projects from US biotech, new program from top global animal health company
items.quote: We have onboarded 2 projects for end-to-end development to commercialization projects from a U.S. biotech. We secured additional new program for one of the top global animal health companies and our existing customer.

items.statement: Biologics RFP funnel at highest ever with multiple projects in advanced stages, driving growth beyond FY28
items.quote: Now same is reflected in our biologics RFP funnel, which is at highest ever with multiple projects in advanced stages. And all this is really going to be driving the growth beyond FY28 for us.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 400+ bps QoQ to 32%; EBITDA grew 53% YoY, 32% QoQ
items.quote: And the margin expanded more than 400 basis points quarter-on-quarter, reaching 32% for the quarter.

items.statement: Operating leverage driving margin improvement; incremental cost limited vs incremental revenue

items.statement: Successfully completed multiple regulatory and customer audits in Q2 FY27
items.quote: during the quarter, we successfully completed multiple regulatory and customer audits.

items.statement: Marginal currency impact of ~$350k in Q2 FY27 reported separately in financials

items.statement: Contribution margin improvement in Q2 FY27 was primarily driven by logistics efficiencies including RTO reduction, density gains, and network redesign.
items.quote: So the primary cause for improvement has been on the logistics side and the efficiencies that we have gained there.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 contribution margin will be substantially better than FY26, with FY28 benefiting from ad monetization as percentage of NMV increasing.
items.quote: From a full-year perspective, we don't give specific guidance. Of course, I think we will continue to make progress on the longer-term contribution margin targets that we have during the course of this year.

items.statement: Management aims to restore logistics-related spread lost in FY26 back to FY25 levels during FY27 as outer guidance.
items.quote: The way we kind of think about it is that we will restore some of the lost logistics-related spread that we had in FY26 back to kind of where it was in past FY25 period during the course of this year.

items.statement: Server cost elevated in Q2 FY27 due to GPU capacity constraints procured in advance for festive season; expected to normalize as percentage of NMV by Q4 FY27.
items.quote: This is expected to come back during the course of let's say the next quarter, Q4 FY27 as a percentage of NMV.

items.statement: Majority of Valmo automation capex investments are being made by Valmo entrepreneur partners, not by Meesho directly.
items.quote: We are seeing a lot of our partners make these investments right now and we expect that to keep happening. And we feel that we have to basically ourselves invest a lot more, we will come out

items.statement: Logistics speed improved 15% due to density increase, capacity creation (e.g., three shifts vs two on same route), network redesign, and GeoIndia LLM address accuracy improvements.
items.quote: So the growth itself and the density kind of leads to better speed across the network. We have also aided that with kind of better network design that has happened across o ur network and some of the 3PL networks as well

items.statement: Valmo had a good festive season with improved capacity availability and operational efficiency; last year's logistics ecosystem problems are largely behind.
items.quote: So some of the problems, let's say, that the overall logistics ecosystem saw last year, I think they are largely kind of behind us and this festive season has been good both in terms of capacity availability as well as efficiency of the operations.

items.statement: No demand-side concerns seen; healthy traffic and conversion on utility categories (personal care, beauty, home, kitchen, baby care) with all-time high festive traffic.
items.quote: On this particular point, actually, from whatever data we have seen on the user behaviour, we do not see any concern yet. We see like now a large part of our platform is about utility products, personal care, beauty, home, kitchen, baby care, a lot of this is stuff that people need and we help them people save money.

items.statement: Festive season sales better than expectations with strong demand-side growth and first-time category buyers, despite seller supply-chain disruptions from crude price volatility.
items.quote: Our festive sales this time have been better than expectations and which gives us confidence that the demand side continues to be quite strong.

items.statement: Pricing investments (passing logistics efficiencies to consumers) are for long-term flywheel: making new categories/products viable and attracting sellers, with payoff over 12-18 months.
items.quote: We have a strong plan of the products and category that we want to scale up on our platform in the next 12 to 18 months and we are very sure that for that to happen, we have to continue reinvestment into our business, into our flywheel.

items.statement: Revenue per order reduced slightly due to carryover of previous quarter pricing pass-through; significant proportion of logistics efficiencies will continue to be passed back to consumers.
items.quote: Yes, some of that is carry over from the previous quarter because let's say when we passed on some efficiencies in the previous quarter, that wasn't accounted for the full quarter itself.

items.statement: Seller base expanded significantly with non-GST sellers; average NMV per seller flat/declining but cohort data shows healthy growth for large manufacturers.
items.quote: But when we look at a cohortised data, which is sellers who are big manufacturers, they continue to expand on their business year-on-year. And they're seeing very healthy growth because the platform continues to scale across categories.

items.statement: Quarterly FCF will remain volatile due to last 15 days of NMV each quarter; positive FCF on LTM basis expected in a few quarters as adjusted EBITDA margin improves.
items.quote: So, if our adjusted EBITDA margin is kind of in line with, let's say, where the quarter is or keeps improving, then we should start seeing positive FCF coming in on a sort of LTM basis in a few quarters as well.

items.statement: New initiatives (including Kirana Club) capital allocation capped at INR200 crores annually.
items.quote: From an investment perspective, this will be as a part of our new initiatives and the cap that we mentioned in terms of capital allocation will hold on the new initiatives that we have, which is about INR200 crores annual cap, including all of the new initiatives that we have.

items.statement: Kirana Club transaction closed recently (as of call date); integration starting but business will run independently with founders remaining.
items.quote: Yes, so I think the closing of the transaction has happened recently, as recent as today. So, I think we'll start the integration process, although it will continue to run fairly independently.

items.statement: Long-term fixed cost base (below contribution margin) target is ~3% of NMV, expected around FY31.
items.quote: So, we expect in the longer run the fixed cost base to come to about 3% of NMV.

items.statement: RTO as percentage of orders improved in Q2 FY27 vs previous quarter, driven by rising prepaid mix and COD RTO reduction efforts.
items.quote: On the RTO side, while I think overall from a value of NMV to GMV, the ratio might not have looked to change significantly, but on the RTO as a percentage, it has improved versus the previous quarter.

items.statement: RTO improvement secularly driven by rising prepaid transaction share (lower RTO) and software/delivery innovations for COD orders.
items.quote: One is obviously our prepaid share of transactions keep going up every quarter and year. And as we kind of mentioned before, on prepaid transactions, we see much lower proportion of RTOs versus cash on delivery transactions.

items.statement: AI-driven discovery feed improvements reflected in rising percentage of orders from discovery feeds, increasing time spent in app, faster new user conversion, and higher transaction frequency.
items.quote: We do see time spent in the app that continues to improve. But beyond that, that also adds up to your conversion improvements, improvements in new users and everything else, right?

items.statement: Long-term NMV growth guidance of ~25% CAGR towards FY31 maintained; revision possible as FY28 visibility improves.
items.quote: On the guidance that we have out is for the longer term towards F '31. So, I think this was a five-year guidance for let's say 25% growth on the NMV side. To maintain for now.

items.statement: Seller supply-chain disruptions from crude price volatility and Middle East events observed in last 20 days; being actively mitigated.
items.quote: Like a large part of the thing that we have highlighted is we continue to see like supply chain disruptions on the seller side. Like a lot of our sellers, because the price have been volatile, it impacts supply chains.

items.statement: No platform/handling fees charged to customers; will increase take rates on logistics/ads instead to maintain trust and long-term LTV.
items.quote: We have always taken a customer-first view here that we will never add any hidden fees at the cart level, convenience fee, platform fee, many other fees that a lot of platforms add. We do not add that on our platform.

items.statement: Server cost is semi-variable: fixed portion benefits from conversion improvement; variable portion grows with compute-intensive algorithms for feed relevance.
items.quote: It's a semi-variable cost technically and there are, for instance, when our conversion, which is let's say when a consumer comes to the app and browses and starts shopping a product, that kind of improves, we see benefit obviously coming in server cost side because a significant portion of the cost is fixed.

items.statement: Marketing spend reallocated based on CAC/LTV; sustained at percentage of NMV with healthy ROI; no signs of CAC/churn deterioration.
items.quote: We continue to basically reallocate our spends in marketing basis what we see in CAC, because the platform frequency has been getting much, much better. We have been basically investing a lot more in users that could be like much higher LTV and so on.

items.statement: Long-term revenue growth guidance maintained at 27-30% CAGR; Express Parcel expected at 27-28% CAGR, Quick Commerce at 30%+ industry growth
items.quote: We continue to maintain our long-term guidance of 27% to 30% growth cumulatively.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 maintained at 3.8-4% of revenue
items.quote: Overall, I think our capex cycle remains on track for the year, where we expect this to be in the range of 3.8% to 4% of revenue as we had committed earlier.

items.statement: Quick Commerce industry continues to surprise with all horizontal players growing fast; 4,000+ dark stores served
items.quote: India's Quick Commerce continues to surprise and amaze us. Despite increasing competition, every single player continues to grow fast.

items.statement: D2C business more than doubled YoY; market share rose 2pp QoQ to above 14%; servicing twice the brands vs year ago
items.quote: Our D2C business has more than doubled year-on-year. Our share of the D2C market rose 2 percentage points quarter-on-quarter to above 14% right now.

items.quote: We also ramped up our delivery partner network by 31% from 2.9 lakh partners in quarter 1 to 3.8 lakh partners in quarter 2.

items.statement: Safety stock held to mitigate shipping disruptions; working capital pressure acknowledged but managed

items.statement: Precision Technology net debt-free; holdco liquidity for inorganic growth; operating company debt separate

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin guided at 22% to 24%

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 22.6% in Q2 FY27, within guided range

items.statement: Calibrated price increases taken to cover absolute cost impact only

items.statement: Nearly doubled modern trade asset deployment over last two quarters

items.statement: Improved market shares at company and Home Care level

items.statement: Agile procurement and global sourcing ensured input material continuity
items.quote: Our global sourcing network ensured continuity in key input materials , while our manufacturing and distribution network responded swiftly to evolving market conditions.

items.statement: Gross margin structurally positioned to improve over 3-5 years

items.statement: Rural growth sequentially increasing over last four quarters

items.statement: Minimalist growth accelerating with offline expansion

We have completed about 60% of the leasing, and the rentals are expected to be upwards of INR 500 pspm for that block, which is higher than the existing

items.statement: Q2 capex outflow Rs 389 crore (Rs 349 crore construction, rest FSI/land); H1 land/FSI spend ~Rs 800 crore, construction ~Rs 700 crore
items.quote: Total capex outflow during Q2 was INR 389 crore, out of which INR 349 crore was towards the construction cost and the remaining toward the FSI and land cost.

items.statement: Advance given for acquisition under discussion; Chandigarh land payment ~Rs 700 crore completed in Q1; incremental land in Coimbatore and Kolkata
items.quote: Now the main large expense towards land this time was the payment for the completion of land payment for Chandigarh, which we completed in quarter one. That was almost a INR 700 crore payout. And we are adding some incremental land around our existing sites in Coimbatore and Kolkata.

items.statement: Phoenix Palassio Lucknow adding ~100,000 sq ft and 100 stores; Palladium expansion adding 150 stores; Rise mall operational CY2027, offices CY2028
items.quote: Puneet, look at it in two ways. One, we are optimizing some of the existing anchor areas. Phoenix Palassio, if we recall, had opened in July 2020. We are optimizing the areas for anchors and hypermarkets to some extent, so that frees up some space. With the addition of the new area that we are planning, I think we should end up adding at least 100,000 sq ft or thereabout to the Lucknow mall.

items.statement: Thane, Chandigarh, Coimbatore malls targeted for operations by Calendar Year 2030; Bengaluru office 400k sq ft and Grand Hyatt hotel targeted CY2028
items.quote: Calendar Year 2030, Biplab. We have to keep some elbow room in terms of the regulatory approval timeline and also the time that retailers may seek to complete their fit-outs. So, 2030 is when we would target or we would expect for operations for Thane, Chandigarh, and Coimbatore.

items.statement: Kolkata residential launch expected in 2 quarters; Surat mall completion by 2027, opening 2028; Bengaluru retail expansion completion by 2027
items.quote: Kolkata will start fit-outs around Q2, and then we expect the launch six months from there on. Begaluru retail expansion also we expected to complete by 2027. Surat again to complete by 2027, open in 2028.

items.statement: F&B revenue share typically 15%-20%+ depending on format; new gourmet formats driving hypermarket category improvement
items.quote: I think in F&B, I would say that our revenue percentages would typically be 15% and higher, depending on the kind of format that is there. It can be 15%, 18%, 20%, or more.

items.statement: Fashion & accessories (60% trading area) grew 22%, F&B grew 21%, entertainment grew 16%; new brands contributing ~1/3 of incremental consumption
items.quote: Fashion and accessories, which account for approximately 60% of our trading area, grew by 22%. Food and beverages grew by 21%, while entertainment grew by 16%.

items.statement: One-third of consumption increase from new stores; new stores bring affluent customers lifting overall sales
items.quote: Another important aspect to highlight is that we are seeing about one-third of the increase in consumption coming from the new stores. The interesting part of new stores is that they bring a wider impact beyond direct sales contribution to those stores, because they bring in a new set of affluent customers, which lifts up the overall sales of all the existing brands in the stores.

items.statement: 50% of retail area leases expiring FY27-FY29 providing opportunity to refresh brand mix and reprice; typically 20% increase on MG rentals at renewal
items.quote: Leases covering around 50% of our retail area come up for expiry between FY27 and FY29, giving us the opportunity to refresh the brand mix in a strategic manner and reprice space.

items.statement: Typically 20% increase on previous minimum guarantee rentals when repricing expiries; expect same trend to continue
items.quote: You would have seen that typically we have a 20% increase on our previous minimum guarantee rentals, when we reprice the expiries, we expect the same trend to continue as well. That will also have a positive impact on the rental growth.

items.statement: Net cash from operations increased 20% to Rs 711 crore in Q2; operating free cash flow after tax and net interest grew 22% to Rs 631 crore
items.quote: Cash generation remained robust in Q2. Net cash from operations increased by 20% to INR 711 crore. Operating free cash flow after tax and net interest grew by 22% to INR 631 crore.

items.statement: Gross debt Rs 6,117 crore, liquidity Rs 2,638 crore, net debt Rs 3,479 crore (down Rs 179 crore QoQ); net debt/EBITDA 1.2x; avg cost of debt 7.66%
items.quote: As of September 2026, gross debt was at INR 6,117 crore, and the liquidity was at INR 2,638 crore, resulting into a net debt of INR 3,479 crore. Net debt reduced by INR 179 crore during the Q2 (compared to June 2026) and was INR 319 crore higher compared to March 2026. Net debt-to-EBITDA remained comfortable at 1.2x, while the average cost of debt declined to 7.66%.

items.statement: ISMDPL acquisition: NCLT approved selective capital reduction in Oct 2026; completion expected Nov 2026; PML stake to increase from 58.33% to 68.1% for Rs 1,350 crore consideration
items.quote: In October 2026, the NCLT approved the Selective Capital Reduction scheme, forming part of Tranche 2. We expect the capital reduction to be completed in November 2026, following which PML stake in ISMDPL will increase from 58.33% to 68.1%. The capital reduction consideration is INR 1,350 crore.

items.statement: Deal pipeline strong; one marquee land parcel at advanced stage with advance given; will announce after approvals and documentation
items.quote: Deal pipeline is very strong, Biplab, but closure of some of these marquee land parcels takes time. We will update you and the investor and the analyst community as soon as we close something. We currently have one at a very advanced stage, for which we have also given some advance consideration earlier in the year.

items.statement: Trading density at Phoenix Mall of Asia crossed Rs 3,300 psf per month; rent-to-consumption ratio improved to 13% from 12% in Q4
items.quote: Trading density, which is retailer sales per square feet of trading area at the center, crossed Rs. 3,300 pspm (per sq. ft. per month).

items.statement: Rent-to-consumption ratio improved to 13% from 12% in Q4; converging toward long-term average of 13.5%-14%
items.quote: If you see this quarter, the rent to consumption has improved to 13% compared to a low of 12% that we h ad in quarter four. So it is, the rent is growing ahead of consumption, and that is reflected in the rent to consumption also normalizing to the long-term average of 13.5% to 14

items.statement: 5% of leasable area under active fit-outs impacting consumption by 2-3 percentage points in Q2; strategic churn ongoing at multiple assets
items.quote: In fact, right now at this time, across our portfolio, 5% of the leasable area is under active fit-outs at this time. This includes the renovations and other optimizations that we are strategically carrying out.

items.statement: Kolkata residential delayed due to plan change and approval delays from elections; launch expected in 2 quarters
items.quote: Second is, the approval has taken longer time than what we were expecting to start this premise because of the election and other reasons. But we are expecting that to start maybe in two quarters' time, and you will see in couple of our investor calls subsequently.

items.statement: Q3 CY26 capex was INR 182 crores, highest quarterly spend; nine-month capex INR 357 crores
items.quote: On the capex, as you can see, clearly, in the third quarter, we have invested INR 182 crores in the third quarter alone, and this has complemented the overall performance, which were a little muted in the first two quarters and our commitment to invest for the future growth of Schaeffler in India stays the course.

items.statement: Strong pipeline of new business wins across Automotive Technologies, Vehicle Lifetime Solutions, and Bearings & Industrial Solutions securing future revenue growth
items.quote: What has kept us going and the revenue growth that you see is because of a strong pipeline of new business wins. We continue to keep the focus on winning new businesses with our existing customers as well as with new customer acquisitions that we do.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin 18.7% vs 19.1% previous quarter; pressure from input cost increases due to West Asia crisis impacting energy and fuel prices
items.quote: The margins did come under pressure due to the increased input costs as a PUBLIC result of the volatility that is existing in the market and also the West Asia crisis, which has impacted the energy cost and the fuel prices and some of the cascading impact that it has had on the downstream operations as well

items.statement: Raw material inflation ~1.1% of quarterly sales; 50% recovered, 50% under negotiation; historically recover 80-85%; recovery takes 4-6 months, mostly retrospective
items.quote: So gross margin is impacted largely because of the input prices, that is the raw material price. And as a percentage of quarterly sales, it is around 1.1% approximately. And 50% of it is already recovered. And 50% of it is currently under negotiation s tage with several customers

items.statement: Working capital increased to ~19% of sales due to planned localization inventory and unplanned e-mobility inventory buildup; free cash flow only INR 41 crores; focus on recovery in Q4
items.quote: What you would see is the increase in working capital, which has gone up and as a percentage of sales has crept to almost 19% levels. The reason for this is we did have some planned increases - due to our localization projects, we have to continue to service the customers.

items.statement: Exports grew 46.3% YoY to 17% of revenue; 45% to Europe, 35% Asia Pacific; mainly bearings for industrial sectors; Q3 typically spikes due to group billing cycle
items.quote: If we look at how the development has taken place, we see that Europe continues to lead in the order book and almost close to 45% of exports is to Europe. And next in line is Asia Pacific with 35% and rest of it is China and America.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Automotive Technologies 37%, Bearings & Industrial Solutions 35%, Exports 17%, Vehicle Lifetime Solutions 11%
items.quote: our Automotive Technologies still continue to be at about 37% of the revenue, Bearings and Industrial Solutions coming in close second with 35%, follow ed by our export, which has cropped up from 15% in the last quarter to 17% and our Vehicle Lifetime Solutions, which is at about 11% of the total revenue kick

items.statement: New business wins across engine applications (lash adjusters, roller tappets), clutch portfolio, rocker arms, aftermarket timing kits, lubricants, railway TAROL/TRB, industrial automation actuators
items.quote: We did have a lot of business in the engine application portfolio such as our lash adjusters, HLA-RFF, the roller tappets and so on. We also had some strong business win in the clutch portfolio for the automotive application, passenger vehicles in particular, and some of the rocker arm assemblies that go into the engine.

items.statement: GST 2.0 driving automotive demand; BS6 to BS7 transition likely 2029 requiring engine/transmission portfolio revamp
items.quote: Also, what is happening is with the talks of the BS6 now moving towards BS7, likelihood 2029, the entire engine portfolio and the transmiss ion portfolio would go through a revamp, correct? Because obviously, the emission norms would drive changes

items.statement: No plan to merge Vitesco India with Schaeffler India; portfolios complementary, sold through Schaeffler India channels; parent stake sale intent to ~67-68% from 74-75%
items.quote: First and foremost, there is no such plan of merger of Vitesco India with Schaeffler India Limited on the cards as of now. Absolutely, there are no discussions on that. And so far as the shareholding, whatever you read in the SEBI disclosure that the promo ter has planned to come down to 2/3, which means keeping significant control. That means close to 67% to 68

items.statement: Management guides for low single-digit revenue growth for FY27, down from earlier high single-digit guidance
items.quote: I think so the position is that we'll be growing by a single low digit, and that is where we are.

items.statement: Management expects about 100 bps decline in gross margin and similar or slightly more decline in EBITDA margin for the year
items.quote: Going forward also, our imagination is that we will deliver low single-digit revenue growth with some, say, about 100 bps loss in gross margin and a similar or slightly more decrease in EBITDA.

items.statement: Q2 demand driven by insecticides due to El Nino; herbicides and fungicides weak; Rabi season outlook depends on South and East zones
items.quote: Due to the dry weather, performance of our herbicides was significantly impacted while insecticide segment has good growth.

items.statement: Management more confident on Southern and Eastern regions for Q3-Q4 due to returning monsoon opportunity
items.quote: Compared to Central and Western, we are more confident of the Southern and Eastern region.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin improved due to tight control on other expenses; gross margin slightly lower YoY due to GST refund impact
items.quote: EBITDA margin improvement is mainly because of the -- you see very tight control on the other expenses. So there is a decline in other expenses because of which the EBITDA margin increased.

items.statement: Q2 product mix: insecticides 47%, fungicides 25%, herbicides 8%, others 20%; insecticides drove growth
items.quote: From a product category perspective, insecticides contributed 47 %. You will notice, as -- I spoken earlier, insecticide segment has done very well and 47% share came from insecticide segment, 25% contribution from fungicide segment and only 8% herbicide contribution was there and 20% others contribution.

items.statement: Raw material prices mixed in Q2; some down from Q1, some up; selectively passed on cost increases
items.quote: Some of the raw material prices have come down from quarter 1 further in quarter 2. Many other raw material pric es have gone up in quarter 2, wherever possible and very selectively and very calculatively, we have passed on the increased cost to the market

items.statement: European and Brazilian subsidiaries hold registrations only; 14 countries with customer appointments, purchase orders from 5 countries
items.quote: We have appointed customers in about 14 countries, and we have purchase orders in hand from five countries, five of the customers.

items.statement: Dahej plant capacity expansion planned for FY28: adding 2 new fungicide products, increasing from 2 to 4 products; capex amount to be disclosed later
items.quote: We have recently aligned to do some capacity expansion in the current plant, wherein we will be increasing capacity of existing products as well as we'll be adding new products, 2 new products in the existing plant itself. So next year, FY 28, we will be having 4 products in our portfolio, up from 2, which we are currently selling.

items.statement: Dahej plant H1 FY27 sales INR55 crores, EBITDA loss INR1.79 crores (vs INR3.5 crores loss H1 FY26); utilization ~70%
items.quote: In the half year basis, Dahej loss was around 50% of the previous year. Last year it was around 3.5, now it's almost 1.79 first half of the financial year. Viraj Kacharia: Okay. And sales, sir? V.K. Bansal: Sales is around INR55

items.statement: Proactive raw material sourcing since July 2026; buying on price decreases; some molecules with carryover inventory at advantage
items.quote: we became very conservative since July 2026. So our purchases are very moderated from July. So whenever the price s were decreasing we buy on every decrease material. And there are certain molecules which we are having the good inventory where you see, we get the advantage of the price increase as well, carryover inventory

items.statement: FICCI CASCADE session in late September addressed fake/spurious agrochemicals; Dhanuka actively pursuing with industry associations and regulator
items.quote: Just late September, FICCI organized session on -- which they call as CASCADE, which is about looking at fake, spurious duplicate products across industries, which included a special session on agrochemicals led by Mr. R.G. Agarwal.

items.statement: Biostimulant revenue Q2 FY27 INR11.7 crores vs INR8.4 crores Q2 FY26 (4 molecules); only 2 molecules billing in Q2, third launching December
items.quote: Biostimulant Q2, in quarter 2, there is -- as compared to previous year increase of around INR3.3 crores as against INR8.4 crores, INR11.7 crores this year.

items.statement: Royalty income from Bayer products Q2 FY27 INR6.5 crores vs INR4.3 crores Q2 FY26
items.quote: This was around INR6.5 crores as against previous year in quarter 2 is around INR4.3 crores.

items.statement: Generic crop protection facing pricing pressure due to tepid demand; unable to pass full cost increases despite rising raw material and freight costs
items.quote: One thing is on the demand side because we have seen a year of tepid demand. So we are able to pass on the increased cost only in a selective and a calculated way, which we are doing. Yet because of the tepid demand, we cannot pass on the entire cost incre ase to the consumer

items.statement: Industry carrying high-cost inventory; Dhanuka avoided via conservative buying since July 2026; advantage temporary as competitors will catch up
items.quote: Unlike the high-cost inventory issues lagging the sector, our proactive raw material sourcing and lean distributor inventory levels ensured zero channel stuffing and healthy cash generation

items.statement: Reach 10M+ farmers via 6,500 distributors and 80,000+ retailers; 40+ warehouses; partnerships with 10 multinational innovators
items.quote: Today, we reach more than 10 million farmers across India through 6,500 distributors an d over 80,000 retailers, supported by our manufacturing facilities, and 40 -plus warehouses we continue to strengthen our ability to deliver product efficiently across key agricultural market

items.statement: North India (irrigated) performed well industry-wide; Dhanuka grew ~22% in North Q2; South/East key for Rabi due to returning monsoon
items.quote: North markets, especially Punjab, Haryana, Western UP, these are irrigated markets. They have canal irrigation relatively easily available. So I'm pretty sure the industry would have done well overall in North India in general as compared to the stressed m arkets of Gujarat, Maharashtra and other markets

name: Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company Ltd

items.statement: Full-year AUM growth guidance maintained at around 25% with net credit costs at approximately 1.4%
items.quote: At the beginning of the year, our objective was to deliver around 25% growth while maintaining net credit costs at approximately 1.4% for the full year.

items.statement: Steady-state AUM growth guidance of 20% to 23% over the medium term
items.quote: We still hold to that 20% to 23% on a steady-state basis, because there are volatilities that is possible.

items.statement: Opex ratio expected to remain broadly in 3.0% to 3.1% range near term, targeting around 2.8% over next 2-3 years
items.quote: As mentioned earlier, we expect the Opex ratio to remain broadly in the 3.0% to 3.1% range in the near term. However, over the next two to three years, our objective is to drive further operating efficiencies and gradually bring the Opex ratio down to around 2.8%.

items.statement: CSEL and Consumer Durables combined pre-tax ROA expected to sustainably exceed 4% over medium term
items.quote: They are already delivering a pre-tax ROA of around 3.6%, and we Cholamandalam Investment and believe that, on a combined basis, they have the potential to sustainably deliver over 4% pre-tax ROA

items.statement: Board approved proposal to raise up to INR5,000 crores capital, subject to approvals, to strengthen capital base and support growth
items.quote: Given the strong growth momentum across our businesses, the Board has approved a proposal to raise up to INR5,000 crores of capital, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

items.statement: October vehicle finance disbursements trending at 18-20% YoY growth; Q3 expected at 20-22% YoY growth
items.quote: Based on the current trends, October growth is trending at approximately 18% to 20% year-on-year compared to October of last year.

items.statement: HCV industry grew 40% in Q2 and 20% in H1; industry expected to deliver 15-20% growth in H2 under conservative scenario
items.quote: Taking all segments together, it appears that the industry should be able to deliver 15% to 20% growth in the second half even under a conservative scenario, supported by healthy demand trends across most vehicle categories.

items.statement: Full-year cost of funds expected to increase by 15-20 bps YoY assuming 50 bps repo hike (25 bps done, 25 bps expected)
items.quote: With respect to interest costs, even if there is an increase of up to 50 basis points during the second half of the year, we believe the overall cost of funds for the full year may increase by only around 15 to 20 basis points on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: NIM pressure expected from modest yield decline of ~10 bps, offset by credit cost improvement; ROTA to remain better than last year
items.quote: While we will make every effort to manage the spread effectively, it would be prudent to factor in the possibility of a modest decline in yields of around 10 basis points. However, in our view, this impact should be more than offset by improvements in credit costs, which are expected to remain favorable.

items.statement: Aggregate disbursements grew 47% YoY to INR35,872 crores; AUM grew 25% YoY to INR2,68,009 crores
items.quote: Aggregate disbursements grew by 47% year-on-year to INR35,872 crores, reflecting healthy demand conditions, execution strength and continued expansion of our distribution franchise. This translated into an AUM of INR2,68,009 crores, registering a growth of 25% year-on-year.

items.statement: Vehicle finance disbursements grew 31% YoY to INR17,801 crores; AUM grew 21% YoY to INR1,29,787 crores
items.quote: Vehicle finance disbursements grew by 31% year-on-year to INR17,801 crores, resulting in an AUM of INR1,29,787 crores, a growth of 21% year-on-year.

items.statement: Secured SME finance disbursements grew 42% YoY to INR9,345 crores; AUM grew 27% YoY to INR72,356 crores
items.quote: The secured SME finance business across all key product lines, including LAP, SME and SBPL continued its strong growth trajectory for the quarter with disbursements increasing by 42% year-on-year to INR9,345 crores.

items.statement: Consumer loan disbursements grew 103% YoY to INR8,726 crores; AUM grew 32% YoY to INR45,902 crores
items.quote: Consumer loan disbursements grew by 103% year-on-year to INR8,726 crores, resulting in an AUM of INR45,902 crores, up 32% year-on-year.

items.statement: Gross Stage 3 improved to 3.25% in Sep'26 from 3.29% in Jun'26; GNPA per RBI norms improved to 4.44% from 4.50%
items.quote: Gross Stage 3 improved to 3.25% in September '26 from 3.29% in June '26. GNPA as per RBI norms improved to 4.44% in September '26 from 4.50% in June '26.

items.statement: Credit cost reduced by 37 bps YoY; PBT ROA expanded by 40 bps YoY; ROE improved to 19.4% from 18.1%
items.quote: Our strong portfolio performance led to a reduction in credit cost by 37 bps. Consequently, our profitability improved with margins, our PBT ROA expanding by 40 bps year-on-year. This translated into a stronger return profile with ROE improving to 19.4% compared to 18.1% a year ago.

items.statement: MSME portfolio delinquencies steadily declining; stress only in small-ticket secured loans below INR5 lakh in select markets, showing recent improvement
items.quote: Across these segments, we are seeing a positive trend, with delinquencies steadily declining. The only area where we have observed some stress is in small-ticket secured loans below ₹5 lakh, particularly in a few select markets.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio overwhelmingly bullet loans (~99%); EMI-based loans only ~1% of book, avoiding delinquency issues seen by peers
items.quote: In cases where customers specifically requested an EMI-based repayment option, we have accommodated them. However, such loans constitute a very small portion of the portfolio, accounting for only about 1% of the overall book.

items.statement: Gold loan branch expansion: opened 120 branches last year, opening 360 this year to reach ~480 total; expansion paced to branch productivity (Phase 1 avg INR21 cr AUM/branch)
items.quote: Last year, we have opened 120. This year, we are opening some 360 branches. Ranjith: 360 branches, so by end of this year, we should be at 480 branches

items.statement: Vehicle finance distribution: combined branch and resident location count of 1,595 + 689 = 2,284; converting ~125 RLHs to branches as they hit critical disbursement numbers
items.quote: We are moving some 125 RL H to branches because they are already hit critical disbursement numbers. So that will happen. And then once that process continues, then we will add more

items.statement: Repricing of floating-rate portfolios in Affordable Housing and LAP to be implemented over next 1-2 months to offset cost of funds increase
items.quote: In addition, wherever there is scope to reprice floating-rate portfolios, we will take appropriate pricing actions. As of now, businesses such as Affordable Housing and Loan Against Property are evaluating these actions and may implement them over the next one to two months.

items.statement: PLR hike in home loans and LAP planned for Q3 FY27
items.quote: We have not done. We will do it in this quarter, coming quarter, quarter 3.

items.statement: Vehicle finance share at 52% of AUM; mortgage (HL+LAP) at 36-37% likely to rise slightly over 3-4 years; CSEL/CD/Gold to stay within 15% max near term
items.quote: Vehicle finance, which is financing for 5 to 6 years, obviously, they will come down from 52% to below 50%. That only the change will happen. As far as the small ticket size and consumer business is concerned, where CSEL, CD and gold is concerned, they are going to be within 15% max in the near term.

items.statement: One of largest players in Maruti financing; continuously increasing market share especially in upcountry/rural markets; preferred partner for entry cars
items.quote: We are one of the largest player in the Maruti, and we have been continuously increasing our market share with them, especially in the upcountry market, rural market, where whatever entry car we are selling, we are the partner with them.

items.statement: Assignment (DA) income limited to 5-7% of book; exhausted limits for committed deals; may not pursue new assignments in near future
items.quote: We have also internally decided to keep anywhere between 5% to 7% of the book as an assigned book. That's what we will work towards to keep that level.

items.statement: Total liquid assets INR21,974 crores including undrawn sanctioned credit lines; CAR 20.62% with Tier 1 at 16.02% as of Sep 2026
items.quote: The company continues to maintain a strong liquidity and capital position with total liquid assets of INR21,974 crores, including undrawn sanctioned credit lines. As of September 2026, the capital adequacy ratio stood at 20.62% with Tier 1 capital at 16.02%.

items.statement: Drought impact assessment: rainfall deficit concentrated in historically drought-prone regions (Vidarbha, Malwa, parts of MP, Karnataka); tractor exposure only 3% of vehicle finance; Rabi season reservoir levels key monitor by Dec
items.quote: The deficit is largely concentrated in regions such as Vidarbha, Malwa, parts of Madhya Pradesh, and certain districts of Karnataka, which have historically been drought-prone areas. Cholamandalam Investment and Therefore, we do not believe this is likely to affect the overall growth momentum

items.statement: Insurance commission reform impact: evaluated scenarios and have alternative revenue levers; awaiting final clarity on extent of reduction before implementing measures
items.quote: On insurance income, as mentioned earlier, we have already evaluated various scenarios and do not believe this will create a significant issue for us. We have alternative plans and revenue levers available. At this stage, we are waiting for greater clarity on the actual extent of any reduction in insurance income.

items.statement: Management reiterated medium-term guidance of INR 700 crore revenue by FY28 with 35-36% EBITDA margin, implying ~20-25% CAGR top-line growth.
items.quote: Yes, medium term, I think we are quite confident. If I may give an analogy for Vimta, it's like a coiled spring now. So there's a lot of potential in this spring. We need the right opportunities for this spring to really jump up because the base is very strong.

items.statement: Capex budget for FY27 is approximately INR 80 crore, including INR 45-50 crore maintenance capex; remaining focused on analytical capabilities and self-service offerings.
items.quote: As stated in our last conference call, we have budgeted approximately INR80 crores for capex for FY '27, which includes a maintenance capex of around INR45 crores to INR50 crores.

items.statement: Capex utilization in H1 FY27 was lower than planned (INR 112-115 crore spent); H2 utilization expected to align with plan.
items.quote: Capex because the first 2 quarters were around INR112 crores, INR115 crores. The capex was not utilized as planned. But H2, we think the utilization will be as planned for H2.

items.statement: Biologics CRADS: initial order booked, active discussions with multiple clients, targeting onboarding a couple more in Q3; revenue contribution modest now, expected to become significant in 2-3 years.
items.quote: We are already working on the initial order that has been booked. And right now, we are talking with multiple clients, and we hope to onboard at least a couple of them more in this quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 35.5% in Q2, 36% in H1; medium-term risk of 100-200 bps correction due to service mix shift toward biologics, though scale economies may offset manpower/material costs.
items.quote: In the coming quarters, we may not see a shift in any significant manner. But medium term, there is a possibility of correction of around 100 to 200 basis points. This is more to do with the service mix rather than input cost.

items.statement: Gross margin dip due to new capacity absorption and slight increase in material consumption; no reclassification between gross margin and other expenses.
items.quote: Gross margin, there are no reclassifications. The gross margin correction slightly is, as anticipated, we have been discussing in the earlier calls as well because of the additional capacity that we had installed it can have -- our margins can have slight correction. That's one thing. And other thing is there is a slight increase in the material consumption as well

items.statement: Net debt-free with INR 701 crore cash; INR 15 crore new long-term borrowings in H1 for interest arbitrage and to keep cash for opportunities; capex guidance of INR 80 crore unchanged.
items.quote: One is the interest arbitrage cost of borrowing was found to be less than using up our own money. That was one thing. And also, we wanted to have cash on hand in case some opportunities come for us to quickly spend that amount of money.

items.statement: Management reaffirmed FY27 revenue growth guidance of high single digit despite H1 double-digit growth
items.quote: Regarding the guidance, I think we'll stick to what guidance we have given at the beginning of the year.

items.statement: R&D spend expected to ramp up significantly in H2 to meet full-year guidance of 6-7% of sales
items.quote: So what I said is that we expect the R&D spend to significantly ramp up in the subsequent quarter. And our expectation is that as that ramps up, we should be able to meet the overall guidance that we've shared with people.

items.statement: Organon acquisition on track to close in Q4 FY27 with regulatory approvals secured in majority of regions
items.quote: We are now on track to close the transaction as per earlier communicated timelines, that is Q4 of FY27.

items.statement: Acquisition-related exceptional costs will continue until closing in Q4 FY27 and some costs are back-ended
items.quote: So the acquisition-relating cost will continue until day 1, and some of these could be back-ended, right? So as we close the transaction in Q4 of FY27, we will have a full estimate in terms of the acquisition-related costs.

items.statement: Organon acquisition debt cost expected to be in line with Organon's weighted average cost of debt; recent NCD issue separate from transaction financing
items.quote: So first of all, when I spoke about the cost of debt, it is the weighted average cost of debt of Organon. You would see that some of the bonds were at a much lower rate, which was raised earlier. So one should look at it in totality. Secondly, the NCDs that we issued now is not part of transaction financing. This is part of our normal financing to repay some of our current borrowings.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue grew 25.14% but PAT only 7% due to raw material cost pressure and higher interest cost from increased working capital
items.quote: As I mentioned in my opening remarks, the EBITDA margin is down primarily because of the increase in raw material costs. So the major reason for lower growth in profit margin is primarily that the increase in raw material cost.

items.statement: Rail volume target of 100,000 TEUs per quarter as bare minimum; double-digit growth targeted for next year
items.quote: So rest of the year also, this 100,000 for the rail volumes is the bare minimum that we're targeting for the quarter. And next year should see some additional growth on that because we'll be getting a full year of Ankleshwar EXIM operations as well. So our guidance remains in that double-digit thing for both -- maybe this full year, we have to see again because Q1 took a big hit. But for next year

items.statement: Rail volumes expected to continue at similar trend with uncertainty month-to-month; Ankleshwar EXIM permissions now in place
items.quote: Yes, volume, we expect to continue at a similar trend. There is still uncertainty overall, like 1 month is good, 1 month is bad, it's been going like that. But overall, we've been able to gain some volumes, a little bit domestic also has started. Ankleshwar has got all its EXIM permissions now in place. So Q3, we'll see some volumes of that come in.

items.statement: Price increases passed through after fuel hikes; cost increased accordingly; Ankleshwar EXIM mix may reduce realization per TEU due to shorter lead distance
items.quote: There was some price increases. This was mainly after fuel hikes came in, so we've passed that on to customers. But our cost also increased accordingly to that. So that was pretty much a pass-through. Ankleshwar mix, yes, that has also made some difference. And with EXIM coming in at Ankleshwar, you'll see the realization per TEU go down a little bit because of its shorter lead distance.

items.statement: 5PL segment grew 1-2% with one customer negative growth, others positive; discussions on verge of closure for new customers
items.quote: So so far, we have not added any new customer in this financial year in 5PL. A few of the discussions are on the verge of closure, yet not concluded. In terms of growth within the partners who are already there, one of the customer has shown a negative growth, but rest have shown a positive growth. And overall segment grew by 1% or 2% to be precise.

items.statement: Snowman adding 23,000 pallets in next few months; another 20,000 pallets under discussion; park-and-pay capacity reduced as leases ended
items.quote: So we do have a plan wherein currently, we are constructing around 23,000 pallets odd pallets, which are under construction and another 20-odd thousand pallets are under discussion. So this will continue to -- I mean, we will continue to grow as per our P&L -- I mean, as per our P&L thing. So, the expansion is on radar.

items.statement: Indore ICD civil and rail works started; targeting operational by December 2027; volumes to ramp up over 2 years
items.quote: Yes, it's in full swing. So civil and rail works have started. We're targeting by within December 2027, if we can be operational. And following, say, 6 months after that, it can start contributing some good volumes. It takes 2 years to ramp it up after operations, but we should start seeing something within the first year itself.

items.statement: Gateway started bundled rail-terminal offerings in 2008; protecting market share in NCR, Punjab, Uttarakhand; increasing share in some areas; using IT advancements like AP integration, OCR tracking

So we are able to protect our market share like NCR, Punjab and Uttarakhand. And so we are able to protect our market share. In fact, in some of the areas, we are able to increase our market share as well.

items.statement: Existing dry capacity around 10-12% of total; three dedicated dry warehouses adjoining cold facilities

items.quote: There are certain guardrails in the contract.
