items.quote: It is about Rs. 1,000 crore in India and about $90 million would be international.

items.statement: International capacity expansion underway in South Africa, Zimbabwe, Morocco, DRC; India adding Suratgarh greenfield plant and PET line
items.quote: international markets, we have to add lines in South Africa, Zimbabwe, Morocco, DRC at all these locations. And the combined capex for all these is under $100 million

items.statement: Gross margin moderated 334 bps YoY to 53.1% in Q3 CY2026 due to higher packaging costs (300 bps impact) and non-beverage sales (100 bps impact)
items.quote: gross margin moderated by 334 basis points year -on-year to 53.1% in Q3 calendar year 2026, primarily due to higher packaging material costs

items.statement: EBITDA margin moderated only 140 bps to 21.6% in Q3 CY2026 despite gross margin pressure, supported by operating leverage from volume growth
items.quote: EBITDA increased by 25.1% year -on-year to the level of Rs. 14,267 million in Q3 CY2026 with EBITDA margin at 21.6%.

items.statement: Packaging costs increased due to geopolitical disruptions; sugar cost increase offset by low/no-sugar portfolio share rising from 44% to 88% in India
items.quote: packaging cost contributed approximately 300 bps of pressure on gross margin. In addition, sales of non -beverage products such as preforms and caps in India increased by approximately 104% during the quarter.

items.statement: Downsized Sting from 300ml to 250ml in May-June 2026; industry discussing price-pack actions if raw material costs remain elevated
items.quote: we have already reduced the pack size of Sting from 300 ml to 250 ml. So, depending upon the market condition, competitive scenario, etc., the other products in the portfolio will also be reviewed from time to time.

items.statement: India volume grew 22.5% YoY in Q3 CY2026; international volume grew 39.9% YoY; consolidated volume up 28.7% to 354.4 million cases
items.quote: Volume grew by a strong 22.5% during the quarter, while international territories recorded robust growth of 39.9%.

items.statement: Low/no-sugar portfolio share in India increased from 44% to 88% YoY; carbonated soft drinks 73.3%, juice 4.8%, water 21.9% of volume mix
items.quote: share of low-sugar or no -sugar products has increased from 44% to 88%

items.statement: Distribution network expanded to 4.2 million outlets; adding 200,000 outlets annually; launched B2B app 'Bandhan' with 0.5 million monthly retailer orders
items.quote: We are already at about 4.2 million as per our last read, which is there. And we are hoping to add a couple of 100,000 outlets every year.

items.statement: Management sees room for all players to grow given low per capita consumption; unorganized sector under margin pressure but not directly comparable
items.quote: the per caps in India are still very low right now compared to even our neighbouring countries and the amount of expansion of growth, which is there even for us and our competition today, we all can grow.

items.statement: African currencies stabilized this year; South African rand appreciated since BevCo/Twizza acquisition; no currency concerns
items.quote: There is no worry, Vivek. The only thing is last year, local currencies had gone up vis-a-vis dollar. This year, this has stabilized.

items.statement: Twizza-BeVCo merger completed August 1, 2026; KIVA Spirits incorporated for RTD/alcoholic beverages; open to inorganic opportunities in alcobev
items.quote: With effect from 1st August 2026, the merger of Twizza with BevCo has been completed, and we expect to unlock significant operational synergies in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Interim dividend of 25% face value (Rs 0.50/share) approved, total cash outflow Rs 1,691 million
items.quote: the Board of Directors have approved an interim dividend of 25% of the face value, Rs. 0.50 per share, resulting in total cash outflow of Rs. 1,691 million.

items.statement: Consolidated net realization per case improved 2.2% YoY; India realization up 0.5% on premium mix and price-pack architecture
items.quote: Consolidated net realization per case for beverages improved by 2.2% year-on-year, supported by a 0.5% increase in India on account of growth in high-value categories

items.statement: rPET constitutes ~25% of packaging mix, internally sourced; provides cost advantage vs virgin PET; next rPET plant operational in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: Our rPET mix, Bhavya, has been about close to 25%, which has helped negate the overall resin cost is what we were mentioning earlier.

items.statement: FSSAI banned 'energy' word on labels; Sting volumes recovering after disruption; Calpis launch planned for December-January
items.quote: the energy is coming back. I am sure you are aware of the whole issue, which happened with FSSAI that they had banned the use of the word energy on labels.

items.statement: Geopolitical war driving packaging cost inflation; uncertainty on duration; industry may take collective price-pack actions if costs persist
items.quote: looking at the geopolitical situation, nobody really knows when this war is going to end and what is going to happen with the fuel prices.

items.statement: AI-driven distribution optimization reduced distributor attrition; 4M+ outlets geo-mapped; order management system with EY provides daily visibility
items.quote: All of the outlets are geo-lat-long mapped now. All our distributors are mapped across India, all the thousands of them we have, all our route operations, route sizing, time to delivery, all of that speed to delivery is mapped basis the AI tool what we use

items.statement: Mondelez distribution agreement in Zimbabwe ($11M existing business); Kenya operations started with BOLT UP and XTREME FIZZ brands
items.quote: They already have an existing business of about $11 million in Zimbabwe with the local partner they were working with, We are sure he was not able to harness the full potential of the market.

items.statement: Non-beverage sales (preforms, caps) up 104% YoY; sold above internal consumption to amortize fixed costs; may continue if material available
items.quote: sales of non -beverage products such as preforms and caps in India increased by approximately 104% during the quarter.

items.statement: Depreciation and finance costs increased 34.5% and 53.5% YoY due to Twizza acquisition and associated debt funding
items.quote: Depreciation and finance costs increased by 34.5% and 53.5%, respectively, primarily on account of acquisition of Twizza in South Africa and the associated debt funding.

items.statement: Expects wealth business to break even in 6-18 months; in-house manufacturing will take longer
items.quote: So we hope that we should break even in the next maybe 6 months to 18 months. But what has happened is that subsequently, we have started in-house manufacturing also. And we are close to about -- roughly about INR4,500 crores, right? In-house manufacturing. We have roughly about INR4,500 crores of in-house manufacturing and we're investing in that. So that, I think, will take a longer time to brea

items.statement: Employee cost of INR194 crores per quarter expected to continue for rest of year
items.quote: Quarter, yes. That'd be the number.

items.statement: Insurance distribution to be focused on for next 2 quarters before new regulations; long-term focus on capital markets distribution
items.quote: And for the next 2 quarters, we'll focus on this because before the new regulat ions kick in. But on the long term, if you ask me, we will focus more on the capital markets distribution rather than insurance distribution

items.statement: Fairfax preferential allotment and open offer under implementation, expected to close in November; Fairfax to join promoter group
items.quote: The pref allotment and open offer are under implementation and we are expecting that we will get closed in this month of November itself. Consequent to this, Fairfax will join the Promoter Group along with existing promoters.

items.statement: Fairfax funds to be used for margin funding and repayment of borrowings
items.quote: See, actually, I think we have the -- fund utilization will happen and bulk of it will go for, I think, margin funding. So repayment of borrowing will be one use of funds and margin funding book will be the other use of funds.

items.statement: Proposing to incorporate wholly owned NBFC subsidiary for lending and credit solutions to HNI segment, subject to RBI approval
items.quote: The other update is, we also propose to incorporate a wholly owned NBFC subsidiary, and we want to -- and this, basically, NBFC is aligned with the company's strategy to expand the financial services offerings and develop lending and credit solutions to HNI segment. This is, of course, subject to regulatory approvals from RBI.

items.statement: Global environment challenging due to geopolitical tensions, elevated oil prices, high interest rates; India GDP grew 7.8% in Q1 FY27, medium-term fundamentals strong
items.quote: The global environment remained challenging during Q2 FY27 because of geopolitical tensions, elevated oil prices, high interest rates, and that has led to increased volatility across multiple asset classes. However, India remains resilient. Our GDP is showing signs of growth. I think it grew 7.8% in Q1 FY27, and it's been supported by manufacturing services.

items.statement: Consolidated operational revenue INR722 crores, up 14% QoQ and 22% YoY; retail equities INR316 crores (+6% QoQ, +17% YoY); institutional equities INR245 crores (+18% QoQ, +31% YoY); FPD income INR159 crores (+27% QoQ, +23% YoY)
items.quote: Consolidated operational revenue for the quarter was INR722 crores, up 14% quarter-on-quarter, 22% year-on-year. If you compare Q2 FY27 with Q1 FY27, the retail equities was INR316 crores, which was up 6%. We saw a significant growth in our institutional and banking revenues. It was up 18%, INR245 crores versus INR207 crores in the first quarter. Basically, we have seen traction in broking as well

items.statement: H1 FY27 retail equity income up 15% to INR613 crores; institutional equity up 16% to INR451 crores; FPD income flat at INR285 crores vs INR275 crores
items.quote: Coming to year-on-year basis for H1 '27 versus H1 '26. Then, we have seen a 15% increase in retail equity, INR613 crores. Institutional equity income was up 16%, INR451 crores versus INR390 crores. FPD income was virtually flat, INR285 crores versus INR275 crores because in the last year first quarter, we had seen some exceptional upfront transactional income.

items.statement: In-house equity products earn ~2-2.5% fee; third-party products earn ~50% cut (approx 1-1.5%)
items.quote: Typically, on the equity products in-house, we get about 2%, 2.5%, 2.25% maybe, and third-party products it will be about a 50% cut. I think these are rough numbers. I hope I give you directionally the answer.

items.statement: FPD ARR assets grew 5% sequentially; key drivers: AUM growth, insurance income uptick expected in next 2 quarters; ARR income from AIF, PMS, mutual funds
items.quote: See, in the FPD income, the key driver earlier was there were some components, which was the ARR income, some amount of transaction income, some insurance income also. I think going ahead, in the next 2 quarters, at least we should see some uptick on the i nsurance income. And the key driver will be growth of AUM. So ARR AUM should increase and that will drive the income

items.statement: Marginal impact from RBI regulations effective Q2 FY27; no prop trading so minimal impact
items.quote: Yes, no. We have seen marginal impact. Nothing to write home about because we have no prop. So I don't think we have any impact, if I can say.

items.statement: Average daily turnover INR3,05,073 crores (F&O INR3,01,785 crores, Cash INR3,288 crores), down ~3% QoQ but up 16% YoY
items.quote: INR3,05,073 crores, of which F&O was INR3,01,785 crores. Cash was INR3,288 crores in Q2 FY27 versus INR3,15,780 crores, F&O INR3,12,480 crores and cash was INR3,300 crores in Q1 FY27, which was down roughly 3% on an overall ADTO basis. We have actually done reasonably well compared to the overall decline in market volumes. On a year-on-year basis, we have seen a 16% increase because that the last

items.statement: Institutional broking ~INR250 crores and investment banking ~INR200 crores in Q2 FY27 (total ~INR450 crores)
items.quote: Coming to institutional broking and investment banking, I think for this quarter, it was roughly about INR450 crores, out of which I think the split would be about INR250 crores of broking and ~INR200 crores of institutional investment banking.

items.statement: Open to selling insurance distribution business to enhance shareholder value
items.quote: Actually, yes. We are open to all discussions to enhance shareholder value. So I think we'll explore.

items.statement: Fairfax transaction ultimately aims to subsume IIFL Capital and Go Digit into a bank as subsidiary per Fairfax disclosures
items.quote: Actually, you have a very good point you've made. So actually, the Fairfax press release mentions about that. But it says that ultimately, the interest of both Go Digit and IIFL Capital will get subsumed into the bank. Maybe become a part of the bank as a subsidiary. So I think that's what will happen in the long term. Although this question is better answered by Fairfax people than us.

items.statement: Promoters will not tender shares in Fairfax open offer; will only sell if open offer doesn't reach 51%
items.quote: See, the way we have structured the transaction is that the promoters and the group -- promoter group will not offer shares in the open offer. As and when the open offer gets concluded, if they don't make it to 51%, only then we'll give shares to them.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 7.5-8% for Q3 FY27 (Oct-Dec) and expected to continue for future quarters
items.quote: For the next quarter, that is coming in as October, November, December quarter is the guidance that we are giving. And I hope, unless there are some other major changes, that should continue for the future quarters also.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin at 5.4% due to elevated milk procurement costs and inflationary pressures on logistics, packaging and overheads
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR64.1 crores translating into an EBITDA margin of 5.4%.

items.statement: Implemented INR2.5 per liter price increase in September; full impact visible in Q3 FY27; further hikes if cooperatives increase prices
items.quote: In response to the rising procurement cost, we implemented the price increase of approximately INR2.5 per liter. Consequently, our average milk sales realization improved to INR61.9 per liter in Q2 FY '27 compared with INR59.4 per liter in the previous quarter and INR57.3 per liter in the corresponding quarter of last year.

items.statement: Milk procurement cost rose to INR43.2/liter in Q2 FY27 from INR41/liter in Q1 FY27 and INR37.3/liter in Q2 FY26; expected to remain at elevated levels with only INR0.2-0.3 variation
items.quote: Average milk procurement cost increased to INR43.2 per liter in Q2 FY '27 compared to INR41 per liter in previous quarter and INR37.3 per liter in Q2 of FY '26.

items.statement: VAP revenue grew 11.7% YoY; curd volume up 23% YoY; summer products softer due to seasonality; festive demand expected for sweets, ghee, paneer
items.quote: Coming to our value-added portfolio, the revenue from this category grew 11.7% on a year-on-year basis. However, the demand for the higher-margin summer-related products such as curd, butter milk, flavored milk, ice cream, etcetera, remained softer as compared to the previous quarters due to seasonality factor.

items.statement: Paneer volume up 64% YoY; lassi volume up 163% YoY; ice cream volume grew; bulk ghee sale absent this quarter affecting VAP revenue comparison
items.quote: So our categories in terms of paneer has improved significantly, for example, in terms of volume and also our other products like flavored milk and others have also improved. For example, paneer has improved by 64%, if I take it as a volume, although the volume is smaller, it is roughly -- it has improved by 2.5 tons per day for us in terms of increase in volume.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex INR66 crores mainly for Maharashtra expansion; total projected capex ~INR600 crores (Maharashtra INR280 crores, Africa INR60-70 crores, OSAM acquisition net INR600 crores) with 5-10% potential increase
items.quote: INR600 crores that you were asking as capex, we had earlier assumed Africa to be around the INR60 crores, INR70 crores, Africa -- I mean, Maharashtra to be INR280 crores and the acquisition of OSAM that we did net of cash of what was available in OSAM to be around INR600 crores.

items.statement: Maharashtra plant: liquid milk operations from March-April 2027, powder operations by September 2027; Uganda greenfield civil work started, targeting FY28 operations start
items.quote: No, it will go ahead. From March, we'll be -- March to April, we'll start our -- the liquid milk operations will start. And by September, we will -- September we'll start our powder operations.

items.statement: Africa revenue INR179 crores, up 56% YoY driven by 68.5% milk sales volume growth; Kenya market share gains; Uganda greenfield expansion underway
items.quote: Moving on to our Africa business. It delivered a strong quarter with a record of INR179 crores, representing a year-on-year growth of 56%.

items.statement: Board approved JV with Meadow India Holdings (40% Dodla, 60% Meadow) for B2B dairy ingredients; Dodla investing INR1 crore; exploratory venture for ingredient supply agreements
items.quote: I would also like to inform you that the Board has approved a proposal to establish a joint venture in India with Meadow India Holdings Limited with Dodla Dairy and Meadow India Holdings Limited having an equity stake of 40% and 60%, respectively.

items.statement: H1 FY27 inventory build-up of INR76 crores (SMP and butter); total inventory INR232 crores as of Sept 2026; cash balance INR659.4 crores sufficient for future capex
items.quote: During the period, we incurred capital expenditure of INR66 crores primarily towards our Maharashtra expansion project. As of September 2026, we maintained a healthy cash and bank balance of INR659.4 crores, which is sufficient for our future capex requirement.

items.statement: Milk procurement 21.3 LLPD in Q2 FY27, up 9.3% YoY; milk sales volume 14.2 LLPD, up 8.4% YoY; spread narrowed to INR18.7/liter from INR20/liter YoY
items.quote: For Q2 FY '27 the milk procurement stood at 21.3 lakh liters per day, registering year-on-year growth of 9.3%.

items.statement: OSAM EBITDA margin 1% in Q2 FY27 vs 2.6% in Q1 FY27; targeting 4-5% EBITDA margin in H2 FY27 as procurement model shifts to direct farmer payments (70-80% by March)
items.quote: Margins are -- for the quarter, EBITDA margins are 1% this year -- this quarter. Last quarter, we had 2.6%. It was reducing. Due to the milk prices increasing, we are not very aggressively going.

items.statement: Feed cost inflation expected due to ethanol and compressed biogas policies diverting maize; government policy impact to be monitored
items.quote: Yes. The price increase will get inflation a little more going ahead because I think it is not only going to be for us, but for the industry as a whole because of ethanol coming into play, compressed biogas coming into play.

items.statement: OSAM region (Bihar/Jharkhand) dominated by Sudha (~70% share) with payment delays; Amul, ITC, UP brands entering; Dodla shifting to direct farmer payment model for competitive advantage
items.quote: Almost 70% of the market share is Sudha. But Sudha is not very active. As usual, the payment running late by 1 or 2 months. There are a lot of market complaints. So many things are there. So definitely, we will have advantage.

items.statement: Orgafeed revenue up 40% YoY in Q2 FY27; margins impacted by raw material costs not fully passed to farmers; exploring Maharashtra feed expansion after integrated facility operational
items.quote: Speaking about our Orgafeed business, it is continuing to deliver a strong growth with revenue increasing by 40% year-on-year in Q2 FY '27. However, margins were impacted by higher raw material costs, which could not be fully passed on to the farmers.

items.statement: Procurement prices front-loaded in H1 FY27; no further significant increases expected in Q3/Q4 FY27 due to steady milk volumes and inventory build-up; farming variability decreasing
items.quote: Yes, B.V.K. will answer the question regarding view. B.V.K. Reddy: Yes, see this is front-loaded already in the second quarter. So this is unusual. Earlier years, normally quarter 2 prices used to come down -- quarter 2 and quarter 3 and quarter 4 used to go up. Now this year, see the quarter 1 and quarter 2 already prices have gone up, quarter 2 also substantially. We don't see any price hike. We

items.statement: Q3 expected to be best ever quarter in almost all businesses with strong growth over Q2
items.quote: We also believe that the EBITDA of the group has grown 20% from Q2 over Q1. We believe we will have similar growth rates of EBITDA sequentially from Q2 to Q3. Q3 this year is likely to be our best ever quarter in almost all our businesses.

items.statement: OLX growth rates expected to surpass current 26% and cross 30-35% in coming quarters
items.quote: We feel the OLX growth rates, which you see, will be surpassed in the coming quarters. We of course think the growth rate will cross 30%, 35% in the coming quarters at OLX.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded to 36% in Q2 from 33% YoY and 31% QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA margins come out at 36%. As you know, your company is focused on building a best-in-class margin structure. You can see here, EBITDA margin has jumped from 33% last year quarter to 36% and 36% over 31% previous quarter same time.

items.statement: Consumer group EBITDA margin reached 41% in Q2
items.quote: If you look at the consumer group, which is the next slide, revenue from operations are up 4%, EBITDA is up 5%, and margins have come to 41%, and PAT is up 13%.

items.statement: OLX EBITDA margin improved to 32%
items.quote: OLX is actually, revenues had a very strong growth. We had 28% half yearly growth, a 26% quarter growth. EBITDA margins are up to 32% in OLX, and EBITDA growth is up to 36% here.

items.statement: Remarketing EBITDA margin up 30%
items.quote: If you go further to the Remarketing business, profits have grown by 47%, margin is up 30%, revenue is up 13% half yearly, 12% for the quarter, and EBITDA margins, 29% growth in EBITDA for the quarter.

items.statement: Festival season delayed by ~10 days this year shifting demand from September to October
items.quote: is also correct that the entire festival season last year ended in October. I think this year it will overflow to November, so it got slightly delayed and that effect you will probably see this quarter

items.statement: SAMIL auctioned 2.35 lakh vehicles out of 1.56 million listed (annualized for Q2)
items.quote: We have about 1.56 million vehicles which were listed, of which 2.35 lakh were auctioned. These are annualized for Q2.

items.statement: OEM revenue share in consumer business at ~74%, up slightly from ~70% previously
items.quote: About 74% would be OEM in total revenues.

items.statement: New products like Elite Buyer, Elite Seller, VAYA Live driving growth; existing products also contributing strongly
items.quote: The growth rates you are seeing are 26%, and the growth rates are going to increase over the next quarter and the quarter after that, is a large part due to the existing products and not just new products. I think new products will come on top of that.

items.statement: VAYA Live development cost not material as built on proprietary data and AI code without LLM token costs
items.quote: The costs are not significant, and I will tell you why. Because a lot of V AYA is built, first of all, it is built on AI code. The second part is that it is built on proprietary data. We do not buy data or use LLM data

items.statement: No significant CAPEX or working capital expense; most profits convert to cash
items.quote: The good thing in a company like ours is there is no CAPEX really. There is no really working capital expense, and most of the profits we generate, almost all the profits we generate go to cash.

items.statement: Cash reserves of INR 1,400 crores earmarked for M&A if opportunities found, else shareholder distribution
items.quote: ideally, this cash, we have talked about before, will get used for M&A, if at all, but M&As are hard to find, and we have been very good with M&A in the past, but we obviously have not found anything at this point in the last two to three years or it will go to distribution back to sharehol ders in the form of buyback and dividend

items.statement: ESOP costs insignificant and declining over last 5 years; no material dilution expected
items.quote: The share-based payment, the amount of ESOPs are just for management, and team members, but it is very insignificant. We really do not see any significant dilution for shareholders at any point. If you see the ESOP cost continuously over the last five years has been coming down in the company.

items.statement: Monthly active users (MAU) at 76 million average for Q2; organic traffic at 96%
items.quote: We receive 76 million MAUs average for this quarter. Organic traffic has jumped to 96%.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue highest ever at INR 213 crores; total income highest ever at INR 236 crores
items.quote: The company in this quarter, I am glad to inform you, has recorded its highest ever revenue in its history at INR 236 crores of total income. PBT is highest ever, again, in this quarter is at INR 85 crores.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA crossed INR 106 crores for the quarter; PAT at INR 66 crores
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA, which is a cash proxy, has crossed INR 106 crores for the quarter. PAT is at INR 66 crores and as I told you earlier, our cash balances are at INR 1,400 crores as of 30th September.

items.statement: Remarketing revenue up 12% QoQ, 13% half-yearly; PAT up 47%
items.quote: If you go further to the Remarketing business, profits have grown by 47%, margin is up 30%, revenue is up 13% half yearly, 12% for the quarter, and EBITDA margins, 29% growth in EBITDA for the quarter. PAT has grown by 47% in the quarter on the Remarketing business.

items.statement: Base effect from GST reduction in Sep 2025 inflated Q2 FY26 growth to 37%, creating tough YoY comparison
items.quote: The one big event last year, in fact, it has been game changing and great credit to the government in the entire automotive industry. I think anybody in automotive has seen a massive jump last year. There is a base effect there.

items.statement: Landmark partnership for curated marketplace; working capital investment and margin sharing equations being finalized
items.quote: We are working out whether from a margin structure, whether we should invest some part of the working capital or not, and that is based on how much margin we want to share. Those equations are being worked out as we go on ahead.

items.statement: VAYA Live rollout expected this quarter for both OEM/dealer and consumer sides
items.quote: We are very hopeful that sometime this quarter. We are already testing it out and we did show a demo of this to analysts in an analyst meeting earlier. But we are very hopeful that somewhere in this quarter, it will roll out for both OEMs and consumers.

items.statement: Total insurance premium expected over ₹40,000 Cr for FY27
items.quote: The total insurance premium for the quarter was ₹9,385 Cr, up 38% year-on-year, setting us up well for over ₹40,000 Cr this year.

items.statement: Demand has been tough this year requiring higher marketing spend to generate leads
items.quote: Actually, demand has been very tough, and I think we've had to spend a lot more money. So I would say that if you look at it on a two-year basis, you'll find it's not that dramatic.

items.statement: PAT margin improved from 8% to 9% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: PAT grew 43% to ₹192 Cr, and PAT margin improved from 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Core renewal and trail revenue over ₹1,000 Cr on rolling 12-month basis, up 42% YoY
items.quote: And our core renewal and trail revenue is now over ₹1,000 Cr, it's almost ₹1,100 Cr. On a rolling 12-month basis, up 42% year-on-year.

items.statement: CapEx increased substantially to support office expansion and staff growth
items.quote: As we have spoken earlier about this, that we have been building capacity, we have been ramping up, and P0 remains our growth. So, this CapEx is largely towards supporting the expansion of offices, as well as supporting the staff.

items.statement: October hiring was a very small fraction of past levels as cost consciousness increases
items.quote: Our approach on that front, as we've already explained, will, and has already started to take a shift. Our October hiring was a very, very small fraction of what it might have been in the past.

items.statement: Health customers pay on average 9% less and up to 30% less than some other channels
items.quote: On price reduction, for the plans they choose, our health customers pay, on average, 9% less and up to 30% less than some other channels.

items.statement: Core online new health and term grew 42% YoY, new health grew 46% YoY
items.quote: Core online new health and term grew 42% YoY, and within this, new health gr ew 46% YoY

items.statement: IRDAI consultation paper aims for lower mis-selling, better claims, lower prices, deeper penetration; company supports goals fully
items.quote: IRDAI's consultation paper aims for lower mis-selling, better claims experience, lower prices, and deeper penetration. We absolutely support all of these goals fully.

items.statement: Lower distribution payouts will reduce insurance distribution revenue; evaluating options to strengthen business
items.quote: Lower distribution payouts will reduce our insurance distribution revenue, for sure. We are working on three fronts. We will expand our non -insurance revenue within and as the r egulator permits

items.statement: POSP business model under question due to open architecture payout structure; may need transition time
items.quote: The way the current regulations are, it says, if you are open architecture, you're going to get paid less than the closed architecture. That in my opinion, does not leave scope for POSP the way it is today.

items.statement: Health claims settlement ratio 97% vs industry 87%; 11,156 rejected claims worth ₹185 Cr reopened and paid last year
items.quote: On claims in the health insurance industry, the industry data says 87% of health claims are settled. That same number for Policybazaar customers is 97%. Last year, 11,156 rejected claims worth ₹185 Cr were reopened after initial rejection and paid.

items.statement: Life persistency 71% at month 61 vs benchmark 51-66%; health renewal 89% rising to 91% from second year
items.quote: On persistency, 71% of our life policies are still in force at month 61. This is against a benchmark of 51% to 66% for the large players. Our renewal in health insurance is at 89%, rising to 91% from sec ond-year renewals

items.statement: Mis-selling complaints: 16 per 10,000 customers in life vs benchmark 30-53; 21 claim complaints per 10,000 claims in health vs benchmark 29-54
items.quote: On mis-selling, in the life insurance category, we get 16 complaints from our customers per 10,000 customers. This is against a benchmark of 30 to 53. In health insurance, we get 21 claim complaints for every 10,000 claims. This is against a benchmark of 29 to 54.

items.statement: 40% of new retail health customers nationwide come through Policybazaar; 25%+ of India's pure term premium and 17.8% of retail health premium
items.quote: About 40% of new customers added in Retail Health across the country come through us. More than a quarter of India's pure term premium, 17.8% of the retail health premium came through us last year.

items.statement: 74% of term policies and 64% of health policies from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities
items.quote: 74% of our term policies and 64% of our health policies come from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

items.statement: AI/GenAI lever to improve efficiency; advisors handling 15-20% more leads, faster training, better conversion
items.quote: There are some slides in the deck about the improvement that we have made, whether in terms of our advisor's ability to handle 15-20% more leads, improve conversion. On the customer service side, on the risk side, on our ability to train our people faster than we used to earlier.

items.statement: PB Partners revenue about ₹700 Cr for the quarter
items.quote: PB Partners revenue; it's about ₹700 Cr.

items.statement: PB Health on track for ₹40-45 Cr monthly run rate by March (~₹500 Cr annual), breaking even
items.quote: We are on track of executing a few new hospitals. So, around March, we should have a run rate somewhere between ₹40-45 Cr per month, which is about ₹500 Cr for the year.

items.statement: Not considering minority stakes in insurers; focused on responsible distribution model with combined operating ratio
items.quote: Taking minority stakes is not one of them. And all I can say is, we are already in conversations with the regulator, of course, in formal conversations.

items.statement: POSP business has cash flow concerns as POSPs paid sooner than collections from insurers
items.quote: There are also cash flow elements in that business, because to a large extent, we end up paying the POSPs sooner than we get paid by the insurance companies.

items.statement: No cash burn intent; cash position is capability but NPV more critical; will assess after final regulations
items.quote: Mentally, the intent is not a cash burn intent. Now, let's see when the paper comes out, and what opportunities arise out of it, and what situations arise out of it.

items.statement: Quarterly revenue grown from ₹280 Cr to ₹2,178 Cr at 51% CAGR since listing; PAT margin from -73% to 9%
items.quote: Since our listing, quarterly revenue has grown from ₹280 Cr to ₹2,178 Cr, a 51% CAGR, and the PAT margin has moved from -73% to 9%.

items.statement: Strategy for next 1000 days: serve customers well, stay cost disciplined, keep investing in underpenetrated market
items.quote: Over the next 1000 days, we will serve customers well, we will stay focused on that, we will stay disciplined on cost, and we will keep investing in a market that remains deeply underpenetrated.

items.statement: GST reduction drove 18% industry growth for 6 months; price elasticity ~1; growth normalized by March; Q4 YoY may not show growth
items.quote: There was an 18% reduction of GST, and that was passed on to the customer. This is a very important data point for informing everyone. For the first 6 months, we saw an incremental 18% growth in the industry.

items.statement: Paisabazaar adding suppliers, new business lines (bill payments, wealth - bonds, FDs); disbursals flat QoQ due to focus on distribution over marketing
items.quote: We saw an opportunity in our customer strata, and we saw a lot of partnerships or suppliers that we could add on our platform, and that will help us grow disbursal. So, in fact, we see in our deck, we've mentioned a few banks that we've onboarded.

items.statement: Market shares up in every segment; growing faster in protection; almost every business outperformed market by at least 2x in Q2
items.quote: Our market shares have gone up in every segment that I can see. We are growing faster in protection. Actually, if you see the spread of businesses in Q2, almost every business has outperformed the market by at least 2x.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 same-store sales growth (SSSG) for EBOs was broadly flat after Q1's 0.6% positive growth
items.quote: After turning positive in Q1 at 0.6%, same-store sales worth for our EBOs in Q2 was broadly flat.

items.statement: Management targets positive SSSG for full FY27
items.quote: Our focus remains on delivering positive SSSG for FY '27 as a whole and the festive quarter will be an important one of that journey.

items.statement: Opened 9 new stores and closed 23 smaller format stores in Q2 FY27; H1 FY27: 24 openings, 89 closures; total 737 EBOs across 196 cities as of Sep 2026
items.quote: During Q2, we have opened 9 new stores and closed 23 smaller format stores in catchments where we already have or are opening a larger store nearby. For H1 FY '27, this takes us to 24 openings and 89 closures for the 6 months and we ended September with a grand total of 737 EBOs across 196 cities.

items.statement: Aim to nearly double square footage over next 5 years with calibrated expansion across Tier-1, Tier-2, Tier-3 cities
items.quote: Over the next 5 years, we aim to significantly expand our footprint with the potential to nearly double our square feet in terms of size.

items.statement: Value-added non-leggings portfolio contributes 70% of revenue, reflecting steady premiumization
items.quote: Our value-added non-leggings portfolio now contributes to 70% of the revenue reflecting the steady premiumization of what Go Colors offers.

items.statement: Target 25-30 dailywear stores by end of FY27; currently 21 operational vs 15 in Q1
items.quote: We remain committed to our target of 25-30 daily stores by the end of FY '27.

We continue to work closely with our partners on assortment, placement and sell-through and LFS contribute

items.statement: Q2 FY27 gross margin 60.8%, down ~200 bps due to higher fabric costs from geopolitical situation; intend to pass on RM inflation via calibrated pricing
items.quote: Gross margins for the quarter stood at 60.8%. As I mentioned on the last call, fabric prices have gone up due to the geopolitical situation, and this higher-cost inventory has started flowing in Quarter 2. We intend to pass on the raw material inflation through calibrated pricing actions which will help restore gross margins in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Price hikes initiated on certain articles recently; more planned post-festive; expect gross margin impact to stabilize in next 2 quarters
items.quote: We have done price hike for certain articles, we have just recently done. And we are in the midst of doing price hike for some other articles as well. So, I think the offset against the gross margin will take a couple of quarters. But I think it will stabilize in the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA before exceptional expenses Rs 56 cr (25.8% margin); H1 FY27 EBITDA before exceptional Rs 123.4 cr (28.0% margin)
items.quote: EBITDA before exceptional expenses stood at Rs. 123.4 crores with EBITDA margin of 28.0%.

items.statement: Exceptional expense Rs 3.4 cr in Q2, Rs 9.9 cr in H1 FY27 from store closure capex write-offs (one-off)
items.quote: During the quarter, we recognized an exceptional expense of Rs. 3.4 crores taking the total of our H1 FY '27 to Rs. 9.9 crores. This exceptional expenditure is a write-off of capital expenditure on account of store closures which has happened through the 6 months. It is a direct consequence of our network consolidation strategy and it is a one-off item.

items.statement: Working capital days 134; inventory days improved to 94 from 100 at end Q1, within guided 90-100 day range
items.quote: Working capital days stood at 134 days, with inventory days improving to 94 days from 100 days at the end of Q1, now within the 90-100 day range which we had guided earlier this year.

items.statement: Operating cash flow (pre-Ind AS 116) Rs 52.6 cr in H1 FY27
items.quote: Operating cash flow on a pre-end year basis stood at a healthy Rs. 52.6 crores.

items.statement: Fabric/yarn cost inflation running at 8-10% blended; RM prices cooled slightly in Jul-Aug but remain high
items.quote: It is between 8% and 10% is what I understand. Because see, the yarn prices and fabric prices have changed every month. But if I have to just take a blended, I think it is about 8%-10% is what we see.

items.statement: Estimate Q3 FY27 gross margin impact of 100-200 bps from RM inflation; Q2 impact was ~200 bps
items.quote: My estimate is, this quarter, we had 200 basis points impact on our GM. I think the next Q3, we should be having a gross margin impact of anywhere between 100 and 200 bps is my estimate.

items.statement: Store closures to reduce considerably in H2; Q3 closures estimated at 15-20 stores vs 23 in Q2 and 58-59 in Q1
items.quote: See, again, because this number changes based on what real estate we find, the closures for Q3 from what visibility I am getting will be anywhere between 15 and 20 stores as of now.

items.quote: If I look at my overall network of large store versus small store, my largest stores are SSSG positive. So, if I take stores which are greater than 750 square feet, they are about 2%-3% or higher SSSG, whereas my smaller stores continue to be negative.

items.statement: Brand ambassador Shraddha Kapoor campaign launched in July; influencer initiatives underway; campaign impact to be assessed post-festive
items.quote: On the brand front, our first campaign featuring Shraddha Kapoor, who came on board as a Brand Ambassador in July, went live during the quarter and it has been very well executed and seen some good results.

items.quote: So, I think our problem of growth, our headwinds of growth is because of our store format rather than anything else. It is mind and management.

items.quote: So, the new facilities are all cold temperature controlled. We have a very minimal share of dry there. Typically, we're planning to shut a chamber and do it in initial time and then convert everything into frozen.

items.statement: Snowman increased scope with major customer to pan-India from 2-3 geographies; 5PL discussions nearing closure for new accounts

items.quote: So all the final arguments have happened now and the order is reserved. So we should be hearing about the order soon. And we're hopeful that it comes in our favor that we can start construction and then plan for operations accordingly.

items.statement: New projects target at least 15% IRR and 7-year payback; includes replacement capex, owned trains, fleet electrification
items.quote: But any new project that we're doing, we're targeting like it's at least a 15% IRR and a 7-year payback, if that kind of helps the guidance a little bit.

items.quote: And in addition to that, the JNPT ports are also working on a strategy that how to increase the rail coefficient, which is very down there. It is only 14% to 15%.

items.statement: Road-to-rail shift potential 10,000-15,000 TEUs/month on JNPT-North route; shipping lines have not indicated increased JNPT calls yet
items.quote: Right now, we've estimated maybe 10,000, 15,000 TEUs moving to North by road can be shifted by the DFC, but it takes time.

items.statement: Snowman power cost increases of 6-8% built into contract pricing at renewal; some contracts not yet renewed
items.quote: No, we typically take like 6% to 8% increase, which is expected in the coming year. When we do a contract, we take that -- we consider that sort of an increase already in the pricing.

And overall segment grew by 1% or 2% to be precise.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 is approximately Rs 200 crore, in line with previous year; FY28 capex not quantified as customer schedules not finalized

items.quote: FY28, it all depends on because we are supplying to our customers. So, right now, the schedules have not finalized where we are setting in. So, in terms of giving you the indication in terms of the capitalization at this moment for FY '28 would be very difficult.

items.statement: Three Greenfield plants have ramped up well and are now operating at optimal utilization levels; considered part of regular plant base
items.quote: As Vaaman sir has also said in his commentary that these three Greenfield plants have progressed, the ramp-up has progressed well. And now, we are operating at a very optimal utilization level.

items.statement: Second half will be compared against higher base post GST reduction; industry expected to continue healthy growth; festive period expected to deliver strong revenue growth
items.quote: Based on current visibility, we expect the industry to continue registering healthy growth. The combination of healthy industry growth, continued premiumization, driving higher content per new vehicle and new model launches provide a favorable backdrop for us.

items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 9.2% improving from 7.6% in Q1 through continued focus on operational efficiencies which led to a resilient performance while headwinds from higher copper prices, minimum wage revisions and other inflationary pressures remain.

items.statement: CRAMS pipeline: >65 active projects in R&D and pilot plant; NMR analytical capabilities deepening engagement with global majors
items.quote: We are currently working on more than 65 CRAMS projects in our R&D and pilot plant. Our NMR-based analytical capabilities have helped us broaden our work with global majors and go deeper into the development pipelines.

items.quote: And the capitalization is happening for the INR200 crores of loans, which we have already taken and the interest rate which is there. So I cannot give you a figure. Otherwise, everybody can know what is the rate. So please excuse me, we can connect separately and I can give it.

items.statement: CWIP of INR700 crores largely for Site 5 (Magnum); ~INR400 crores expected to be capitalized by end of FY27
items.quote: It's a Site 5 majorly. And by end of this year, this financial year, we expect that approximately INR400 crores should be capitalized.

items.statement: Management avoids hazardous chemistries (HF, F2, H2S) and focuses on safety-compatible competencies; says no to inquiries quickly to maintain strategic focus

items.quote: First of all, it's a very flat organization. items.statement: Oil & gas major to dedicate entire Magnum plant with first refusal on adjacent block; announcement expected soon
items.quote: We have one plant with an oil and gas major, which should be an announcement coming very fast, very soon in terms of dedicating an entire plant to them, which -- and they have also asked to reserve the plant next to it and give them the first right of refusal.

items.statement: Multinational material sciences company (one of world's largest) in special collaboration for 2 Magnum plants with 2 more reserved; announcement expected in coming months
items.quote: We have 2 plants that are coming in for a multinational, one of the largest chemical companies in the world, material sciences in a special kind of collaboration that should also be an announcement coming out over the next few months. And they have also asked for 2 plants in reserve.

items.statement: Another customer discussing 4 Magnum plants; if all pipelines convert, only 1 of 16 blocks remains unallocated
items.quote: And so if all of these goes through, we essentially -- and if you have been counting, we essentially have only one plant left. And of course, this is a realistic -- this is the best case scenario. It's a realistic best scenario, but still is the best case scenario. But if the firm pipeline goes through, you're looking at only one plant that we don't have vision for.

items.statement: Baker Hughes new products covered by original Strata site capex; no additional capex required
items.quote: This will all be covered by original capex from the Strata site.

items.quote: Yes. It will be 3, 3.5x at maturity once the -- once the production stream is matured. So we should be around 3x to 3.5x, you're right.

items.statement: Target 40-50% revenue growth for CDMO/CMO segment in FY27
items.quote: We remain on track to achieve our target of 40% to 50% revenue growth over last year on this business segment.

items.statement: Xanthine revenue expected to reach INR1,400-1,500 crores at full capacity if prices remain high
items.quote: Yes, if the prices remain high, we expect this to go up to INR1,400 crores to INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: CDMO long-term target of INR1,000 crores revenue maintained
items.quote: See, as I mentioned, our target remains 100 million or INR1,000 crores, whichever comes first.

items.statement: API segment expected to grow 10-15% annually over next 3-4 years
items.quote: we'll have 10% to 15% growth every year on this business, or we probably in certain years we can have higher growth also.

items.statement: Total capex targeted at INR350-400 crores for FY27
items.quote: Overall, we have targeted a capex of around -- total capex of around INR350 crores to INR400 crores for the year.

items.statement: Xanthine expanded capacity to reach full production by end of FY27, full utilization over next two years
items.quote: The ramp-up of xanthine expanded capacity is progressing and we plan to achieve the full capacity by the end of FY27 and we will achieve the utilization sequentially in the next year.

items.statement: Atali Block 2 ground breaking done, targeting commercialization in H2 FY28
items.quote: The ground breaking of the Atali dedicated block, that is block number two has been done and we target to commercialize this block in the H2 FY28.

items.quote: So, it won't have too much difference or too much bearing on overall capacity addition that we will have in Atali by doing the Phase 1B. But overall, we see that we will be able to completely utilize this Atali asset in the second half of this financial year.

items.statement: Steroid API block debottlenecking completed and contributing to production and revenue
items.quote: The capacity expansion of the steroid block of API plant was completed and it has started contributing to the production and the revenue.

items.statement: Peptide lab to be operational by end of FY27, customer business expected from FY28
items.quote: By the end of this financial year, we will have operational peptide labs with all the equipments. We have already started recruiting, the teams which have experience of peptide and we hope that for the next, calendar year we will start making customer business, start getting customer business in next financial year on the peptide and oligonucleotide side.

items.statement: CDMO has 59 active projects (39 commercial, 20 development) across 23 customers
items.quote: The number of active projects now is 59, out of which 39 projects are in commercial stages and 20 are under different stages of development, both at customers end.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 22.2% in Q2 FY27 vs 17.7% YoY; expect 1 percentage point variation in H2
items.quote: The EBITDA margins have remained healthy at 22.2% as compared to 17.7% in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: CDMO growth and raw material pass-through to drive absolute gross margin increase in H2
items.quote: But in the absolute number, I think gross margins will keep on increasing whatever as we do more quality business going forward.

items.statement: Passing on elevated raw material costs to customers in Xanthine and API segments
items.quote: Due to geopolitical turmoil, the raw material costs have stayed elevated and we are passing on the raw material increase to our customers.

items.statement: Xanthine realization up 10-15% YoY on average; spot segment prices under pressure but pharma/beverage stable
items.quote: The xanthine prices, on an average, our realization is up, 10% to 15% over last year, realization.

items.statement: Xanthine volume growth of ~15-20% YoY expected for FY27; Q2 shipments held up by dispatch constraints

items.quote: Overall, in this entire year, we will have, probably close to 15%, 20% jump over last year's volume.

items.statement: API growth in Q2 largely volume-driven after steroid debottlenecking; headwinds subsiding
items.quote: This is largely volume-driven. The current growth was largely volume-driven.

items.quote: The sub-segment wise breakup is 57% for the regulated market, 33% for the ROW market and 10% for the non -regulated market.

items.quote: Overall working capital cycle remains close to 165 days or 167 days for us. What has happened is that since the sales turnover has gone, sales has gone up, of course, the need of working capital will also go up.

items.statement: Short-term borrowings increased to INR650-660 crores; more debt needed for remaining FY27 capex
items.quote: Well, we will need more debt.

items.statement: New CSO joined 9 months ago, new API R&D head joined; further R&D hiring underway for peptide/oligonucleotide expansion
items.quote: We have the new CSO who has joined since last 9 months. And then we also had a new API R&D head who joined us. We are also further recruiting on the R&D side for the team.

items.statement: Atali new blocks expected to achieve 1.2-1.4x asset turns
items.quote: But I think the newer blocks, we have given the guidance that it will have 1.2 to 1.4 kind of a turn on asset side.

items.statement: Xanthine spot segment pricing under pressure; pharma and beverage segments more stable
items.quote: In Xanthine, there are three segments. So, in the spot segment, the prices will have pressure. I think the pharma and the beverages section, anyway, we will have more stability on the price.

items.statement: Several oncology API patent expiries expected next FY; launching with partners in regulated markets
items.quote: Out of which next financial year, we will have several patent expiries expected. And those products will be launched with our partners in their markets where they have partnered with us.

items.quote: As I have been suggesting, we are looking towards FY28 with CCL, on the old numbers given in the past guidance, including consolidated, at a ₹2,500 crore top line, with EBITDA of 14% and PAT of 11%.

items.statement: Management expects FY27 PAT margin around 6.25% and tax rate near last year's ~15%.
items.quote: The PAT margin this year is expected to be around 6.25%.

items.statement: Management targets base business revenue of ₹1,315 crore in FY27 and ₹1,800 crore by FY28.
items.quote: Last year we did ₹1,080 crores. This year we are reaching the projected target of ₹1,315 crores and we are very much in line with this year's proj ections. Up to FY28, we are targeting to reach ₹1,800 crores as top line

items.statement: Phase 2 capex of ~₹58 crore ongoing for fasteners, tubes, sheet metal and clips to support revenue growth to ₹1,800 crore.

items.statement: CCL project planned investment of ₹338 crore over 2-3 years plus ₹86 crore for captive solar plant, approved under ECMS scheme.
items.quote: The planned investment by Ratnaveer is ₹338 crores over the next two to three years, approved under the ECMS scheme by the Government of Gujarat as well as the Government of India. The plan also covers an ₹86 crore investment in a solar plant for captive use.

items.statement: CCL prices up 300%+ YoY while raw material up 40-50%; management expects huge margin gap and drastic bottom-line improvement; revised guidance coming soon.

items.statement: CCL raw material prices increased 40-50% max vs 300%+ finished goods price increase; no domestic CCL producers currently.

items.statement: CCL facility will produce Tg 140-180, FR4, prepreg, single/double-sided, copper thickness 15-35 microns, thickness range 0.8-3.2 mm covering automotive, EV, drone, satellite, aerospace, data centres.
items.quote: we are producing from 140 Tg to 180 Tg, and we are concentrating on all PCB manufacturing companies, including the automotive industry, EVs, electrical and electronic vehicles, the drone industry, satellite equipment, aerospace and all kinds of electronic devices that use CCL.

items.statement: CCL market growing 60-70% CAGR with zero domestic manufacturers; no saturation; competition only when market saturates; target 7-8% market share in 5 years from ~2% after five lines.

items.statement: 50% cash subsidy on CCL capex available under ECMS scheme; term loans cover five lines; interest subsidy also available.

items.quote: On the working capital part, we have already completed a very successful rights issue, which gives us enough liquidity for the working capital requirement.

items.statement: Five CCL lines mostly covered by term loans; banks available if needed; ECMS interest subsidy and 50% capex cash subsidy reduce funding burden.
items.quote: Mostly, all five lines are covered through term loans, and if required, banks are available. In addition, the interest subsidy and the ECMS scheme are also available, so there is no concern there either.

items.statement: No plan for any equity raise or new fundraise; rights issue completed successfully.
items.quote: No, not at all. There is no plan right now for any kind of equity raise or any new fundraise.

items.statement: 22 Chinese engineers plus 1 CTO (30 years CCL experience) arriving mid-Nov for 2-year stay to install all five lines and manage production/quality.
items.quote: There are other engineers as well. Twenty-two engineers, for the various machines, are arriving, and one person will be staying here for the next two years to set up all the lines and handle the plant, the production and the quality of the product.

items.statement: Initial teething challenges may cause 2-3 week delays in machine synchronisation and formulation establishment; technical team confident on roadmap.
items.quote: Initially, testiing challenges are possible, maximum two to three weeks here or there, but the product can be established

items.statement: PCB manufacturers fully booked for 2-4 years, entering long-term contracts; CCL shortage structural; demand not a constraint for Ratnaveer.

items.statement: FMEG segment targeting full-year EBIT breakeven in FY27

items.quote: Further, the board has approved an investment of INR 200 crores towards land acquisition in Rajasthan to support our future expansion plan.

items.statement: Next year capex estimated around INR 300 crores

items.quote: For H1, the segment losses reduced to approximately INR 12 crores from approximately INR 19 crores last year. The H1 loss margins narrowed to 2.2% from 4.5%, supported by growth in scale and improved absorption of operating costs.

items.statement: Wire volumes grew double-digit, cable volumes single-digit in Q2; exports grew faster than domestic
items.quote: Our overall volume growth was in high single -digits, where wire outpacing cables. If we further see, our wires were growing in double digits, while cables, we have seen a single digit growth. And same in our exports. Exports growth was faster than domestic.

items.statement: H2 typically sees higher volumes year-on-year; confident of achieving full-year growth plan
items.quote: If you see normally H2 is always we have seen higher volumes year-on-year. I have experienced in over my experience of previous so many years. Still I think we will be able to achieve this, our growth plan, whatever we have done, even based on these higher volumes. We are quite confident to achieve that.

items.statement: Export share moving towards ~35% of revenue; cable exports growing faster than wire exports
items.quote: see our overall always export was very big in our revenue pie and it was always in the range of 25%-30% and now we are moving towards approx. 35% kind of range also. At the same time, the growth in export, majority is coming from cable side where earlier we were having limited capacities, but now after installing

items.quote: Our net working capital cycle improved to 46 days as of September '26, from 49 days in March and 50 days in June.

items.statement: Trade payables/LC-backed facilities increased to ~INR 1,290 crores due to higher raw material prices
items.quote: Yes. Yes, it is like if I see overall amount of LC back there is INR 1,290 crores or something like that.

items.statement: Debt expected to increase to fund capex and working capital; leverage at ~0.55x considered healthy
items.quote: Yes, there will be some increase in debt. See, first of all, if you see even my debt leverage is quite favourable. It is like we are not over-debt company, and quite efficiently we are working. It is around 0.55%, which is quite healthy for any growing company.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR 6.50 per equity share declared
items.quote: I am also pleased to share that our board has declared an interim dividend of INR 6.50 per equity share.

items.statement: Roorkee plant relocation underway with no production disruption; will increase FMEG capacity
items.quote: In Roorkee, we are shifting our plant, but we have a plan in such a way that there will be no disturbance. But we will increase our capacity in FMEG also. But it is not disturbing any current production cycle like that.

items.statement: UM Cables plant has low capacity utilization; plan to improve utilization and revenue
items.quote: Since this plant was having very low capacity utilization, so we will improve our capacity utilization and improve revenue as immediate effect also.

items.statement: Gross margin contraction due to product mix and high raw material base prices
items.quote: One is, of course, product mix is there. Secondly, since we are working on very high raw material base prices, there will be some impact. If we see overall profitability, as per our business plan only, we are moving ahead.

items.statement: Competition always exists; focused on own growth plans and efficient plant utilization
items.quote: I always believe competition was always there, and it will remain always because competition is part of business, though there may be players may change or their competition intensity can be changed, but it is part of business and we have our own growth plans, and we will keep growing as per our planning by doing efficient utilizations of our plant and as well as improving on our sales and marketi

items.statement: Wire and cable volume growth: high single-digit in Q2, low teens in H1
items.quote: Overall wire and cable volumes grew by high single -digit in Q2, and for H1, the volume growth stands at low teens.

items.statement: FMEG revenue grew 42% in Q2 and 35% in H1; appliances and new products driving growth
items.quote: For H1, the business recorded revenue of approximately INR 562 crores, up 35% year-on-year. The growth was broad-based. During Q2, revenue growth was seen across categories, led by robust performance in appliances and contribution from new products.

items.statement: Volatility in commodity prices and near-term demand fluctuations acknowledged
items.quote: We remain attentive to commodity price movements and their impact on both realization and margins. Overall, we are encouraged by our H1 performance while recognizing the importance of sustainable volumes, cash conversion, and discipline execution in the quarters ahead.

items.statement: FY27 ROA guidance raised to 2% for full year from earlier quarterly target
items.quote: We have given the guidance of ROA 2%, quarterly ROA by the year end. But as things stand today, our guidance changes to ROA of 2% for the full year.

items.statement: FY27 cost-to-income ratio guidance maintained at around 60%
items.quote: We aim to maintain cost-to-income ratio of around 60% for the year.

items.statement: FY27 credit cost expected around 2% for full year
items.quote: We estimate the same to remain in the range of 2% for the full year.

items.statement: FY28 credit cost estimated at 1.5%
items.quote: Next year, again, all the backlogs have already been cleared. We hope that 1.5% will be a good guess.

items.statement: Loan growth moderated in Q2 due to IT migration; FY28 growth expected to return to earlier projections
items.quote: This quarter's growth was moderated because, as we mentioned, we were focusing on migration. So that took some attention of the team. So that is why the growth was a little moderated. But by FY28, we expect that the earlier growth projection will continue.

items.quote: Yield on advances continue to be in a comfortable zone and cost of funds remained largely stable in Q2 FY27, leading to net interest margin at 8.2%. The funding cost is expected to marginally go up in Q3 but have enough cushion to absorb in the current NIM levels.

items.statement: Total business Rs 52,400 crore, up 25% YoY; gross advances Rs 23,934 crore, up 25% YoY; deposits Rs 28,466 crore, up 24% YoY

items.statement: Added 10 new banking outlets in Q2; total footprint 831 outlets, 722 ATMs, 1,060 CSCs, 31 IBCs across 24 states and 2 UTs

items.statement: Vigilant on global tensions, RBI monetary stance, supply chain disruptions, weather-related issues

items.statement: CARE ESG rating improved from 75.4 to 77.6; rated higher than industry in all three ESG aspects
items.quote: As a result, our CARE ESG rating has improved from 75.4 to 77.6. The Bank has been rated higher than the industry in all three aspects of environmental, social and governance, thus reflecting our continued progress towards responsible and sustainable growth.

items.statement: Management does not provide forward-looking volume or margin numbers but expects to outgrow the AC industry and improve margins via PLI discount rollback and mix shift
items.quote: Rabindra-ji, we don't give out forward-looking numbers. But yes, we are looking at industry to grow and even competitive terms. And as EPACK continues its focus on increasing its share of business and growing partnership with newer customers, we definitely believe that we should outgrow the industry.

items.statement: Industry primary and secondary AC sales improved in Q2 with comfortable channel inventory, giving a clean start for the coming season
items.quote: Primary sales for room air conditioners in July to September quarter were better than last year. items.quote: Through short-term BESS contracts, we have locked in more than INR1,600 crores of revenue for partial sale of FY27 capacity and more than INR1,500 crores for partial sale of capacity for FY28, with the balance to be tied up through future bids.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin 86.7% (renewable 90.8%, BESS 78.3%) in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our blended EBITDA margin was 86.7%, which comprises 90.8% from renewable generation and 78.3% from BESS operations, where the cost of power purchased to charge the batteries sits within the operating expenses.

items.statement: Strong tender pipeline of 20+ GW across solar+BESS, FDRE, CfD, PHSP; 50 GWh peak power bids rolled out, 200-250 GWh near-term, 20 GWh medium-term peak-only tenders expected
items.quote: A strong tender pipeline, 20+ gigawatts of upcoming tenders across solar plus BESS, FDRE, CfD, and PHSP. 50 gigawatt-hour of peak power builds already rolled out till September 27th, and another 200 gigawatt to 250 gigawatt-hour of short-term peak power contracts expected in the near term -- near to medium terms, and 20 gigawatt-hour of medium-term peak-only tenders expected shortly.

items.statement: BESS capex below INR1 crore/MWh (INR90 lakh-1 crore) due to existing AC infrastructure at operational substations; lithium carbonate prices down, copper up, 6% Chinese export tax from Jan
items.quote: On the BESS capex, of course, we have done lower than INR1 crores per megawatt-hour. Because, as you know, the key difference, in the capex for us is we are installing BES S at operational substations, right? So the capex for the transformers and the AC infrastructure exists at these plants. So we are not doing a greenfield installation. So that saves us around INR20 lakhs per megawatt-hour of cap

items.statement: Weighted average cost of debt 8.4% for operational projects; 65% from PFC, REC, IREDA, NaBFID with stable long-term rates; CRISIL upgraded outlook to AA- positive
items.quote: The weighted average cost of debt for our fully operational projects is around 8.4%. Around 65% of these borrowings are from PFC, REC, IREDA, and NaBFID, whose rates follow their own long-term cost of funds and which limits interest rate volatility. Further, CRISIL has upgraded ACME Solar Holdings rating outlook to AA- positive from AA- stable.

items.statement: Strategy focuses on return-led self-financing platform: BESS as cash engine (~10 GWh rolling), execution excellence (higher CUF, ready ahead of grid), margin improvement (curtailed solar charges BESS), contracted revenue visibility (long-te

First, return on capital and profitability. We allocate capital to the highest return opportunities. Megawatt matter -- megawatts matter, but the measure we would hold ourselves to is earnings growth and the quality of these earnings.

items.statement: Defence market size INR 4,000-5,000 crore over two years; company holds highest market share

items.statement: Data centre opportunity large but no orders yet; guidance excludes data centre revenue until 2028

items.statement: Service teams at all major naval ports; dedicated lifecycle support strategy
items.quote: We believe that it's not only delivering products, but we believe that we need to support the product for the life cycle. And therefore, service forms an extremely important and integral part of our strategy. And therefore, we have a very, very wide network of servicing centres and resources positioned in those centres.

items.statement: Only company with integrated HVAC, AC, Ref plant and control panel manufacturing; SIDM award for import substitution
items.quote: We are the only company in HVAC and AC and Ref plant, where we can manufacture our own electrical control supply. The simple task, we control the complete value chain of our product range.

items.quote: When we talk about a new capacity, new opportunity, which may need a fund also, so that time we probably will go to a market to raise a new fund also. But our earning call of 40% CAGR, as of today, we don't need a fund, neither we need a capacity, unless and until we see a new opportunity in the market.

items.statement: Evaluating organic and inorganic opportunities

items.statement: Primary market activity rebounded strongly in Q2 FY27 with INR 90,000 crores raised via IPOs and 90 lakh demat accounts added, up 14.2% YoY.

items.quote: For H1, however, our market share increased to 17.4% from 16.6% in the corresponding H1 of 2026. Fintech brokers have continued to get added. And today, they account for 23.5% of our incremental demat account sourcing.

items.statement: YUva and women's demat plans together account for ~45% of incremental demat account additions in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: We would also like to highlight our continued traction in the YUva Plan, the youth plan that we launched and the women's demat plan, which now together account for approximately 45% of our incremental demat account additions in Q2 FY2027.

items.statement: Issuer base crossed 118,000; unlisted issuer market share 72.5% with 3,197 companies admitted in Q2 FY27.

items.statement: E-voting events increased to 3,160 in Q2 FY27 from 2,924 YoY; market share stable at 52.4%.
items.quote: The total number of events on our e -voting platform increased in the quarter to 3,160 from 2,924 last year same quarter, and our market share remains broadly stable at about 52.4% in Q2 FY2027.

items.statement: Pilot launch of Demat 2.0 using DLT and RBI CBDC for tokenized bonds with instant settlement; 3 issuances worth over INR 1,000 crores so far.
items.quote: We also achieved an important milestone with the pilot launch of the Demat 2.0, which is a next -generation platform, which leverages the distributed ledger technology to support tokenized securities and enable real-time settlement through integration of the Reserve Bank of India's CBDC or the Central Bank Digital Currency infrastructure.

items.statement: Enabled online Form 121 submission, API interface with NSE for Electronic Gold Receipts, and API connectivity for online bond platform providers.
items.quote: We enabled online submission of Form 121, which was announced by Honorable Finance Minister in the budget through NSDL's corporate website, simplifying compliance and providing issuers and stakeholders with seamless digital integration.

items.statement: Supported SEBI's Project Jagruk investor awareness program; conducted 1,259 multilingual programs reaching 55,000+ participants across 10 states/UTs.

The second part of the problem which can impact the demand is the interest rates, which are going up in the process consumer finance, many other triggers can lead to demand beginning to slow down.

items.quote: Commercial refrigeration has much more steel and much more plastic. And the cold rooms also has a lot of metal content and the products which are based petroleum-based. There the price increase that is required is around 24% to 25%.

items.statement: Rejigging product portfolio with differentiated, cost-optimized SKUs; removing unwanted features, alternate components, outsourcing entry-level products

items.statement: Outsourced product share in RAC may increase from ~15% to ~30%

items.statement: Data center order inflows strong; inquiry inflows good from factories; defocusing from infrastructure segment

items.statement: No pricing discipline expected from peers; capacity exceeds demand 1.7-2x; aggressive competition to continue
items.quote: We don't expect that at all because the fact of the matter is the production capacity in the country today, including the OEMs, all put together is much more than the demand. It will be 1.7 to 2x if they want to produce, this is what will be available. Next is this is the fastest-growing market segment within consumer durables. And there will be competition, there will be aggression.

items.statement: Heat pump supplies to U.S. market continuing; potential for USD 100 million additional revenue; pursuing more OEMs in U.S. and Europe

We are pursuing development and testing of products and solutions for a few more OEMs in the U.S. and Europe. We expect this business to accelerate once tariff-related uncertainties are resolved.

items.statement: Net cash position of Rs. 289 crore as of September 30, 2026 vs net borrowings of Rs. 417 crore a year ago due to better working capital management

items.statement: Moved from net borrowings of Rs. 417 crore to net cash of Rs. 289 crore year-on-year
items.quote: The quarter ended with net cash position of Rs. 289 cr as of September 30, 26 as compared to the net borrowings of Rs. 417 cr as of September 30, 2025.

items.statement: Sold MedTech business for Rs. 35.6 crore; transaction completed August 31, 2026; warranty provisions written back
items.quote: During this quarter, the company sold its MedTech business for total consideration of Rs. 35.6 cr. The transaction was completed on August 31, 2026. Since the company is no longer required to render warranty obligations for MedTech business, the provisions pertaining to same have been written back, which resulted in improved profitability.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex ~Rs. 130 crore; full-year guidance Rs. 300 crore max including R&D and digital spend
items.quote: For full year, we are guiding for a capex of around Rs. 300 cr, you can say at the max. And this capex will include certain R&D expenditure, which will be there on the products and also a certain amount of digital expenditure, which we'll be doing.

items.statement: Data center projects require specialized skills and resources; defocusing from infrastructure to allocate resources to data centers and factories
items.quote: As we begin to execute data center projects, we will more and more defocus from infrastructure segment because it requires resources. And these are time-bound projects, and these are specialized skills are required.

items.statement: Room AC market share held after April loss; regained share from May-September
items.quote: We had lost the market share in the month of April in the tertiary sales. We tried to pass on the price increase in April aggressively, it didn't happen. We had to correct (prices ) through the customer offers. In the process, we gained market share marginally from May onwards. So May, June, July, August, September, we have been gaining market share of what we lost in the critical month of April.

items.statement: Monsoon shortfall, lower farm income, interest rate hikes could impact demand; raw material costs still rising with no softening
items.quote: The monsoon shortfall, consequent drop in farm income and interest rate hike can have a potential impact on demand. On the other hand, the conclusion of U.S. trade deal and possible resolution of West Asia crisis can be the tailwinds.

items.statement: Rs. 77 crore provision write-back in Q2 including Rs. 12-13 crore from MedTech; rest from normal warranty and incentive provisions
items.quote: See, the one item which I can recollect is that there will be certain amount of warranties, et cetera, which are written back even in the normal course of business. Then there are other items like incentive (provisions ) also which get written back when they are not required. And most of these adjustments kind of come in quarter 2 for whatever are the incentives, warranties provided for in the ear

items.statement: Depreciation increase driven by R&D amortization, new offices, warehouses and lease accounting; current run rate normalized
items.quote: Yes. So you can say this quarter's run rate, you can take it as a normalized run rate, okay? So I don't see any additional properties or anything getting coming on board. So this should be a normalized run rate.

items.statement: Expects H2 FY27 to be significantly stronger than H1

items.statement: Targets full-year finance costs 9-10% lower than FY26

items.statement: SIOP margins sustained around 40% over last 4-5 years

items.quote: On a steady state, on whatever is today, we should get back to the PVC-CPVC spread which was available in Quarter 1, which is around Rs. 25-Rs. 30 per ton.

items.quote: On 26th October, there was a recommendation of controlling duty made by DGTR on imports of PVC from China. It has to be approved by the Ministry of Finance, which may take couple of months.

items.statement: CPVC demand supported by plumbing and infrastructure; Q2 impacted by monsoon seasonality

items.statement: PVC demand expected to be good in H2 driven by Jal Jeevan Mission and government schemes

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA 0.12x; gross debt/EBITDA 1.5x; finance cost Rs. 13.6 crore in Q2 (down 8% QoQ, 12.5% YoY)

items.statement: Power cost 75% captive (coal/lignite), 25% imported (mostly renewable); coal prices rising, offsetting solar savings

items.statement: HVDC equipment component typically 40-65% of project value depending on line length

items.statement: Ibuprofen prices stable for last quarters, expected to remain same for next 2-3 quarters
