items.quote: An amount of approximately INR 137.08 crores remains to be utilized towards the development of the Namakkal and Tiruchirappalli network.

items.statement: Domestic, commercial, industrial PNG connections grew 14%, 48%, 8% respectively in H1 FY27
items.quote: The domestic, commercial, and industrial PNG connections also grew by 14%, 48%, and 8% respectively, strengthening our platform for future growth.

items.statement: Gas sourcing mix in Q2: APM 21%, new well 13%, HPHT 33%, LNG 30%, spot 1-2%
items.quote: In Q2, approximately, APM on the portfolio basis is around 21%. The new well gas is around 13%. HPHT, we have taken around 33% on the overall portfolio basis. LNG, is around 30%, and remaining 1-2% is on the spot basis.

items.statement: Gas costs: APM capped at USD 7/MMBtu, new well USD 10.2, HPHT USD 8.9, RLNG USD 11-12; blended average ~USD 9.5
items.quote: APM is capped at USD 7. So, we are availing on the same cap at the USD 7 MMBtu. There's new well gas, NWG also, again, linked to this A PM. So, we have do ne at around USD 10.2. This H PHT is again , it is a subsidized cost available into the market, public data available. This is around USD 8.9. And LNG or RLNG is between USD 11-12 MMBtu.

items.statement: Higher gas costs from HPHT allocation change and Brent spike passed on to consumers except industrial segment
items.quote: Currently, whatever extra costs we have incurred, that is all getting passed on to the consumers and consumers are accepting it without much of issues, except the industrial area, the suppl y side, where we have very meticulously balance the demand and the

items.statement: Revised HPHT allocation methodology in September temporarily reduced gas availability; 80% rectified by October phased implementation
items.quote: The revised HPHT allocation methodology by the Government of India introduced in September resulted in a temporary reduction in gas availability towards the beginning of Q3. This has affected our volume for approximately a fortnight.

items.statement: Diversified sourcing with long-term GAIL agreement and IOC/GTN hookups in Namakkal-Trichy and Diu-Gir Somnath
items.quote: We responded by further diversifying our sourcing portfolio, including a long -term agreement with GAIL and asking calibrated pricing action to manage higher gas costs. Some Brent-link and HPHT, we have had the mix with them, and this will be able to make up our gas requirement to a great extent.

items.statement: Long-term gas arrangements tied up to 2030 via Shell India, GSPC, IOC, GAIL; pausing new long-term deals due to volatility
items.quote: Currently, we are already tied up upto 2030. Most of the arrangements we have done through Shell India and also with GSPC. Currently, we have entered two more contracts with the Indian Oil Corporation and with GAIL. So, these are giving us sufficient visibility up to 2030.

items.statement: MoU with Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation for captive CNG facility; 83 buses converted, fleet now 183 in Namakkal, 55 in Trichy
items.quote: During the quarter, we entered into an MoU with Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation. For captive CNG dispensing facility in NT, we have created recurring supplies to them and also created a recurring institutional demand base there in NT. We facilitated the conversion of 83 TNSTC buses to CNG, taking the CNG fleet to 183 buses in Namakkal and 55 buses in Tiruchirappalli.

items.statement: Providing compression services to BPCL in Namakkal & Trichy; evaluating spare capacity utilization
items.quote: For example, we are already providing compression services to BPCL in Namakkal and Trichy. We have LCNG stations in these areas, and wherever spare compression capacity can be utilized by another company or another geographical area at an attractive margin, we are open to such opportunities.

items.statement: Income tax paid net of refund INR 4.5 crore in H1 (INR 12.5 crore paid, refund received)
items.quote: So, we have paid around INR 12.5 crore in this quarter. So , this INR 4.5 crore is a net of the refund only, because we also got some refund from the previous year as well. So, this is the net.

items.statement: Net debt-free as of Sep 2026: total debt INR 45 crore vs cash/MF INR 253 crore; net worth INR 1,050 crore
items.quote: As of September, '26, the total debt stood at approximately only INR 45 crore against cash bank balance and mutual fund investment of available fund of INR 253 crore, which is resulting in the IRM Energy net debt-free position as of today.

items.statement: Interest cost ~7-8% on INR 45 crore debt; bank guarantee charges 0.5-0.6% also in finance cost
items.quote: The one is the INR 45 crore interest cost, which is around 7-8%, and another one is the bank guarantee. So, we are also having multiple bank guarantees, which we had given for the PNGRB. We are also going to taking permission and all for the local authority. So, that bank guarantee is within the range of 0.5-0.6%.

items.statement: IPO proceeds INR 496 crore received; INR 358.68 crore utilized (INR 170.18 cr NT network, INR 135 cr debt repayment, INR 53.5 cr GCP)
items.quote: With respect to the IPO proceeds, INR 496 crore was received against the stated object of the issue. As of September 30, 2026, INR 358.68 crore had been utilized, including INR 170.18 crore towards the development of the city gas distribution network in the NT area, INR 135 crore towards the repayment of the borrowing, and INR 53.50 crore towards general corporate purpose.

items.statement: Selectively evaluating acquisition and diversification opportunities across energy landscape
items.quote: We would like to also say the focus area remains on selectively evaluating acquisition and diversification opportunities across the energy landscape.

items.statement: Buyback considered by promoters/board but no decision yet; promoter bought stake last quarter
items.quote: At the right point of time, if they collectively decide so, they would like to increase their promotors' stake also and also offer a buyback position . That is not out of question. But we can say as of now, there is no such thing to happen.

items.statement: Royalty to promoters continues at 2% of revenue from operations as per IPO prospectus
items.quote: So, other expense includes royalty as well. So , that will remain continue d. It is 2% on the revenue from operations.

items.statement: NGT order in favour (Feb 26); implementation by Punjab Pollution Control Board in progress
items.quote: If you look at the NGT order, it came in favour of us on 26th February, and the NGT has guided the Punjab Pollution Control Board to implement it effectively. So, we are in constant touch with the local Pollution Control Board for its implementation.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty in West Asia and Brent volatility may impact H2; Q3 impacted by HPHT transition
items.quote: Given the evolving regulatory environment and continued geopolitical uncertainty in West Asia, we also can't remain fully immune, but we expect the operating environment to remain, a little uncertain during H2 FY27 also.

items.statement: CNG now ~66% of total volume, strengthening sales mix
items.quote: CNG now accounts for approximately 66% of our total overall v alue, strengthening our sales mix

items.statement: Banaskantha 47%, Fatehgarh Sahib 33%, Diu & Gir Somnath 9%, Namakkal & Trichy 11% of H1 FY27 volume
items.quote: I'm happy to share that in H1FY27, Banaskantha GA accounted for approximately 47% of our total volume, Fatehgarh Sahib, 33%, and Diu & Gir Somnath, 9%, where the Namakkal & Trichy, 11%.

items.statement: Promoter bought stake last quarter; board/stakeholders evaluating buyback
items.quote: And promoter to last quarter has done by buying out the stake. So, that is just for your information.

items.statement: Depreciation lower in Q2 (INR 13.8 cr) vs Q1 (INR 16.4 cr) due to Q1 catch-up from physical verification
items.quote: So, there were some exceptional dep reciation we have booked in this Q1 because of that. So , we have done our physical verification and everything in this Q1, and we have identified some of the assets where the depreciation was not charged in the previous quarter. So that was impacting this Q1.

items.statement: Loan book target of over INR16,000 crores and 300+ branches by FY29
items.quote: We continue to target a loan book of over INR16,000 crores-plus and a network of more than 300 branches by FY29.

items.statement: FY27 loan growth guidance of 20-22% with positive bias given H1 at 23%
items.quote: Current year, in the beginning of the year, we've given a guidance of 20% to 22%, and we are talking H1 and 23%.

items.statement: Target 30%+ branches outside Punjab by FY29 from 21% currently
items.quote: As part of our Vision 2029, we are targeting that we need to have 30% plus branches outside the state of Punjab.

items.statement: Out-of-Punjab advances target 32-37% by FY29 from 25.7% currently
items.quote: We believe that with the 30% branches out of Punjab, our out of Punjab book shall be anything between 32% to 37%-odd.

items.statement: ROA target 1.6% by FY29 from 1.39% currently driven by NIM and opex
items.quote: Our next growth journey in ROA, which is 1.39% to 1.6% is based typically on 2 figures. That is the NIM and opex.

items.statement: NIM target 4.3-4.35% by FY29 from 4.24% currently via CD ratio expansion
items.quote: NIM, which is presently 4.2%, I believe that there's opportunity to take it from anything between 4.3% to 4.35%.

items.statement: Operating cost target 280-285 bps by FY29 from 3.05% currently
items.quote: Yes, we can safely take that. Today, we are around 3.05%.

items.statement: Disbursements up 36% YoY to INR1,095 crores in Q2 FY27 indicating healthy demand
items.quote: Disbursements stayed strong throughout the quarter and stood at INR1,095 crores, up 36% year-on-year.

items.statement: Out-of-Punjab advances grew 39% YoY vs overall 23% showing strong demand in new geographies
items.quote: Advances there grew by over 39% year-on-year this quarter, comfortably ahead of our overall loan growth of 23%.

items.statement: NIM improved to 4.24% in Q2 FY27 from 4.04% YoY and 4.21% QoQ
items.quote: Our net interest margin held steady at 4.24% against 4.04% a year back in a quarter where the rate environment actually turned.

items.statement: Yield on advances stable at 11% YoY; cost of deposits fell 24 bps YoY to 5.68%
items.quote: Yield on advances for Q2 FY27 remain at 11% against 11% last year Q2. So we have seen a repo rate hike in October, so the benefit of that has not been pulled into the yield on advances in Q2.

items.statement: 52% fixed rate advances, 48% floating; EBR-linked portfolio 13-14% reprices monthly
items.quote: If we talk about the balance sheet, we have around 52% fixed rate advances and 48% floating rate advances. So we can say around 50 -50 each. So 50-50 each is typically fixed and floating. And if I talk about the flo ating, floating is a fair balance of the MCLR linked as well as the linked with the EBR. So EBR-linked portfolio will be typically around 13% to 14% of the portfolio is EBR linked

items.statement: Gross advances INR9,755 crores, up 23.4% YoY and 7.5% QoQ as of Sep 30, 2026
items.quote: Our gross advances stood at INR9,755 crores as of September 30, '26, up 23.4% year-on-year, and 7.5% over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Business loans now 28% of book vs 23% YoY; Mortgage 24%, Agriculture 26%, Corporate 14%
items.quote: As of September 30, our portfolio continues to remain well diversified and Business Loan segment is presently the largest segment, which increased to 28% of the book against 23% a year back.

items.statement: Gross NPA 2.36% in Q2 FY27, down 11 bps QoQ and 34 bps YoY; Net NPA 1.12%
items.quote: Gross NPA come in at 2.36%, an improvement of 11 basis points over the previous quarter and 34 basis points over a year ago.

items.statement: SMA1+2 at 3.31% of advances, down from 4.78% QoQ and 4.42% YoY
items.quote: SMA1 and SMA2 accounts for around 3.31% of the advances, down from 4.78% a quarter back and 4.42% a year back.

items.statement: H1 FY27 annualized gross slippage 1.11%, net slippage 0.24%; no agri stress from deficit rainfall
items.quote: Even if we talk about the current year, we have a gross slippage for the H1FY27, 1.11% on annualized and net slippage of 0.24%, with our credit cost of 0.18% for Q2 and 0.24% for the H1.

items.statement: 97% secured book; 76.7% portfolio and 89% ex-corporate backed by immovable property or own FDRs
items.quote: Our book remains firmly secured and around 97% is secured, over 76.7% of the portfolio and 89% of, excluding the noncorporate book is backed by immovable property or own FDRs.

items.statement: Average ticket size INR19.53 lakhs vs INR17.1 lakhs YoY; granular portfolio
items.quote: The book is also granular with the average ticket size of about INR19.53 lakhs against INR17.1 lakhs in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: CASA 34.5% of deposits vs 33.9% YoY; Punjab CASA 35.3%, out-of-Punjab 25.3%
items.quote: CASA stood at 34.5%. It is a touch lower than what we had last quarter, and that is seasonal and in line with what the whole industry is seeing in a high term deposit rate environment. But it remains higher than a year ago. That is 33.9% a year back.

items.statement: Deposit market share in Punjab improved to 1.3% from 1.17% in 15 months
items.quote: Even within the state of Punjab, our market share, if I talk about the deposit first, our deposit market share against the whole of the industry has improved to 1.3% which was 1.17% at the end of 31st of March 2025.

items.statement: 222 branches across 5 states and 2 UTs; 47 branches (21%) outside Punjab
items.quote: As of September, our network stood at 222 branches across 5 states and 2 union territory, strengthening our footprints in rural and semi-urban markets.

items.statement: Out-of-Punjab branches at INR80 cr+ business per branch for 5+ year vintage vs INR72 cr
items.quote: Business per branch in these markets, that is the out of Punjab market are continuing to show upward trajectory with business per branch has started hitting INR80 crores plus for branches with a longevity of 5 years and above, against INR72 crores at the end of

items.statement: CAR 20.8% with Tier 1 at 18.5%; LCR ~216%; no immediate capital raise needed
items.quote: Our capital adequacy ratio closed at 20.8% with Tier 1 capital at 18.5%, giving us ample legroom to fund our growth with no immediate need to raise the fresh capital.

items.statement: Cost-to-income 59.8% vs 61.7% YoY; operating leverage benefits expected
items.quote: On efficiency, our cost-to-income ratio is 59.8%, an improvement from 61.7% last year, even as we continue to invest in branches, technology and people.

items.statement: IRDAI draft circular on banca commission; banca 12-13% of PBT; preparing mitigation
items.quote: Since that being in a still draft stage, let it come from a discussion paper to a draft stage first. So today, we are in a discussion paper document to a draft stage document. So that is the one journey, and we have already started working on the same

items.statement: No agriculture lending in Rajasthan yet; monitoring canal irrigation progress before entry
items.quote: I can say, I started studying about Rajasthan since that is a new territory. But up to now, my initial study results are not that encouraging. So we have not opened the gates of agriculture in Rajasthan.

items.statement: Consumption loans 7% of book, mostly cross-sell to existing customers; includes 1.5-2% loan against FDRs
items.quote: Consumption, which is presently constituting 7% of the portfolio is typically the second or the third hook. What I mean by this, consumption is not our start point. Consumption is the second or the third hook to our existing customer.

items.statement: Evaluating consumption-led products to fast-track growth; running internal pilots
items.quote: We are running some pilot projects internally already, that how to expand it and fast track this particular subset within this particular product.

items.statement: ROA 1.39% vs 1.26% YoY; ROE 12.23% vs 10.22% YoY
items.quote: Return on assets stood at 1.39% against 1.26% a year back and 1.3% a quarter back, while return on equity at 12.23% against 10.22% a year back and 11.2% a quarter back.

items.statement: Average CD ratio 85.4% vs 81.5% YoY; target mid-to-high 80s for NIM expansion
items.quote: Our average credit-to-deposit ratio for the half year was 85.4%, up from 81.5% a year ago, which shows we are deploying our funds efficiently.

items.statement: PPOP INR68 crores up 31% YoY; PAT INR46 crores up 31% YoY
items.quote: Pre-provision operating profit, PPOP, was INR68 crores, up 31% year-on-year and profit after tax is at INR46 crores, up about 31%.

items.statement: Aim to sustain double-digit profit growth, improve return ratios, grow to more than 1 lakh customers by 2027, and see wealth, merchant banking, and insurance contribute meaningfully to bottom line
items.quote: Our priorities are clear. We aim to sustain double -digit profit growth, improve our return ratios, grow to more than 1 lakh customers by 2027, and see wealth, merchant banking, and insurance contribute meaningfully to the bottom line.

items.statement: MTF book crossed INR100 crores and is fully collateralized by client shares and cash
items.quote: Our MTF book has crossed INR100 crores and is fully collateralized by our client shares and cash.

items.statement: Consolidated net profit margin improved to 41.7% in H1 FY27
items.quote: Our net profit margin improved to 41.7%.

items.statement: Domestic institutions bought close to INR3.9 lakh crores of equities and monthly SIP contribution reached record INR32,400 crores in September
items.quote: Over the same 6 months, domestic institutions bought close to INR3.9 lakh crores of equities. The monthly SIP contribution reached a record of over INR32,400 crores in September.

items.statement: Added insurance distribution via subsidiary Pune Finvest with IRDAI corporate agency approval in July, began advisory operations in September under brand QURA Insure
items.quote: In insurance, our subsidiary Pune Finvest received its IRDAI corporate agency approval in July this year, and we began advisory operations in September under our brand QURA Insure.

items.statement: Mutual fund distribution AUM over INR240 crores with SIP book over INR1.5 crores across 36 AMCs and 500+ schemes serving 1,600+ investors
items.quote: Our mutual fund distribution business works with 36 AMCs and more than 500 schemes. Serves more than 1,600 investors with overall AUM of over INR240 crores. Our SIP book is over INR1.5 crores.

items.statement: PESB Alpha Fund Category III AIF manages around INR55 crores, PESB invested INR15 crores, delivered about 25% post-fees post-tax return in first year
items.quote: The PESB Alpha Fund, our Category III AIF launched in November 2025, now manages around INR55 crores. PESB itself has invested INR15 crores in the fund.

items.statement: Serve more than 65,000 clients, of whom more than 17,000 are traded clients, holding more than INR9,000 crores of assets in demat
items.quote: Today we serve more than 65,000 clients, of whom more than 17,000 are traded clients, and together they hold more than INR9,000 crores of assets in the demat held with us.

items.statement: Plan to open flagship branches in high visibility locations, grow MTF book carefully, scale algo trading for retail investors, build Gift City merchant banking, secured lending, and insurance business
items.quote: We will work towards this by opening flagship branches in high visibility locations, growing the MTF book carefully, scaling algo trading for retail investors, and building our Gift City merchant banking, secured lending, and insurance business.

items.statement: Short-term borrowings INR65 crores used mainly to fund MTF book, long-term borrowings down to INR0.6 crores
items.quote: Short -term borrowings were INR65 crores against INR47 crores in March and are used mainly to fund MTF book while long -term borrowings came down to just INR0.6 crores.

items.statement: Converted warrants into 18 lakh equity shares and issued 16 lakh new convertible warrants at INR234 each with 25% subscription received
items.quote: Apart from the profit for the half, this reflects the conversion of warrants into 18 lakh equity shares and the issue of 16 lakh new convertible warrants at INR234 each, on which 25% of the subscription amount has been received.

items.statement: Paid final dividend of INR1 per share for FY26
items.quote: We also paid a final dividend of INR1 per share for FY26.

items.statement: Promoters equally participated in warrant round so promoter stake not majorly diluted
items.quote: Firstly, to address the dilution part, there is no major dilution happening because promoters have equally participated in this warrant round. So promoter's stake is not going to get diluted.

items.statement: SEBI measures on F&O more than halved option volumes in 2026 and reduced individual F&O traders by about a fifth; higher STT on derivatives added pressure
items.quote: SEBI's measures on futures and options more than halved option volumes in 2026 and reduced the number of individual F&O traders by about fifth. And in April this year, higher security transaction tax on derivatives added to the pressure.

items.statement: IRDAI capping insurance commissions may reduce margins but expected to increase volumes and consumer participation
items.quote: So basically the insurance industry might improve due to that, and more and more people will start taking up insurance products. So in a way, ev en though margins are going to come down, we expect the volumes might increase

items.statement: Regulatory risk is primary risk; SEBI and IRDAI changes may cause short-term margin pressure but long-term clarity benefits industry
items.quote: So as and when new regulations or new notifications come in, we need to adapt to those guidelines and framework. And due to that, whatever risk, most of the industry players might have to face, we will also be facing that.

items.statement: Merchant banking division earned first fees in 2026; first IPO Apar Advertisers approved, planning to list within couple of months; multiple SME and mainboard IPOs in pipeline
items.quote: So our first IPO, we have already got the approval. That's Apar Advertisers. It's in the public domain, and within next couple of months we are planning to list the company. That's an SME company. There are multiple other IPOs which are in pipeline. A few are SMEs and few are main board issues.

items.statement: Relationship managers handle clients face-to-face; digital team expands bandwidth digitally for cross-sell of mutual fund, advisory, AIF, equity products
items.quote: So we have a number of relationships managers in our organization who are handling all the clients. So we have face-to-face access to our RMs for the customers, as well as we have a team of people who handle our digital platforms and try to expand our bandwidth digitally so that we can approach and access more and more number of clients across the places where our presence is not there.

items.statement: Reinvesting all profits and fresh inflow of funds into MTF and merchant banking; warrant proceeds and continuous profit inflow are sources for investments
items.quote: So we are continuously finding good opportunities to deploy our funds for MTF purposes, and we are reinvesting all our profits and fresh inflow of funds into such areas like MTF, as well as, as we are going to sign more merchant banking and as our IPOs keep on coming, our capital will be deployed in that area as well.

items.statement: Industry margin trading book grew from INR1.4 lakh crores to INR1.6 lakh crores; activity moving towards cash market and funded positions
items.quote: Industry's margin trading book grew from over INR1.4 lakh crores at the end of June to about INR1.6 lakh crores by the end of September.

items.statement: Broking future depends on meaningfully serving each client with research, advice, funding, technology, wider financial products, not just opening accounts or single product volumes
items.quote: For us, the message is clear. The future of broking cannot depend only on opening more accounts or on the volumes of a single product. It will depend on how meaningfully we serve each client with our research, advice, funding, technology, and wider range of financial products.

items.statement: Building open API-based algorithmic trading platform for retail investors to automate strategies on PESB platform
items.quote: We are also building open API-based algorithm trading platform for retail investors so that clients can automate their strategies on our platform.

items.statement: Total equity INR225 crores on 30th September 2026 vs INR180.6 crores in March; profit, warrant conversion, and new warrant issue contributed
items.quote: Total equity stood at INR225 crores on 30th September '26 against INR180.6 crores in March. Apart from the profit for the half, this reflects the conversion of warrants into 18 lakh equity shares and the issue of 16 lakh new convertible warrants at INR234 each, on which 25% of the subscription amount has been received.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue from operations grew ~30% to INR34.2 crores, EBITDA grew 31% to INR22.3 crores, net profit grew ~37% to INR14.3 crores, highest for any first half
items.quote: Our consolidated revenue from operations grew around 30% to INR34.2 crores. EBITDA grew by 31% to I NR22.3 crores, and net profit grew almost 37% to INR14.3 crores, our highest for any first half of the

items.statement: Consolidated ROE 12.2% and ROCE 14.2% for FY26; improving return ratios is clear priority as capital-led businesses contribute more
items.quote: For FY26, our consolidated return on equity was 12.2% and our return on capital employed was 14.2%. Improving return ratios is clear priority for us as our capital -led businesses in wealth, merchant banking, and insurance contribute more, we expect these ratios to move up steadily.

items.statement: Internal aim is to deliver year-on-year top-line and bottom-line growth in H2 despite headwinds; Q3 expected to be tough.
items.quote: Internally, what we are aiming for is that just still manage to deliver year-on-year growth both on top line and bottom line. That is kind of like the framework we are working with right now.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA grew 27% on 16% GTV growth, demonstrating operating leverage for second consecutive quarter.
items.quote: We have shared the numbers, but I do want to highlight that the 16% growth in GTV led to a 27% growth in adjusted EBITDA. So, we are continuing to demonstrate operating leverage for the second consecutive quarter.

items.statement: Long-term framework: SG&A investment should grow slower than GP growth; trailing 12-month EBITDA margins best gauge.
items.quote: In the long run, conceptually, I feel we have gotten to a point where we know that the investment in SG&A should largely be less than the growth in GP that we are anticipating.

items.statement: Investing in AI and technology to automate processes and build sales/operations tools; constant currency SG&A growth at high single digits.
items.quote: We are continuing to invest in building or using AI and technology to automate processes, to build tools for our sales team to become more effective, and tools for our operations team to automate a fair bit of work that they do.

items.statement: Classic GP per dollar GTV nearly double organic business; booking window 365 days for groups, several quarters for hotels.
items.quote: The upside with Classic is that the GP is significantly more, right? It is almost double the GP of the organic business, which means that if any $1 we add in Classic is equal $1 GTV we add in Classic is equivalent to $2 of GTV that we add to our organic business.

items.statement: India monthly transacting buyers grew 1% in Q2 and 4% in H1 on base of ~24,000; focus on non-air cross-sell to larger partners.
items.quote: In the quarter, our monthly transaction in India have actually grown by 1%. Keeping in mind the base is very large because almost 24,000 operate with us on a quarterly basis. On the H1, it was up by 4%.

items.statement: Air GP expected to range 1-1.2% depending on ad-hoc airline incentives; may recover in future quarters.
items.quote: Generally the GP, what we have been telling as well is, should range between 1% to 1.2%. We may see some quarters it is lower, and sometimes it may recover in the next quarters as well.

items.statement: Meaningful working capital release in Q2 from timing differences: Middle East receivables post-Eid, Brazil receivables, and shift from virtual credit cards to credit lines.
items.quote: For example, there were certain overdue, specifically in the Middle East, due to the war situation and the Eid at the March end, those receivables had got released. We had certain receivables because of the anticipation-related thing that we had not done in Brazil in the last year. Those receivables have been released.

items.statement: FEMA adjudication order received post quarter-end; appeal to be filed; legal advice indicates high chance of winning and penalty not sustained; no provision made.
items.quote: Subsequent to again the quarter end, we have received the adjudication order, and based on the advice from our legal consultants, we would be going ahead and filing an appeal against the same. Again, based on that legal advice, we believe that the chances of winning our appeal is high, and the penalty amount may not be sustained.

items.statement: FX loss Rs 9 crore in Q2 (Rs 5.5 crore prior quarter) due to hedging premium costs and unhedged exposure losses; hedge ~75% of open exposures.
items.quote: Because we are obviously now doing hedging, the cost line item would remain. However, as we mentioned earlier, we do not hedge the entire exposure. We generally hedge between 75% of our open exposures.

items.statement: Organic international GTV grew 28% in Q2; management expects 'reasonably more' once geopolitical recovery occurs.
items.quote: In the international market, even in this quarter, the organic growth is 28%. We would expect to do something reasonably more than that once recovery happens.

items.statement: OTAs unlikely to easily pivot to B2B agency model due to credit line complexity, channel conflict with suppliers, and past failures; TBO acknowledges threat but sees barriers.
items.quote: Some have tried in the past and failed. One, because there is a lot of knowledge which you need when it comes to the credit lines, et cetera, with the travel agents. Second, I think the channel conflict comes in very significantly here.

items.statement: Classic sales team largely new (half <6 months, quarter <3 months); productivity not yet maximized; takes 3-4 years to max out.
items.quote: At this point in time, we do believe that their productivity has not maximized for two reasons. One, a lot of sales teams is still new, so less than a year in the business or maybe on average 15 months into the business. It takes three, four years for them to truly max out their own ability to kind of maximize their order book.

items.statement: Q3 headwinds: Saudi airport attacks hit inbound/outbound; European riots in Paris, Madrid, Barcelona, Italy causing cancellations; U.S. election outcome pending.
items.quote: crisis in Saudi with the attacks happening on Saudi airports meant that both Saudi inbound and Saudi outbound has been very badly hit. Prior bookings have also gotten canceled. On top of it, the spread of rioting across major European cities has also been a major headwind

items.statement: Constant currency GTV growth targeted for Q3; reported growth depends on currency appreciation which cannot be forecast.
items.quote: I am keeping fingers crossed for constant currency growth. The currency uplift is on top of it because that is, we do not contribute to it.

items.statement: Hotel GP margins held in Q2 despite Middle East competition; hope to maintain similar percentages if supply/demand balance unchanged.
items.quote: If the situation, remains the same, we hope to continue with the similar kind of margins that we have achieved in Q2.

items.statement: Classic integration not a cost-efficiency play; thesis is learning luxury supply/sales to entrench globally; synergies hard to quantify but supplier access and talent attraction cited.
items.quote: The investment thesis is that what we learn on acquiring luxury supply, on selling to luxury travel advisors, engaging with luxury consortia like Virtuoso and Travel Leaders, et cetera, that will allow us to, one, build the right tools and right playbooks for growing the organic Classic business in North America.

items.statement: AI viewed as long-term tailwind for complex/luxury travel; travel seen as AI-proof experience; bots may capture point-to-point but complex multi-destination trips need human advisors.
items.quote: there is a general sentiment that travel will become one of those AI-proof experiences. A lot of stuff that you do will probably be replaced with AI, but travel will remain one of those rare things which actually remain AI-proof in terms of just experiencing something more human

items.statement: CDMO volume growth above 20% YoY for last 4 quarters; expects healthy volume traction to continue in current quarter with 60-day order cycle visibility
items.quote: On the volumes, as of now as I said, we have seen multiple quarters where the volume growth was significant and we have a 60-odd day of order cycle visibility. So for the current quarter as well, we see good traction in our penetration in the CDMO services. So the volume growth still continues to remain healthy.

items.statement: Domestic branded formulations to deliver growth on par with IPM by FY28 as current initiatives bear fruit
items.quote: We expect the segment to deliver growth on par with IPM by FY28 as the current initiatives start bearing fruits.

items.statement: International branded formulations expected to maintain growth momentum and be key engine for Akums growth
items.quote: It is expected to maintain this momentum going forward in the year and will be key engine to drive Akums' growth.

items.statement: API segment targeting EBITDA breakeven over next 3-4 quarters; current loss run-rate ~INR5 cr +/- INR1 cr per quarter
items.quote: So no time lines as of now. I think consistently around you've seen the numbers, roughly INR5 crores plus/minus INR1 crores is roughly what we bleed as on today. But the endeavour is that over the next 3, 4 quarters, we should be breakeven in this segment.

items.statement: Zambia JV: $25 million revenue confirmed with margins slightly better than CDMO; commercial supplies from Indian plant in Q4 FY27, revenue booking in Q1 FY28; second $25 million round committed
items.quote: So that all remains consistent. And subsequently when we deliver this, we will again have a discussion on another $25 million round of supplies committed by the Government of Zambia.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex INR210 cr (includes Baddi plant ~INR43 cr and Oriflame acquisition ~INR56 cr); historical annual run-rate ~INR300 cr plus ~INR100 cr maintenance capex on INR2,400 cr gross block
items.quote: So for this quarter, as I mentioned, there is an investment of INR210 crores. H1 total is INR210 crores that we made. So we historically have been around a number of close to INR300-odd crores. We see this slightly higher this time because we are operationalising Baddi and we've acquired this plant.

items.statement: New Baddi facility Phase 1 (oral solids, 6+ billion units/year) operational in next 3-4 months (Q1 FY28); full facility ~12 billion tablets plus other dosage forms; adds to existing ~50-51 billion annual capacity
items.quote: So, this is a large facility, which will commission. So, in the Phase 1 of it, we will start with oral solids. So, this will be 6 billion tablets. So, we largely have 50 billion, 51 billion annual capacity. So, this is 6 billion on top of it, which is oral solids, which we'll have across various forms of tablets.

items.statement: Current CDMO utilization above 50%; Oriflame plants (beauty & personal care) successfully integrated
items.quote: We today operate at healthy utilization levels of above 50%.

items.statement: CDMO order cycle visibility of 60 days; strong order book driving >20% volume growth on September net MAT basis
items.quote: Led by strong order book and improved utilization of newer facilities, the CDMO business achieved a volume growth of more than 20% on September net MAT basis showcasing increasing penetration of our offering within the India pharma market.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 14.5% in Q2 FY27 vs 9.3% YoY and 15% QoQ; CDMO EBITDA INR168 cr (+99.6% YoY, +2.9% QoQ); Domestic branded EBITDA INR24 cr (-8.9% YoY, +103% QoQ); International branded EBITDA INR9.9 cr (+80.5% YoY, +43.8% QoQ); AP
items.quote: Margins were healthy at 14.5% as against 9.3% in Q2 FY26 and 15% in Q1 FY27. EBITDA with other income stood at INR224 crores, an increase of 76.3% year-on-year and an increase of 9.1% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: API prices up 2-3% QoQ and 5-7% YoY as a basket; slight upward trajectory expected in near term; input costs (KSMs, solvents, husk) also up dramatically
items.quote: If you really look at it quarter-on-quarter, these have moved roughly 2% to 3%. While if we compare it to last quarter 2 FY26, these would have moved up by 5% to 7% as a basket. So this is on the API prices.

items.statement: API segment focusing on higher gross margin products, removing low-margin SKUs, diversifying geographies (2 CEPs approved, 2 in pipeline, EDQM audit done); CDMO portfolio mimics Indian market therapy mix (~10-11% market share)
items.quote: The focus of the management over there is how do we curtail the losses and by which, we are meaningfully driving it with improvement of our product mix as well as by product mix, I mean removing products which have low gross margins and focusing on general products which have better gross margins.

items.statement: CDMO growth across existing and new customers (prescription, private label, regional); domestic branded field force ~1,600 MRs + 450 line managers (added 200 in Q1); PCPM ~2.5 overall, mature gynae divisions >3.2
items.quote: We today have almost 1,600 people on ground. We recently added people as we mentioned in our last call. So we have grown roughly 8% year-on-year in this business and the endeavour is how can we maintain an 8% to 10% growth in this business as well with continued improvements in PCPM and profitability.

items.statement: H1 FY27 free cash flow INR45.5 cr after business acquisition; operating cash flow to EBITDA 69.2%; cash & equivalents INR1,680 cr; trade generics pruned to reduce working capital drag
items.quote: company had a free cash flow for H1 of INR45.5 crores after account for business acquisition driven by healthy operating cash flow to Akums Drugs & EBITDA at a ratio of 69.2

items.statement: Capex funding flexibility: will use internal funds or debt depending on cost vs investment returns; healthy cash balance INR1,680 cr
items.quote: So we have the flexibility of raising debt and we have our own funds. I mentioned during our presentation that the company sits on a healthy free cash flow. We will weigh our options of what is more beneficial. If the loans are available at lower the cost of our investment, we'll take loans. Otherwise, we'll liquidate our investment.

items.statement: European advance $100 million ($20 million utilized, $80 million remaining); proportionate recognition over contract period; interest income ~20% of PBT currently
items.quote: Let's say if the contract is for 60 months, so you Akums Drugs & will probably have the advance, which is the 80 million which is left of the first 20 million, that will probably get set off and the remaining money will start coming in with the

items.statement: Oriflame acquisition (2 plants, ~INR56 cr) integrated; peak revenue target 3x investment; color cosmetics ramp-up underway; negligible PAT contribution currently
items.quote: Oriflame, we bought it at around INR56 crores. This is again, as I was mentioning to an earlier question, we expect that peak should deliver a 3x revenue for us.

items.statement: R&D spend ~3-3.5% of CDMO revenue (~INR130 cr); 375 scientists + ~100 support staff; ~30 DCGI approvals annually (2-3 per month)
items.quote: So this is broadly 3% of our revenues. We largely do roughly INR130-odd crores in our R&D. The whole endeavour for R&D is how can we have good products identified, researched upon.

items.statement: API price volatility (commodity-linked); Zambia shipping timeline 100-120 days delays revenue recognition; European dossier approval timing uncertain (1-2 quarters)
items.quote: Since this like most of our CDMO is ex works. So in our factory once it leaves our warehouse, we book the revenue ex works. Here we have to deliver at Lusaka warehouse of the Zambian government. So that shipping time lines from Haridwar from where we'll mostly manufacture to Lusaka in Zambia is roughly 100 and 120 days.

items.statement: Sustainability: EcoVadis Bronze medal; CII Water Management Champion Award; ERP transition to S/4HANA completed for real-time analytics
items.quote: We are proud to announce that our company has an EcoVadis Bronze medal. We are on our journey to be amongst the top global companies focused on environment, labor rights, ethics and sustainability. We also won the Water Management Champion Award by CII for green practices.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR13,000 crores plus; PAT margin 4% to 4.2%
items.quote: At a company level, we are targeting the revenues to be in the range of INR13,000 crores plus. That's the guidance we have already given in the market. And we see that this guidance is achievable as of now from the numbers which we have seen. PAT margin of 4% to 4.2% is what we have given the guidance earlier.

items.statement: Aspirational FY29 revenue around INR17,000 crores plus; CAGR FY27-29 ~25%
items.quote: We had done a 3-year plan, which is more of an aspirational plan, but it will be difficult to right now pin a number to it. On a broad level, we should be at around -- sorry, around INR17,000 crores plus by -- and I think our CAGR for FY '27 to '29 should be around 25% year-over-year

items.statement: Plan to open 23 new stores in FY27, total ~103 by year-end; 8-10 in Q3, rest in Q4
items.quote: We remain on track to open around 23 new stores in FY '27, taking our total store count to approximately 103 by the year-end. Expansion will gather pace over the next 2 quarters, driven P N Gadgil Jewellers Limited October 30th, 2026 primarily by the franchisee-led model across both legacy and YOOU

items.statement: FY28 onward: 50-50 COCO/FOCO split; targeting 30-35 stores/year (17-18 legacy, rest YOOU)
items.quote: Going ahead, next year -- from next year onwards, we plan to do a 50-50 allocation between COCO and FOCO. And that too also in the legacy and the YOOU by PNG format, it will be 50-50. So what we're talking of adding around 30, 35 stores, out of which 17 to 18 stores would be legacy, half the balance would be YOOU by PNG.

items.statement: UP/Central India stores: stock turn ~1.1x, revenue ~INR60 crores/store, stud ratio 17.4%
items.quote: roughly the stores around -- average age would be around a year, 11 to 12 months. And on average, the stock turn there would be at 1. So like we had projected there that each store should be doing around INR50 crores, INR55 crores of revenue, and that is where we are. So our planning is on track, and we are -- in fact, we are a little higher. We are at around 1.1 stock P N Gadgil Jewellers Limited

items.statement: Mature store target: 3.5-4x stock turn, ~INR200 crores revenue, stud ratio 22-25%
items.quote: The turn again should be the same. We are looking at 2.5 to 3 stock turn per store. And then after the year -- after year 4, we should look at reaching 3.5 to 4 stock turn. So that would translate into around INR200 crores once the store is fully mature. And I think the stud ratio which we are projecting there should be in the range of around 22% to 25%.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 8.4% (+186 bps YoY); adjusted EBITDA margin 8.2% (excl. INR5 cr unhedged gain)
items.quote: Our EBITDA increased 57% to INR224.6 crores with a margin expanding 186 bps to 8.4%. Excluding an unhedged inventory gain of INR5 crores, adjusted EBITDA grew 60% to INR209.6 crores with an adjusted EBITDA margin improving to 8.2% from 6.3% a year ago.

items.statement: Gross margin QoQ dip 50 bps due to franchisee mix rising to 17% from 12%
items.quote: On the gross margins, you have picked up right that we have increased our gross margins on a year-on-year basis. And there is some dip on a Q-on-Q basis, primarily driven by the franchisee share increased to 17% from 12% in the Q-on-Q number. So that's the reason why the gross margin has reduced by 50 bps on quarter-to-quarter.

items.statement: Franchisee growth dilutes gross margin but improves EBITDA margin and ROCE (no store opex/capex in PNG P&L)
items.quote: So what happens, we have explained it earlier also when the -- at a gross margin level, the increase of franchisee dilutes the margin at a gross margin level. But at an EBITDA level, we are pretty much there. So that's the reason also even though the gross margin have shifted a bit on the Q-on-Q basis, my other expenses have come down because I don't have a cost to operate those stores into my P&L

items.statement: YOOU stud ratio 53.1% (vs 32.9% last quarter); brand is ~70% diamond, 30% gold
items.quote: We rebranded LiteStyle as YOOU by PNG, which is a lightweight diamond jewellery brand for younger style-conscious consumers and the response has been very encouraging with YOOU stud ratio rising to 53.1% from 32.9% last quarter.

items.statement: Navaratri revenue ~INR200 crores shifted to Q3; Diwali/wedding season outlook positive with soft gold prices driving volume
items.quote: Yes, around -- if you look at the entire season of the 10 days of Navaratri, around INR200 crores would have been the revenue from those 10 days. So that revenue has been pushed to Q3.

items.statement: Navaratri good, Diwali season (first 15 days Nov) expected good; lots of bookings and customer interest
items.quote: Navaratri has been good and so the season looks positive as we speak. Prices have remained soft, and that has been also tempting of people to enter the market. So we are positive that Diwali should be -- Diwali season, the entire 1st November, first 15 days should be good. The indications are there are a lot of bookings, a lot of interest from people to make the purchases.

items.statement: Hedge coverage raised to ~80%; QIP proceeds partly deployed to festive inventory working capital; ~INR600 crores in bank FDs
items.quote: We have also strengthened our risk management framework, raising the hedge coverage to approximately 80%, making our earnings more resilient to gold price swings.

items.statement: QIP funds: some deployed to working capital for festive inventory; balance in bank FDs (~INR600 crores); FD balance rose INR637 crores QoQ to INR1,191 crores
items.quote: So currently money is parked in bank FDs., So around INR600 crores in bank FDs right now as we speak. Deepak Vijay: Also, if you will see quarter-on-quarter, my FDs -- the balance in my FDs last quarter, it was INR554 crores. This is around about INR1,191 crores in FY -- in quarter 2 end. So we have increased our FDs also by INR637 crores in -- between 2 quarters now

items.statement: Target to reduce borrowings 20-25% by FY29-30; net borrowing reduced INR167 crores QoQ (GML loans up for hedging, but FDs/collateral up more)
items.quote: So the borrowing, as like Saurabh has already mentioned earlier that we plan to reduce the borrowing by FY '29, FY '30 in the range of 20% to 25% and upwards of that. That's the goal which we have set for ourselves.

items.statement: Raised INR700 crores via QIP (oversubscribed 1.5x); CRISIL reaffirmed A+ stable
items.quote: In Q2 of FY '27, we also raised INR700 crores through QIP, which was over oversubscribed 1.5x. CRISIL also reaffirmed our credit rating at A+ with stable outlook.

items.statement: Completed 100% acquisition of Silvostyle (silver fashion jewellery) on 1 Oct; 18 stores + 68 shop-in-shops; FY24-26 revenue CAGR 64%, PAT CAGR 99%
items.quote: On 1st October, we completed the 100% acquisition of Silvostyle, a fast-growing silver fashion jewellery brand that grew revenue at 64% CAGR and PAT at 99% CAGR between FY24 and FY26 and already operates 18 stores and around 68 Shop-in-shops at PNG & YOOU and Silvostyle, we now have one house and three brands.

items.statement: SSSG 25.5% YoY in Q2; mature store SSG ~7-8% (ex-gold price surge); new store year-2 SSG ~80%
items.quote: Retail revenue increased 31% year-on-year to INR2,061 crores, supported by a healthy SSSG growth of 25.5%.

items.statement: Gold price softness driving volume growth; when prices fall, volume rises; when prices rise, value rises
items.quote: See, we always maintain -- I mean, when prices come down, you'll see more volume. When prices go up, you'll see more value. So by that logic, yes.

items.statement: CRISIL reaffirmed credit rating at A+ with stable outlook
items.quote: CRISIL also reaffirmed our credit rating at A+ with stable outlook.

items.statement: Employee cost down INR6 crores QoQ due to variable payout differences
items.quote: So on the employee expenses, there is a small drop of around about INR6 crores. That's majorly because of the variables which were there -- that's the difference of the variables across the 2 quarters and quarter 1 last year -- quarter 2 last year and this year. So that's the difference on the variable payouts.

items.statement: Operating expenses (ads, promotions) rationalized; INR86 crores in Q2 vs INR85 crores Q1; H2 expected similar moderation vs high base last year
items.quote: So if you compare quarter-on-quarter, last quarter, it was INR85 crores. And this quarter, it is INR86 crores. So we are pretty much in line with what we have committed in the quarter 1 call. You have pointed that H1 versus -- H1 last year versus this year, we have also improved, and that's primarily because of the advertisement and the campaign discounts, which we have said we will kind of ration

items.statement: Vehicle finance business on track to achieve EBITDA break-even this year
items.quote: Talking about vehicle finance, where we gave a narrative at the start of the year that this will be the year of EBITDA break -even, we are on track to achieve that.

items.statement: Tolling GTV typically grows in Q3 and Q4 as industry picks up seasonally
items.quote: Typically, Q3 and Q4 is when the whole industry picks up. Similar to the trend of last year, Q3 is where you typically start seeing the growth.

items.statement: Contribution margin remains north of 90% despite telematics mix impact
items.quote: The contribution margin profile continues to be the same, much north of 90% levels . High quality technology revenues, broad-based revenues and hence such quality contribution margin.

items.statement: AUM managed by partners in vehicle finance continues to steadily climb
items.quote: The AUM managed by partners with us continues to steadily climb, that will help us get to the EBITDA break-even point.

items.statement: No capex guidance provided; depreciation linked to telematics growth
items.quote: Currently, there is no guidance on how it will pan out.

items.statement: Super loads present in 14 cities (2 earlier, 12 newer) with working capital light model
items.quote: I think same numbers as before that we had mentioned: we are present in 14 cities, of which 2 cities are earlier cities and the remaining 12 are newer cities.

items.statement: UPI MDR impact on tolling business expected to be close to zero using sub-2000 transactions and PDN route
items.quote: So, using mix of these strategies, we believe the impact of MDR on UPI will be significantly close to zero possibly for our business.

items.statement: Telematics acceleration driven by AIS mandates and new products like fuel sensor and dash cam
items.quote: The large part of the acceleration is because of AIS mandates happening across states for various different use cases and inside that we are playing a material role by capturing incremental market share and that is leading to higher sales of devices incrementally every quarter.

items.statement: Repeat truck buyers with existing fleet stick to Blackbuck software for new trucks
items.quote: Because he already has a fleet of trucks and is using Blackbuck software, he first of all for a new truck itself does not use something else for a new truck; he uses us.

items.statement: Super loads is a cash-and-carry business with few days of working capital
items.quote: It is a very working capital light business, having a few days of working capital on an overall basis.

items.statement: Transacting customers at 9 lakh growing 13% YoY; power users at 4.8 lakh growing 20% YoY
items.quote: We had close to 9 lakh transacting customers, growing at about 13% year -on-year basis. Covers a large part of the medium and heavy commercial vehicle customers which are relevant for the intercity trucking audience. Power users, who use more than two services, growing at about 20% roughly more than half these users are power users, which is close to 4,80,000.

items.statement: Tolling GTV at 7,070 crores growing 17% YoY
items.quote: GTV of tolling, which is a large part of our payments business we do, growing healthy rate of about 17% year -on-year basis broadly 7,070 crores this quarter.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA grew 30% YoY to 55 crores including new business investments
items.quote: On an adjusted EBITDA basis, that is 55 crores, which is a growth of close to 30%. Again want to remind you here that this is a blended metric including the investments we are doing in our newer and emerging businesses.

items.statement: Telematics deferred revenue grew 56% YoY on half-year basis, 4-5x absolute growth vs depreciation
items.quote: On the half-year balance sheet, you would have seen that growth on deferred revenues also has been 56% year-on-year, growing strongly at four to five times the absolute growth in depreciation.

items.statement: No guidance on depreciation trajectory as it follows telematics growth path
items.quote: We continue to touch newer highs in telematics, so that growth path as we figure out, depreciation will follow that route. Currently, there is no guidance on how it will pan out.

items.statement: Targets INR 100 crore PAT for FY28 if UPI MDR is implemented
items.quote: And so with the additional UPI upside, definitely, we are targeting INR 100 crore PAT for next financial year if UPI MDR comes out.

items.statement: Expects payments revenue to increase by at least INR 100 crores in FY28 from UPI MDR
items.quote: Right. So high level, we believe that in financial year '28, the payments revenue, we estimate will go up by at least INR 100 crores.

items.statement: Expects INR 20-25 crores of UPI MDR revenue to flow to EBITDA/PAT
items.quote: And out of that, INR 20 crores to INR 25 crores should flow into the EBITDA or PAT levels.

items.statement: Guided for more than INR 1,000 crores quarterly lending disbursals in upcoming quarters
items.quote: Definitely, we had guided last quarter that in the upcoming quarters we will be doing more than INR 1,000 crores in quarterly disbursals.

items.statement: Expects strong double-digit growth in lending disbursals to continue
items.quote: That's right. It may not be the same percentage of growth, but definitely, it will be strong double-digit growth.

items.statement: Merchant GMV grew 76% YoY and 18% QoQ; Merchant revenue grew 150% YoY and 29% QoQ
items.quote: we have delivered absolutely amazing growth in terms of Merchant GMV having grown 76% Y-o-Y, and Merchant revenue has grown 150% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 7.5%, up 977 bps YoY and 204 bps QoQ; Contribution Profit jumped 50%
items.quote: EBITDA margin is 7.5%, our best yet, which is a 977 bps improvement Y-o-Y and 204 bps Q-o-Q.

items.statement: Merchant Payments net margin improved by 1 bps to 3.4 bps
items.quote: Even the net margin in Merchant Payments has improved by 1 bps and landed at 3.4 bps in the current quarter.

items.statement: Blended payment margin currently 13 bps; expects improvement from UPI MDR on eligible transactions >INR 2,000
items.quote: As you know, our blended payment margin right now is about 13 bps. And the eligible pool, which is transactions above INR 2,000 will One MobiKwik Systems Limited (“MobiKwik”) November 02, 2026 definitely yield stronger revenue for us

items.statement: UPI MDR implementation expected to be net positive for payments revenue and bottom line
items.quote: overall, it will definitely be a net upside on the payments revenue for the company as well as on the bottom line for the company.

items.statement: On merchant side, expects 20-25% of 40 bps gross UPI MDR to flow to bottom line (8-10 bps net)
items.quote: we believe that maybe 20% to 25% on the merchant side is what we will get at the bottom line.

items.statement: On consumer side, expects 8 bps (20% of 40 bps) to flow directly to net take rate
items.quote: On the consumer side, yes. However, there are other facets also. There are certain transactions which have flat fees as compared to the 40 bps.

items.statement: Merchant Payments now 22% of total payment GMV, growing faster than Consumer Payments
items.quote: Merchant Payments is currently about 22% of our total payment GMV, and we expect this to grow even further from here.

items.statement: Lending disbursal mix: 79% FLDG model, 21% pure distribution model; agnostic to model mix
items.quote: currently, our disbursal mix is 79% under the FLDG model and 21% under the pure distribution model.

items.statement: Onboarded 2 new lending partners, total active lending partners now 11
items.quote: We have also onboarded 2 new partners for a total active lending partner count being at 11 now.

items.statement: Acquiring higher quality users with >INR 2,000 transaction size using filters on device price and first transaction
items.quote: we apply a lot of filters and qualifying criteria as to what kind of user we want to acquire. Now that could be the price of your device, that could be your first transaction.

items.statement: UPI MDR announced 15 Sep, launch delayed to after Diwali; final implementation date not yet announced
items.quote: around 15th of September, the UPI MDR was announced and to be launched on 15th October. And subsequently, the date is going to be sometime after Diwali is the last update.

items.statement: Completed NBFC migration and slump sale in August; met all RBI conditions; awaiting final CoR approval
items.quote: We have met all the conditions of RBI, and now we are waiting for the final go-ahead from RBI so that we can get the CoR and start the operations.

items.statement: Total income INR 302 crores (8% YoY, 5% QoQ); Revenue from operations INR 295 crores (9% YoY)
