items.quote: Plant operations in Enschede stopped end of first quarter. And as we speak, there is a team on the ground which is now working towards the whole dismantling of equipments, sale, etc., which will take its own two to three quarters to bring it to a full closure.

items.statement: Working capital contracted in H1 due to plant shutdown payouts; expect normalization in H2 with seasonality benefits
items.quote: first half I think a large impact was also due to the payouts related to the plant shutdown. Now that is behind us, so as you rightly indicated the second half should see stable working capital norms and also the seasonality aspect in Europe will come in and the cash flows tend to get better in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA at 0.9x as of Sep 30, 2026; comfortable leverage despite ongoing capex
items.quote: As on 30th September 2026, consolidated net debt to EBITDA stood at just 0.9 times, providing substantial capacity to fund future growth while maintaining a prudent capital structure.

items.statement: Raised ~INR 1,500 crore gross debt in H1 including INR 1,250 crore NCDs at 8.5%; more debt likely for expansion but leverage to stay comfortable
items.quote: we have taken a gross debt of around INR 1,500 crores this year in first half. A nd I think you also have mentioned that INR 1,250 crores is from the non -convertible debentures. So, of which 8.5% is the interest

items.statement: Reifen business stable; Q2 EBITDA margins slightly lower YoY due to cost pressures; expect uptick in Q3 due to seasonality
items.quote: Reifen is a fairly stable business. And by and large, it has remained at the same levels as what we would have seen in the past years. But coming specifically to quarter two, our margins, our EBITDA margins have been, and you also have to understand there is a bit of seasonality in that business. So, quarter two margins are slightly subdued, which you will see changing in quarter three.

items.statement: SAP S/4HANA implemented for US business; rollout underway for Europe and India operations
items.quote: During the quarter, we successfully completed the SAP S/4HANA implementation for our US business and now we are on our way to implement the same for the European and the Indian operations.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty and commodity volatility create near-term uncertainty; RM trajectory depends on geopolitical developments
items.quote: while geopolitical developments and commodity volatility continue to create uncertainty in the near term, the underlying fundamentals of a business have continued to strengthen.

items.statement: OEM price increases largely formula-linked with one-quarter lag; some negotiated increases also achieved
items.quote: So, it's largely formula linked. So that of course comes with a lag of one quarter, but there were some OEMs wherein it was not formula linked. And as I mentioned, we have also managed through negotiations get an appropriate price increase to maintain the cost, to take care of the cost increase on raw material

items.statement: Export outlook uncertain due to global volatility; being conservative on exports given strong domestic demand
items.quote: Difficult to say at this stage, you know, because you can see the volatility is quite beyond control. And as we see international markets, our exports are all around, you know to Europe to America and even to the Middle East, Southeast Asia. So, I think it will be very difficult to say but as of now we are being very careful and conservative on the exports because we see a strong demand momentum i

items.statement: Enschede closure exceptional cost EUR 2.3 million in Q2; minor dismantling costs to continue for few quarters
items.quote: In this quarter itself if you would have seen there is around EUR 2.3 million exceptional item in the European operations which was largely as a fallout of some bit of employees that were remaining in a different legal entity and that also now has been taken into the books.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin target of INR14-15 per kg (12.5%-14% range)
items.quote: we have estimated. And we are continuing to remain our target remains same, and we are on track. So on a full year basis, we are expecting EBITDA margin roughly around INR15 per kg on an average.

items.statement: Q2 PBT flat at INR153 cr vs INR158 cr YoY due to raw material cost lag
items.quote: PBT during the quarter was at INR153 crores as against INR158 crores of quarter 2 FY26.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA margin ~11.7%; full-year target 12.5%-14%
items.quote: Six months ended roughly around we are having 12.5% something kind of thing. But year as a whole, 12.5% to 13% and 14% somewhere around, we'll be ending up.

items.statement: Q2 volume up 28% YoY to 83,407 MT on channel restocking and stabilized PVC prices
items.quote: During the quarter, sales volume grew 28% over year -on-year basis to 83,407 metric tons as channel destocking eased and the PVC prices also kind of stabilized during the quarter.

items.statement: October volume YoY positive; full-year volume outlook uncertain due to geopolitics
items.quote: October was a relatively good month as compared to the previous years. okay? And so if I look at it from today's perspective, if I take into account the October performance also then year-on-year, I'm slightly on the greener side on a percentag e basis, volume growth, yes.

items.statement: MIP at $767/t CIF; DGTR recommended CVD on China PVC imports
items.quote: MIP is at CIF price, which is $767 per metric ton. So any imports are not allowed. And the CVD, which you are talking about is only, I think, only on the China region -- and MIP is for all irrespective...

items.statement: FY27 capex ~INR150 cr for debottlenecking and maintenance
items.quote: this year also, we have roughly planned for a capex of INR150-odd crores. This includes more or less routine capex. And as we have been talking about, this will be for the further debottlenecking in the process.

items.statement: No material related-party transactions impacting operations
items.quote: Definitely, we do not get into any related party transaction other than the non directors and all. There is no separate substantial related party transaction, which can impact the operations of the company. No related party transactions.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty in West Asia affecting crude, shipping, raw material supply
items.quote: geopolitical developments in West Asia, they continue to remain uncertain. And with respect to the raw material supply and also with respect to the PVC supply. But we continue to, as always, monitor them very closely.

items.statement: Full-year device guidance of 36 million pens expected to be exceeded
items.quote: We have delivered 10.4 million devices in the quarter and remain on track to exceed our full year guidance of 36 million devices.

items.statement: FY28 device volume target around 15% growth over FY27
items.quote: As far as next year is concerned, the number you stated, give or take, 15% is what we're targeting.

items.statement: Healthcare revenue grew 78% YoY to INR175 crore, now 55% of total revenue
items.quote: Healthcare is now the primary engine of our business, contributing 55% of revenue and growing 78% year-on-year.

items.statement: Consumer business stabilized over two sequential quarters but remains below prior year levels
items.quote: Third, the Consumer business has finally stabilized over two sequential quarters, although it continues to operate below last year's levels.

items.statement: Gross margins recovered to 60%, up ~70 bps YoY after Q1 cost pressures
items.quote: Second, gross margins recovered to 60%, about 70 basis points higher than a year ago, following the cost pressures we highlighted in quarter 1.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 31.9% in Q2 FY27, flat YoY; operating leverage expected to protect margins despite pricing pressure
items.quote: There is pricing pressure. And for all the long-term contracts that we currently have in place, a) price erosion has already been built into that contract. Now I'm very confident we will be able to maintain our margins.

items.statement: Consumer Electronics and Semiconductor capex estimated around INR100 crore, could vary INR80-120 crore
items.quote: Whether INR100 crores goes to INR120 crores or INR80 crores, I don't know, but that is going to be about that.

items.statement: New 25 million pen capacity line starting qualification next week; commercial sales expected from December
items.quote: If all goes well, we should be in a position to start selling from that capacity in December.

items.statement: Machine utilization rose to 52.5% in Q2 from 47.8% a year ago
items.quote: Machine utilization across our plants rose to 52.5% in quarter 2 compared to 47.8% a year ago.

items.statement: Two active customers for emergency use auto-injector development; clinical batches due end of 2027
items.quote: We have 2 active customers on emergency use for whom we are developing this product. From a time line perspective, the clinical batches are due end of '27

items.statement: Eye applicator completed qualifications; supply expected by end of Q2 or early Q3 FY27
items.quote: Eye applicator has just completed qualifications. We should be in supply by the end of this quarter, early next quarter.

items.statement: Toby Reusable auto-injector launched at CPHI; 80% developed; seeking partner for co-development
items.quote: Toby Reusable was just launched at CPHI. It's a product where we have completed potentially 80% of development. There are still some bits which are yet to be completed, which we're working on at the moment.

items.statement: Polymer price pass-through to Consumer customers with 2-4 month lag depending on customer
items.quote: With some customers, you would have a lag of 2 months, with some customers, you would have a lag of 3 to 4 months. So that's how it happens.

items.statement: Pen contracts have index mechanism to pass on material inflation; price erosion built into long-term contracts
items.quote: For material prices, we do have an index mechanism with our pen pricing where at least the inflationary measures will be passed on. So even with erosion at a baseline, you will have not a situation where you're going to end up losing out on your margins.

items.statement: Exports 62.9% of H1 FY27 revenue vs 71.7% in H1 FY26; shift due to Healthcare supplying Indian pharma serving global markets
items.quote: Exports accounted for 62.9% of revenue in H1 FY27 compared to 71.7% in H1 FY26. The shift is primarily attributable to growth in the Healthcare business where we supply Indian pharma customers who, in turn, serve global markets.

items.statement: CARE Ratings reaffirmed long-term at CARE A+ stable and upgraded short-term to CARE A1+ from CARE A1 in October
items.quote: In October, CARE Ratings reaffirmed our long-term bank facilities at CARE A+ with a stable outlook and upgraded our short-term facilities to CARE A1+ from CARE A1.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity 0.2x as of 30 September 2026
items.quote: Debt to equity was 0.2x, and the fixed asset turnover was 2x as of 30th September 2026.

items.statement: ROCE 41.1% and ROE 29.7% as of 30 September 2026
items.quote: ROCE and ROE were at 41.1% and 29.7%, respectively, as of 30th September 2026.

items.statement: Cash PAT INR138 crore in H1 FY27, up 19% YoY
items.quote: Cash PAT was INR138 crores, up 19% from INR116 crores.

items.statement: Semiconductor tray commercial shipments expected from Q4 FY27; trial production in Q3 FY27
items.quote: We would start trial production of Semiconductor Packaging in Q3 FY27, expect to start commercial shipments in Q4.

items.statement: Consumer Electronics commercial supplies commenced for 5 components; scaling production progressively
items.quote: Commercial supplies have commenced for Consumer Electronics, and we are progressively scaling production of the 5 components awarded by our new customer.

items.statement: On-body auto-injector (Mira) customer not yet finalized; 14-month timeline to clinical batches after customer sign-up
items.quote: We're close to finalizing a customer for the on-body Mira, post which we will have a 14-month time line to deliver clinical batches

items.statement: Confident of onboarding 1-2 innovator pharma customers by end of calendar 2027; revenue ramp 3-4 years post win
items.quote: I'm fairly confident that, yes, by the end of calendar '27, we should be able to crack 1 or 2 innovators. Having said that, when you crack an innovator, the revenue isn't going to start flowing from '28. It's going to be a 3- to 4-year journey before you see revenue flow in.

items.statement: Aerospace & defense: supplying high-precision components indirectly but no direct headway yet
items.quote: We've been supplying indirectly some of the high-precision components for quite a long time. But have we made any headway in that, in aerospace and defense? The answer is no, we haven't.

items.statement: FY27 volume guidance of approximately 7 million tonnes
items.quote: We remain confident of achieving our FY '27 volume guidance of approximately 7 million tonnes supported by our expanded capacity and improving demand outlook.

items.statement: FY27 full-year EBITDA revised to ₹350-375 crore (₹525-550 per ton)
items.quote: I think we should comfortably do. Unfortunately, the input prices have scaled up, but we should be up of ₹350 crore to ₹375 crore for the full-year, which should roughly translate to ₹525 to ₹550 tons per EBITDA per ton.

items.statement: FY28 volume target of 8-8.25 million tonnes
items.quote: I think we are targeting it around 8 million to 8.25 million.

items.statement: FY28 EBITDA target of ~₹500 crore at ₹650 per ton on 8-8.25 million tonnes
items.quote: What we are pencilling in is around ₹650 EBITDA per ton for 8 million ton to 8.25-million-ton kind of a volume. Around ₹500 odd crores is what we are looking at for the next year.

items.statement: Net debt to halve from ~₹1,600 crore to ~₹700 crore over next two years
items.quote: Our stated goal is to look at cutting it by half over next two years' time from current ₹1,600 crore, ₹1,450 crore kind of net debt position. Yeah, we would like to see some ₹700 crore kind of a thing over next two years' period.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA per ton at ₹265
items.quote: From an operational standpoint, EBITDA per ton for the quarter stood at ₹265.

items.statement: H2 FY27 EBITDA per ton expected at ₹650
items.quote: I think we should, yeah, we should look at ₹650 kind of an environment.

items.statement: Completed 0.75 mt grinding capacity in Andhra; total capacity now 11.75 mt
items.quote: On the CapEx front, we completed 0.75 million ton grinding capacity in Andhra during the quarter, further strengthening our manufacturing footprint and taking our overall capacity to 11.75 million.

items.statement: Capex largely complete; minor cash flows may extend to Q1 FY28
items.quote: Except for probably some cash flow related to CapEx might flow into Q1 of next year, but everything is done. Everything is done.

items.statement: Plant utilisations: Mattampally 73%, Gudipadu 85%, Bayyavaram 52%, Jeerabad 72%, Jajpur 38%, Dachepalli 57%
items.quote: In terms of plant-wise operations, our Mattampally facility operated at 73% utilisation, while Gudipadu, Bayyavaram, Jeerabad, Jajpur, and Dachepalli operated at 85%, 52%, 72%, 38%, and 57%, respectively during the quarter.

items.statement: Target overall capacity utilisation of 65-70% in H2 FY27 and FY28
items.quote: Yes. I think we are looking at if same demand trends continue, I think next year we are targeting close to around 65% to 70% capacity utilisation at overall numbers, at full capacity, Mr. Niteen… Niteen S. Dharmawat: And for H2? Sreekanth Reddy: Yeah, I think H2, we should be up of close to 65% to 70

items.statement: Power & fuel cost ₹1,473/ton in Q2 FY27 vs ₹1,428/ton in Q2 FY26; freight ₹900/ton vs ₹855/ton
items.quote: Power and fuel cost stood at ₹1,473 per ton during the quarter compared to ₹1,428 per ton in Q2 FY '26. Freight cost stood at ₹900 per ton, compared with ₹855 per ton in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Realisation up ~₹500/ton from Q2 exit to Oct; South non-trade +₹20/bag in Sep, +₹20 in Oct; trade +₹20 in Sep, +₹5 in Oct
items.quote: What we have seen at Sagar is ₹25 per bag on an average from exit of August all the way so far. Again, it includes September and all the way up to end of October. We have seen on an average ₹25 per bag, which is roughly translating to ₹500 odd per ton increase at realization level.

items.statement: Freight cost to remain flat after diesel price stabilisation
items.quote: Diesel prices have gone up as you are aware. I think it should stabilize, hoping that diesel price, there may not be any significant reason in that. The freight more or less should remain flat from here on.

items.statement: Q2 demand resilient despite monsoon; infrastructure, housing, industrial projects supportive
items.quote: Construction activity across key markets remained reasonably healthy, supported by steady progress in infrastructure projects undertaken by both central and state governments, alongside continued demand from the housing and construction sectors.

items.statement: State-wise H1 FY27 growth: AP/Telangana +15%, Karnataka flat, TN +10%, Kerala +12%, Maharashtra +10%, Odisha flat, MP +7.5-8%, Gujarat ~5%
items.quote: think year-to-date, AP and Telangana have grown up of 15%. Karnataka has grown more or less at 2% to 3%. I would assume that it is flat. Tamil Nadu has grown at Sagar Cements Limited (SAGARCEM) Q2 & H1 FY '27 Earnings Conference Call November 2, 2026 plus 10%. Kerala has grown at plus 12%. Maharashtra at plus 10%. Odisha almost flat. Madhya Pradesh has grown at around 7.5% to 8%. Gujarat has grown

items.statement: Vizag land monetisation: ₹350 crore total value; ~₹150 crore advance expected by end FY27
items.quote: I think at this point of time, I would stick to what we have indicated before. So, we are expecting ₹350 crore of total monetisation value for that Vizag land. Around ₹150 odd crore is what we are expecting as advance.

items.statement: Gross debt ₹1,735 crore (₹1,482 crore long-term); net worth ₹1,781 crore; D/E 0.83x; cash ₹106 crore
items.quote: Gross debt as of September 30th, 2026, stood at ₹1,735 crore, out of which ₹1,482 crore comprising long-term borrowing, while the balance represents working capital borrowing. Consolidated net worth stood at ₹1,781 crore, while the debt-to-equity ratio was at 0.83:1. Cash and bank balances stood at ₹106 crore as of 30th September, 2026.

items.statement: Net debt stabilised in Q3 FY27; aggressive reduction from Q4 FY27
items.quote: We believe that for Q3, net debt probably should remain where it is. From Q4 onwards, it would aggressively start coming down.

items.statement: Target ~₹250 crore debt reduction in FY28 plus Vizag land proceeds
items.quote: I think we should start looking at around ₹250 crore of debt getting reduced from next year onwards, plus the realisation, monetisation from the Vizag land.

items.statement: Fuel mix shifted to domestic; petcoke mainly at Gudipadu & Jeerabad; some South Africa/US imports
items.quote: I think we are mostly shifted to domestic. We have less petcoke. The petcoke primarily is both at Gudipadu and Jeerabad, and primarily are the domestic sources. There is some percentage which is coming from South Africa or U.S. I mean, this is the mix which should go forward because that's how we have made our inventory.

items.statement: WHRS savings: Andhra ~₹1.5 crore/month when commissioned (FY28); Jeerabad solar 7-8 MW ~₹4-4.5 crore/year
items.quote: For Andhra, when waste heat recovery will get commissioned, we should expect ₹1.5 crore per month kind of a saving at Andhra. For solar, we are expecting close to around ₹4 crore to ₹4.5 crore at Jeerabad for full-year, as and when it gets commissioned.

items.statement: Jeerabad incentives: ₹30 crore/year expected; ₹50 crore for 2.5 years pending receipt
items.quote: See, I think the expected incentive for Jeerabad is at ₹30 crore per year. I think we did receive another ₹50 crore is what we are expecting for the two and a half years.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 loss after tax ₹52 crore
items.quote: Loss after tax stood at ₹52 crore.

items.statement: Superfine Building Materials to contribute ₹25-30 crore EBITDA in FY28 at 35-40% margins
items.quote: For the next year onwards, the next year being the first full-year of operations for that, we are only assuming certain capacity utilisation. I think it should contribute Sagar Cements Limited (SAGARCEM) Q2 & H1 FY '27 Earnings Conference Call November 2, 2026 anywhere between ₹25 crore to ₹30 crore of EBITDA for the next year, subsequently to scale up

items.statement: Reiterated double-digit growth in average EBITDA per tonne over FY26 levels
items.quote: We reiterate our guidance of double-digit growth in average EBITDA per tonne over FY26 levels. We remain committed to that guideline.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of around 7% now challenging; EBITDA guidance maintained
items.quote: On the volume, we had said around 7% or so volume growth. That is a little bit challenging right now, both from the point of view of the availability of raw material as well as the competitive markets where we want to address this year. But the EBITDA guidance continues.

items.statement: Aquapharm targeting double-digit revenue growth for FY27
items.quote: We are working towards double-digit revenue growth for FY27, supported by executions, customer deployment, and new products.

items.statement: Domestic demand supported by strong OEM performance and replacement demand; cautious procurement affecting volumes
items.quote: Domestic demand continues to be supported by strong OEM performance, a steady replacement demand and activity across key automotive segments. However, cautious procurement and inventory management by customers is affecting volumes during the quarter.

items.statement: Export volumes pulled back due to unprofitable economics; expect growth as market stabilizes
items.quote: See, the exports, as Raj was mentioning, we actually pulled back some volume where the contribution was not positive. And to a large extent, it was a mix of the crude and the raw material price and the freight cost.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA INR 310 crores, up 12% YoY; EBITDA per tonne INR 17,500 net of tariff refund
items.quote: We made INR 19,800 roughly, out of which about INR 2,300 was on account of tariff refund. So net-net, around INR17,500 is what we made at per tonne EBITDA.

items.statement: Project Alchemy cost savings of INR 200-250 crores on track; INR 10-15 crores realized in Q2
items.quote: We stay positive about the INR 200 crores being delivered over the quarters coming forward. So the initiatives are getting proven. Then the next step, of course, is horizontal deployment.

items.statement: Expanding long-term supply and offtake arrangements with strategic customers for Specialty Carbon Blacks
items.quote: Expanding the proposition of business covered under long-term supply and offtake arrangements with strategic customers remains a key priority, improving revenue visibility, reducing demand volatility and supporting a more predictable earnings profile.

items.statement: INR 300 crores capex plan for FY27; coal distillation project in final approval stage
items.quote: We are in the final stage of approving that. As I said, last time, we were looking at both the supplier contracts as well as the technology we want to use. That is now almost finalized. We should be announcing that shortly.

items.statement: Specialty Carbon Black capacity ~75,000 tonnes; Mundra Line 6 commercialized; can dial up volumes as gas and raw material availability improves
items.quote: So on Specialty, the capacity that we have is around 75. So we are good to market that. We are tying up more and more resources for raw material, which is feedstock, which is unique for Specialty Chemicals.

items.statement: Total carbon black capacity ~8 lakh tonnes including Andhra; significant export growth expected over next few years
items.quote: We should see significant growth in exports over the next few years. We have a fairly small market share today with some of the largest customers globally. And we are entering into conversations with them on long-term tie-ups, which should easily see our volumes multiplying as we progress over the next year.

items.statement: Price increases announced in spot market for November-December; gradual pass-through as higher cost inventory comes in
items.quote: That said, we have already announced the price increase in the spot market as well, which should be getting through. In November and December, we expect that price increase to go further up. So it's gradually being moved up as the higher cost inventory comes in.

items.statement: Aquapharm expanded critical raw material inventory coverage to protect supply chain against volatility
items.quote: On the raw material front, we have expanded our critical raw material inventory coverage to protect our supply chain against ongoing market volatility.

items.statement: Specialty Carbon Black operations impacted by global uncertainty; progressing on strategic growth initiatives across products, applications, geographies
items.quote: During the quarter, Specialty Carbon Black operations were impacted by global uncertainty, elevated oil prices and higher freight costs, which affected trade flows across key markets. Despite these external challenges, we continue to make meaningful progress on our strategic growth initiatives across products, applications, and geographies.

items.statement: Russian carbon black and CBFS exports shrinking due to refinery disruptions; Chinese coal tar prices firming up; import volumes into India declining
items.quote: Disruption of Russian refineries continues to impact availability of CBFS. As we highlighted last quarter, Russian refineries throughput has fallen to multi-decade lows with a meaningful share of capacity off-line. This shrinking of the Russian supplies is impacting both their export of carbon black as well as CBFS and keeping global feedstock availability relatively tight.

items.statement: Domestic competitors chasing volume at low prices; management believes unsustainable long-term
items.quote: I don't want to reflect on competition, what is happening there. But it's just that some people are chasing volume and I assume some degree of cash. But when we look at benchmarking across, I don't think it's possible to afford low prices for long in this industry.

items.statement: US tariff refund of INR 33 crores received (100% of amount due); tariff volatility remains a concern for large customers
items.quote: And the INR 33 crores what we got refund from the U.S. tariff, it is the 100% of what we were supposed to receive? Nilesh Koul: Yes

items.statement: Freight and logistics costs risen sharply due to vessel shortage, longer transit times, war risk premiums
items.quote: Freight and logistics costs have risen very sharply with shortage of vessels, availability and longer transit times. Longer shipping routes are increasing ton miles while higher freight rates and war risk premiums are adding to the landed cost of feedstock.

items.statement: Customer destocking and lean inventories affecting volumes; no inventory buildup seen as crude stayed elevated
items.quote: Some customers continue to maintain lean inventories and adopt a wait-and-watch approach amid expectations of softening prices, adding to the pressure on quarterly volumes.

items.statement: Aquapharm Q2 FY27: Sales volume 24,253 MT, Revenue INR 433 crores, EBITDA INR 42 crores; Home Care +7% YoY, Water Solutions and Oil & Gas -20% YoY, Application-specific +15%
items.quote: Aquapharm reported sales volume of 24,253 metric tonnes, revenues of INR 433 crores, and EBITDA of INR 42 crores in Q2 FY27. During the quarter, Home Care sales volume increased by 7% on a year-over-year basis. Both the Water Solutions and Oil & Gas segment reported a 20% year-over-year decline, while remaining steady sequentially. Application-specific solutions posted strong double-digit growth o

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions (West Asia, Russia-Ukraine) disrupting trade routes, elevating freight costs, influencing customer destocking
items.quote: Geopolitical developments, particularly the conflict in West Asia and between Russia and Ukraine continue to disrupt trade routes, elevate freight costs and influence customer destocking decisions.

items.statement: US tariff volatility a residual challenge; customers hesitant to shift significant volume without trade deal certainty
items.quote: The one residual challenge is that there is still some degree of concern on the volatility of tariff. Right now, it is low. But all the large customers contract out volume for the full year besides, of course, there is some spot volume available. But when they are doing that calculation, they don't want to forgo local capacity.

items.statement: Aquapharm antidumping duty on HEDP and ATMP provisionally imposed by DGTR; impact not yet incorporated in forecasts
items.quote: On the second question, yes, antidumping in India, that's provisional right now. And we are working on getting it over the line so that it's finalized. We have not incorporated any impact of antidumping yet in our forecast.

items.statement: Imperial Blue and Mansion House registered secondary volume growth of 8.5% and 7.1% QoQ in Q2 FY27, driving market share gains.
items.quote: Firstly, both our flagship brands, Imperial Blue Whisky and Mansion House Brandy have registered a robust secondary volume growth of 8.5% and 7.1%, respectively, in Q2 FY27 versus Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Overall volumes increased 160% YoY and 2% QoQ in Q2 FY27; growth was flattish QoQ due to higher primary in Q1 from TSMA exit states.
items.quote: In Q2, our overall volumes increased by 160% on a year-on-year basis and 2% on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Maintain FY27 volume growth guidance of high single-digit to low double-digit for combined business; beyond FY27, mid-teens volume and mid-to-high teens revenue growth over next couple of years.
items.quote: We maintain our guidance for FY27 of achieving a high single-digit to low double-digit volume growth for the combined business. And beyond FY27, including new launches planned for FY28 onwards, we maintain our volume growth guidance of mid-teens and revenue guidance of mid-to-high teens over the next couple of years.

items.statement: NSR moderated 0.75% QoQ to Rs 1,174/case in Q2 FY27 due to state and brand mix change; grew 4.2% YoY on H1 basis.
items.quote: The overall NSR moderated by 0.75% to Rs. 1,174 per case for Q2 FY27 from Rs. 1,183 per case in Q1 FY27 and increased by 3.2% from Rs. 1,138 per case in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Adjusted gross margin 41.8% in Q2 FY27 vs 42.1% in Q1 FY27; excluding inflationary pressures, margin would be closer to 44%.
items.quote: Adjusted for subsidy, we have achieved a gross profit of Rs. 432 crore in Q2 FY27 and a margin of 41.8% compared to 42.1% in Q1 FY27. Excluding the impact of inflationary pressures, the margin would have been higher, closer to 44%.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin 14.1% in Q2 FY27; excluding inflationary pressures, margin would be approximately 16.5%.
items.quote: Adjusted for subsidy, the EBITDA grew by 143% to Rs. 146 crore and a 14.1% margin on the combined business. Excluding the impact of inflationary pressures, the margin would have been approximately 16.5%.

items.statement: Packaging costs (glass) rose meaningfully over last two quarters due to geopolitical tensions; ENA prices started showing inflationary trend at Q2 exit with rising fuel and grain costs.
items.quote: The ongoing geopolitical tensions have resulted in continued inflationary pressures across packaging inputs particularly glass, resulting in a meaningful increase in packaging costs during the last 2 quarters. While exiting Q2 FY27, ENA prices have also started to show an inflationary trend with rising fuel and grain costs.

items.statement: Raw material inflation impact estimated at ~2.5% or Rs 25 crore per quarter on gross margins compared to pre-West Asia crisis levels.
items.quote: See, it has been around 2.5%. The way we are looking at this is pre-West Asia crisis. So, compared to Q4, the kind of impact that you are looking at is more like 2.5%. On a net basis, you can consider around Rs. 25 crore on a quarterly basis in Q1 as well as Q2.

items.statement: Price increases taken in Eastern/Northeastern states; discussions ongoing in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh; expect price hikes in a couple of states annually driving ~200 bps price mix benefit.
items.quote: So, many of the Eastern states, we have already taken a price increase, like in the Northeast states of Assam & Meghalaya. I think we are underway in Arunachal Pradesh as well. The South states are something which we are discussing actively with the governments. In two of the large states, Telangana and Andhra Paresh, we are discussing with the government for a price increase.

items.statement: Mansion House Reserve Brandy grew 25% QoQ and 50% YoY in September 2026 in Tamil Nadu; highest volume month ever.
items.quote: Mansion House Reserve Brandy has seen 25%+ quarter-on-quarter volume growth with 50% year-on-year volume growth in September 2026, emerging as the highest volume month ever.

items.statement: Imperial Blue recorded highest ever quarterly volumes in Karnataka with market share crossing 40%, up 900 bps QoQ.
items.quote: During Q2, Imperial Blue Whisky recorded its highest ever quarterly volumes in the state with market shares crossing 40%, a massive 900 bps increase on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Strategic investment of Rs 22 crore for 30% stake in Black Tiger Distilleries (Bodega Suprema Tequila) over two tranches: Rs 6 crore invested, Rs 16 crore over next 12 months.
items.quote: We have agreed to invest Rs. 22 crore for a 30% stake in the company, over 2 tranches - Rs. 6 crore, which has already been invested and, another Rs. 16 crore will be invested in the next 12 months.

items.statement: Gross debt Rs 2,202 crore, net debt Rs 2,074 crore as of Sep 30, 2026; slight reduction vs June 2026; target net debt in March 2027 below March 2026 levels.
items.quote: As on 30th September 2026, our gross debt stood at Rs. 2,202 crore and net debt stood at Rs. 2,074 crore. There is a slight reduction in net debt levels as compared to June 2026. I want to reassure you that our target is to take the net debt in March 2027 to below March 2026 levels.

items.statement: Annualized net working capital days at ~65 days on gross basis including Telangana overdues of Rs 550 crore; days increased ~5 days vs March 2026; expect similar levels going forward excluding overdue recovery over 12-24 months.
items.quote: As it stands today, you are looking at an annualized net working capital days on gross basis at around 65 days. This obviously is taking into account the overdues of Telangana of around Rs. 550 crore as well. In terms of going forward, excluding the benefit of potentially getting the overdues over the next 12-24 months, you should be looking at similar levels from a net working capital days perspe

items.statement: Karnataka excise policy reforms driving strong growth in Prestige & Above category; Mansion House highest selling brandy in Karnataka in Sep 2026.
items.quote: Karnataka, on the back of the recent progressive excise policy reforms, has witnessed strong growth in the Prestige & Above category with significant benefits for both Imperial Blue Whisky and Mansion House Brandy. Additionally, Mansion House Brandy emerged as the highest selling brandy in Karnataka in the month of September 2026.

items.statement: Early reform signals in Tamil Nadu (ordering changes on depletion basis) boosting tertiary sales; Mansion House Reserve Brandy volumes up sharply.
items.quote: Further, there are early signals of reform in Tamil Nadu, the largest brandy market in India. We are very confident that TI, the largest P&A brandy player in India will be one of the biggest beneficiaries of any reform, which

items.statement: UK FTA benefit of ~100 bps on consolidated EBITDA margin baked into upper end of 18% FY29 guidance; no benefit in Q2 due to inventory; resolution being pursued with authorities.
items.quote: So, with respect to UK FTA, the kind of benefits that we have taken as a part of the upper end of the margin guidance of 18% is approximately 100 basis points on a consolidated basis on a full year perspective.

items.statement: A&P reinvestment rates increased 61 bps QoQ in Q2 FY27 due to strong ATL/BTL execution ahead of festive season.
items.quote: A&P reinvestment rates increased by 61 bps in Q2 FY27 versus Q1 FY27 on the back of strong ATL and BTL execution drives ahead of the festive season.

items.statement: Samsara Gin grew 50% in H1 FY27 vs H1 FY26; business skewed to H2 (65% of annual volumes).
items.quote: Samsara has grown by 50% in the first half compared to last year. It is important to note that SSL's business is largely skewed towards H2 compared to H1, with H1 contributing approximately 35% of the overall yearly business, compared to 65% in H2.

items.statement: IB integration: states transitioned out of TSMA stabilized; last remaining state to transition by end of FY27; exceptional transition costs significantly reduced in Q2 and to continue at same levels for next two quarters.
items.quote: On the IB integration front, I am happy to inform you that the states which transitioned out of TSMA under TI operations have been stabilized, marking another step towards successful integration. The last remaining state will also be transitioned towards end of FY27. As a result, exceptional costs relating to the transition has significantly reduced during Q2 FY27 and will continue at the same lev

items.statement: Exceptional integration costs of Rs 10-11 crore per quarter expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27; no TSMA fees in FY28.
items.quote: No, we will not be seeing any TSMA fees in FY28. And you should be expecting over the next 2 quarters around Rs. 10 crore - Rs. 11 crore on a quarterly basis. So similar levels what you have seen in Q2, in Q3 and Q4 as well.

items.statement: ENA prices expected to remain elevated in near term due to hardened grain prices; difficult to predict long-term trend.
items.quote: We expect that ENA would be on elevated side in the near term.

items.statement: Imperial Blue distribution leveraged to launch Madira Rum in Uttarakhand; luxury portfolio (Monarch, Seven Islands, Samsara) to roll out in northern states in H2 FY27.
items.quote: So, it is early days. I think one introduction, which we did was of Madira Rum in Uttarakhand on the back of the Imperial Blue distribution. And in Q3 and Q4 we will roll out our luxury portfolio from House of TI in many of the northern states where Imperial Blue is widely distributed.

items.statement: New brandy entrants in AP and Telangana focused on popular segment; TI maintaining market share in Prestige & Above segment.
items.quote: But I think just one thing that I do want to bring out over here is that, yes, there have been new players which have come in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, but they have been more on the popular and below side. So, at our relevant price points, to be very frank, we are still maintaining market share.

items.statement: Operating cash flow negative in H1 FY27 due to inventory and receivables build-up; Telangana on 6-month overdue cycle (~Rs 550 crore).
items.quote: Compared to March 2026, the number of days has increased slightly by around 5-odd days, but then what one needs to consider in this entire thing is that the Telangana is working on a 6-month overdue cycle. By March, I only had 4 months of Imperial Blue overdue sitting within the books.

items.statement: Management guided EBITDA margin to be close to 15-17% band in Q3 and Q4 FY27
items.quote: We are quite confident that we will be quite close to that 15% to 17% band that we have indicated. In the third quarter, and possibly also in the fourth quarter as well.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin was 39.3% in Q2 FY27 and 40.1% in H1 FY27
items.quote: Consolidated, you know, if you look at the figures, we are at the range which we normally operate in. Even in this quarter, we were at 39.3, you know, against 40.1 on a half-yearly basis.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin was 36.6% in Q2 FY27 and 38.1% in H1 FY27, within normal 38-41% range
items.quote: On a standalone basis, quarter two was 36.6, but on a half-yearly basis, it stands at 38.1. We normally operate in the range of 38 to 41, as far as gross margin is concerned, so it is well within that range.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin dropped to 10.8% in Q2 FY27 vs 14.4% in H1 FY27 due to Rang bana rahe campaign spend
items.quote: In quarter two, the EBITDA dropped to 10.8% versus 14.4% for the half-yearly position. Our guided range is 15 to 17, so at the end of half-year, we are at 14.4, which is close to that.

items.statement: October saw highest sales growth in 25-30 months; festive demand shifted to Q3 due to later Diwali
items.quote: October was the month when we had the highest, you know, sales growth in the last possibly 25, 30 months. So, therefore, you know, festive season looks good.

items.statement: Decorative volume growth 3% in Q2 FY27, 5.6% in H1 FY27; value growth 11.9% Q2, 12.3% H1
items.value: 3% vol Q2, 5.6% vol H1, 11.9% val Q2, 12.3% val H1
items.quote: Volume growth, 3%, and on the half-yearly basis, if you look at it, it is 5.6%. This is stand alone. Value growth, 11.9%, and half-yearly basis, 12.3%.

items.statement: Industrial business delivered robust high double-digit volume and value growth across segments
items.quote: In industrial performance, we delivered robust high double-digit volume and value growth.

items.statement: Industrial price hikes recovered ~90% of targeted increase by end-November, balance 10% by December
items.quote: We have been able to pass on, partially the price increase, you know, and some more price increases we have got in the month of October. Some we are planning to get in November as well, hoping that, you know, we will be recovering almost 90% of the increase that we want at the end of November.

items.statement: Completed Hindukur plant expansion; evaluating new West Bengal incentive policy for Panagar investment; planning Orissa factory
items.quote: We just, completed the expansion in our Hindukur plant. Today, the West Bengal government has announced a new industrial incentive policy. We will take a look at it and then decide to the scale of investment that we want to make in Anagar. Which is in

items.quote: Retail store network is at 2,000 plus, as on half-year financial year 2027. In tinting machines, we added 4,800 machines as of first 6 months, and during the quarter, we added 2,700 machines.

This was a planned inventory

items.statement: Market share stable at ~20.2% in H1 FY27 vs 20.3% earlier; new entrant raised prices to industry level but increased rebating
items.quote: We are at the end of half one. We are more or less at the same level at which we were earlier. At that, we were earlier at 20.3, we're still at about 20.2 at the end of half year.

items.statement: Home seal segment outperformed with roof coolant seal and dam shield as key drivers; wood coatings strong double-digit growth; differentiated products outperformed
items.quote: The home seal segment continued to outperform, with roof coolant seal and dam shield emerging as key growth drivers. Wood coatings registered strong double-digit value growth

items.statement: Launched waterproof tile adhesive (first in India), decorative panels (tech from Bolix), Long Life Parapet Coat, Dam Shield with 3-year warranty
items.quote: Some interesting new products which we introduced in this period. One is the waterproof tile adhesive. It's a unique tile adhesive introduced by us for the first time in India, which is waterproof by nature. The second is, you know, decorative panel, which we sell in good quantities in, Poland, France, UK.

items.statement: Urban market share low (7-8% in Bangalore, lower in Pune/Mumbai) vs 20% all-India; MEGA strategy experiment yielding positive results, to accelerate from April FY28
items.quote: For example, in Bangalore, we may have only 7-8% market, right? You know, in Pune or Mumbai, we may have even lower market share. So, it is, for us, it is a huge opportunity that is there to improve our market share.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth 13.2% Q2, 12.5% H1; operating profit growth 5.2% Q2, 11.1% H1; PAT growth 5.2% Q2, 19.3% H1
items.quote: Consolidated results, as we look at it, you know, total income from operations. 13.2% was the Revenue growth? Operating profit growth at 5.2%, and PAT growth also at 5.2%. Half-yearly basis, you know, total income from operations, 12.5%. Operating profit growth at 11.1%, and PAT growth at 19.3%.

items.statement: Standalone revenue growth 11.9% Q2, 12.3% H1; operating profit -4.4% Q2, +6.1% H1; PAT -7.3% Q2, +13.2% H1
items.quote: On a standalone basis, if you look at the results, you know. 11.9%, largely driven by gross margin compression. Pbdit minus 4.4%. And PAT is minus 7.3%. In terms of the half-year result, you know, it stands at 12.3% revenue growth. Operating profit growth at 6.1%, and pad growth at 13.2%.

items.statement: Raw material price volatility makes gross margin recovery timing uncertain; competitive intensity remains with new entrant rebating
items.quote: prices are so volatile, it's difficult to say that, I mean, how they will fluctuate month on month. Of course, we have a lag between the consumption and it converting into the COGS, cost of goods sold.

items.statement: Consolidated sales growth guidance for FY27 revised to 15% excluding Foskor and AWUKO
items.quote: In the last earnings call, we revised this earning the sales increase to 15%, and we maintain the revised guideline.

items.statement: Consolidated Ceramics sales growth guidance revised upward to 25-28% for FY27
items.quote: Consolidated Ceramics, we initially communicated a growth of 15% to 15.5%. In the last earnings call, we revised this to 23% to 25%. We further now revise upward to 25% to 28%.

items.quote: Considering the standalone margin drop in H1, the cost pressures, we expect the full year margin to be 8% to 8.5%, excluding AWUKO.

items.statement: Consolidated Ceramics margin guidance for FY27 raised to 22.5-23.5%
items.quote: Consolidated Ceramics margins were expected to be 20.5% to 21% as per the last guidance. We expect this to go up to 22.5% to 23.5%.

items.statement: Consolidated Electrominerals margin guidance retained at 9-9.5% for FY27
items.quote: Consolidated Electrominerals margins were expected to be 9% to 9.5%. In FY '26, the reported margin was 5.6%. If we exclude Foskor Zirconia loss, it would be 9.1%. I retain the same guidance.

items.statement: Capex guidance retained at INR 400 crores consolidated for FY27
items.quote: We retain the capex guidance of INR 400 crores at consolidated level.

items.statement: Semiconductor equipment components revenue potential INR 300-350 crores by FY30-31
items.quote: We expect the top line from this segment could be somewhere in the range of about INR 300 crores to INR 350 crores.

items.statement: RHODIUS expected to reach break-even by Q1 FY28
items.quote: So we feel that step one is that they should get to a break-even by Q1 of next year, and that's the first step that we are looking at.

items.statement: Strong demand across industrial activities, construction, and infrastructure-led demand driving Abrasives growth
items.quote: The growth is aided by growth in industrial activities, construction, and infrastructure -led demand, new geographical coverages, new product introductions, and better go-to-market initiatives from our team.

items.statement: Ceramics demand strong across all three regions: India, Americas, and Australia
items.quote: Ceramic growth was driven in all the 3 regions, that is India, Americas, as well as in Australia.

items.statement: Electrominerals demand strong from refractory and abrasive customers both domestic and exports
items.quote: Strong demand from refractory and Abrasive customers both in India and abroad helped achieve this growth.

items.statement: Standalone Abrasives PBIT dropped 19.9% YoY due to higher fuel and input costs not fully passed on
items.quote: Abrasives cost of manufacturing went up due to higher fuel prices, increase in input costs such as phenol, resins arising out of oil price increases. We could pass on a very small portion of the cost increase to the market. This resulted in a drop in margins.

items.statement: Standalone Ceramics PBIT grew 48.2% YoY to INR 67 crores
items.quote: Ceramics PBIT was INR 67 crores compared to INR 45 crore, marking a growth of 48.2%.

items.statement: Standalone Electrominerals PBIT grew 49.1% YoY to INR 29 crores
items.quote: Electrominerals, PBIT was INR 29 crores compared to INR 20 crore, marking a growth of 49.1%.

items.statement: Consolidated Ceramics PBIT grew 62.1% YoY to INR 101 crores
items.quote: Ceramics PBIT, in Q2 FY '27, consolidated Ceramics PBIT was INR 101 crores compared to INR 62 crores in Q2 FY '26, a growth of 62.1%.

items.statement: Consolidated Abrasives PBIT grew 20.8% YoY to INR 40 crores
items.quote: At the consolidated level, Abrasives PBIT was INR 40 crores in Q2 FY '27 compared to INR 33 crores in Q2 FY '26, marking a growth of 20.8%.

items.statement: Standalone Abrasives margins bottomed out, targeting 15% trajectory
items.quote: So yes, the answer is the margins is bottomed out is my view. These are specific issu es that we are facing largely because of the sudden cost increases, particularly on the phenolic resins, all the oil -based products, and that cost, and of course, you don't stock these items much

items.statement: Strong project orders in Refractories business driving Ceramics growth
items.quote: The project orders are also pretty strong, and that is how we are seeing at this point in time.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex spend INR 127 crores vs INR 162 crores last year
items.quote: Capex for H1 FY '27, we spent a capex of INR 127 crores compared to last year INR 162 crore.

items.statement: INR 66 crores already invested in semiconductor equipment components for anchor customer
items.quote: I think you had mentioned a capex of about INR 66 crores that we have already incurred for our anchor customer.

items.statement: Total semiconductor investment could scale 3-4x current investment
items.quote: You had also flagged that the total investment would scale up to about 3x to 4x of whatever we have already invested.

items.statement: Thin wheel facility established in Hosur, qualification with 6-7 major international customers underway

items.statement: Export duty withdrawal on Chinese imports helping Indian abrasives competitiveness
items.quote: It's a welcome thing as far as the Indian manufacturers are concerned. So we see that it's a good step from our point of view, and that could also play a role in the growth.

items.statement: Chinese competition continues but improving due to export duty withdrawal and strong dollar
items.quote: As far as Chinese competition is concerned, continues to be definitely be affected by the Chinese competition. It is getting better because of this export duty benefit withdrawal, plus the strong dollar and weak rupee.

items.quote: If you see that the volume, the sales growth is pretty high, and these are happening when you look at the September month sales, and that gets collected in October and So, what happens, suddenly there is a surge. That should get reversed, and we should get it. The second is the normal inventory going up, which is also typical of you need to prepare yourself for a higher growth in H2, so you need t

items.quote: Yes. I think your observation is correct, and this should get reversed in H2, is our view. We are also working towards this.

items.statement: Consolidated debt INR 362 crores, cash INR 251 crores, net debt INR 111 crores, debt-to-equity 0.09
items.quote: Cash and debt position, consolidated debt was at INR 362 crores and cash was INR 251 crore. This is excluding cash at VAW, leaving a net debt of INR 111 crore. Consolidated debt-to-equity ratio is at 0.09.

items.statement: AWUKO closure proceeding with asset sale for INR 5.34 crores and employee settlement completed
items.quote: As part of the closure process, AWUKO Abrasives entered into agreements in October '26 for the sale of all its property, plant, equipment, and inventory for an aggregate consideration of INR 5.34 crores. AWUKO has also entered into a reconciliation of interests and social plan with all its employees in accordance with applicable German labor law requirements.

items.statement: Foskor Zirconia exit expected to complete in Q3 FY27
items.quote: Let me say that realistically think that we can complete it in this quarter.

items.statement: Standalone sales grew 28% YoY to INR 911 crores in Q2 FY27, highest ever quarterly sales
items.quote: In Q2 FY '27, standalone sales was INR 911 crores compared to INR 712 crores. This is a growth of 28%. This is the highest ever quarterly sales reported, as well as I think 14 quarters, the quarter-on-quarter growth is pretty high.

items.statement: Consolidated sales grew 13.1% YoY to INR 1,455 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: In Q2 FY '27, consolidated sales was INR 1,455 crores compared to INR 1,287 crores in Q2 FY '26. This is a growth of 13.1%.

items.statement: Consolidated PBT grew 22.9% YoY to INR 138 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: In Q2 FY '27, consolidated profit before exceptional items and tax was INR 138 crores, which is a 22.9% growth compared to INR 113 crores in Q2 FY '26, and a growth of 16% compared to INR 119 crores in Q1 FY '27.

items.statement: VAW Russia status quo remains with no volume improvement expected
items.quote: The status quo predominantly remains the same. No specific update. We continue to operate at the same level of constraints, and that is what currently is continuing.

items.statement: No specific tax incentives available for new age businesses under new tax codes
items.quote: No. there is no specific program tax benefit currently being made available. If you see the new tax codes, they have dispensed with many of these incentives. We are all at the normal tax rates. So there is no specific benefit that we are enjoying.

items.statement: Management expects FY28 EBITDA of INR 1,800-2,200 crore driven by cost levers, operating leverage, and Zone IV ramp-up
items.quote: So we have talked about the three focus areas that are important for us to achieve that trajectory in our previous calls and we remain on track on execution of all of those initiatives under these three areas.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA reached record Rs 418 crore, up 44% YoY; H1 FY27 EBITDA up 58% to Rs 802 crore
items.quote: Q2 FY27 EBITDA increased by 44% year-on-year reaching Rs. 418 crore. Our H1FY27 EBITDA increased by over 58% to close at over Rs 802 crs, as against Rs 507 in H1FY26.

items.statement: Zone IV target is INR 250-350 crore bottom line in first 18 months; aspiration to be EBITDA additive in FY28
items.quote: From a margin standpoint, in the first 18 months, our target is to achieve INR250 crore to INR350-odd crore of bottom line from Zone IV, and I think we continue to push for that aspiration.

items.statement: Pass-through mostly on absolute basis; percentage margins compress in high RM price environment but absolute contribution protected
items.quote: I think typically, our pass-throughs are on an absolute basis, not on a percentage basis and that is where in an inflationary scenar io of significantly higher RM prices, sometimes the percentage might get impacted, while the absolute EBITDA or absolute contribution on the product remains relatively concrete

items.statement: Non-Energy demand tailwind steady and strong across domestic and global markets; NCB demand very strong, DCB second half strong, NT chain developing downstream markets
items.quote: I think the demand tailwind both in domestic as we ll as in the global market in Non-Energy application remains very steady and strong, and we can go value chain by value chain

items.quote: The gasoline-naphtha crack, it was very robust. It was $20-plus per barrel, if I look at last quarter. So overall, demand remained quite robust.

items.statement: Signed 10+ year manufacturing and supply agreement with global specialty chemical major with ~Rs 1,500 crore revenue potential; commercial operations targeted FY29
items.quote: On October 13, 2026, we also entered into a dedicated 10+ year manufacturing and supply agreement with a global specialty chemical major, representing a revenue potential of ~Rs. 1,500 crore.

items.statement: Augene Chemicals JV trial production underway; order book gaining traction; steady-state revenue projected at Rs 300-400 crore
items.quote: On the Augene Chemicals JV (Partnership with Superform), the facility is ready with the trial production which is underway, while the orde r book is gaining traction. Commercial production is expected to commence soon, with steady-state revenue projected at Rs. 300-400 crore
