items.quote: Our product portfolio continues to expand across energy, agrochemical intermediates, advanced polymer formulations, and pharma building blocks, supported by our planned FY27 CAPEX of Rs. 700 crore to Rs. 800 crore.

items.statement: Zone IV to introduce 5-10 products in FY27, expanding to 20-25 products across 5 chemistry blocks by FY28; remaining 4 chemistry blocks online within FY27
items.quote: In Zone-IV, we plan to introduce 5 to 10 products in FY27, expanding to 20 to 25 products across 5 different chemistry blocks by FY28. The remaining 4 chemistry blocks are expected to come online within this financial year.

items.statement: Fuel Additives capacity expanded from 290 to 360 KTPA in Q1 2026; running at near full capacity in Q2
items.quote: In Fuel Additives, the capacity utilization remained strong in Q2 following our expansion from 290 KTPA to 360 KTPA in the first quarter of 2026.

items.statement: DCB debottlenecking to 140 KTPA aligned with downstream PDCB demand; NCB capacity expansion under evaluation due to elevated utilization
items.quote: For DCB, the capacity debo ttlenecking to 140 KTPA rema ins aligned with downstream PDCB demand. ● With current NCB asset utilization remaini ng elevated, the capacity expansion initiatives are under evaluation by the management team

items.statement: MMA running at almost full capacity in Q2; focus on stabilizing at current capacity and integrating value chain before further expansion
items.quote: I think in the second quarter, we ran almost at full capacity.

items.statement: Raw material prices surged: Sulphur up 5-6x, elevated freight costs; pass-through with lags in some segments (AgChem quarterly contracts); acid value chain unable to fully pass through sulphur inflation
items.quote: Almost all of our raw materials saw significant price increase, while RMs such as Sulphur saw prices surge by over 5-6x, combined with sharply elevated freight costs, strained global supply chain economics.

items.statement: In Agrochemicals, quarterly contracts create one-quarter lag in price pass-through; other long-term arrangements also have delayed impact
items.quote: In many of the segments, for example, in Agrochemicals, we have quarterly contracts, right. So there is a lag of quarter when it comes to pass-through of the pricing.

items.statement: Elevated RM prices stretched working capital; net debt over Rs 4,650 crore; optimized to 55-60 days working capital; forward booking contracts to minimize inventory risk
items.quote: Elevated RM prices have also stretched our working capital requirements over the past two quarters, pushing our net debt to over Rs. 4,650 crore and leading to higher finance costs.

items.statement: Inventory on waters roughly INR 800-1,000 crore at any time; margins accrue to P&L only on delivery; working capital days optimized to 55-60 days
items.quote: Given the size of the business that we are running at any given point in time, we roughly have anywhere between INR 800 crore to INR 1,000 crore worth of inventory on the waters for which we have to account for margins as they get accrued to the P&L only when the material is delivered to the customer.

items.statement: Board approved enabling resolution to raise up to Rs 1,000 crore for deleveraging, strengthening balance sheet, and long-term flexibility beyond FY28-29; approved by shareholders in EGM Oct 31, 2026
items.quote: To strengthen our balance sheet, support long-term growth, and optimize our capital structure, the Board, on October 1, 2026, approved an enabling resolution to raise up to Rs. 1,000 crore by way of various avenues and/or any combination of fund raise.

items.statement: Enabling resolution approved for up to Rs 1,000 crore fund raise via various avenues; primary objective deleveraging and balance sheet strengthening
items.quote: The primary objective of this capital raise is to deleverage our balance sheet, strengthen our financial position, an d build long-term flexibility to support strategic growth initiatives beyond FY28, FY29

items.statement: Energy segment ~50% of revenue in Q2; medium-term expectation to settle at 30-40% as Zone IV ramps up and pricing corrects
items.quote: We expect the energy to settle somewhere between 30% to 40% kind of a range of our overall portfolio and especially as the Zone IV ramps up pans out, many of the products coming out of that site as well as revenue getting contributed will balance the overall portfolio.

items.statement: Long-term contracts currently 25-30% of business; aspiration to increase share; fixed costs well covered including inflation in most contracts
items.quote: Usually, it is around 25% to 30% of our business that comes through some of these long-term partnerships. We hope the share of that will go up going forward as we do more and more such partnerships.

items.statement: Active conversations with global majors for long-term partnerships in personal care, flavors & fragrances, batteries, defense; one 10+ year agreement signed with revenue potential ~Rs 1,500 crore
items.quote: We have seen very good traction when it comes to inbound inquiries to do long-term partnerships for specialty chemical manufacturing in India to serve markets in Europe, in Japan, in U.S.

items.statement: PDA chain facing huge overcapacity and dumping by Chinese players; evaluating alternative use of capacity; NCB chain benefited from China's anti-involution strategy and VAT rebate removal
items.quote: No, we see huge overcapacity and dumping by some of the Chinese players for this particular product in the global market.

items.statement: MMA competition exists but Aarti has opened new geographies and customers; market size not well established; focus on end-market affordability and octane booster demand
items.quote: It is difficult to quantify that number, to be ho nest, because the market it self is not very well established in terms of absolute size

items.statement: China's anti-involution strategy and VAT rebate removal (up to 13% of product price) dramatically improved NCB chain; similar policy change in PDA could drive turnaround
items.quote: The biggest lever for there was China's anti-involution strategy, which impacted NCB chain, right, where we removed the VAT subsidy rebates that Chinese players used to get, which was as high as 13% of the product price.

items.statement: Europe becoming sensitive to Chinese imports; FTA trends with Western markets creating opportunities; inbound inquiries for long-term partnerships from Europe, Japan, US increased
items.quote: Europeans becoming very sensitive with respect to Chinese imports coming into the region and that, coupled with FTA trends of Indian sort of market with some of those Western markets is creating very interesting opportunity for us.

items.statement: H1 FY27 PAT grew 117% to Rs 324 crore from Rs 149 crore; Q2 PAT Rs 169 crore up 60% YoY
items.quote: While on the half yearly basis, our H1FY27 PAT grew by 117% to Rs 324 crs from Rs 149 crs in last year

items.statement: Effective tax rate for FY27 expected between 15-20%; deferred tax liabilities to kick in as new assets commercialize
items.quote: We will be somewhere between 15% to 20%. As the new assets get commercialized, there will be the element of deferred tax liabilities which will start kicking in.

items.statement: Revenue Q2 FY27 Rs 3,887 crore, up 73% YoY; H1 FY27 revenue growth driven by volume gains and input price pass-through
items.quote: Revenues in Q2 FY27 were at Rs. 3,887 crore, an increase of 73% over Q2 of last year.

items.statement: Trading volume ~Rs 500 crore in H1 FY27 done to build market for expanded capacities; partially contributed to lower margins
items.quote: There is a trading volume. I think for the full firs t half, it was roughly around INR500 crore and that was done in anticipation to build the market for our expanded capacities

items.statement: Methanol availability not a challenge but pricing volatile linked to Middle East; Aniline supply challenges from China, developing diversified supplier network including Europe; one of largest merchant buyers of Aniline for non-MDI usage
items.quote: Methanol has not been a challenge from an availability point of view. Typically, we have been able to source whatever volume we need. Our pricing, of course, remains quite volati le linked to Middle East situation

items.statement: Inventory loss risk remains top priority; forward booking product contracts to match RM pricing; risk cannot be fully eliminated due to import/export heavy business
items.quote: We are trying to ensure that to whatever extent possible, forward book some of the product contracts to ensure that wherever we have booked the raw material that pricing is passed on to our customer.

items.statement: R&D efforts shifting from Zone IV commercialization to next-generation platforms; 50+ GenAI use cases executed last quarter; partnering with strategic customers on R&D
items.quote: As we are going through a commercialization phase for Zone IV, now the R&D efforts have shifted towards the new generation platform. We are making interesting progress and we would; and this time, we are also doing a lot of R&D in partnership with our strategic customers.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance maintained at 14-16% and EBITDA margin guidance at 22-23%
items.quote: In earlier quarters, we have given that -- earlier quarter, we have given guidance that overall growth guidelines was almost around 12% to 13%, which was revised to 14% to 16%. So tha t would remain. And consolidated EBITDA margin guidelines was from 22% to 23%, that will also stand there

items.statement: Medium-term consolidated EBITDA margin improvement of 1-1.25% per year and standalone EBITDA improvement of 1.5% per year
items.quote: Every year, we should be improving by almost around 1% to 1.25% of EBITDA on a consolidated basis. And Ipca EBITDA will grow by almost around 1.5% stand-alone EBITDA.

items.statement: Domestic formulation business grew 14% YoY to INR1,157 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our domestic formulation business for Q2 FY '27 has delivered growth of around 14%, and it has reached to around INR1,157 crores as against IN R1,019 crores in Q2 FY '26

items.statement: Export formulation business grew 32% YoY to INR653 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: On export formulation business, on a stand-alone basis, Ipca has grown by 32% in Q2 FY '27 to around INR653 crores as against INR493 crores in Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Pain segment grew 14% in H1 FY27 to INR1,216 crores and 16% in Q2 FY27 to INR628 crores
items.quote: Overall, for, let's say, April to September, if you look at -- our pain segment has grown by around 14% from 1,000 internal numbers from 1200 -- from I NR1,065 crores to around INR1,216 crores. So we have -- is continuously growing at 14 % for the first half of the current year. And in fact, in the second quarter -- this quarter of t he current financial year, on pain segment, we have grown by aro

items.statement: Pain franchise expected to continue 14-15% growth for next 3-4 years from current INR1,500 crores umbrella brand
items.quote: And in fact, from current INR1,500 crores of umbrella brand, we are looking similar kind of growth to continue for next 3, 4 years, yes.

items.statement: Pain segment volume growth 8-9% and price growth 4-4.5%
items.quote: Volume-led growth may be almost around 8% to 9% and price growth may be around 4% to 4.5%, yes.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 22.97% in Q2 FY27 from 21.68% in Q2 FY26 despite input cost increases
items.quote: In spite of all these factors, overall consolidated EBITDA margins have improved to around 22.97% in Q2 FY '27 as against 21.68% in Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 26.6% in Q2 FY27 from 25.46% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Stand-alone EBITDA margin of Ipca has improved to 26.6% in Q2 FY '27 as against 25.46% in Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Unichem EBITDA margin at 11.3% in Q2 FY27 impacted by INR30 crores extra freight costs
items.quote: Let's say, Unichem has delivered almost around 11.3 % kind of EBITDA margin in current quarter. I think overall because of freight increase, the freight was significantly increased in this particular quarter. And freight numbers almost arou nd INR30 crores extra has gone in this quarter

items.statement: Unichem EBITDA margin may range 11-13% if high freight and energy costs persist
items.quote: But if your freight and all th ese cost -- energy costs and it remains high, maybe it may remain between 11% to 13% kind of thing, EBITDA margin

items.statement: Unichem gross margin around 58% may vary 1-2% due to input cost fluctuations
items.quote: It may be 1% or 2% here and there vary because input costs are fluctuating too much, yes.

items.statement: Institutional business H1 FY27 at INR236 crores, full year may reach INR325-340 crores vs INR300 crores guidance
items.quote: It will certainly exceed because, say, what this IN R25 crores was never taken into account on guidance. So maybe it may become INR325 crores, INR330 crores, INR340

items.statement: Branded business in ROW markets grew 19% YoY to INR172 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our promotional branded business in ROW markets has delivered growth of 19% for Q2 FY '27 to around INR172 crores against INR145 crores in Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Generic market excluding tender grew 36% YoY to INR364 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Generic market, excluding tender, delivered around 36% growth in Q2 FY '27 to around INR364 crores as against INR268 crores in Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: US portfolio growth 9% in dollar terms; Ipca portfolio 74% growth to $5.8M, Unichem portfolio $38.5M in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Overall, let's say, U.S. in dollar terms, if you lo ok at overall portfolio growth is almost around 9%. And Ipca's portfolio is, let's say, value growt h is almost around 74% in dollar terms. So I think Ipca's portfolio, I think, for the quarter ha s given almost around $5.8 million of sale. And Unichem's portfolio is almost around -- has become $38.5 million for the quarter

items.statement: European generic business grew 23%, Australia/NZ 24%, US 31%, Canada 45%, South Africa 46% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Overall, generics-wise, if you look at in Q2, European business has grown by around 23%. Australia and New Zealand has grown by around 24%. U.S. has grown by 31%. Canada has grown by 45%. South African business has grown by 46%.

items.statement: UK business returned to profitability after INR2.5M loss last year due to portfolio rationalization
items.quote: But because of that kind of scenario, there are lots of disturbance in U.K. market today that a lot of products are going in short supplies and all. An d prices are returning back because situation of selling product at lower price cannot continue f or long. So that has changed and the -- our European -- U.K. subsidiary has also delivered prof it in this year

items.statement: Pisgah subsidiary will take more time to improve; API order positions good, expected to improve by next financial year
items.quote: Let's say, except one subsidiary, which is Pisgah, all subsidiaries have done well. And they are all in profit, yes. Pisgah will take some little mo re time because there are good order positions on their API side. And so maybe I think by next financial year, things will start improving

items.statement: Significant price increases on inputs, logistics, shipping, fuel and energy costs in Q2 FY27
items.quote: For Q2 FY '27, we continue to see significant price increase on inputs, logistic cost, shipping cost and even fuel and your -- energy cost.

items.statement: Foreign currency debt fully repaid; only INR155 crores rupee term loan remaining, expected to reduce to INR70-75 crores by year-end
items.value: INR155 crores, reducing to INR70-75 crores
items.quote: So right now, we have only a very small borrowing of around INR155 crores or so on rupee term loan, which probably at the year-end would be -- we will close by around INR70 crores, INR75 crores.

items.statement: Company effectively debt-free with INR700 crores cash against minimal debt; not prepaying low-cost rupee loan
items.quote: So -- and practically, we are debt-free company bec ause we are getting almost around INR700 crores cash in books and debt are hardly any. That debt also, we are not prepaying because that debt is contracted at very low rate compared to the current market rate of what we are realizing on deploying money in mutual funds and all

items.statement: Interest cost run rate of INR12 crores per quarter will decline in H2 FY27
items.quote: Yes, yes, it will decline. Yes, it would decline, yes.

items.statement: Domestic market share improved to 2.11% in MAT September 2026 from 2.09%
items.quote: MAT September 2026, Ipca's rank remained 16 as per IQVI A. Our market share has improved to around 2.11% from -- as against 2.09% in September '26

items.statement: Chronic segment growth 20% vs IPM 17% in MAT September 2026; acute segment growth 11% at par with market
items.quote: As per IQVIA, the -- on chronic segment MAT September 2026, Ipca has achieved a growth of a round 20% as against IPM growth of around 17%. As per IQVIA, the acute segment, Ipca has achieved a growth of around 11

items.statement: Zerodol SP rank improved to 8th from 11th in Q2 FY26; Zerodol umbrella brand crossed INR1,500 crores, 4th largest in IPM
items.quote: Out of to p 6 brands, Zerodol SP is the top brand of the company, and it has improved its rank to 8th rank as against 11th in the Q2 FY '26. Zerodol as the umbrella brand has crossed INR1,500 crores sales as per IQVIA in September 2026. It has become the fourth largest brand in IPM

items.statement: Branded business guidance of 15-16% growth maintained for India; H1 grew 22% except West Asia decline of 3%
items.quote: So we maintain our guidelines of 15% to 16% growth overall in India.

items.statement: Freight costs significantly increased with air shipment percentage rising from 5-6% to 25% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Air percentage of overall has gone up almost in this quarter to around -- from 5%, 6% to around 25% -- so that has taken almost around INR30 crores out of the freight expenses out of EBITDA that has gone.

items.statement: Brazil business was loss-making in first two quarters but started delivering profit in Q2 FY27
items.quote: The Brazil till now, they were incurring losses for first 2 quarters of the current financial year. That has started delivering now the profit.

items.statement: Management expects growth in FY27 and FY28 but declines to provide a specific range or number.
items.quote: I think 2027 will grow and then 2028 will also grow , but yes, I do not think we are precise enough to go into more clarity there.

items.statement: Capex outflow in H1 FY27 was Rs.261 Crores; three-year capex guidance indicated at approximately Rs.1,700-1,800 Crores.
items.quote: Our capex outflow during the first half of FY 2027 was Rs.261 Crores

items.statement: Module 1 peptide facility capex ~Rs.250 Crores; Module 2 configuration to be finalized in next 3-6 months.
items.quote: I think so far we spent maybe around Rs.250 Crores just for Module 1, so you can probably do some approximate math.

items.statement: Commissioned new peptide block (Module 1) at Unit One; planning to inaugurate new process R&D center at Genome Valley, Hyderabad, fully operational by early next year.
items.quote: We have commissioned our new peptide block at Unit One, which has seen encouraging traction and has given us greater confidence and visibility as we plan the next modules of our peptide expansion.

items.statement: Acquired ~134 acres of land at Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh for future expansion; first right of refusal on additional ~60 acres, potential total ~200 acres over next two years.
items.quote: During the quarter, we took another long-term step through the acquisition of approximately 134 acres of land at Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh.

items.statement: RFP activity in current financial year is the strongest to date; steady flow of new proposals; commercial NCEs to drive near-term growth.
items.quote: One development that has been particularly encouraging is the level of RFP activity that we have seen in this financial year, and it has been the strongest to date.

items.statement: Made meaningful headway establishing relationships with big pharma; diversification of customer base a priority; several proposals from sustained efforts to build new customer relations.
items.quote: We have made meaningful headway in establishing relationships with big pharma, and we are continuing to make steady progress in this direction.

items.statement: FY26 was first year with CMS revenues exceeding GDS; increasing CMS contribution expected to remain important part of evolution.
items.quote: FY 2026 was the first year where we actually had greater revenues contributing from CMS in comparison with GDS.

items.statement: Filed 2 DMFs (Fezolinetant and Ivacaftor) in H1 FY27, strengthening GDS portfolio.
items.quote: We have filed 2 DMFs during this period one is Fezolinetant and the other is Ivacaftor, strengthening our GDS portfolio.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 gross margin 59.4% vs 60.1% in Q2 FY26; EBITDA margin 22.9% vs 30.4% YoY; input cost increases and geopolitical volatility cited.
items.quote: Gross margin for the quarter stood at 59.4 % compared to 60.1% in Q2 FY2026.

items.statement: Increase in input costs in H1 FY27 due to geopolitical environment and conflicts causing raw material price volatility and freight/logistics cost escalation.
items.quote: During the first half of the financial year, we also experienced increase in input costs.

items.statement: Working capital at 104 days of sales in Q2 FY27 vs 84 days in previous quarter; focus on inventory management, collections, and aligning with business scale.
items.quote: Working capital for the quarter stood at 104 days of sale compared to 84 days in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Free cash flow for H1 FY27 stood at Rs.99 Crores; net debt negative Rs.208 Crores (net cash position).
items.quote: free cash flows for the period stood at Rs.99 Crores while net debt stood at negative Rs.208 Crores.

items.statement: Peptide demand rising globally; synthetic peptides between IND and commercial doubled from 500 (Jan 2025) to 1,000 currently; India peptide capacity still low vs demand.
items.quote: The same number in Jan uary 2025 it was only 500, so the world of drug discovery and development is also changing

items.statement: Lumpiness inherent due to few large commercial molecules; shipment timing shifts cause quarterly revenue variability; patent expiries for key molecules not expected before 2030.
items.quote: Molecules can progress differently from initial expectations, customer timelines can move, and the increasing value of individual commercial shipments can amplify the impact of timing movements between quarters.

items.statement: Staff costs increased in Q2; further headcount additions planned for R&D center and peptide/manufacturing sites.
items.quote: Certainly, there will be certain additions in terms of our headcount to cater one in the regular R&D but also on a longer note there will be additions not only at the R&D center, but also at the manufacturing site for the peptides or other APIs.

items.statement: Peptide PPQ-related revenues expected in 6-9 months; MSA/commercial supply agreements to follow 6-9 months after successful validation; commercial peptide revenues ~1.5-2 years away.
items.quote: Maybe 6 to 9 months away, Chirag, to see like PPQ-related revenues coming from peptides.

items.statement: GLP-1 euphoria creating global peptide overcapacity risk, especially in China; players with only equipment but no R&D capabilities may face challenges when customers leave.
items.quote: There will be some testing and then again there will be a correction and I think that happens in any thriving industry and I expect the same with peptides as well.

items.statement: Specialty segment muted due to customer manufacturing difficulties; expected to normalize by Q4 FY27 with revenue recovery from key products.
items.quote: We expect that the thing will be done probably by Q4 we should be able to start seeing more revenues from the products , which contribute significantly both to the topline as well as the bottomline from those specialty products.

items.statement: Key commercial CMS molecules have patent protection in meaningful markets until at least 2030; peptide inflection and new molecules expected to offset any post-2030 revenue dip.
items.quote: In terms of the patent cliff for these molecules which are key, I think in the meaningful markets and markets which contribute significantly to our customers, we do not see any expiries happening before 2030.

items.statement: Board approved additional land acquisition to expand Unit I footprint; Kakinada investment may be modulated/slowed if commercial business impacted.
items.quote: Our Board had today approved investment to add some more land , which will expand our Unit I footprint.

items.statement: AI-driven drug discovery may increase early-stage candidates but not seen as direct threat; Neuland focuses on IND onwards development and GMP manufacturing where AI cannot replace physical process work.
items.quote: We do not see a direct threat of AI taking away our work because most of our work is actual work that goes into generating material or designing and demonstrating a process that generates material.

items.statement: Work on hand dipped from $4.5 million to $4.2 million QoQ, but October bookings brought it back above end-June levels.
items.quote: See, the work at our hand has dipped a bit from about $4.5 million last quarter to around $4.2 million now. But in the month of October, we have record bookings again, and the number is now better than what it was at the end of June.

items.statement: Structural steel detailing contributes 80-82% of revenue (~$4.4M of $5.3-5.4M), with the rest from fixed MES teams and minimal BIW (~$100K/quarter).
items.quote: I can tell you roughly 75-80% of the revenue is coming from structural steel detailing and those areas. And in the overall, $5,400,000 -- I think $5,300,000, $4,400,000 has come from civil structural work. That's almost 80% -- 80-82%.

items.statement: Utility services team ramped from 30-40 to 70-75 people, targeting 120 by March 2027; training 40-45 more engineers.
items.quote: Utilities, we are ramping up very rapidly from a team of 30-40 people last year. We are already 70-75 and planning to ramp it up to 120 people by March next year because it's very difficult to build up these skill sets.

items.statement: US power distribution demand surging due to data centers; utility services have fixed committed demand for 110-120 engineers.
items.quote: The power distribution demand across the country has improved, gone up by several times, demanding more and more engineering work required in that domain. So, from a small team of 30-40 people last year, today, we are around 70-80, and we have demand for beyond 120 people, and that too on a fixed committed basis.

items.statement: Actively evaluating acquisition of a structural design firm to complement civil/land development entry; previous target not yet finalized due to concerns on scalability.
items.quote: We had a good conversation with the prospective seller. We're also studying into their line of business and their ability to ramp up. So, we have a few concerns which we have expressed to them, and we are waiting for their reply. I don't say that we have made any confirmed decision on that. It is still liquid, but we are still looking at other options also.

items.statement: Beryl acquisition integration progressing: design head placed, 6-engineer Hyderabad team supporting $1M Hillsborough County design order; targeting breakeven in Q3 FY27.
items.quote: This $1,000,000 Hillsborough County order what we received two months ago is predominantly designed. So, it is now -- timing is good, that what can be handled through our design team, which is centered with our six engineers.

items.statement: Beryl expected to turn profitable from FY28; Q2 loss narrowed to $25K from $70-75K, targeting breakeven in Q3.
items.quote: Q3 Beryl is just little below the breakeven. They had a small loss of about $25,000, which has come down compared to the previous quarter, which was $70,000 to $75,000. So, it's now $25,000 loss in Q2. And, hopefully, in Q3, we look forward to it crossing the breakeven.

items.statement: New civil/land development domain launched with leading US client via MOU; work expected to start end-November, meaningful contribution from Jan-Feb 2027.
items.quote: That is the area we along with Beryl are tying up. Already tied up an MOU with the client, and the work has to really take off from November end. So, hopefully, when we meet next time in February, March, I'll be able to share more details.

items.statement: Forex gain of INR 70 lakhs in Q2 vs INR 1.5 crore gain in Q1; rupee stabilizing around 95/USD expected to yield gain in Q3.
items.quote: In fact, Forex gain-forex loss is around INR 70 lakhs in this quarter compared to INR 1.5 crores gain in the last quarter. So that means if you effectively take away the forex element, the profit growth compared to Q1 is much better.

items.statement: No major recruitment or infrastructure investment planned; growth to be driven by efficiency, automation, and project-driven hiring only.
items.quote: So, there is no need for huge recruitments going forward. That will be client driven or project-to-project driven. We don't want to now create a situation like in BIW where we entered three years ago, built up a huge team and could not find the proper work for them for the last two years.

items.statement: Secured 3-year fixed-team MSA with leading plant engineering company for 25 utility engineers; currently staffed 10-15, ramping to full by Dec 2026.
items.quote: It is a fixed team arrangement. And in fact, the team is still under buildup. We have -- again, it's 25 people they wanted. We have only 10 to 15 people currently being offered, and we are in the process of ramping up.

items.statement: Connection design revenue targeting $1M in FY27; exploring acquisition to accelerate structural design capability.
items.quote: The connection design is still improving. We are in line with our expectation of reaching about a million dollars in this year. And we are also looking at opportunities for acquisition in the design field, structural designing.

items.statement: Key risk is US construction demand slowdown; mitigated by expanding from 2% high-rise niche into 10-20x larger residential/civil market via Beryl.
items.quote: If suddenly US stops growing or they don't go into manufacturing or the civil industry -- construction industry gets into a non-negative trajectory, that could probably be the only thing which can impact our performance. That too marginally, because when such a thing happens also, US will continue to grow at least at 2-3%.

items.statement: US outsourcing demand structural due to core engineering talent shortage; no choice but to outsource civil/mechanical engineering.
items.quote: Everybody now in USA has no choice but to outsource, especially in core engineering like civil, there's no civil engineers coming out in US in numbers they require. Core engineering of mechanical, core engineering of civil, even AI or anything, there will be increasing demand only.

items.statement: BIW headcount cut from 155-160 to ~50; further 5-10 reductions possible; retraining 20-25 engineers for poles/towers.
items.quote: The BIW has been brought down from 155-160 people to hardly 50 people now. And that team is having moderate work, so we are also really looking into whether any further reduction is required. Maybe another 5-10 resources if they're found to be redundant.

items.statement: Poles/towers utility services growth visibility for 5-10 years driven by data center power infrastructure; current 70-75 engineers vs 120+ demand.
items.quote: Some of the contractors and utility managers are telling me in my trip to US recently that they are expecting growth in the next 5 to 10 years to continue because of the several data centers that are coming up across USA and substations and power lines have to be drawn and they are to be created in the next 5 to 10 years.

items.statement: Targets 3,000+ keys and ARR ~Rs 8,000 by FY30 under KHIL 3.0 vision
items.quote: Our footprint will expand from 10 states to 11 states. Our portfolio will expand from 24 to 31 properties. Inventory will increase from 1900 plus keys to 3000 plus keys. ARR we are targeting at portfolio level, a 33% lift from existing 6000 to around 8000.

items.statement: Expects to cross Rs 130-135 cr EBITDA in FY27 and cumulative Rs 750 cr over next five years
items.quote: If you look at our cumulative EBITDA for next five years, it will be in the range of Rs. 750 crores. Now, my debt is at zero. By this year end, we will be net zero debt company.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 26%, up 1300 bps YoY; H1 margin 28%
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 26%, a massive 13% point expansion. This is the operating leverage which is at the best.

items.statement: H2 FY27 demand outlook robust; Q2 driven by corporate at business hotels and leisure at resort properties
items.quote: Outlook looks very promising. The demand is expected to be robust. And as I said earlier, we will show heightened revenue and EBITDA growth in H2 as compared to previous H2.

items.statement: Invested in EV fleet (100% electric) and electric kitchens to reduce fuel cost volatility
items.quote: Electrifying our hotels is one of the main where we have EV cars. We are the first in the industry to adopt EV cars for our hotel fleet. And today we are at 100% all EV cars within our organization.

items.statement: Gwalior (lease) and Dwarka, Nashik (management) opening Dec-Jan adding 250-266 keys; Rishikesh, Dehradun in pipeline
items.quote: We have in the month of December, January, Gwalior, which will open up. Apart from that, we also have Dwarka and Nasik. Though they are under management, Gwalior is under lease. But Dwarka under management, we expect that these properties also will add a lot of boost adding more than 250, 266 keys to our portfolio.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 31 cr (0.23x EBITDA) at Sep-26; repaid Rs 30 cr to Axis Finance post quarter; targets net zero debt by FY27 end
items.quote: As of 30th September 2026 our gross debt was Rs. 96 crores. Cash and cash equivalent was Rs. 65 crores and net debt was Rs. 31 crores. Now if you look at net debt to EBITDA it was 0. 23x versus 0.52x as of last quarter, more than halved in just one quarter. And from 0.52 we are at 0.23 and we did not stop there. Subsequent to quarter end we have repaid Rs. 30 crores loan to Axis Finance Limited.

items.statement: Pays 6% royalty to promoter entity Plaza Hotels for Mumbai hotel land; interest-free deposit of Rs 60 cr (1994) + Rs 20 cr; evaluating merger to eliminate royalty
items.quote: We consider it once, can this be amalgamated both so that the royalty component goes away and promoters get incremental shares. We are still evaluating that, but it is not in the interest of minority shareholders. But again, we will look at it.

items.statement: ADR flat ~3% YoY in Q2; occupancy rose 50% to 58%; RevPAR up 20%; rate hikes to follow occupancy gains
items.quote: Our ADR growth was flat around 3%. But our occupancy has grown from 50% to 58% at portfolio level. So higher the occupancy, higher revenue and excluding the variable cost everything flows into EBITDA.

items.statement: Lease model requires 80-100+ keys for viability; management model flat 6% of revenue, minimum 35-40 keys; GST structure hurts small hotels
items.quote: We need basically properties which are in the range of 80 to 100 for us to take on particularly lease. On particularly lease. Because today, especially because of GST and the way GST is structured, the cost of GST has again gone back to the old VAT days where the cost of VAT was a cost.

items.statement: Same-store revenue up 31%, EBITDA up 98%, margin 27% (+900 bps) in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Now with these adjustments our revenue was up 31% same store basis to Rs. 85 crores. EBITDA up 98% to Rs. 23 crores almost doubled. And EBITDA margins were at 27% up 90 0 bps a 9% point jump.

items.statement: Pipeline of ~620 keys across 7 properties; actively negotiating in existing states; disciplined asset-light expansion
items.quote: a current pipeline of almost 620 keys across seven properties. And this is, what is the visibility on adding further properties beyond this pipeline? And what are the key markets and destinations that you are prioritizing for the expansion

items.statement: Expects Rs 600 cr post-tax cash over 5 years and ~Rs 1,000 cr capacity including debt headroom for growth

items.quote: Our EBITDA margin stood at 20.8%, while PAT falls at 16.7%. EBITDA and PBT grew QoQ, even with annual wage increase in Q2.

items.statement: 70% of annual revenue is recurring/backlogged; 40-50% of new deal value recognized in first year
items.quote: In any given year whatever revenue numbers that you see, 70% of it is recurring or backlogged. That is, I open my account with a recurring set, and then the balance comes from the new orders that we win in the year.

items.statement: Partner Ecosystem Management (PEM) product modernized and winning deals; AI agent squads (FraudZap) closed in 90 days
items.quote: We are modernizing it. We are adding newer features to it, and market has responded quite well to it, actually. So our strategy is to push a lot more time into the market.

items.statement: Three technical POCs closed successfully in last quarter; converting to commercial deals; active conversations with several customers for AI agents
items.quote: So we have been able to do three technical POCs and demonstrate that we met all the exit criteria successfully. Where it is right now? The sales team is sort of making it into a commercial arrangement.

items.statement: R&D expensed through P&L, not capitalized; R&D intensity increased annually
items.quote: R&D of course, you know R&D we do use – R&D increased expense. We do actually increase the, or I would say increase intensity of R&D every year, but that does not flow through the balance sheet.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents INR 198 crores at quarter end vs INR 184 crores previous quarter
items.quote: Cash and cash equivalents stood at now INR 198 crores as of quarter end, as against INR 184 crores at the end of previous quarter.

items.statement: Actively running inorganic growth pipeline; primary cash utilization for acquisitions
items.quote: So our cash utilization, we will be looking at some inorganic growth opportunities, the first utilization of cash that we are looking at. We are actively sort of figuring this out.

items.statement: Buyback not possible due to negative retained earnings; ESOP trust to buy shares from market spaced out
items.quote: In terms of buybacks, we can't do a buyback right now, because I think all of you on the call are aware that we have negative retained earnings. So we cannot do a buyback right now, actually.

items.statement: AI SDLC delivering 14-15 features per sprint vs 10 previously; HyperSense deployment timeline reduced 15-20%
items.quote: What we have seen is that we have been able to do 14, 15 features. So our ability to do it more has actually become much better with AI SDLC.

items.statement: Revenue INR 85.59 crores, up 7.7% QoQ and 24% YoY; five consecutive quarters of QoQ growth
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter stood at INR 85.59 crores against INR 79.45 crores for the previous quarter. This reflects a 7.7% growth.

items.statement: INR depreciation benefit ~2-3% QoQ, ~8-10% YoY; constant currency growth lower
items.quote: Our INR benefit is around, I would say, a 2% or 3%. And YoY be around 10% or maybe 8% -- QoQ, it's been flat, actually, so yeah.

items.statement: Architecture of Autonomy (AOA) with modular independent agent stacks; interoperable with telco AI stacks (Snowflake, Databricks, DataRobot)
items.quote: We are trying to move towards, architecture of autonomy. We call it, you know, AOA, where we want to make sure that everything that we are doing, we are able to qualify our agents to do that.

items.statement: Jio building own stacks per prospectus; limited India opportunity; consolidation among PEM competitors opening market share
items.quote: If you read the Jio prospectus, which we did, it actually explicitly says that they will do their own stacks. They will maintain their own stack. They will build their own stack.

items.statement: Plan to publish investor meeting schedule with UI; resume NDRs post silent period; maintain or increase engagement momentum
items.quote: We definitely plan to continue this, and we are working with UI, actually, on a plan. So maybe we'll publish a plan you know, and to the investors, so that you know which are the cities that we are coming to.

items.statement: Middle East geopolitical volatility and US elections as wildcards; baked into planning; no major execution challenges expected
items.quote: I think Middle East is one impact, and of course, US and elections are always, I don't know, a wildcard. How that plays out, it remains to be seen.

items.statement: FDA inspection at Gagillapur concluded with 11 observations, none on data integrity or cross-contamination
items.quote: The U.S. FDA conducted a cGMP inspection of the facility from October 19 to October 30. This was the first FDA inspection since the warning letter issued in February '25, following the 2024 inspection. The inspection concluded with a Form 483 containing eleven observations.

items.statement: Observations relate to investigations, change control, process qualification, visual inspection and documentation
items.quote: Based on our assessment, none of the observations relate to data integrity, cross -contamination or facility upkeep. They concern investigations, change control, process and recruitment qualification, visual inspection controls and documentation practices.

items.statement: No impact on manufacturing or distribution; comprehensive response within 15 business days
items.quote: There is no impact on manufacturing or distribution of products from this site. We will submit a comprehensive response within the stipulated 15 business days detailing our corrective and preventive actions.

items.statement: Management does not give formal revenue guidance but expects current growth trajectory to continue
items.quote: As you know, we don't give guidance, but all I can tell you is our current rate of growth and the current progress we are making will continue. There will be no change in that.

items.statement: Revenue grew 20% YoY to INR15,600 million, crossing INR15,000 million quarterly revenue for first time
items.quote: Revenue grew 20% year-on-year to INR15,600 million, crossing INR15,000 million in quarterly revenue for the first time in our history.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 21% YoY to INR3,376 million; EBITDA margin 21.6%, up 19 bps YoY, down 131 bps QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA was INR3,376 million, up 21% year -on-year and stable quarter-on-quarter. EBITDA margin stood at 21.6%, up 19 basis points year -on-year and down 131 basis points quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin 64.4%, down 134 bps YoY and 126 bps QoQ due to higher input and freight costs from West Asia conflict
items.quote: margin stood at 64.4%, down 134 basis points year -on-year and 126 basis points quarter -on-quarter. The moderation primarily reflected higher input costs arising from the ongoing conflicts in West Asia, partly offset by lower cost safety inventory carried into the quarter in U.S.A

items.statement: Engaging customers to pass on input and freight cost increases with a time lag
items.quote: We continue to monitor input costs and freight costs closely and are engaging with the customers to pass on increases wherever possible, although with a time lag.

items.statement: Complex generics share at 47% of formulations revenue; medium-term target 50%+
items.quote: our medium path we guided is 50% of our formulation portfolio will be around complex generics. So quarter-on-quarter, a few basis points here and there is expected, but we will have to see year-on-year basis. And I would say we are ahead of what we have stated. And proba bly we will be doing more than 50% in the medium term

items.statement: 3 potential sole first-to-file ANDAs filed (DYANAVEL XR, Sodium oxybate ER, Ruxolitinib ER); several more targeted over next 6-7 quarters
items.quote: Over the last 3 quarters, we have announced filings for 3 potential sole first-to-file ANDAs, generic DYANAVEL XR or Amphetamine-based extended-release OTT, Sodium oxybate ER and Ruxolitinib ER. Several more such products are under development with filings targeted over the next 6 to 7 quarters.

items.statement: 26 ANDAs pending approval providing strong pipeline for next wave of launches
items.quote: Alongside these opportunities, we have 26 ANDAs awaiting approval, providing a strong pipeline for the next wave of launches.

items.statement: 5 US launches planned in H2 FY27, including 2 controlled substance extended-release products
items.quote: But in total, we have about 5 launches within the next 2 quarters. 3 launches are -- well, all of them are in the U.S. market. 2 products are controlled and the other products are uncontrolled, but we have non-controlled. We have 5 products coming up.

items.statement: Capex INR1,304 million in Q2 FY27; INR2,000 crores growth capex planned over next 3-4 years for peptide CDMO, US platform, oncology and API expansions
items.quote: Capex was INR1,304 million compared with INR890 million in Q1 FY27 and INR2,112 million in Q2 FY26. We continue to strengthen our manufacturing and packaging capabilities.

items.statement: INR2,000 crores capex over 3-4 years for peptide CDMO expansion in Zurich and India, US platform, oncology and API capacity
items.quote: This INR2,000 crores growth capex over the next 3 - 4 years will be largely into one , expansion of infrastructure and capacity for peptide CDMO both in Zurich as well as India. And other capex will be going towards U.S. platform, enhancing the manufacturing capability and overall distribution. Third is on oncology side, where we have certain plans of launches.

items.statement: Gagillapur capacity utilization ~75%; Genome Valley ~25%, expected to cross 50% by Q4 FY27
items.quote: Tushar, the current capacity utilization are similar what it was earlier, which we said around 75% is what we are using

items.statement: Genome Valley utilization ~25%, expected to cross 50% by Q4 FY27
items.quote: So Genome Valley is under 25% or roughly 25% as of now, which we are expecting by Q4, it will cross 50%.

items.statement: Net working capital to sales 30%, stable vs 29% in Q1 FY27 and Q2 FY26; cash conversion cycle 231 days vs 229 days
items.quote: Net working capital to sales was 30% compared with 29% in Q1 FY27 and 29% in Q2 FY26 and remained stable in this range.

items.statement: Operating cash flow INR650 million vs INR3,874 million in Q1 FY27 due to planned working capital increase for growth
items.quote: Cash flow from operation was INR650 million compared with INR3,874 million in Q1 FY27 and INR1,937 million in Q2 FY26. This was mainly due to a planned increase in working capital to support the business growth.

items.statement: Net cash position INR8,280 million vs net debt INR1,012 million in Q1 FY27 after warrant proceeds receipt
items.quote: We closed the quarter with a net cash position of INR8,280 million compared with net debt of INR1,012 million in Q1 FY27. Receipt of balance proceeds of warrants moved us into a net cash position, strengthening our balance sheet and supporting growth, capacity expansion and R&D.

items.statement: R&D expenses INR885 million (5.7% of sales), up 26% YoY, focused on CII, ADHD, oncology, MUPS, complex formulations
items.quote: R&D expenses were INR885 million about 5.7% of sales, up 26% year-on-year and 1% quarter-on-quarter. R&D is the engine of our transformation from a volume led to a value -led innovation-driven company.

items.statement: ROCE 17.6%, up 138 bps YoY, broadly stable QoQ despite working capital and capex investment
items.quote: ROCE was 17.6%, up 138 basis points year -on-year and broadly stable quarter -on-quarter compared with 18%. This improvement was achieved even as we continue to invest in working capital and capex to support our next phase of growth.

items.statement: Senn Tides peptide CDMO: H1 revenue INR109 crores, cumulative EBITDA loss INR28 crores; targeting EBITDA to PAT neutrality in H2 FY27
items.quote: With the revenue that you projected will be somewhere between an EBITDA neutrality to the PAT neutrality, depending -- it largely d epends on the kind of product/project mix that we do. We are hopeful to close near our stated ambition and all the key to that lies in our smooth Q4 executions, where the offtakes are the maximum from the customer

items.statement: Senn Tides Zurich site completed Swiss medic GMP inspection with no critical findings; strong RFP/RFQ inflow in recent months
items.quote: During the quarter, Senn Chemical site in Zurich successfully completed its Swiss medic GMP inspection with no critical findings and acceptable GMP compliance status. This reflects a meaningful progress in strengthening our quality system and regulatory capabilities compared with previous inspection 2 years ago.

items.statement: Senn Tides: theranostics project revived; renewed engagement with 2 major peptide CDMO players; India Vizag facility planning underway
items.quote: A theranostics-reated pharmaceutical project has been revived after nearly 2 years, driven by progress in its clinical development. We have also renewed engagement on supply partnership with 2 major peptide CDMO players and initiated discussions for a second-year manufacturing campaign with another CDMO partner following successful delivery last year.

items.statement: FDA warning letter remediation completed except 2 CAPAs; new observations not related to original warning letter items
items.quote: The FDA -- the remediation plan was completed except for 2 CAPAs. And like CMD mentioned, I think even in the press release, we did not get any observations on the points that were stated in the warning letter.

items.statement: FDA response timeline ~90-100 days; EIR with VAI/NAI expected, then 30-90 days for approvals of pending applications
items.quote: Tushar, typically, it takes about -- it should be about 90 to 100 days for response, but it all depends how things go.

items.statement: 9 applications pending from Gagillapur; 2 already transferred to US facility; no on-site re-inspection believed required
items.quote: And Giovganne, let me also add here, it's 9 that are filed from there. But out of that, 2 are already transferred to our U.S. facility out of 8. So actually, we don't need to get those approvals here. They will be -- continue to made in U.S.

items.statement: US controlled substances market share #3; maximizing quota utilization and earnings per kg
items.quote: Market share depends product to product, but we are #3 in the U.S. with respect to controlled -substances.

items.statement: Remediation expenses to moderate significantly from Q4 FY27; Q3 similar to Q2
items.quote: Second question with respect to remediation expenses, Q4 onwards, it will moderate significantly. Q3 also will be similar to Q2.

items.statement: Freight costs increased due to West Asia conflict; cost pressures continuing, working on price pass-through
items.quote: In other expenses, the significant increase in the current quarter is freight cost, which has gone up because of the West Asia conflict. The freight rates of the shipments have gone up.

items.statement: Warrant proceeds receipt moved company to net cash position; cash to fund organic and inorganic growth
items.quote: You are absolutely right. That is also the intent when we have raised this money. So currently, we have a good amount of cash, which will be used for both organic growth as well as inorganic growth.

items.statement: Global expansion filings: ~8 filings in last 6 months across geographies for short to mid-term revenue
items.quote: We've started filing a few products around the world. We've done about 6 filings in the last -- no, about 8 filings in the last 6 months. These are the products that will give us midterm revenues -- short to midterm revenues.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to stay in H1 FY27 range (~34%)
items.quote: For this year itself, for FY27, just to be clear, we are going to be working on the margins that you see for the first half in the same sort of range for the year.

items.statement: Annual capex framework INR700-1,000 cr; FY27 capex ~INR700 cr
items.quote: our capex frame will be in the INR700 crores to INR1,000 crores every year. INR700 crores this year is what we are looking at given where we are.

items.statement: HFO contract with Solstice extended 4 years to Dec 2032; adds ~USD180 mn revenue potential
items.quote: The tenure of our existing HFO supply contract with Solstice Advanced Materials has been extended by 4 years until December 2032 and will have an additional revenue potential of approximately USD180 million.

items.statement: CDMO order book visibility near USD100 mn target; Phase 2 cGMP-4 (INR125 cr) operational by Q4 FY27
items.quote: we are at the striking distance of our USD100 million target in terms of order book visibility. And so there will be growth for that business too by the end of this year.

items.statement: CDMO Phase 2 cGMP-4 capex ~INR125 cr, operational by end Q4 FY27; peak revenue potential 3x capex ~INR900-1,000 cr by FY28-29
items.quote: Phase 2 of the cGMP-4 facility involving a capex of approximately INR125 crores is progressing as planned and is expected to become operational by the end of Q4 FY27.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 34.2%, up 367 bps YoY; Q2 EBITDA margin 34.2%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA grew by 69% to INR765 crores, with margins expanding by 367 basis points to 34.2%.

items.statement: AHF plant utilization improving, not yet at full capacity; MPP debottlenecking commissioned Sep 2026; R32 plant commissioning shortly
items.quote: Our new AHF facility has witnessed an improvement in utilization, contributing to our growth momentum and R32 capex is progressing as planned and remains on track for commissioning shortly.

items.statement: HFC pricing firm, realization improved sequentially; HF merchant sales exceed plan, placed internationally; pricing pass-through in HFO contracts
items.quote: The pricing environment for HFC remains firm, with realization improved on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals targeting INR350 cr run rate; 5 new molecules with campaign orders through FY27+; Nectar ramp to 60-65% PAR in FY27, balance FY28
items.quote: I think, probably in the last 2, 3 quarters, where we've consistently said that this business will become more like a INR350 crores business.

items.statement: Advanced Materials incubated as new vertical; target 10-15% of expanded revenue by 2030; focus on data centers, electronics, semiconductors, defense
items.quote: if you think of Navin from now to 2030 and look at 20% to 25% growth, Advanced Materials will be roughly about 10% to 15% of the expanded pie by 2030.

items.statement: Deepening engagement with European CDMO major; existing molecules seeing positive trial results; expanding in oncology, cardiovascular, neurology, animal health
items.quote: Our engagement with leading European CDMO major continues to deepen, driven by increasing demand for an existing molecule and expanding role in the customer supply chain.

items.statement: Net operating working capital days 72 in H1 FY27, within financial framework (70-75 days target)
items.quote: our net operating working capital days stood at 72 days, which is within our financial framework.

items.statement: EBITDA conversion 60-65% sustainable; capex funded internally; strong balance sheet supports INR700-1,000 cr annual capex frame
items.quote: we are able to generate an EBITDA conversion of 60% which 60 %, 65% on a more sustainable basis.

items.statement: Interim dividend declared INR8 per equity share (face value INR2)
items.quote: I am also pleased to share that the Board has declared an interim dividend of INR8 per equity share with a face value of INR2 per share.

items.statement: H1 FY27 PAT INR513 cr (+93% YoY), EPS INR100; Q2 PAT INR269 cr (+81% YoY)
items.quote: Profit after tax also increased to INR513 crores, a growth of 93% year -over-year. Our EPS stood at INR100

items.statement: Signed 1200 MW solar PPA with NTPC Renewable Energy and floated 500 MW/2000 MWh tender for long-term renewable power procurement
items.quote: In the last quarter, we have signed 1200 megawatts of solar PPA with NTPC Renewable Energy and have floated 500-megawatt / 2000 megawatt-hour for procurement of long-term power in the renewable energy space.

items.statement: Expect power prices to remain firm during peak hours due to renewable penetration and low storage capacity
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect power prices to remain firm particularly during peak demand hours, morning and evening as the increasing penetration of renewable energy continues to reshape the power supply mix.

items.statement: No volume guidance provided for Q3 or full year FY27
items.quote: Right now we do not have any numbers for the guidance. We do not see any dramatic change in the situation which is currently there.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 trading margins: short-term 0.69 paisa/unit, medium-term 3.17 paisa/unit, cross-border 6.98 paisa/unit, long-term 7.98 paisa/unit, overall 2.89 paisa/unit
items.quote: For the quarter, the short-term margin is 0.69 paisa per unit. For medium term it is 3.17 paisa per unit. For cross border trade it is around 6.98 paisa per unit. For long term trade it is 7.98 paisa per unit. Moderator: And the overall trading margin? Pankaj Goel: Overall trading margin per unit is around 2.89

items.statement: Net surcharge income fell from Rs 42 crore to Rs 26 crore due to improved DISCOM liquidity and reduced receivables
items.quote: Net surcharge income from Rs. 42 crore to Rs. 26 Crores roughly, it has gone down. If you look at it, it also indicates better management of the receivables.

items.statement: Cash and bank balance of Rs 2,431 crore as of 30 September 2026
items.quote: Cash on hand on 30th September is Rs. 2,431 crore.

items.statement: PFS disinvestment process on track with transaction advisor appointed; no fixed timeline due to regulatory approvals
items.quote: Regarding PFS disinvestment, as we have already informed in our previous earning calls also, we have initiated the process. We have appointed transaction advisory consultant. And in the due course of time, we will be sharing the news as developments happen.

items.statement: JV with NLC formally started; business plan formulation underway but connectivity delays may push execution beyond 2-3 years
items.quote: Actually, I mean JV has now formally started working and the first meeting of their Board of Directors has happened. Yesterday and today itself we have had a series of meetings with the concerned counterparts of the NLC. We are in the process of formulating a viable business plan and we hope to take those things forward.

items.statement: Mineral exchange initiative leverages existing C&I relationships and exchange-setting experience; five minerals including iron ore targeted initially
items.quote: The thought process is twofold. Number one, I mean, all the minerals which are traded, so they are also basically big power consumers also. We already have a portfolio of 500, 600 big C&I, meaning commercial and industrial consumers in our book.

items.statement: Mineral exchange to be regulated by Indian Bureau of Mines; HPX market share capped at 5% if PTC trades on it
items.quote: Regulatory is Indian Bureau of Mines. So obviously, this is going to be a regulated entity and will have to follow all the rules.

items.statement: Dividend practice remains annual; no interim dividend expected soon after recent special and final dividends
items.quote: So basically, it has always been our practice to declare the dividends only once in a year. We hope to follow that practice. I do not see any dramatic change in the status and since recently we had declared one very special dividend and also we have paid previous year's final dividend.

items.statement: PFS book well-provisioned with no hidden NPAs; market price discount not reflective of asset quality
items.quote: Vivek, the question that you asked, one, we are talking about market price. So on that we don't comment. But as far as NPAs goes, it is only what you see disclosed in our books. So it is a well-provisioned book. There are no surprises.

items.statement: Mineral exchange capex manageable given cash position; open to partnerships for the platform
items.quote: Third thing is whether we can put up some money in it. So, given the cash position and our current balances strength, we can definitely support this exchange insofar as CapEx part is concerned.

items.statement: Cross-border operations stable with Bangladesh; 1200 MW winter supply contract signed with Bhutan; import/export commenced with Nepal
items.quote: In the cross-border markets, our operations continue across all three-grid connected neighboring countries which is Bhutan, Nepal and Bangladesh. Energy flows to Bangladesh remain stable under the agreed contractual framework with regular flow of payments to our accounts.

items.statement: Trading volumes grew 18% YoY to 58.25 BUs in H1 FY27 vs 10.64% energy generation growth
items.quote: During the first half of this Financial Year '26-'27, while total generation of energy grew by 10.64%, our trading volumes actually grew by more than 18% to 58.25 billion units.

items.statement: Diurnal price variation from <Rs 1/unit to Rs 10/unit ceiling due to <20 GWh storage; storage additions expected in 12-18 months to moderate peaks
items.quote: With installed energy storage capacity still below 20 gigawatt-hour, the power market is witnessing significant diurnal price variation ranging from less than Rs. 1 per unit to regulatory ceiling of Rs. 10 per unit.

items.statement: Guidance to reduce total debt by Rs. 500 crores in FY27
items.quote: Debt during H1 FY27 is reduced by Rs. 126 crores, and we maintain our guidance of reduction in total debt by Rs. 500 crores for FY27.

items.statement: Gross debt expected at Rs. 1,670-1,700 crores by end of FY27
items.quote: And at the gross level, if you look at somewhere around Rs. 1,670 crores to Rs. 1,700 crores will be the number.

items.statement: Aim to reduce Rs. 300-400 crores debt in FY28
items.quote: And for next financial year, we aim to reduce Rs. 300 crores to Rs. 400 crores of debt for the next financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 18.23% in Q2 FY27 from 13.5% in Q2 FY26 and 17.96% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The EBITDA margin improved to 18.23% for the quarter compared with 13.5% in Q2 FY26 and 17.96% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Aspiration to cross previous peak EBITDA margin of 20-21% but not in next 1-2 quarters
items.quote: And I think margin right now, our aspiration is to cross the previous peak of the margin. I think we are slowly getting there, but I don't think it is going to happen in next quarter or the quarter after that.

items.statement: Expect 30-50 bps EBITDA margin expansion per quarter
items.quote: And you have seen in past couple of quarters, the margin expansion, 30 basis points to 50 basis point margin expansion is there every quarter. And I think we will continue to work on that.

items.statement: Revised FY27 capex guidance to Rs. 550 crores for entire group
items.quote: And I think we should be ending this year close to around Rs. 550 crores throughout our entire group.

items.statement: JV investment of Rs. 50-55 crores pending, Rs. 15-20 crores in H2 FY27
items.quote: JV still about RS. 50 crores, RS. 55 crores investment is pending. This will be done in next one year time. So partly will go in this year, maybe Rs. 15 crores, Rs. 20 crores more in the next half, rest will be the next financial year.

items.statement: New order wins of Rs. 673 crores in Q2 FY27 with 4-year program life
items.quote: During the quarter, the company secured new order wins worth Rs. 673 crores across CV, EV, LV and Farm Equipment segments. These orders have a program life of approximately 4 years and further strengthen our revenue visibility over the coming years.

items.statement: Casting orders of Rs. 447 crores including Rs. 272 crores for North America LV exports
items.quote: Worth mentioning against the new order wins, Rs. 447 crores comes from the casting side of our business, against which Rs. 272 crores is for the North American export market for light vehicle applications.

items.statement: Aluminum forging capacity at 3,000 tons with >50% utilization
items.quote: Sir, if I'm correct, for aluminum forging our current capacity is 3,000 tons, right? Milesh Gandhi: Right, sir.

items.statement: Casting capacity sufficient for new orders, no immediate capex needed
items.quote: In terms of capacity addition, I will only be able to say right now, we have enough capacity. In terms of when we plan to do any capex, whatever it is, in the next financial year.

items.statement: Railway wheels JV: 300 wheels ready for inspection, trial supply in Nov, 2,000-3,000/month from Dec, 4,000-5,000/month by Q4
items.quote: We are expecting 20,000 to 25,000 wheels in this financial year to be supplied to railways.

items.statement: FY28 expected to be strong in both domestic and international markets
items.quote: I think in FY28, we are looking at a strong market. So, both in domestic and both in international market and FY28 is going to be a strong market.

items.statement: Strong visibility and very strong market for next 6 months
items.quote: We see strong visibility and a very strong market in next 6 months.

items.statement: Shipping cost net impact Rs. 8-9 crores in Q2 FY27, partially passed to customers
items.quote: And the impact on this quarter on the shipping cost is around Rs. 8 crores to Rs. 9 crores to th e company, net impact

items.statement: Domestic steel price hikes fully passed on; export markets only pass on local steel price increases
items.quote: Commodity pricing every quarter, we have been able to pass on in the domestic market. In export market, in contract to contract, it differs. And region to region, it differs.

items.statement: Expect another steel price hike in India in January, prepared to pass on to customers
items.quote: But in terms of our commodity estimates, we believe that in India, there is going to be another steel hike maybe in January. And I think we are well prepared to pass on the increase to our customers.

items.statement: Passenger vehicle segment to contribute 10%+ growth by CY28/FY29
items.quote: We are looking at almost in the next 2 years by CY28 or FY29 basically, we are looking at almost 10% plus growth to come in from passenger vehicles.

items.statement: ROCE target 12-15% by end of FY27, aspiration for 20% in FY28
items.quote: By the end of FY27, we will be in the range of 12% to 15% on ROCE.

items.statement: Railway wheels JV target EBITDA margin 18-20% at optimum utilization
items.quote: So, at the optimum utilization, we can achieve around 18% to 20% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Net working capital increased Rs. 140 crores in value but days stable; shipping delays causing inventory/debtor build-up
items.quote: So, if you look at the cash flow, there is a net increase in inventory and debtors in terms of value and that is net of the creditors, there is a net increase of about RS. 140 crores in terms of net working capital. But if you look at the number of days, we are almost there what we are having in March.

items.statement: Working capital days to improve in upcoming quarters
items.quote: We will say we will improve it. We are working on improving these numbers, and you will see some improvement in working capital levels in upcoming days.

items.statement: Finance cost to reduce by ~Rs. 40 crores annually with Rs. 500 crore debt repayment at 8% interest
items.quote: See, finance cost will go down if we reduce the entire Rs. 500 crores of debt by almost Rs. 40 crores per annum, okay? So, it's about 8% interest cost we are paying right now.

items.statement: New North America casting order from new customer and new product line for passenger vehicles
items.quote: This is a new customer addition and new product. Sahil Sanghvi: Possible to share what product is this? Naresh Jalan: No, I think that's not possible, but we can very safely say it's basically LV business, you can say it is a passenger vehicle business, and it's a new customer and new product line

items.statement: Export growth driven by new product launches, not vendor replacement
items.quote: No, we are not replacing any vendor. Basically new businesses which are coming in basically are new product launches, which are happening in due course. And we are part of those new launches.

items.statement: No major inquiries from UK FTA; Europe FTA still pending EU approval
items.quote: No, I think with the current FTAs of U.K., we are not seeing any major inquiries or anything. I think Europe FTA is still to be approved by the European Union.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues and shipping costs remain key monitorable risks
items.quote: Currency movements, rising input costs as well as a sharp rise in shipping costs also rem ain key areas to monitor

items.statement: Shipping costs settled at peak but may increase further depending on geopolitics
items.quote: It has largely settled down right now at the peak. But in case there is any further increase, we will have to go back to the customer and speak to them. But right now, there is no incremental increase we are seeing in terms of the shipping cost. But we cannot say. I think it all depends on how the geopolitical issues keep in and out.

items.statement: Aerospace business progressing well, targeting engine and frame forgings directly with OEMs
items.quote: me answer you. It's not that we are going forward with any Tier 1, Tier 2s. We are in discussion directly with OEMs. And currently, the components which we are aiming at is from the engine Q2 & H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call Transcript 23 side, but at the same time, frame components are also being explored together

items.statement: Power demand grew 15% YoY in H1 FY27, with peak demand up 14.5% and non-peak up 9.5%; October demand grew 21% YoY
items.quote: The country recorded year-on-year growth of about 11% in power generation and about 15% in power demand during the first half of the current fiscal year.

items.statement: Peak demand reached 271 GW and non-peak 253 GW in H1 FY27; July saw peak demand increase ~50 GW and non-peak ~34 GW
items.quote: The maximum demand met during the period was 271 gigawatts for peak demand and 253 gigawatts for non-peak demand.

items.statement: NTPC Group installed capacity reached 91,506 MW as of H1 FY27; added 2,398 MW in H1 (NTPC 196 MW, NGEL 1,136 MW, others 1,066 MW) plus 162 MW in Oct 2026
items.quote: As on H1 FY27, NTPC Group's installed capacity stood at 91,506 megawatts. We have added 2,398 megawatts of capacity, out of which NTPC is 196 megawatts, NGEL Group is 1,136 megawatts and other group companies have added 1,066 megawatts.

items.statement: FY27 capacity addition target revised to ~8 GW (from 9.5 GW) due to renewable transmission delays; FY28 target 9.6 GW (1,460 MW thermal, 444 MW hydro, 7,735 MW RE); FY29 target 10.9 GW (3,070 MW thermal, 7,807 MW RE)
items.quote: Yes, the NTPC Group, the earlier expectation was 9.5 gigawatts, which we are scaling it down, based on the dispensation on the renewable side. So it would be now close to 8 gigawatts.

items.statement: Plans to tender ~4.8 GW new thermal capacity (800 MW each at Jhabua Stage 2, Talcher Stage 4, Bhilai, BRBCL Stage 2; 1,600 MW at Talcher Kaniha Stage 3) largely in Q1-Q2 next year; estimated capex INR 67,000 cr
items.quote: we have plans for tendering out close to 4.8 gigawatts further. This will be l argely from Q1 and Q2 of the next year. This will comprise of 800 megawatts at second stage of Jhabua . There will be another 800 megawatts from Talcher Stage 4. Then Talcher Kaniha Stage 3 will have 2 units of 800, which would become 1,600. Bhilai, we are planning a single unit of 800. And BRBCL Stage 2 will be 800. So

items.statement: 37 GW capacity under construction: 17 GW coal, 3.6 GW hydro, ~16 GW renewables
items.quote: With over 37 gigawatts of capacity under construction, including 17 gigawatts of coal-based capacity, about 3.6 gigawatts of hydro and around 16 gigawatts of renewables, our immediate focus is on timely project execution and maintaining maximum availability of power stations.

items.statement: Standalone PAT Q2 FY27 INR 5,320 cr (+14% YoY); H1 FY27 INR 10,662 cr (+13% YoY); Adjusted PAT H1 FY27 INR 10,469 cr (+17% YoY)
items.quote: NTPC's profit after tax for Q2 FY27 is INR 5,320 crores as against INR 4,653 crores in the corresponding quarter of previous year, registering a growth of 14%.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT H1 FY27 INR 14,247 cr (+26% YoY); Consolidated adjusted PAT Q2 FY27 INR 7,152 cr, H1 FY27 INR 13,917 cr
items.quote: PAT for group for H1 FY27 is INR14,247 crores as against previous year INR11,334 crores, an increase by 26%.

items.statement: NGEL consolidated revenue H1 FY27 INR 2,045 cr (+58% YoY); Operating EBITDA INR 1,818 cr (+60% YoY); EBITDA margin 89%
items.quote: consolidated revenue from operation increased by 58% to INR 2,045 crores in H1 FY27, while Operating EBITDA grew by 60% to INR1,818 crores as compared to H1 FY26. EBITDA margin remained at 89%.

items.statement: Coal stock at stations 5.2 MMT (7 days requirement); captive coal dispatch grew 21% to 26.13 MMT in H1 FY27; tenders issued for 13 MMT coal for H2 FY27 from alternative sources; awarding 4 MMT additional domestic coal
items.quote: Presently, we have 5.2 MMT of coal stock at our stations, sufficient for 7 days of coal requirement. Despite supply constraint from CIL and Singareni Collieries Company Limited. dispatches from our captive mines grew by nearly 21% in H1 FY27.

items.statement: Group capex H1 FY27 INR 23,932 cr vs INR 23,115 cr in H1 FY26; standalone capex INR 14,398 cr vs INR 14,149 cr; gross PP&E increased 11% to INR 4,85,444 cr
items.quote: in H1 FY27, we have incurred a group c apex of INR23,932 crores as compared to INR23,115 crores in H1 FY26, while on a standalone basis, NTPC has incurred c apex of INR14,398 crores in H1 FY27 as compared to INR 14,149 crores in H1 FY26

items.statement: Loan agreement USD 750M executed May 2026 with SBI, HDFC, BoB (IFSC Gift City); availed RBI concessional USD-INR swap for USD 450M; weighted avg interest rate on borrowings 5.72% in H1 FY27 vs 5.98% in FY26
items.quote: The weighted average interest rate on borrowings during H1 FY27 stood at 5.72% compared to 5.98% in FY26, reflecting the benefits of proactive refinancing and restructuring of company's loan portfolio.

items.statement: Board recommended first interim dividend FY27 at INR 3 per share
items.quote: I am pleased to inform that NTPC Board has recommended first interim dividend for FY 26-27 at INR3 per share, in line with the company's commitment to delivering value to its shareholders.

items.statement: Government approved Green Energy Corridor Phase 3 on 30 Sep 2026: strengthens intrastate transmission for 135 GW RE evacuation and 50 GWh BESS; total outlay INR 1,86,405 cr with central support INR 54,082 cr; target completion FY32-33
items.quote: the Government of India approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase 3 schemes on 30th September 2026. The scheme will strengthen intrastate transmission systems to evacuate up to 135 gigawatts of renewable power and provide 50 gigawatt-hour of battery energy storage.

items.statement: Implementing 5 GWh BESS at thermal stations; NGEL plans 40 GWh BESS (proposals under process); 3 GWh storage in service mode contracted, 12 GWh under tendering; overall BESS plan ~47 GWh
items.quote: are already implementing 5 gigawatt hour of battery energy storage system at our thermal power stations alongside pursuing other long-duration storage opportunities

items.statement: NGEL RE capacity addition: added ~1.3 GW in H1 FY27; revised FY27 estimate ~6.5 GW constructed but 1.5 GW may lack transmission; expect ~3.5 GW more by year-end; initial target was ~8 GW
items.quote: we have added capacity close to 1300 megawatt at the end of October. And our estimation is that another 3.5 gigawatt is something which would be able to do. Close to 1615 megawatt is something which would be on the ground, but which will be covered under probably the delay in the transmission.

items.statement: Nuclear program advancing: land acquisition commenced at one project; nuclear team strengthened to 100+ members; Government published draft rules under SHANTI Act for nuclear plants (under consultation)
items.quote: With commencement of land acquisition process at one of our projects, our nuclear program has picked up speed. We have also strengthened our nuclear team, bringing the team strength to over 100 members.

items.statement: Issued expression of interest for 26% equity to C&I consumers under group captive route; EOI closes end-November; exploring 100 MW data centers at couple of locations
items.quote: Recently, we have also issued expression of interest for offering 26% equity to commercial and industrial consumers u nder group captive route, which will create an additional pillar of sustained growth moving forward

items.statement: NTPC coal stations PLF 75.11% in H1 FY27 vs all-India average 68.35%; group generation 236 BU (+10.4% YoY); NGEL generation 10.88 BU (+60% YoY); NVVN traded 31 BU (+25% YoY)
items.quote: NTPC coal stations achieved a PLF of 75.11% against rest of India's average of 68.35%. Generation from NGEL group during H1 FY27 stood at 10.88 billion units as compared to 6.76 billion units in H1 FY26, registering a growth of 60%.

items.statement: Coal stations fixed cost disincentive reduced to INR 332 cr in H1 FY27 from INR 625 cr in H1 FY26 (half); O&M gains achieved
items.quote: the disincentive, how we coin it, it is INR332 crores. This is half of what was there in the last year of INR 625 crores. So, the disincentives have dropped and the better seasons await us.

items.statement: Ratnagiri gas cost: LNG spot $16-32/MMBtu, average <$28-29; fuel cost ~INR 26/kWh; sales through market operations (TRAS) not take-or-pay PPA
items.quote: The cost is varying from $16 to $32. So, whatever it is available in the spot, we are purchasing, or we are tying through long-term tie-up. So average, we can say we are getting less than $28 to $29

items.statement: Lara Stage 3 (1,600 MW) awarded in Q2 FY27; limited notice to proceed issued pending environmental clearance
items.quote: NTPC has awarded Lara Stage 3, (1,600 megawatts ) and issued limited notice to proceed pending environmental clearance in Q2 FY27.
