items.statement: Group thermal stations co-fired 0.83 MMT biomass in H1 FY27 (+65% YoY); submitted proposal for 5 lakh TPA synthetic natural gas at Talaipalli under coal gasification incentive scheme; planning participation in round 2 for methanol/DME/urea
items.quote: Our group thermal stations co-fired 0.83 million metric tons of biomass, which is 65% more than biomass co-fired during

items.statement: Standalone regulated equity INR 92,926 cr (Sep 2026) vs INR 94,454 cr (Sep 2025); reduction due to coal mining business transfer to subsidiary; consolidated regulated equity INR 1,21,786 cr vs INR 1,16,022 cr
items.quote: Standalone regulated equity for conventional power business as on 30th September 2026 is INR 92,926 crores, as against INR94,454 crores as on 30th September 2025. The reduction is due to transfer of coal mining business from NTPC Limited to wholly owned subsidiary

items.statement: Other income dropped INR 432 cr in H1 FY27: interest from JV/subs up INR 180 cr, but dividend down INR 481 cr and late payment surcharge down 28% (better collection efficiency)
items.quote: other income, there is a drop by INR 432 crore. That is because interest from JV /subsidiary, while it has gone up by INR 180 crores, the dividend from JV /subsidiaries, we have received less by INR481 crores. And the LPS, late payment surcharge, has also dropped by 28%, which is reflective of a better collection efficiency

items.statement: NGEL facing RE curtailment due to transmission constraints; expects resolution by mid-July 2027; PPA terms extended so revenue shifted not lost; only depreciation not covered; T-GNA revenue covers O&M and interest
items.quote: our transmission constraint or the connectivity issue which we are facing will all be surmounted by next year, mid-July. So, beyond which we will not have this continued thing. So, pending this, we are trying to optimize this through, wherever possible, through temporary And the other significant thing which we would like to point out is, wherever we are facing this problem, the PPA terms get exte

items.statement: Pumped storage: first DPR (Maharashtra) by Dec 2026; Amba DPR by Mar 2027; THDC and NEEPCO working on PSPs; will award after DPR and TEC completion
items.quote: Coming to the pump storage, we will be completing our first DPR, that is in Maharashtra, by December. Then other DPR will be completed in the month of March, that is for Amba. Then our subsidiaries THDC and NEEPCO are working on PSPs. Once DPR is completed and TEC is done, then we'll be going for award.

items.statement: BESS procurement: constrained by GFR Rule 144 preventing direct China imports; now permitted direct procurement; 40 GWh ICB tender coming soon for direct sourcing from Chinese/other suppliers
items.quote: We have been pursuing actively with the government and we have now been asked to procure directly, and we would therefore be going ahead with a 40 gigawatt -hour tender coming up soo n, which would be an ICB tender. Procurement of it would be directly from all the Chinese or the other related, the places from where we were not able to source directly

items.statement: THDC profit up INR 221 cr in H1 FY27 due to full-year effect of PSP (500 MW) and Khurja (660 MW) commissioned Sep 2025; BRBCL Q2 profit up INR 64 cr from finance cost reduction (refinancing) and fly ash/security billing
items.quote: the capacity of PSP has been added, 500 megawatts, and capacity addition of Khurja, 660 megawatts , the full effect of that will be seen in this year because we commissioned this in September last year, so it had effect of part month, whereas t his year, it will have a full effect

items.statement: Regulatory deferral: INR 862 cr reversal of excess depreciation at Bongaigaon coal station; nil P&L impact as appears on both income and expenditure sides
items.quote: No, it's a kind of a reversals of the excess depreciation till date of INR 862 crores. That is the reason for this, because this pertains to Bongaigaon coal station. But it will have nil impact on profitability because it will figure in both the sides of income and expenditure.

items.statement: Expect profit growth to significantly exceed regulated equity growth in coming quarters due to efficiency gains (O&M, operational)
items.quote: Yes, we can fairly expect that. Yes.

items.statement: Internal plan targets 25,000-30,000 tons incremental volume growth per year for FY28 and FY29, not formal guidance
items.quote: we have moved on to planning for next 2 years for fiscal year '28 and '29 and getting back to a growth of at least 25,000, 30,000 tons each year and then potential upside is all the various things that we have discussed come to fruition.

items.statement: Mining volumes flat YoY; Chile mine stopped production for ~2 months in Q2, resumed in current quarter
items.quote: in this particular quarter for almost 2 months, that mine had stopped production. And therefore, our dispatches were also very low to this particular mine, which has again started at the normal traction from the current quarter.

items.statement: Mexico volume loss due to 50% import duty imposed by Mexico (under US influence), peak volume was 7,000-8,000 tons/year
items.quote: Mexico has applied a 50% duty tariff to a large number of countries as part of their NAFTA obligation. It's not against India as a country or us as a company.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin declined 2.5-3% YoY due to steep export freight cost increase (>3.5% YoY)
items.quote: The primary reason for this decline on an operating EBITDA level basis is a steep increase in the cost of export freight, which has grown by over 3.5% in Q2 and H1 of this year on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Freight cost reached ~10% of sales in Q2 (abnormal), normally 7-8%; expected to normalize to 7-8% range in current quarter
items.quote: See, this 10%, I would say, is a little abnormal. In a normal scenario, it should not be more than 7%, 8%. This particular quarter, due to some composition of freight, part of it being air freight as well is a little bit on the higher side, coupled with high sea freight.

items.statement: Realization per kg increased ~INR178 largely due to freight pass-through; gross margins directionally comparable
items.quote: That also is the reason why if you -- most of you will see that the realization per ton or per kilo on per kg basis has increased about INR178, largely attributable to the increase in the freight, which has been passed on.

items.statement: Order book rose to INR10.7 billion (from INR5-7 billion range) due to large orders received in last month of Q2; no dispatch bunching
items.quote: we have recently got some good orders, some large -- reasonably large orders which have come in the last month of this quarter. And therefore, the order book has really actually gone up a little bit.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex INR86 crores; additional ~INR250 crores planned in H2 (corporate house land + INR50-75 crores maintenance/incremental)
items.quote: we've incurred a total capex of INR86 crores in the first half. We believe that we should be incurring additional about INR250 crores in H2, largely due to the corporate house land that we will be completing the transaction and also some normal maintenance and incremental capex of about INR50-odd crores to INR75 crores.

items.statement: Ghana and China expansion on hold for one more quarter; may reconsider by end of next quarter
items.quote: right now, for one more quarter we are still maintaining the position of putting this Ghana, China right now on hold, though very honestly, we are going to reconsider this very soon. However, right now, as I said, the focus is continued on the trials and all strengths on that. We will be definitely looking at reactivating our geographical expansion at some point in time, hopefully by end of next q

items.statement: Net working capital cycle ~129 days in Q2/H1 (41 days raw material, 79 days WIP/finished, 87 days receivables)
items.quote: my net working capital cycle in this Q2 as well as H1 remained more or less at about 129 days. That includes about 41 days of raw material stock, 79 days of WIP and finished and then about 87 days of receivables.

items.statement: Q2 product mix shifted slightly away from higher-margin other castings vs Q1, partially offsetting freight impact
items.quote: It's also a function of product mix. So if you see in Q1, there was a higher element of other castings. In Q2, it is slightly lower. So it has a compensatory effect that your freight increased so your product mix has gone a little down.

items.statement: Chilean copper customer happy with grinding media conversion; hopeful for migration to more mines but no timeline
items.quote: they are happy with what they bought in grinding media. We are hopeful that it will migrate into more work in the future. But just to exceed expectations there. We are on track for that as well.

items.statement: Freight uncertainty (Red Sea, Hormuz) creates friction in conversion trials; mitigation via containerized cargo and extra sea stock
items.quote: there is an uncertain global environment around shipping and logistics and the long delivery lead times. This is true for any producer which is producing at one end and there is some time line from the use of the product. And that uncertainty does -- so when we have spoken about last 2 years, the uncertainty in the shipping environment, right, between Red Sea, the Hormuz, a lot of other things hav

items.statement: Export benefits highest ever in Q2 despite lower volumes; timing difference between export dispatch and end-customer billing
items.quote: Export benefit reflects what India has sold, exported, but that may not have converted into billing, right? So the supply chains are longer. So there is a timing difference in that. So sometimes it's lower than our revenue, sometimes it's higher.

items.statement: Geopolitical shipping uncertainty (Red Sea, Hormuz, potential Iran war) is a structural risk beyond cost; may not normalize soon
items.quote: Now there are pundits that tell us that Iran war will get settled in the next few months. It may not, right? And it is not a cost factor. It is the uncertainty linked to depending on a shipping-linked supply chain, I think, is the question.

items.statement: H1 FY27 sales volume 126,000 metric tons (flat YoY); Q2 production 63,600 MT, sales 61,500 MT
items.quote: We did about 61,500 metric tons sales in Q2 on a production of about 63,600 metric tons. That translates into sales of about 126,000 metric tons in the first half of the current fiscal, slightly above 124,000, 125,000 tons that we did in the corresponding H1 on a Y-o-Y basis last year.

items.statement: Mining segment H1 FY27 volume ~79,000 tons (up YoY); Q2 mining volume 39,700 tons
items.quote: mining sales stood at about 39,700 tons in this Q2, resulting in about 79,000 tons in the first half, more or less showing some increase on a Y-o-Y basis on an H1 to H1 basis and also a little bit increase on a Q2 to Q2 basis in the current fiscal.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA INR361 crores; H1 EBITDA INR786 crores; Q2 PAT INR249 crores; H1 PAT ~INR550 crores (all slightly down YoY)
items.quote: You would have seen that we did an EBITDA of about INR361 crores in the Q2 of the current fiscal. And INR786 crores again in H1 of the current fiscal. That resulted into a PAT of about INR249 crores in Q2 and INR550-odd crores PAT in Q2 of -- in the first half of the current fiscal.

items.statement: NGDS+liner trials elongated; one mine delayed, one in redesign; no outcome guidance for next quarter
items.quote: At one mine the trials have been delayed and the other has gone in for a reiteration, they went for a redesign. So we will update when we have a little better guidance to give on it.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR4,800-5,000 crores by FY29 with existing assets and balancing capex
items.quote: So we are expecting that by going in FY29, we aspire that we should reach anywhere between INR4,800 crores to INR5,000 crores by -- with our existing assets and balancing some of them.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance range of 16% to 20%
items.quote: We have not guided for 20%. First of all, Varun ji, I would like to highlight that. We have told that a range is 16% to 20%.

items.statement: Commercial production for all expansion divisions expected by end of December 2026
items.quote: Commercial production in all the divisions is expected to commence by the end of December '26 as planned.

items.statement: Renewable energy capacity to increase from 41 MW to 95 MW by end of December 2026
items.quote: On renewable project investments, are progressing per schedule and expected to get operational by end of December '26. This will take our renewable energy capacity from 41 megawatt to about 95 megawatt

items.statement: Next year modernization and balancing capex of INR80-100 crores planned
items.quote: In the next year, we are -- since we are planning to modernize and rebalance our capacities, we expect that we'll be spending in the range of about INR80 crores to INR100 crores for our modernization and other things.

items.statement: Spinning capacity utilization over 98% and woven fabric utilization about 90% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: In Q2 FY27, the spinning capacity utilization was over 98% and woven fabric capacity utilization was about 90%.

items.statement: New capacity to add INR1,000 crores annual revenue, INR300-350 crores in FY27
items.quote: So second, the total revenue out of this new project, which we are expecting is about INR1,000 crores. So we're expecting that we should be able to increase the revenues by another INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 17.8%, up 471 bps YoY, sustained at Q1 level
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 17.8% as against 13.1% in Q2 FY26, that is an expansion of 471 basis points and was sustained at the Q1 FY27 level of 17.78%.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin 18.5% excluding trial production loss of INR1 crore on INR21 crore revenue
items.quote: So if you remove that part of this, the EBITDA would be around 18.5%.

items.statement: Expect to maintain current margin levels with RE power and cost initiatives cushioning input cost increases
items.quote: So we expect that we should be able to retain the margins at what level we have. As far as the upper level or upper -- it is always the endeavor of the company to reach the top level of margins. But still, I think we are far from there.

items.statement: Yarn realization up 12.5-13% QoQ, fabric realization up 6% QoQ in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our -- the fabric realization has increased year-on-year by about 6%[Errata: To be read as "Increased Quarter-on-Quarter by about 6%"]. And yarn realizations have increased year-on-year by about 12.5% to 13%[Errata: To be read as "Increased Quarter-on-Quarter by about 12.5% to 13%"] .

items.statement: Input cost pressures from dyes, chemicals, coal, packaging, sea freight increasing
items.quote: We are seeing a lot of the input costs going up, including the dyes, chemicals, coal, packaging cos ts, the freights are increasing. Also, we are seeing the sea freight increase

items.statement: Yarn demand healthy with steady buying from major importing countries and domestic players
items.quote: Yarn demand stayed healthy with steady buying from major importing coun tries as well as domestic players, amid stable tariff

items.statement: Exports contributed 68% of revenue in Q2 FY27, grew over 40% YoY driven by dollar depreciation and yarn realization increase
items.quote: this 40% increase is basically some of -- there is increased depreciation in the dollar. That is one part. Secondly, increase in the yarn realizations of the yarn. This itself has c ontributed about 20%, 25

items.statement: Peak total debt expected at INR1,950 crores by March 2026 (term debt INR1,440 crores + working capital INR500 crores)
items.quote: First of all, the peak debt which we are going to have will be about our total term debt will peak in this March at about INR1,440 crores, I think. And working capital, which is at about INR400 crores at this point of time, can reach maybe about INR500 crores plus during that time. So total debt could be about INR1,950 crores at the end of March '26.

items.statement: Annual term debt repayment of INR180-200 crores for next 6-7 years
items.quote: And the repayments are every year about in the range of about INR180 crores to INR200 crores for the next 6, 7 years.

items.statement: Blended cost of debt 6.5-6.75% with 2.5% interest subsidy on capex loans
items.quote: Our cost of -- total blended cost will be in the range of about 6.5% to 6.75%.

items.statement: Receivables up 40% since March due to higher export receivables and lower bill discounting utilization, no major overdues
items.quote: First of all, the increase is pri marily due to increase in the export receivables. We have not extended any additional credit. Rather, we have not negotiated part of the documents with the banks, which has been -- which would have resulted in realization of the documents

items.statement: Import duty exemption on cotton expected to continue due to domestic crop shortage and consumption growth
items.quote: Government is very well aware about th is fact that there is a shortage already. Even the cotton crop is lesser than last year by about 4% to 5%. And the consumption is increasing consistently, the overall textile is growing by 5% to 6%. So consequently, the gap is increasing. So as to bridge that gap, government is definitely going to help us in keeping -- this particular product at par with the

items.statement: Cotton prices: domestic INR67,000-68,000 per candy, international USD0.80/lb, expected range USD0.75-0.90
items.quote: We expect that it should remain in the range of USD0.75 to USD0.90 band with an averaging of about USD0.84, USD0.85 kind of thing going forward as the consumption is increasing world over and also we are seeing that the cotton will be lesser.

items.statement: Company moving up value chain with higher finished fabric and value-added yarn capacity, 28-30% yarn capacity dedicated to woven fabrics post expansion
items.quote: Actually, as I have indicated many times that normally for the industry like ours, where we have now post this expansion, nearly 28% to 30% of our capacity will be for the -- yarn capacity will be dedicated to woven fabrics.

items.statement: No single geography driving export growth; broad-based across all geographies
items.quote: This is all along. We are practically operating in all the geographies, and it is not that one particular geography has improved substantially.

items.statement: Bangladesh LDC extension for 3 years not a concern as India FTAs will bring parity
items.quote: I think no change in status. They were already in the LDC, and this was very well with the kind of turbulence happening all around the world and also in Bangladesh, it was already expected that they may increase this LDC benefits for 1 or 2 years. So it has gone up by for 3 years. But fortunately, for us, that we have -- we'll have all our FTAs in place, and we'll be at par with them, no way lesse

items.statement: Near-term risks: inflationary conditions across commodities/services, liquidity strain in downstream channels
items.quote: In the near term, the inflationary conditions across commodities and services and liquidity strain in the downstream channels are factors which are closely to be watched.

items.statement: Input cost volatility (dyes, chemicals, coal, freight) and slow fabric price pass-through may pressure margins
items.quote: Plus, we also need to see that there is a slow pass on of the increases in the fabrics. So that also takes some time. So both of these should also be considered when you extrapolate the margins for us.

items.statement: No garmenting capex initiated yet; aspiration remains but no timeline
items.quote: I have also indicated in our last conference call that is a logical thing which we should go into. So that was the aspiration. But as of date, we have not done anything. As soon as we get into something like that, we'll definitely let you all know about it.

items.statement: Depreciation to increase to INR53-54 crores/quarter (INR200+ crores annually) with new capacity
items.quote: With this new capacity expansion, which is going to come in, this should increase to about INR53 crores to INR54 crores going forward. So every quarter, I'm talking about every quarter. Going forward, next year, it should be in the range of INR200 crores, around INR200 crores plus.

items.statement: Knitting fabric utilization low due to yarn price volatility and US tariff concerns; segment <2% of total investment, mostly depreciated
items.quote: If you see from the investment point of view, it's a very small investment from the -- in case of size of our company. The knitting investment is out of our total investment, it is less than 2%. And most of it is fully depreciated because we have not added major capaci ty in the last 4, 5 years in this particular

items.statement: Trial production revenue INR21 crores with EBITDA loss of INR1 crore in Q2 FY27
items.quote: In this particular quarter, we have some small revenues coming in from of our trial production and all the cost, etcetera related with that is also being debited to the P&L account only. And that is -- it means about -- the top line is about INR21 crores, we have also displayed that -- we have produced about 41 lakh meters out of which -- some of it was in stock and some were sold for INR21 crores

items.statement: Export shipment spillover of INR35-40 crores from Q1 to Q2 FY27
items.quote: Not much. I think I have informed that some quantity we were not able to dispatch at the end of the quarter. So that has been -- maybe that is to the extent of about INR35 crores to INR40 crores, not more than that.

items.statement: Subdued advertising demand impacted radio business; festive date shift moved revenue to Q3
items.quote: The operating environment remained challenging with the subdued advertising demand impacting our radio business. The shift in festive dates also moved more advertising and event revenue in the quarter 3.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA improved 9.5% YoY to INR11.3 crores despite revenue decline
items.quote: Despite the softer revenue environment, we reported EBITDA of INR11.3 crores, on an improvement of 9.5% over the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Radio 53%, Digital 29%, Events and others balance of domestic revenue
items.quote: Radio now contributes approximately 53% of our domestic revenue and digital 29%, with events and other businesses accounting for the balance.

items.statement: Non-FCT EBITDA margin improved to 30.8% from 27.8% YoY
items.quote: Importantly, profitability remained healthy with our EBITDA margins improving to 30.8% from 27.8% in the previous quarter last year.

items.statement: Digital EBITDA loss reduced 23.3% YoY to INR7.5 crores
items.quote: Digital EBITDA losses reduced by 23.3% to INR7.5 crores, compared to INR9.8 crores in the corresponding quarter of previous year.

items.statement: No formal guidance given; green shoots seen in Q3 advertising environment
items.quote: So generally, we don't give any guidance, but what we are seeing in Q3, there has been some green shoots from the advertising environment, and we believe that should continue.

items.statement: Radio inventory utilization at ~70%, down ~6%
items.quote: The inventory utilization is about 70%-odd. It has been down about 6%.

items.statement: Radio market share ~25%
items.quote: So, we are a strong player. It's about 25% market share for us on the Radio side.

items.statement: Cash balance INR371.5 crores; decline due to vendor advances for events, dividend, digital capex
items.quote: No. So, there has been advances to vendors because of the events coming in. There's dividend, and there was some capex in the digital business also on the tech side, which we did. That's the reason.

items.statement: Gaana EBITDA breakeven target Q4 FY27; may delay 1-2 quarters due to high acquisition costs
items.quote: Yes, that's been the ambition for us, and we keep focused on that. There are certain headwinds on the acquisition cost, as they are reflecting pressure on the broader D2C ecosystem, if you look at. The AI search is reducing referral traffic and inventory a lso. So, this leads to a high acquisition cost. So, what for us is always to believe we acquire a customer at a healthy LTV. We don't just blin

items.statement: Event business grew but margins lower than radio; competition increasing from TV, news, internet companies
items.quote: But having said that, we are very cognizant of the margins. The event margins and the traditional media radio margins are very different. Event margins will never be similar to radio margins. So, we need to be very cognizant of the fact that we gun for revenue with a subdued margin, or we look at a very healthy margin situation. Having said that, we are riding the wave of the event business, which

items.statement: Digital capex incurred on tech side in Q2
items.quote: There's dividend, and there was some capex in the digital business also on the tech side, which we did.

items.statement: Other current assets increased due to prepaid items accumulation
items.quote: Yes. It is because of accumulation of some prepaid items there in this current quarter.

items.statement: Management expects to surpass the annual revenue guidance of INR14,000 crores for FY27 and cross the defense revenue target of INR4,500 crores.
items.quote: We expect to surpass our stated annual guidance, which we have given at the start of the financial year FY27.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to cross 29% on average for FY27, up from the initial guidance of around 28%.
items.quote: We believe that by the year-end, we should be able to cross on an average 29%.

items.statement: Total order book stands at INR20,178 crores, with defense order book at INR17,568 crores, mostly from international markets.
items.quote: The total order book what we have as of now is around INR20,178 crores. And in that defense is around INR17,568 crores.

items.statement: Guided Pinaka order expected around INR3,000 crores, taking total Pinaka family order size to INR9,000 crores.
items.quote: Guided Pinaka, we were in the final stage of negotiation. And we hope that this will get concluded very soon. And order book now since we have already given our best price, so we know the size or the value of orders. So that should be around INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: Domestic explosives demand strong due to below-average monsoon and record Coal India offtake; growth momentum expected to continue in H2.
items.quote: The demand was quite good due to the lower monsoon or below average monsoon in most of the mining markets. The demand was pretty good and that has resulted into the better sales from domestic market.

items.statement: International explosives business maintained momentum with deeper customer relationships and sustained demand across key geographies.
items.quote: Our international explosive business maintained its momentum, supported by deeper customer relationship, improved market penetration and sustained demand across key operating geographies.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin at 29.02%; H1 EBITDA margin at 28.45%.
items.quote: Quarterly EBITDA was INR1,021 crores with a margin of 29.02%.

items.statement: Focus on expanding manufacturing footprint through acquisitions and greenfield expansions for international operations.
items.quote: We remain focused on scaling our international operations through acquisitions and greenfield expansions.

items.statement: Domestic volume growth target of 10-15% annually vs industry growth of 6-7%; capacity additions underway across the country.
items.quote: The industry growth rate should be around 7% by and large, and we should be able to enhance our growth by -- or grow every year by around 10% to 15% range.

items.statement: Defense revenue share increased to 29% in Q2 (INR1,002 crores) and 27% in H1 (INR1,935 crores); domestic explosives 27%, international explosives 43% in Q2.
items.quote: Defense revenue has increased to 29% from 24% and stands at INR1,002 crores.

items.statement: Supplying to 90+ countries; inquiries and orders from practically all permitted nations globally.
items.quote: We are supplying our products to 90 plus countries across the world. So we always keep getting inquiries practically from every nation whoever requires such kind of products.

items.statement: Positioned as one of the most competent private sector partners for tactical missile programs; participating in critical missile development programs.
items.quote: We are one of the most competent private sector partner for such kind of tactical missile programs. So all these development provides plenty of opportunities to definitely expand our current participation.

items.statement: Missile technologies opened to private sector by government; well aligned with Solar's capabilities in energetic materials, propellants, warheads, rocket and missile integration.
items.quote: For Solar, this opportunity is definitely well aligned with the capabilities, which we have built over the years, which span across energetic materials, propellants, warheads and rocket integration, and we also started making missile integrations.

items.statement: International orders constitute most of the INR17,568 crore defense order book; Pinaka rockets already supplied to international customers.
items.quote: Out of this order book, most of the orders are from international market. So as we are moving forward, as we are expanding our product portfolio, and as we are expanding our global reach, we are getting inquiries and orders from various countries across the world.

items.statement: Defense revenue target of INR4,500 crores for FY27; H1 defense revenue at INR1,935 crores.
items.quote: As per our annual guidance, we see that we should be able to reach INR4,500 crores. We still believe that we should be able to cross defense also.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues, supply chain disruptions, and commodity price fluctuations create uncertainty for guidance revision.
items.quote: Currently, due to geopolitical issues, supply chain disruptions and commodity prices are also fluctuating a lot, so it will be too difficult for us to revise guidance looking at these kind of uncertainties.

items.statement: Omnia acquisition pending approvals; no further updates until completion.
items.quote: On Omnia front, we had a detailed call a couple of months back and there is no more updates to be provided at this stage. So your questions can be answered once the acquisition is completed.

items.statement: Bhargavastra internal trials expected to conclude in calendar year 2024; field trials also targeted this year; commercial orders to follow after trials.
items.quote: We are likely to conclude all our internal trials in this calendar year and we are still very optimistic that we should be able to complete the trial and conduct the field trial also in this calendar year.

items.statement: 155mm shell facility set up; intermediate product deliveries commenced; final product expected by end of FY27; orders captured in defense order book.
items.quote: We have already shared that the total order book from defense as of now is around INR18,000 crores, and most of the orders are from international markets. And all these orders capture variety of products, which includes the products from 155 mm also.

items.statement: MALE UAV development ongoing indigenously; not impacted by current procurement programs; will participate when programs materialize.
items.quote: MALE UAV is definitely a strategic program. And as we have already shared that we are developing these products indigenously. So we will take our own time.

items.statement: New missile program orders expected after 2 years; trials completion in 6-12 months, RFP and contract finalization another 1-1.5 years.
items.quote: Even if we complete trials, let's assume for some of the programs in next 6 to 12 months' time, but RFP and then contract finalization will also take another year or 1.5 years. So for next 2 years or after 2 years, we should see orders flowing up from the new missile programs for Solar.

items.statement: Interest and finance cost increased to INR55 crores in Q2 (INR31 crores YoY) and INR97 crores in H1 (INR58 crores YoY).
items.quote: Interest and finance cost stands at INR55 crores versus INR31 crores, and for half year at INR97 crores versus INR58 crores.

items.statement: Depreciation increased to INR88 crores in Q2 (INR61 crores YoY) and INR168 crores in H1 (INR117 crores YoY).
items.quote: Depreciation stands at INR88 crores versus INR61 crores, and for the half year, it stands at INR168 crores versus INR117 crores.

items.statement: Raw material consumption increased to INR1,676 crores in Q2 (INR988 crores YoY) and INR3,533 crores in H1 (INR2,082 crores YoY).
items.quote: The raw material consumption for the quarter stands at INR1,676 crores versus INR988 crores, and for half year at INR3,533 crores versus INR2,082 crores.

items.statement: Employee cost increased to INR266 crores in Q2 (INR195 crores YoY) and INR522 crores in H1 (INR378 crores YoY).
items.quote: Employee cost for the quarter stands at INR266 crores versus INR195 crores, and for the half year at INR522 crores versus INR378 crores.

items.statement: Other expenses increased to INR571 crores in Q2 (INR347 crores YoY) and INR1,111 crores in H1 (INR688 crores YoY).
items.quote: The other expenses for the quarter stands at INR571 crores versus INR347 crores and for half year stands at INR1,111 crores versus INR688 crores.

items.statement: Commercial explosives growth benefited from higher ammonium nitrate prices and capacity additions.
items.quote: Growth so far has benefited from both higher ammonium nitrate prices and capacity additions, domestically.

items.statement: Management will provide FY28/FY29 guidance clarity after FY27 results; restricting discussion to current quarter and half-year.
items.quote: So this call is basically for the quarterly results and half-yearly update. So I would like to answer all this in the next -- once we share the financial results of FY27.

items.statement: Revenue and profitability targets under Vision 2028 retained; EBO store target optimized to 800 by FY28
items.quote: While retaining our revenue and profitability targets same, we have optimized our EBO store targets to 800 stores by FY28.

items.statement: Committed to double-digit revenue growth for FY27
items.quote: We remain confident in pursuing a double-digit growth target for this financial year and are committed to pursuing our revenue and profitability goals through a calibrated, disciplined and sustainable business model.

items.statement: Killer EBO SSG negative 10% on half-yearly basis; expected flattish on 9-month basis
items.quote: The SSG for Killer EBO stores on a half-yearly basis was negative 10%.

items.statement: Overall revenue double-digit growth expected for full year FY27
items.quote: We are focused on our commitment to achieve double-digit growth by the end of the year. That is all I can say.

items.statement: Incremental store size increase requires additional rental investment only
items.quote: The incremental size has an additional investment only in terms of rental.

items.statement: Killer store count unchanged at 477 EBOs; shift to larger 800-1,000 sq ft stores
items.quote: The Killer store count remains unchanged, with a shift towards larger store size of 800 to 1,000 square feet to support a broader product offering and improved revenue potential per store.

items.statement: Lawman target revised from 175 to 125 stores; focus on larger D2C-led stores
items.quote: The Lawman target has been revised from 175 stores to 125 stores, reflecting a more focused D2C-led strategy centered on establishing larger, higher-quality stores in strategic selected locations that strengthens the brand visibility.

items.statement: Kraus target increased from 50 to 75 stores
items.quote: Conversely, the target for Kraus stores has been increased from 50 to 75 stores, supported by the encouraging brand traction witnessed through this format.

items.statement: K-Lounge format to be phased out and excluded from EBO expansion plans
items.quote: Additionally, the company plans to gradually phase out the K-Lounge format over time and therefore, we have excluded it from our revised EBO expansion plans.

items.statement: Net addition of 5 EBOs in Q2 FY27; total network at 675 stores as of September 30
items.quote: In line with our strategy of expanding our retail footprint, we have added a net of 5 EBOs during quarter 2 of FY27, taking our total network to 675 stores as of September 30th.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA grew 12% YoY to INR80 crores with 21% margin; PAT up 15% to INR54 crores
items.quote: Consolidated revenue increased to INR373 crores, supported by growth in apparel sales and value. EBITDA grew by 12% year-on-year to INR80 crores with an EBITDA margin of 21% and profit after tax increased by 15% year-on-year to INR54 crores.

items.statement: Kraus EBITDA margins in line with KKCL overall margins
items.quote: The EBITDA margins for Kraus are in line with KKCL.

items.statement: Focus on reducing discounts and increasing fresh sales to improve EBITDA margin
items.quote: We are seeing that discount in the markets have grown too much. We believe that to improve EBITDA, we have to reduce discounts. We want to work on realistic prices and focus more on rotation, which will improve profitability.

items.statement: No incremental EBITDA margin improvement expected despite store rationalization
items.quote: I think on the margins, the EBITDA margins are almost above industry average, I don't feel that there will be incremental EBITDA margins ahead.

items.statement: Price hikes taken in first half; inflationary pressure may continue in Q3-Q4; will try to pass on via MRP or discount reduction
items.quote: We have already started facing that inflationary pressure. I am not too sure. I feel that it is too early to comment on that. We have taken a price increase in the current two quarters also. If possible, we will try to pass it on to the consumers.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue up 5% YoY to INR373 crores despite floods and festive shift
items.quote: Despite these macro headwinds and the shift of the festive season into Q3, we have demonstrated business resilience by delivering a positive 5% year-on-year increase in consolidated revenues.

items.statement: Floods impacted Q2 sales growth by 3-4%
items.quote: On the quarter 2 number, I would put it at 3% to 4%.

items.statement: Retail sales impacted by festival shift; Q2+Q3 merged view shows better result
items.quote: Actually in retail, because of the festival shifting, you have to look at Q2 and Q3 merged together. When you merge them, you will see a better result.

items.statement: Positive outlook on winter wear category; expect better fresh sales vs last year
items.quote: We are positive on the winter wear category this time. Okay. I think winter will be there and it will be cool climate, and fresh sales should be better compared to last year.

items.statement: Kraus grew over 25% in Q2; expansion into online, exports (Middle East) and MBO channels
items.quote: The brand Kraus delivered a growth of over 25%, representing an encouraging milestone in our strategy to strengthen our presence in the womens wear segment.

items.statement: Lawman re-strategized as retail-focused and online-focused brand
items.quote: Lawman, as we said, we have re-strategized in terms of brand positioning and we have made it a more retail-focused and more online-focused brand.

items.statement: Integriti delivered double-digit growth in H1 FY27
items.quote: Sahil, it has delivered double digit growth.

items.statement: Category expansion planned: kids wear, formal blazers, winter wear, accessories to increase store throughput
items.quote: We are also looking at category expansion, which we are looking at along with the brand. So, it is not only jeans, shirt, t-shirt or trousers that we make in menswear, other accessories, other categories, which is, maybe, as a formal, a blazer as a category and winter wear, which will be adding up and which will increase the throughput for the store.

items.statement: EBO repeat customer ratio ~22% with frequency of 2 purchases per year
items.quote: The repeat ratio is close to around 22% of the customer with a frequency of 2.

items.statement: Net working capital at ~130 days in Q2 FY27, in line with last year; inventory higher due to festive dispatch shift to Q3
items.quote: The current working capital -- net working capital for the current quarter was close to 130 odd days, which was in line with last year.

items.statement: Kraus exports started in Middle East; getting traction
items.quote: We have already started with some exports in the Middle East, and, okay, we have also started getting good traction from the second quarter from online.

items.statement: No incremental update on inorganic growth initiatives
items.quote: As such, there is nothing right now. As soon as there is something, we will definitely let you know.

items.statement: Share buyback suggestion noted; too early to decide
items.quote: We will keep your suggestion in mind and whenever any such strategy is formed, we will let you know. Because today, it is too early to say anything about this, but since you mentioned it, we will think about it.

items.statement: Floods caused 7-10 days production loss at Vapi/Daman factory
items.quote: And, the factory was in the water. It was completely in the water, so we were not able to do anything. So around 7, 8 to 10 days went waste.

items.statement: Winter quarter historically impacts EBITDA mix by 1-2% due to discounting
items.quote: Winter has always been difficult because it gives you, a sixty days window, in a period of winter, definitely has impact on discounting. It may change your EBITDA mix by a 1% or 2% scenario. Okay, for the particular quarter, which is Q3.

items.statement: Marketing spend to increase digitally
items.quote: However, on the marketing side, okay, there will be more spend done digitally.

items.statement: Brand pivots under Vision 2028 still early; need 2 more quarters for update
items.quote: Sahil, I still feel it's too early scenario, okay, We have not been able to crack it a as well as we thought. You'll have to give me at least two more quarters to get an update on that.

items.statement: Board approved a rights issue of around INR250 crores backed by promoters; draft letter of offer to be filed tomorrow; proceeds for augmenting working capital
items.quote: our Board today approved a rights issue of around INR250 crores. So, we'll be filing our draft letter of offer to stock exchanges by tomorrow and wait for their approvals, and very soon, we'll launch the issue.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved from 6.35% to 8.04% in specialty ingredients; overall gross margin fell ~2% due to high input costs, dollar strength and channel financing costs
items.quote: EBITDA obviously improved from 6.35% to 8.04%. This has this -- with adequate liquidity support, this should very first go to the double digit.

items.statement: Gross margin reduced from INR2,142 million to INR1,958 million; overall EBITDA fell from 3.4% to 2.5% due to liquidity-driven channel financing and overdue payables
items.quote: on an overall basis, our gross margin has reduced from INR2,142 million to INR1,958 million in this quarter. And this has percolated down and eaten up our EBITDA, which anyway was 3.4% has almost come down to 2.5% in this quarter.

items.statement: Unable to pass on raw material cost increases (phenol more than doubled) to customers due to local competition; channel financing and overdue payables add ~4% to cost (INR190-200 million per quarter)
items.quote: the main culprit here is the liquidity issues. However, payables had increased, but to support more and to have more working capital, we had used channel financing, both on the purchase side as well as sales side.

items.statement: Aroma revenue dropped from INR774 million to INR472 million due to plant changeover and underutilisation; blends revenue stable at ~INR2,970 million; straights revenue recovered from INR927 million to INR1,109 million
items.quote: Almost our revenue in Aroma reduced from INR774 million to INR472 million, and this is entirely almost ethyl vanillin sale. Blends and the straights, the specialty ingredient business has been always the hallmark, and it has always done well.

items.statement: Visibility of 2,500-2,700 tons vanillin demand from US and 1,300-1,500 tons from Europe for next calendar year; expect 1,000 tons/quarter from Q4 FY27
items.quote: From the U.S., we have visibility of about 2,500 to 2,700 tons for the next calendar year. And Europe is about 1,500 -- 1,300 to 1,500. So that's why we are saying that probably in Q4, that is the Q1 of next calendar year, we should be at about 1,000 tons.

items.statement: Working capital cycle normally 200 days; currently appears at 60 days due to INR130 crore of channel financing; rights issue proceeds to unwind channel financing and clear overdue payables
items.quote: my working capital days are looking at 60 days, which is impossible. So our general working capital cycle is 200 days, and that's looking lower because we have INR130-odd crores of credit.

items.statement: Net debt increased slightly from INR5,260 million to INR5,380 million mainly due to forex revaluation; interest cost stable at ~INR163-169 million; loans repaid despite crisis
items.quote: It was around INR5,260 million, which has gone up to INR5,380 million and a large portion of that is because of the foreign exchange updation. Our interest cost without forex was around INR163 million, which was INR169 million.

items.statement: Net vanillin realisation $12-12.5/ton after tariffs and distribution costs; blended realisation $13.7 with ethyl and methyl vanillin; Chinese material rerouted via Thailand/Malaysia muting prices
items.quote: the realization should improve from the levels that we are at $12, $12.5 net realization, net of tariffs and net of distribution costs.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty ~15% in place; Syensqo acting to block illegal Chinese imports routed through Southeast Asia; expect realisations to improve in 3-4 quarters as rerouting stops
items.quote: the principal mover of the antidumping duty is Syensqo, who has been acting to stop and block that entry of illegal imports coming into U.S. and Europe. And that is the reason why the realizations are at this point, slightly muted.

items.statement: Distributor model preferred over direct B2B to large F&F companies (90-120 day credit) because distributors offer ~30 day terms, saving 90 days working capital
items.quote: if you go to direct customers, the credit period is generally much longer. The large F&F companies typically ask for minimum 90 to 120 days. So -- which is actually the reason why we are introducing channel partners is b asically to improve that liquidity and improve that sales cycle because typically, large distributors are now looking at terms of not more than 30 days

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA target of INR200 crore on INR2,000 crore revenue will not be met; turnaround expected in Q4 FY27 with INR600 crore revenue and INR60 crore+ EBITDA assuming current raw material prices
items.quote: Q4 will be the first quarter with the liquidity with us. The turnaround will happen in Q4. The turnaround, we expect the top line to be INR600 crores and the EBITDA to be INR60 crores plus in Q4

items.statement: Promoters to subscribe to their 48% share of rights issue; final dilution depends on issue pricing yet to be decided
items.quote: the promoters have to put their 48%. So there is unlikely that they will get diluted. They have more than the likely to dilute the equity… Nirmal Momaya: So the total equity dilution, we will know only when the pricing is done

items.statement: Full-year FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at over 50%
items.quote: I think we should still surpass the 50% guidance that we had for the whole year.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 gross margin target 29-30% and EBITDA margin 13.5-14.5% post-Ind AS
items.quote: With gross margin now at 30%, we aim to sustain around 29% to 30% gross margin and 13.5% to 14.5% EBITDA margin for the full year.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin target 7-8%
items.quote: I think we would be targeting a pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin of 7% to 8% for the whole year.

items.statement: FY28 store addition guidance 120-150 stores, revenue growth 35-40% if only 100 stores opened
items.quote: For FY28, our current guidance would be anywhere between 120 to 150 stores.

items.statement: FY28 revenue growth would be 35-40% if store additions reduced to 100
items.quote: I think it would be around 35%, 35% to 40%.

items.statement: Opened 106 stores in H1 FY27, highest ever half-year addition
items.quote: In the first half of FY27, we opened 106 stores and closed 4. This is our highest ever H1 addition.

items.statement: Backend infrastructure can support 150+ stores per year
items.quote: We have reached a stage where our back end, which is the design, sourcing, warehousing and talent can support 150-plus stores per year.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 volume growth 31% YoY, H1 FY27 volume growth 43% YoY
items.quote: In the second quarter, volume growth was 31% year-on-year. In the first half of FY27, volume growth was 43% up year-on-year.

items.statement: Demand slowdown observed in last 3 months, macro delta +/-5%
items.quote: In the last 3 months, definitely we saw some sort of a demand slowdown.

items.statement: H1 FY27 gross margin 29.8%, EBITDA margin 13.6% post-Ind AS
items.quote: Gross profit grew from INR384.4 crores to INR566.4 crores with a 29.8% margin. EBITDA grew from INR172.7 crores to INR259.7 crores, a growth of 50%.

items.statement: Raw material cost inflation 3-7%, MRP hikes 5-10% taken to maintain gross margin
items.quote: The hike in cost was around 3% to 7%. So to maintain gross margin, we will have to increase the MRPs by 5% to 10%.

items.statement: ASP down 3% in H1 FY27 managed via product mix shift to value/economy
items.quote: If you see the ASP, the ASP has actually come down 3% in the first half of the year. So how we manage that is by a better product mix.

items.statement: Revenue mix: men's 40%, ladies 29%, kids 22%, lifestyle 9%
items.quote: Revenue mix remained primarily the same, men's wear about 40%; ladies, 29%; kids, 22%; and lifestyle, 9%.

items.statement: Increasing fashion quotient in assortment from <20% to 30% to attract Gen Z
items.quote: We have introduced a lot more fashion quotient in our assortment. So earlier, it used to be less than 20%. Now we are trying to take it up to 30%.

items.statement: Repeat customer frequency improved from 5.5 to 4.4-4.5 months, mature store repeat sales 55% to 70%
items.quote: The average frequency of our customers, repeat customers, used to be almost 5, 5.5 months, which has reduced to just 4.4 to 4.5 months now. And for our mature stores, the repeat customer sales has increased from 55% to almost 70%.

items.statement: Borrowings INR528 crore (INR45.6 cr non-current, INR483 cr current) vs INR253 cr March 2026
items.quote: Borrowings stood at INR528 crores, of which INR45.6 crores is non-current and INR483 crores is current versus INR253 crores in March 2026.

items.statement: Inventory INR1,447.8 crore vs INR1,141 crore March 2026, increase for 106 new stores and festive stocking
items.quote: As of September 30, 2026, Inventory stands at INR1,447.8 crores versus INR1,141 crores at the end of March 2026. The increase of about INR306 crores of inventory is for the 106 new stores, advanced festive stocking for quarter 3 and the new store pipeline for quarter 3.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 SSSG -14.9% calendar, +0.5% normalized; H1 SSSG -3.7% calendar
items.quote: The FY27 SSSG showed minus 14.9%, but normal SSSG was plus 0.5% because Q2 last year had an early Durga Puja and an extended wedding season, while this year, the festive season shifted to quarter 3.

items.statement: H1 FY27 average bill value INR917 vs INR900 YoY, ASP INR307 vs INR309, full price sales 91%
items.quote: Our aver age bill value was INR917 in the first half of FY27 compared to INR900 last year. Our average selling price was around INR307 in the first half of the year versus INR309 in the first half of the last year. Full price sales was 91% in quarter 2 and H1 versus 92% last year

items.statement: If Q3 SSSG remains muted, FY28 store additions reduced to 100 from 150-200 target
items.quote: If this trend continues to the third quarter, then next year we'll only open 100 stores, which initially the target was 150 to 200.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 expected around INR 150 crore
items.quote: This year, capex will be in the region of about INR150 crores.

items.statement: Gross margin 34.3% in Q2 FY27 vs 37.6% YoY and 36.9% QoQ due to higher input costs and mix change
items.quote: Gross margin stood at 34.3% in Q2, compared to 37.6% in the corresponding quarter last year and 36.9% in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 9.1% in Q2 FY27 vs 8.1% YoY; H1 EBITDA margin near 9.5-10%
items.quote: EBITDA margin was 9.1% in Q2 this year compared to 8.1% in Q2 last year.

items.statement: Electronics segment sustainable margin 16-17% normal year, 18% in good year
items.quote: About 16%, 17% is okay. 18% can be in a good year.

items.statement: 2-3% pricing gap remains to pass through input cost increases; price hikes of 6-12% across categories underway
items.quote: As we stand today, we have a 2% to 3% gap in pricing that is yet to be passed through.

items.statement: Wires revenue growth 41.2% YoY was almost entirely price-led (~40% price increase) with volumes flat
items.quote: I think Cables volumes are flat. I think it's probably flat. Almost all of it has come from pricing growth, which is close to... Sudarshan Kasturi: 40

items.statement: Volume growth ex-Wires: 25% volume, 10% price in Q2; H2 volume growth expected mid-teens
items.quote: H2 growth will be lower than H1, but revenue-wise; sorry, volume-wise, maybe it will be like mid-teens or something like that.

items.statement: Channel inventory normal; good offtake seen; confident of sustaining growth momentum in upcoming quarters
items.quote: So channel inventory is normal. So as you can see from our numbers, the velocity underlying growth has been good across all our categories.

items.statement: Electronics segment revenue grew 60% YoY in Q2 led by Solar, Inverter & Battery; Electricals grew 41.2%; Consumer Durables grew 20%
items.quote: The Electronics segment—comprising Stabilizers, UPS Systems, Inverters & Batteries and Solar panels—reported particularly strong revenue growth of 60% YoY in Q2.

items.statement: Solar Power Systems sold mainly in South via system integrators; 75% sales in 3-10 kW residential range; not B2B
items.quote: Our solar products are mainly from 3 kilowatt, so 75% of our sales is 3 kilowatt to 10 kilowatt and it is going to residential households.

items.statement: Lighting launch 3-4 months old; 40-50% SKUs landed; focused on few districts in couple of states; full portfolio expansion targeted by April-May
items.quote: The Lighting launch in the market is not more than 3 to 4 months old. And so we have still been able to land only maybe 40%, 50% of the SKUs that we want to bring to market.

items.statement: Sunflame integration complete; NPD refresh across Gas Stoves, Chimneys, Built-ins landing over next 6-12 months
items.quote: The NPD refresh is landing. And it has partly landed, and there is more to come over the next 6 to 12 months.

items.statement: General trade ~70% of revenue; modern trade, e-commerce, canteen stores ~30%; e-commerce under-indexed vs industry
items.quote: I think general trade will be about 70% of our revenue and maybe modern trade, e-commerce and canteen stores maybe about 30% of our revenue.

items.statement: Solar manufacturing not yet started; supply chain still forming; Gegadyne battery pilot orders may start in few months
items.quote: Not yet. But that's why I said we are still nascent in this business. And we are working on various dimensions in this space.

items.statement: Innovation centre set up 3-4 years ago to strengthen electronics capability and support new categories like Lighting, Solar, Batteries
items.quote: We put up the R&D center probably about 3 years back or 4 years back, It is an investment for what is going to come now in the next 3, 4 years.

items.statement: A&P spend ~2.3% of revenue, stable; allocation shifts across segments quarter to quarter
items.quote: Or 2.3% of revenue, which is broadly in line with what we have.

items.statement: NPD target 21-22% of non-wire revenue (first 12 months sales); range 18-24% depending on product roadmap
items.quote: Typically, we target to deliver about 21%, 22% of, let's say, non-wire revenue through NPD.

items.statement: BLDC fan share upwards of 35-40% driving growth in Ceiling Fans
items.quote: BLDC share is also decent, maybe upwards of maybe 35%, 40%.

items.statement: New wire entrant launch very recent; no material retail presence yet; impact assessment in couple of quarters
items.quote: From what we can gather, not a very significant or substantial portion of materials have reached to a significant number of outlets.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation monitored; further commodity price movements possible in September-October
items.quote: We continue to monitor the geo-political situation and will take appropriate actions necessary to protect supplies and margins.

items.statement: Targets full-year FY27 volume growth of double digits and EBITDA per kg in INR45-46 range
items.quote: Yes, we are confident we'll be maintaining now anything around INR45, INR46 range for sure because even this third quarter started on a strong note and we feel that the momentum going forward only can help it.

items.statement: Targets FY27 EBITDA of INR250 crores and capex of INR75-80 crores
items.quote: We are aiming at doubling the cash flow from INR107 crores to INR215 crores, as I mentioned in the beginning of the year. So I'm still standing on that. I hope to -- we hope to see an EBITDA of INR250 crores compared to INR173 crores last year.

items.statement: Targets INR50 EBITDA per kg in 2-3 years
items.quote: So as you said, in 2 to 3 years, it is nothing wrong to hope for a INR50 EBITDA margin in the coming 2, 3 years. So that is what is our internal target is.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 sales volumes up 10.1% YoY; pharma volumes up 26.3%, food & FMCG up 23.7%, paints up ~9%, lubricants down 12.3%
items.quote: I'm very glad to inform you that the sales volumes of the company in the Q2 have gone up by 10.1% compared to last Q2. And profits have jumped by 36%, resulting in a very healthy EBITDA per kg of INR46.5.

items.statement: October demand very strong, best month-on-month growth so far
items.quote: Yes, the demand is pretty good in October, and the numbers compared to the last October, I'm saying, is very satisfying. Maybe it is too early to talk about it, but definitely, it's much better than what -- on a month-on-month growth-wise, October stands out as the best month so far.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA per kg INR46.6 vs INR40.6 in H1 FY26, up ~15%
items.quote: I think, as I said, our EBITDA has shot up a clean 15%, 18% in the last 2 quarters from INR40.6 last H1 to INR46.6 in the current H1.

items.statement: Pharma targeting INR50+ crores turnover in FY27 and INR70-75 crores in FY28
items.quote: And going this rate, we'll be able to maintain our projection of INR50 crores plus in the full year this year and probably INR70 crores, INR75 crores for the next financial year.

items.statement: Vibe specialty closures targeting INR50-60 crores top line in 2 years with ~30% EBITDA
items.quote: Yes, 2 years down the line, we should be able to see at least $5 million to $6 million, let's say, INR50 crores to INR60 crores top line, with a very strong EBITDA of somewhere around 30%.

items.statement: Iodex balm packs commercial production starting Dec/Jan; 3 new MNC products launching Dec/Jan
items.quote: And another good news is that Iodex project, which has been on hold for more than 3 years, has been cleared with some changes, and the chain molds are also getting ready by December -- November, and probably in December or Jan, we'll be starting commercial production of Iodex balm packs.

items.statement: Ophthalmic eye dropper packs molds ready by Jan, commercial production by March; revenues from Q1 FY28
items.quote: In case of ophthalmic eye dropper packs, we have already ordered the molds, and some molds are being made in -house. And I think by January, we'll be having the molds ready. And then trial runs would take at least 2 months. So by March, our product wil l be ready for testing and commercial production.

items.statement: Semiconductor tray discussions with 3-4 top companies; meaningful revenues expected FY28-29 onwards
items.quote: And accordingly, we are getting prepared to be there when the semiconductor products start in India, which is expected to be in a bigger way in '28, '29 onwards.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected INR75-80 crores; INR60 crores spent in first 7 months
items.quote: And coming to the investments, as I said, investments have been under, I would say, lower levels compared to the last 3, 4 years, and they should be ending up somewhere around INR75 crores for the full year. Already INR60 crores has been spent in the first 7 months.

items.statement: Vibe Phase 1 investment INR10-15 crores for molds and machines to reach INR40-50 crores turnover
items.quote: So based on that, the investment will be in the tune of around INR10 crores to INR15 crores in the Phase 1, which will be sufficient to give us a turnover close to INR40 crores to INR50 crores.

items.statement: Current capacity ~66,900 tons, reaching ~70,000 tons by start of FY28; targeting 50,000-51,000 tons volume in FY28
items.quote: 66,900 will definitely become 70,000 by beginning of the next financial year. And that, again, we'll be aiming at least somewhere close to 50,000 tons from somewhere around 42,000 last year, and probably this year we may end up around 46,000, 47,000.

items.statement: IML volumes 77% of total (up from 77% last Q2); IML value share 78.25% (up from 76%)
items.quote: Yes. IML volumes, I think are close to, one second, 77% now and non -IML, that's labelled products, and non -labelled products are 22.68%.

items.statement: Successfully passing through raw material price increases; clients accept hikes as packaging is non-fungible
items.quote: If the clients are not willing to participate in the price rise and they want to stick on to their old price, you would not see this kind of performance from Mold -Tek. This is the ability of Mold -Tek to get th e price rise actually faster than previously agreed terms.

items.statement: Finance cost as % of revenue rose from 4.1% to ~5% due to higher raw material prices; modeling 4.5-4.7% for FY27
items.quote: But if you look at it as a percentage, it moved up earlier from 4.1% to almost 5% now. And probably it will come down back to 4%, 4.2% in the future of the total revenue, maybe once the raw material prices come down. But as it looks, unless there is a sudden complete peace in West Asia, the raw material prices are not expected to drop in a hurry. So for the year, we are factoring almost 4.5%, 4.7%

items.statement: Inventory holding ~52 days (25 days RM, 25-27 days SFG+FG); no 4-month inventory
items.quote: Even if you consider the SFG, FG and raw material put together, it will be maximum 1 month, because they're very voluminous. And our carrying time is 52 days. Now currently, it is 52 days because the raw material, maybe half of it, let's say, 25 days is raw material. SFG and FG will be remaining 25, 27 days.

items.statement: Targeting operating cash flow of INR215 crores in FY27 (double INR107 crores FY26); expect cash surplus after INR75-80 crores capex, interest, tax, dividends
items.quote: We are aiming at doubling the cash flow from INR107 crores to INR215 crores, as I mentioned in the beginning of the year. So I'm still standing on that.

items.statement: Long-term debt expected to start declining by end of FY27 due to cash surplus
items.quote: So this time will be a cash surplus, and there may not be -- you may see the long -term debt or debt as a overall start coming down at least in this year -- end of this year.

items.statement: Exports growing steadily but not multiples due to freight costs; Egypt pharma client visit in Dec after CPHI show
items.quote: We are now, in fact, in Decem ber, expecting a client for our pharma products from Egypt, and that is a big opportunity, and they have already tested our samples and approved them.

items.statement: Growth shifting to lighter, higher-value food/FMCG/pharma/Vibe products; volume growth understates value growth
items.quote: So even if the volume growth looks 10%, in my opinion, it's equivalent to 14%, 15% growth of last 3 years, because those days, paints used to be a major contributor to our top line and bottom line. But nowadays, slowly, food and pharma and tomorrow Vibe will start contributing to the growth.

items.statement: Adding 2-3 big pharma clients per quarter; Panipat plant adding food/FMCG clients; Qpack new major detergent player order from Nov
items.quote: Every quarter, we are adding 2 or 3 big hands. And going this rate, we'll be able to maintain our projection of INR50 crores plus in the full year this year and probably INR70 crores, INR75 crores for the next financial year.

items.statement: Raw material price rises do not phase out competitors; Mold-Tek's edge from product range expansion, consolidation, cost efficiencies
items.quote: No, I don't think they -- nobody will be phasing out at any stage because, as I said, whatever applies to Mold-Tek will -- I mean, more or less applies to other molders also. It's basically our ability to expand our product range, consolidate our operations and bring efficiencies in the costing is what really brought us a better bottom line compared to maybe compared to others.

items.statement: IML volume share 77%, value share 78.25% (KPI)
items.quote: Yes, value is 78%, up from 76%, 78.25%.

items.statement: Manufacturing EBITDA target maintained at INR5-7 per litre annually
items.quote: these developments support our confidence in maintaining the INR5 to INR7 per litre annual EBITDA targets, whilst recognizing that actual allocations, offtake and input prices will determine the outcome.

items.statement: R&O EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 16-18%
items.quote: So we've always maintained the sort of guidance on R&O margins of between 16% and 18% at EBITDA levels. So we are very much within that zone.

items.statement: QIP proceeds of INR200 crores used for debt repayment and consumer business growth
items.quote: INR200 crores was the raise, INR150 crores or approximately INR150 crores has been used to pay down debt and the balance amount is currently liquid.

items.statement: Debt reduced by INR200 crores between March and September; debt-to-EBITDA improved to 2x
items.quote: By September end, INR155 crores had been utilized towards repayment of long-term debt, contributing to an overall INR200 crores reduction in the debt between March and September.

items.statement: Operating cash flow INR139 crores in H1 FY27 vs INR270 crores in H1 FY26 due to higher receivables
items.quote: Cash flow from operating activities for H1 FY27 stood at INR139 crores compared to INR270 crores in H1 FY26. The moderation in operating cash flow is primarily attributable to an increase in trade receivables driven by higher business volumes during the period.

items.statement: Interest savings estimated at INR6 crores in H2 FY27, INR11-12 crores annualized
items.quote: We estimate interest savings of approximately INR6 crores in H2 FY27, equivalent to INR11 crores to INR12 crores on an annualized profile basis.

items.statement: Expect meaningfully higher capacity utilization in ethanol year 2026-27 due to lower sugar ethanol availability
items.quote: In addition to this, there is a very important aspect that is we are expecting higher capacity utilizations going forward because of a lower sugar ethanol demand next year.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization 80-85%, expected to be meaningfully higher in coming year
items.quote: So we've been consistently between 80% and 85%. And I believe in the year to come, that number is going to be meaningfully higher.

items.statement: Rice prices INR27-28/kg and maize INR23-24/kg at end of Q2; up from Q1 levels of INR21-22/kg maize and INR24-25/kg rice
items.quote: I think September end, we should have finished -- should have ended September at about INR27, INR28 per kilo of rice and about INR22 -- it's about INR23, INR24 for maize.

items.statement: Maize ethanol share of total ethanol sales was 60% in H1; may drop to 30% going forward as mix shifts to FCI and broken rice
items.quote: On total sale of manufacturing for H1 on maize is almost 60% on the ethanol part.

items.statement: Expect 900 crore litres grain ethanol demand from OMCs, 100-150 crore litres from chemical industry, 300-400 crore litres from beverage industry
items.quote: So we are expecting a demand of about 900 crores litres for grain-based ethanol from OMCs for grain-based ethanol. There is about 100 crores to 150 crores litres, which the chemical industry uses. And there's about 300 crores to 400 crore s litres that the beverage industry uses

items.statement: Expect much higher volumes in next ethanol year starting November
items.quote: Volumes are going to be great. We are going to have significant volumes.

items.statement: P&A business now has 5 profitable states out of 12; expanding to 5 duty-free channels and 2 new states in FY27
items.quote: We now have 5 profitable states across our 12 market P&A footprint, while net sales value trends have stabilized sequentially. Our focus is to deepen established markets and expand selectively where we see a clear path to profitable scale. Our next phase of expansion includes 5 additional duty-free channels and entry into 2 new states during FY27.

items.statement: R&O growth driven by UP; Rajasthan growing at mid-single digit volumes with 4-6% annual price increases
items.quote: R&O Rajasthan has been growing at the rates it was in the past, which is small single-digit sort of, mid-single-digit volume growth. A lot of the balance growth, in fact, entirely the balance growth has come from UP.

items.statement: Rajasthan market share stable at ~50% of private sector (60% of market); state-owned company holds 40%
items.quote: And within that 60%, we have about a 50% market share. So given how entrenched we are, there is limited room to grow market share unless the state market share reduces.

items.statement: Delhi allocation doubled but industry volumes significantly lower; re-evaluating Delhi plans
items.quote: whereas we've got an allocation of a larger amount, you are right, but we are seeing that the industry sale volume is much lower, significantly lower than what they had envisaged. So given that Delhi is currently not a business which is meaningful, not in teresting. So we are sort of re- evaluating our plans for Delhi currently

items.statement: Haryana contributing but not growing meaningfully; West Bengal zero currently, re-entering next financial year
items.quote: Haryana contributes. West Bengal is zero currently. We will be re-entering Bengal in the next financial year. Haryana is contributing, but not growing as meaningfully as UP.

items.statement: Packaging material inflation due to petroleum prices impacted margins; Rajasthan price increases offset this almost entirely
items.quote: the one thing that's played out this year, which is unique and not prevalent in the last or the preceding years is the packing material inflation due to the whole oil scenario in the world. A lot of our raw materials are dependent on petroleum prices. So that has impacted our margins to some extent. Of course, the price increase in Rajasthan helps that -- help mitigate that almost entirely.

items.statement: P&A EBITDA loss narrowed to INR0.2 crores in Q2, near breakeven; H1 revenue INR114.9 crores, volumes 0.88 million cases
items.quote: EBITDA loss narrowed down to INR0.2 crores, bringing the segment very close to breakeven.

items.statement: R&O revenue grew 14% YoY to INR242.8 crores, volumes up 16% to 4.24 million cases, EBITDA up 4% to INR38.6 crores in Q2
items.quote: Revenue grew 14% year-on-year to INR242.8 crores, while volumes increased 16% to 4.24 million cases. EBITDA grew 4% to INR38.6 crores.

items.statement: Manufacturing Q2 revenue INR455 crores, volumes 55.26 million litres, EBITDA INR25.4 crores, EBITDA/litre INR4.6
items.quote: Manufacturing revenue in Q2 was INR455 crores with volumes of 55.26 million litres and EBITDA of INR25.4 crores. EBITDA per litre came at INR4.6 a litre, reflecting higher grain and fuel costs.

items.statement: H1 manufacturing EBITDA INR5.59/litre; trailing 12-month INR6.6/litre
items.quote: For H1, EBITDA was INR5.59 per litre, whilst trailing 12-month figures stood at approximately INR6.6 per litre.

items.statement: Power and fuel cost INR6.3/kg in Q2, up 10-11% QoQ; total cost INR60.43 crores
items.quote: This quarter, it was INR6.3 per kg, which last quarter, it's an inflation of 10% to 11%.

items.statement: Completed INR200 crores QIP during quarter; welcomed new institutional shareholders
items.quote: We completed our INR200 crores QIP during the quarter. We welcome our new institutional shareholders and particularly value the continued support of existing investors who participated in the fundraise.

items.statement: Ethanol supply year 2026-27 begins November; reduced sugar ethanol availability creates opportunity for grain-based producers
items.quote: Looking ahead to the ethanol supply year '26-'27, which is scheduled to begin later in November, reduced availability of sugar-based ethanol is expected to create greater procurement opportunities for grain-based producers.

items.statement: FCI broken grain norm reduced from 25% to 10% from Kharif marketing season 2026-27, increasing broken rice availability
items.quote: We also expect enhanced broken rice availability following the reduction in permissible broken grain content in raw rice from 25% to 10% being implemen ted progressively from the Kharif marketing season '26-'27

items.statement: ENA exports ~5 million litres in H1; not tracked as separate business but part of manufacturing basket
items.quote: My sense would be that H1, there would be about 5 million litres or so would have been the exports, just to give some sense to the numbers, that's H1.

items.statement: Risk in Rajasthan is staying ahead of consumer preferences and new product launches; no meaningful risk seen currently
items.quote: So the risk really for us is to be on the ball with regard to new products and changing consumer preferences. And up until now, I think we've done an okay job with that. And yes, so I mean, beyond that, I don't really see a meaningful risk in Rajasthan.

items.statement: Large industry capacity exists but Globus has long-term OMC offtake agreements at all facilities except Bihar
items.quote: Aside from our Bihar unit, Globus Spirits has long-term offtake agreements at all of its facilities, Bihar and -- pardon me, aside from Bihar, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, where in any case, where in Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, there is no ethanol capacit y, all other units have long -term offtake agreements

items.statement: P&A growth strategy prioritizes growth over profitability; 5 profitable states fund investment in 7 other states
items.quote: So it's a conscious decision to chase growth given the strength of the balance sheet and the strength of our cash flows.

items.statement: UP R&O margins lower than Rajasthan but within 15-18% range; UP on journey to optimal profitability
items.quote: So Nitin, I mean, Rajasthan is definitely a little bit higher on that range and UP is a little bit lower on that range. So that's the spread. I mean there's no significant concern on the UP profitability.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at 10% to 15%
items.quote: We continue to maintain our FY27 revenue growth guidance to 10% to 15%.

items.statement: FY27 planned capex of INR550 crores to INR600 crores for product registrations
items.quote: FY27, we aim to increase product registrations with a planned capex of INR550 crores to INR600 crores, backed by strong pipeline that reflects our resilience and growth focus

items.statement: Total product registrations at 3,044 with 946 applications in pipeline as of 30th September 2026
items.quote: Our total product registr ations stood at 3,044 as on 30 th September 2026. Additionally, 946 applications for product registrations are in the pipeline

items.statement: Q2 FY27 gross margin expanded 140 bps to 35.9%, EBITDA margin up 70 bps to 15.6%
items.quote: Gross margins expanded by around 140 basis points to 35.9%, while EBITDA grew 18% to INR164 crores, taking our EB ITDA margin to 15.6

items.statement: H1 FY27 gross margin 36.3% up 130 bps, EBITDA margin 16.1% up 140 bps
items.quote: Gross margin stood at 36.3% in H1 FY27 as against 35% in H1 FY26, an increase of 130 basis points. EBITDA grew by 22% to INR343 crores with EBITDA margin at 16.1% as against 14.7% in H1 FY26, an increase of 140 basis points.

items.statement: NAFTA revenue grew ~30% YoY with significantly better margins; LATAM agrochemical revenue up over 80%
items.quote: NAFTA was the standout of this quarter Revenue from the region grew about 30% year-on-year with signif icantly better margins. LATAM also did well with agrochemical revenue up by over 80

items.statement: Europe saw slight moderation due to extended heat and drought; distributors cautious on restocking
items.quote: Europe, our largest market, saw a slight moderation this quarter coming off an exceptionally strong financial year '26. The weather challenges were highlighted last quarter continued through the September quarter with extended heat and drought conditions in parts of Central a nd Eastern Europe

items.statement: Expect Europe recovery in second half which is seasonally stronger period
items.quote: And as conditions normalize, we e xpect the region to do well in the second half, which is seasonally our stronger

items.statement: Q2 revenue growth driven by increased prices, positive forex, improved product mix of 18.3% with volume degrowth of 5.1%
items.quote: the 13% revenue growth was on account of increased prices, positive forex impact and improved product mix of 18.3% . With a volume degrowth of minus 5.1%

items.statement: H1 revenue growth driven by increased prices, positive forex, improved product mix of 14.5% with volume degrowth of 3.5%
