items.quote: For the half year, the 11% revenue growth was on ac count of an increased prices, positive forex impact and improved product mix of 14.5% (Errata: Actual number to be read as positive 14.5%) with a volume degrowth of minus 3.5

items.statement: Non-agrochemical 68% YoY growth driven by conveyor belts and rubber belts for transportation and material handling
items.quote: Mainly because of conveyor belts, rubber belts, which are used for transportation of goods and material handling.

items.statement: Non-agrochemical demand surge due to stock replenishment after international market uncertainties and transportation problems
items.quote: Sir, this is purely depending upon the demand because of a lot of uncertainties in the international markets and problems of transportation and other things. People were waiting for the things to improve. And all of a sudden, they found that they are running short of their stocks, and they started buying at a faster speed.

items.statement: Registration portfolio: Europe 1,701, NAFTA 333, LATAM 760, Rest of World 250; Pipeline: Europe 548, NAFTA 103, LATAM 155, Rest of World 140
items.quote: So total registration on 30th September is INR3,044. That includes Europe, 1,701; NAFTA 333, LATAM 760 and rest of w orld is 250. And in pipeline, out of 946, Europe is 548, NAFTA is 103, LATAM is 155 and rest of world is 140

items.statement: Registration capex unpredictable due to government authority requirements and arbitration processes
items.quote: Sir, I have said in every conference call that the process of r egistration is absolutely unpredictable. And the things change at the last moment, the go vernment authorities come out with new requirements at the last moment and the approval proce ss also gets delayed because the authorities are not able to meet so frequently and many thi ngs which are totally beyond anybody's guesswork or plannin

items.statement: Q2 FY27 geographic gross margins: Europe 41%, NAFTA ~40%, LATAM 14%, Rest of World 31%, overall 35.9%
items.quote: European region, our gross margins have been 41%, NAFTA region also around 40%, LATA M 14% and rest of the world 31%, overall, 35.9

items.statement: NAFTA margins driven by good demand and limited availability; considered sustainable
items.quote: We feel they are sustainable.

items.statement: Tariffs not affecting agrochemical business; easy to pass on tariff increases to customers due to registration restrictions
items.quote: Tariffs are not affecting agrochemical business at all. Because these products are not freely tradable, not freely available and not freely marketable. Every product needs to be registered and if in case of trading companies like us, we are restricted to source it only from an approved source which is approved by the authorities and a customer has not much choice.

items.statement: Pricing environment improving but speed below expectations; still far below pre-COVID levels
items.quote: It is improving. The speed of improvement is still not as per our expectation, but it is improving. It is still far down compared to the pre-COVID days, but still, it is not impacting the general business so much.

items.statement: Red Sea/Hormuz shipping disruptions causing extra time and freight cost increases but not affecting performance
items.quote: See, Hormuz channel. It is not affecting us much at all because our goods are travelling to western, I mean all around the globe on the western side you kn ow. So it's only taking extra time. The cost of freight is also increasing but it is not affecting the performance

items.statement: Euro-Dollar cross-currency impact unpredictable but in steady range last 3-4 months; not badly affected
items.quote: See, we have an impact of this cross-currency exchange rates, b ut these things are also very unpredictable. It is almost in the steady range in the last 3-4 months. Earlier, the Euro-Dollar exchange rate was more favourable to us, but the things will get normalized. And another thing is we have no control, but we have not been affected so badly by these exchange

items.statement: Working capital days improved to 70 days as of 30th September 2026, down 28 days from March 2026
items.quote: Working capital days stood at 70 days as at 30th September '26, showing an improvement by 28 days as compared to March '26.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with cash and liquid investments of INR846 crores as of 30th September 2026
items.quote: The company continues to remain a debt-free company with cash; bank liquid investments stood at INR846 crores as on 30th September 2026.

items.statement: H2 gross margins expected to hold or go up from current levels
items.quote: Sir, they are expected to hold or go up.

items.statement: Depreciation and amortization increased to INR100 crores per quarter from INR70-75 crores; leading indicator for future revenue growth from newly capitalized registrations amortized over 5 years
items.quote: Yes, I think what you are saying it is leading to that our amor tizations over last 2 quarters is more compared to last year same period and this will continue e ven for balance H2 with this whatever we have already capitalized and spent on intangible assets, on our product registration capex and amortized over a period of 5 years. That is the amortization policy. The second question is, is it lea

items.statement: Quarterly operating cost expected to remain between ₹680 crore and ₹700 crore over the next few quarters
items.quote: What we are saying is that, over the next few quarters, my cost will not increase in proportion to what it was doing earlier. It will remain between ₹680 crore and ₹700 crore.

items.statement: Invested ₹100 crore in AI business over the last year to build MSOCK and Purple Fabric internally
items.quote: We mentioned last year that we are investing ₹100 crore in the AI business. That was a clearly self-identified number. Instead of keeping that cash for investors, we are investing it back into the AI business.

items.statement: MSOCK, Purple Fabric, and eMACH.ai are now three independent product offerings that can go to market separately

items.statement: Employee cost increase due to actuarial valuation impact, ~10% organization-wide hike, and new sales force footprint addition

items.statement: H1 FY27 gross margin up 390 bps to 65.2%; EBITDA (ex-other income) up 20.5% to INR 107.7 cr

items.statement: Solar Phase 3 savings INR 30 cr/yr EBITDA (Phase 1&2 gave INR 16-17 cr in FY26); Phase 4 adds INR 12 cr/yr from Q4 FY27

items.statement: Hydra two double-wall lines running >80% utilisation; third line to add portfolio breadth from Q4 FY27

items.quote: Premiumization across categories, even in our appliances, whether it's a Vita rich or it is the hand blenders or even in the cookware segment, we have categories which the mix have been good for us.

items.statement: Not competing on price; differentiated quality positioning; appliances CAGR >25% despite 51 competitors

items.quote: The total amount of government incentives is roughly INR 55 crores. Out of that INR 1.2 crores is what we have received and the balance will be receiving in the subsequent years every year.

items.quote: The sequential improvement in profitability was partly driven by the absence of the one-time upfront minimum guarantee payment made in Q1 to support the expansion of our global lounge business. No similar one-off expense was incurred during Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Bank balances and liquid investments increased to INR 187.8 crores as of 30th September 2026 from INR 148.9 crores as of 31st March 2026
items.quote: As of 30th September 2026, bank balances and liquid investments stood at INR 187.8 crores, compared with INR 148.9 crores as of 31st March 2026, while Net Worth stood at INR 290.1 crores against INR 313.8 crores at the end of last fiscal year.

items.statement: Non-airport lounge services accounted for more than one-third of topline in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Importantly, non-airport lounge services continued to make a meaningful contribution, accounting for more than one-third of our topline during Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Global lounge network exceeds 1,100 lounges with focus on South-East Asia expansion
items.quote: Global lounges remain an important growth engine for DreamFolks. With a network of more than 1,100 lounges, we have built a strong foundation for further international expansion.

items.statement: Railway lounge coverage across 100% of railway lounges in India with new addition at Nashik
items.quote: Our railway lounge business continues to offer significant growth potential, supported by our nationwide network coverage across 100% of railway lounges in India. During the quarter, we further strengthened this presence with the addition of a new railway lounge at Nashik.

items.statement: DF Club Membership now live on loyalty platforms of multiple major banks creating additional distribution channel
items.quote: A significant development during the quarter is that DF Club Membership is now live on the loyalty platforms of multiple major banks. This creates an additional distribution channel for our membership offering, enabling us to reach customers through established bank loyalty platforms that are already part of their engagement ecosystem.

items.statement: Launched DreamFolks Club Nagavalli Wilderness Estate spread across approximately 30 acres including 25-acre golf course with 37 cottages
items.quote: An important milestone in this journey has been the launch of DreamFolks Club Nagavalli Wilderness Estate, our private club set in the Eastern Ghats on the Odisha –Andhra Pradesh border. Spread across approximately 30 acres, including a 25-acre golf course, the Estate brings together golf, nature, adventure and the living culture of the region.

items.statement: Priorities for rest of FY27: deepen distribution and adoption of launched services, drive programme activity across global network, scale railway business through Ten11, expand lifestyle offerings through banking and loyalty partners
items.quote: As we move through the rest of FY27, our priorities are to deepen distribution and adoption of the services already launched, drive greater programme activity across our global network, scale the railway business through Ten11 and expand lifestyle offering s through banking and loyalty partners

items.statement: Will continue investing in technology and operating capabilities to support growth while maintaining focus on execution, improving contribution and revenue absorption, and disciplined capital allocation
items.quote: Alongside this, we will continue investing in the technology and operating capabilities required to support growth, while maintaining a strong focus on execution, improving contribution and revenue absorption, and disciplined capital allocation.

items.statement: Managing liquidity prudently with focus on aligning pace of investment with business development, monitoring service-level economics, phasing capex, and maintaining visibility on operating cash flows
items.quote: We continue to manage our liquidity prudently, with a focus on aligning the pace of investment with business development. This involves closely monitoring service -level economics, phasing capital expenditure where appropriate and maintaining visibility on operating ca sh flows

items.statement: FY27 consolidated sales growth guided at 10-12%, India Engineering at mid-to-high teens
items.quote: To sum it up, I want to reaffirm the previous growth guidance given in the earlier calls that it is to say, on a full year basis, FY 2027, we should achieve a sales growth in mid- to high teens in India, while on a consolidated basis, it could be anywhere between 10% to 12%.

items.statement: India Engineering volume growth targeted at 12-15% globally
items.quote: Yes. So we are in general, planning on a global basis, about 12% to 15% volume growth is what we are working towards.

items.statement: Cage segment expected to grow at least 20% in FY27
items.quote: we expect a significant ramp -up in sales in this segment in second half of financial year 2027, which should result into an overall annual growth of at least 20% in the current financial year in this segment.

items.statement: Bushings segment targeting 30% growth in FY27 and INR300 crore annual sales in 3-4 years
items.quote: I'm confident that we should be able to attain about 30% growth in current financial year in this segment, aided by good demand visibility from key windmill gearbox manufacturing companies.

items.statement: Stampings segment targeting over 30% growth in FY27 and INR300 crore annual sales in 4 years
items.quote: Thus, we are seeing a fairly confident of seeing over 30% sales growth in this segment in this current financial year compared to revenue sales of about INR72 crores we achieved in FY26.

items.statement: Solar business revenue guided at INR150-200 crore for FY27 and FY28
items.quote: Similar what we have given in the range of INR150 crores to INR200 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected at 17-18% for H2 FY27
items.quote: At a consol level for Engineering business also, we expect it to remain in the range of around 17% to 18%.

items.statement: India Engineering EBITDA margin expected around 22% steady state
items.quote: At the India level, we expect it to continue in around 22% for the EBITDA margin profile.

items.statement: Total capex of INR220 crore over 12-15 months for Advantek and China expansions
items.quote: 18 months capex, we have already announced is of around INR220 crores, out of which, as you rightly said, first half is around INR70 crores plus.

items.statement: Advantek total capex expected around INR350 crore including building and infrastructure
items.quote: we ex pect capex of around INR350 crores plus at an overall Advantek level, out of which building and infrastructure would be around INR100 crores plus spend

items.statement: Advantek capex loan of around INR250 crore planned
items.quote: And I see that total capex loan we will take is around INR250 crores in Advantek.

items.statement: Maintenance capex at consolidated level around INR25-30 crore annually
items.quote: Harsha at a consol level, I will say, around INR25 crores to INR30 crores at a console level because we also need some of the operational or maintenance capex at China Romania site.

items.statement: Advantek expansion for Bushings, Stampings and large Cages on track, production in next few quarters
items.quote: Thus the Advantek expansion project involving substantial expansion of capacities to manufacture Bushings, Stampings as well as large-size Cages is on track. It should commence production in next few quarters.

items.statement: New resourcing outsourcing project commercial sales to start Q3-Q4 FY27, peak run rate INR75 crore/year
items.quote: At peak level, the sales can reach a run rate of around INR75 crores per year.

items.statement: Two additional resourcing projects from Europe and North America, first in FY27-28, second in FY28-29
items.quote: And also, we are working on a couple of other resourcing, outsourcing projects from Europe and North America markets.

items.statement: Strong demand traction for Cages in India industrial and automotive, and exports to Europe, US, Japan
items.quote: we have witnessed a decent demand traction, both from industrial as well as automotive segment in India. Similarly, on the export front, we have witnessed continued strong demand coming largely in industrial segment from key geographies of Europe, U.S. as well as Japan and other countries.

items.statement: China growth moderated to 5-7% for current portfolio, acceleration expected with new capacity in Q3 FY28
items.quote: So in general, we are seeing a moderate growth for our current portfolio and current business, about 5%, 7% is what we estimate.

items.statement: Romania downsizing strategy to arrest operating losses by end of FY27, focus on finished Cage sales
items.quote: We have internally worked out a strategy of downsizing the operations and correspondingly also reducing the operating cost. However, we will continue to focus on increasing the sales of finished Cages out of our Romania facility.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin 18.6% vs 15.9% YoY, driven by mix, pass-through, operational efficiency and lower solar share
items.quote: it is both and top on to that, not only both, I will say operational efficiency also has contributed. And at an overall level, the solar contribution is lower for the month, including on the cost side as well as the revenue side.

items.statement: Brass price increase partially passed through in last 6 months, further pass-through depends on metal price movement
items.quote: There has been some pass -through because of -- we have seen last six months increase in the brass prices, which is copper and zinc. So some portion of that has already been passed through.

items.statement: Approximately 4-5% of H1 FY27 25% growth attributed to material pass-through, rest volume growth
items.quote: Our approximate estimate is that about 4%, 5% of it would be linked to a material pass-through related thing and rest of it is real volume growth.

items.statement: Capturing large share of incremental Cage business from SKF, Timken capacity expansions
items.quote: We believe that we are capturing a very large sh are of that incremental business. And we are seeing good traction in the market for that

items.statement: Japan-based customer revenue grew 15% QoQ to INR24 crore, driven by delayed projects coming online
items.quote: While revenue from Japanese customer was around INR24 crores with a growth of 15% against the last quarter.

items.statement: NRB Bharuch facility demand for SRB/CRB localization factored into guidance
items.quote: Yes. It is all factored. We are seeing positive demand coming from that, and it is all factored into our guidance.

items.statement: No incremental borrowings assumed for FY28, comfortable at current debt level backed by lower rates and subsidies
items.quote: So we do not, as of now, assuming incremental borrowings in FY28. What we have alrea dy taken is for our Advantek expansion plans and our China Phase 2 expansion plan

items.statement: Consolidated working capital at 135 days vs 139 days YoY and 116 days QoQ
items.quote: Overall working capital at our consolidated level is around 135 days against 139 days in the same quarter last year and 116 days in our previous quarter.

items.statement: H1 FY27 exports from India at INR280 crore vs FY26 full year INR480 crore
items.quote: export from India have remained quite strong with our H1 exports at around INR280 crores against annual export of INR480 crores achieved last year.

items.statement: Bushings revenue INR42 crore (+26% QoQ), Stampings INR23 crore (+19% QoQ), LSB INR14 crore (+35% QoQ) in Q2 FY27
items.quote: For the last quarter, revenue from Bushings was around INR42 crores, Stampings was around INR23 crores and LSB was around INR14 crores, which has grown by 26%, 19% and 35%, respectively, compared to the previous quarter.

items.statement: Q3 historically soft due to calendar year-end buying slowdown by international buyers
items.quote: historically, Q3 tends to be a little soft in terms of demand considering the fact th at almost all large international buyers whose accounting year calendar year ends in calendar year, so it tends to show a little bit slow

items.statement: Romania downsizing may involve one-off costs, details to be announced next quarter
items.quote: We are in the process of working all the nitty gritties and details. Please give us one more quarter, and we will come with all the specific answers.

items.statement: Metal price volatility remains ongoing challenge for margin predictability
items.quote: it is done 100% because it's a very much ongoing thing and different customer has a different time lines. So definitely, we see if the metal price will settle, this margin will either improve or will remain at the same

items.statement: Bromine volume guidance for FY27 maintained at 18,000-20,000 tons, expected at lower end
items.quote: No, as of now, we are expecting to be at the guidance, Sanjesh, albeit at the lower end of the guidance.

items.statement: Salt volume guidance for FY27 at 4.5 million tons, management confident of 4.2-4.3 million tons
items.quote: We are still pretty much working on that number, right? Because that's what we have given as an indication earlier. We are still very much focused on getting that done.

items.statement: Bromine full-year average yield guidance maintained at INR300 per kg minimum
items.quote: we kind of said that we expect the year to be at a INR300 average yield for the full year, and at the minimum every quarter. We will still remain strong of belief that we'll hold that number.

items.statement: Core business capex within depreciation curve, debt at 0.6-0.7x on 3-year window
items.quote: I think with the exception of the flame retardant project, I think the rest of it, our capital spend will be remained within our depreciation curve. And we will probably be at 0.6 to 0.7 debt.

items.statement: Bromine debottlenecking on schedule for 25,000 tons run rate next year
items.quote: Our debottlenecking program on Bromine capacity continue to be as per schedule. We had given earlier guidance on the fact that we expect next year to be at a run rate of around 25,000 tons, and we are on schedule there.

items.statement: Semiconductor plant construction started in Odisha, 18-24 month timeline, EC received mid-October
items.quote: During the quarter, we have obviously achieved a key milestone, the start of our civil work of the project in Odisha. As I said earlier, we expect construction to be around 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Brine field expansion adding 8,000 hectares in two phases, first 4,000 hectares completed and operational by end of quarter
items.quote: Our total brine field, when it is fully expanded, will be 24,000 hectares. We had 16,000 developed, and the expansion is about developing another 8,000 in 2 phases, 4,000 and 4,000.

items.statement: PVC demand weakness causing caustic soda volume deferrals, rebound expected this quarter
items.quote: But we do expect that there will be a rebound in this quarter in PVC pricing, and that should help provide a fillip to the industry, and should actually start helping see some more firmness in our order schedules.

items.statement: Agriculture demand tepid due to monsoon impact on agrochemicals and brominated derivatives
items.quote: The agriculture sector, which is another big demand driver for us, continues to be fairly tepid in demand due to the impact of the monsoons.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals demand strong, especially semiconductor chemicals
items.quote: Demand for specialty chemicals, especially for semiconductor chemicals, remains strong.

items.statement: Bromine cost inflation mitigated through consumption efficiency and productivity improvements
items.quote: The inflation in cost of sulfur, hydrated lime, and other elements has largely been mitigated through improvements in consumption efficiency and productivity, and we will continue to focus on those for the remainder of this year to ensure that we are operating at optimum margin levels.

items.statement: Acume EBITDA loss of INR1 crore in Q2 due to unfavorable mix, one-time costs, inventory revaluation; H1 EBITDA positive
items.quote: While we had strong volume growth, we did have some unfavourable mix impact because of the lower demand for organic compounds, some one-time period costs, and a one-time inventory revaluation, which had an adverse impact on earnings for the quarter. And for the quarter, we reported an EBITDA loss of around INR1 crores.

items.statement: HSD prices rose from INR87/liter in Q2 FY26 to INR136/liter in Q2 FY27; coal and propanol up 40% YoY; sulfur prices more than doubled
items.quote: HSD prices were approximately INR87 per liter for industrial HSD in Q2 FY26, continued to rise sharply, and in Q2 FY27, they averaged around INR136. Prices of coal and propanol have increased by around 40% year-on-year.

items.statement: Transportation costs increased 15-30% due to road diversions; largely mitigated with new road operational from early October
items.quote: Transportation costs alone, which have probably gone up by around 15% to 30% in the range based on which route, port, et cetera. That should more or less get mitigated this quarter, right? Because of the route change.

items.statement: Industrial salt order book solid but shipments impacted by PVC/caustic soda market deferrals
items.quote: Despite a solid order book, shipments were impacted by deferrals of major or multiple orders, largely due to the state of the overall PVC and caustic soda market.

items.statement: Bromine export order boards very strong with stable pricing; domestic demand impacted by agro slowdown and pharma muted trends
items.quote: Bromine remains kind of a mixed bag. Our export order boards are very strong, and we continue to see a pretty stable pricing environment there. The domestic demand, though, has been impacted by slowdown in agro and muted trends in pharma.

items.statement: Acume commercialized 4 new products including NPBr for pharma and IPBr; 8 new molecules under development for H2 release
items.quote: During the quarter, we have commercialized 4 new products, including NPBr for pharma, and IPBr, and 8 new molecules are under further development, which should get relea sed through the second half of this year

items.statement: Salt customer base expansion succeeding with new orders from Vietnam and Oman
items.quote: during this quarter, we did see some success with some new orders from these markets, especially from Vietnam and Oman.

items.statement: Salt business 80% long-term contracts (18-24 months), 10-20% spot; spot share higher currently due to reschedules
items.quote: I think most of our salt business is long-term contracts. These are contracts which are essentially set up on an 18 to 24 months window. That is around 80% of our business.

items.statement: Exports 79% of revenue in Q2 FY27 vs 75% YoY; Acume Asian exports 15% of volume
items.quote: Exports comprised 79% of our revenue compared to 75% in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: SOP feedstock throughput behind plan; KTMS production lower in H1, ramping up in H2
items.quote: We have also had lower KTMS production, right, in the year, in the first half of the year. We are trying to ramp that up in the second half.

items.statement: Semiconductor project INR1,000-1,100 crores investment largely debt-funded, front-loaded over FY28-FY29
items.quote: But broadly, the INR1,000 crores plus of funding which we will invest into the business will largely come from debt on our balance sheet in the near term.

items.statement: Chemical business ROCE improved from 15.5% to 16.5% in H1 YoY; overall business ROCE from 11.1% to 12.2%
items.quote: ROCE for the chemical business alone grew from around 15.5% in H1 last year to 16.5% in H1 this year.

items.statement: Key risks: winter impact on bromine recovery, fuel cost increases (WTI/Brent trending up), volume uncertainty from PVC/caustic soda deferrals
items.quote: Probably the biggest one is just we get into winter, and we do see some impact at times because of that on recovery across our entire system. So that is an operational risk, which is there. I think fuel costs could jump further.

items.statement: Offgrid Energy zinc bromide battery pilot started, REACH certification completed for zinc bromide supplies
items.quote: Offgrid Energy Labs started zinc bromide battery pilot plant last quarter, and we continue to work on supplying zinc bromide to them. We have worked closely with them to complete REACH certification for zinc bromide supplies as well.

items.statement: Hajipir land lease extension with Gujarat government in progress, no operational impact currently
items.quote: Lastly, the land lease for the Hajipir site, we continue to work closely with the government of Gujarat to complete the lease extension. There is no material change from last quarter on this, but we continue to work with them.

items.statement: Electric truck pilots ongoing but not cost-effective currently due to charging downtime on 55 GVW trailers
items.quote: We end up havin g a fair amount of downtime because of charging time, and that actually ends up creating a very -- it increases the turnaround time for truck quite substantially and kind of mitigates any cost benefit we will get substantially

items.statement: Semiconductor talent hiring in waves over 24 months; construction and project management teams being staffed first
items.quote: We are also in the process of hiring talent for the construction work at the site, and the project management team. So those are getting staffed. And that will be followed by investing in our GTM teams and our design teams as well.

items.statement: Logistics costs at peak; margin improvement of 1.5-2% expected when costs normalize
items.quote: So, what we are feeling, once this all war situation and the tension in the Middle East region has been finishing or diluting, we hope that the charges what we were paying before, at least we will be able to secure the half of it. So, it will definitely increase our margin. And roughly, we can pull it out 1.5-2%. There are the chances to get margins in premium.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at 65-70%; no major capex needed for existing products
items.quote: As of now, the company has its own capacity where we are only utilizing our 65-70%. So, we still have the opportunity if we receive more volumes, more orders, so we are easily able to capable our own infrastructure.

items.statement: No major capex required; only routine small machine capex and working capital needs
items.quote: As of now, we are not making any huge CAPEX requirements because, as I told in the first question, which was asked in the same call, that we are already using our 70% of the capacity. So, the big CAPEX is right now not required. The only CAPEX or we need the working capital. If the more orders are coming, there will be a need of working capital only. There is no CAPEX requirement for the existing

items.statement: Strong demand from Southeast Asia, South Africa, GCC; African continent emerging

South Africa is one of the countries which is giving us very good response, and also from the GCC sector. items.statement: Exporting to 49 countries across four continents; all markets where Indian product has access
items.quote: Currently, we have a clientele in almost 49 countries, and we are catering in four major continents. So, there are 49 countries where we are serving to our clients.

items.statement: Indian buffalo meat priced at roughly half of Australian/New Zealand/Brazil due to rural economy advantage
items.quote: The price difference is almost, you can say, double. Because in Australia, they have a farming culture, so they do their cattle rearing and farming. items.statement: Started vacuum-chilled meat as high-end premium product for hypermarkets and supermarkets
items.quote: And regarding value addition, we have recently started vacuum-chilled meat also, which is a high-end product and which is good for hypermarket, supermarket, and all the kinds of stuff.

items.statement: Chilled meat segment commands premium margins due to premium positioning
items.quote: When we're going through the chilled section, the chilled section always get premium because it is a premium product, which is selling in premium places. So, there are good chances to be get good margins with the premium value addition.

items.statement: Buffalo meat demand strong in Southeast Asia, MENA, GCC, Africa; Egypt, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia key buyers
items.quote: So Indian product, you can say, by default is organic. It is economical, and we are having a good demand, good response from our Southeast Asian region, from our MENA region, and GCC countries. Also, there is a new emerging market that's coming these days is from the African continent. Egypt is there. There are many countries.

items.statement: Expanding into rice, seafood, fruits to complete food basket; early stage but leveraging brand value
items.quote: There are good chances to get growth from these products because we are trying to complete our basket. We are trying to serve our existing customers and new customers a basket of food what they are looking. Rice, meat, seafood are one same generic, and it comes to about a complete meal. So, we are looking at a very strong perspective on these products. And for rice, seafood, it is the initial stag

So, if we got good trade agreement with Europe and once the trade agreement finish, there are the chances that in few European countries, India will get the new market access, which does not yet India is having for our product.

items.statement: Revenue growth driven by both volume and value; logistics and handling costs passed through to pricing
items.quote: The revenue growth here, what you've seen in two quarters, it is both. It is in volume also and it is in value also. As I told you that the price, the product is becoming more value because of the extra cost of logistic and extra cost of handling. So, it is in both in volume and also in value, both realizations.

items.statement: Working capital needs will increase with higher order volumes; no capex required
items.quote: The only CAPEX or we need the working capital. If the more orders are coming, there will be a need of working capital only. There is no CAPEX requirement for the existing product.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 5.3% in Q2 FY27 from 4.3% in Q2 FY26

items.statement: Added 4 new significant logos in BSS during Q2 FY27

items.statement: Appointed Rajeev Bhardwaj as COO for IFM business to separate operations from business development
items.quote: First, to strengthen execution in our IFM business, we have appointed Rajeev Bhardwaj as the Chief Operating Officer.

items.statement: Appointed Jigyasa Sharma as CEO-Designate for Matrix subsidiary effective 1 April 2027
items.quote: Jigyasa Sharma, Executive Director on the UDS Board, has been appointed as CEO-Designate for our subsidiary Matrix from 1 April, 2027

items.quote: Denave has initiated closure of 2 small step-down subsidiaries, Denave Europe and Denave Korea.

items.statement: India office market absorption reached record 66 million sq ft in first 9 months of CY2026, GCCs accounted for 28 million sq ft

items.statement: White collar hiring growth moderated to 2% YoY in September; BPO, ITeS, GCC hiring grew 4%; traditional IT subdued

items.statement: PF ceiling raised from INR15,000 to INR25,000; full-year impact INR5-6 cr without pass-through, but substantial pass-through limits net impact to INR1-2 cr

items.statement: No formal forward guidance given; suggested extrapolating H1 EBITDA of INR85 cr and PAT of INR62 cr by multiplying by 2 for full-year estimate

items.statement: Capital allocation prioritizes investments in technology and capabilities, selective value-accretive acquisitions and shareholder returns
items.quote: Our capital allocation approach will remain disciplined, prioritizing investments in technology and capabilities, selective value-accretive acquisitions and shareholder returns.

items.statement: Previous acquisition target fell through on valuation; actively considering another opportunity but deal may not happen this year

A deal may not happen this year, but we will update the markets at the right

items.statement: Net cash from operating activities for H1 FY27 was INR46 cr vs INR33 cr in H1 FY26; cash and equivalents INR404 cr as of Sept 2026 with no long-term borrowings

items.statement: Net debt to equity negative 0.21x as of September 2026; company remains net cash with no long-term borrowings

items.statement: IFM client retention at ~95% over multi-year window

items.statement: Athena BFSI concentration reduced from 85% in FY25 to 80% in FY26
items.quote: BFSI concentration has already come down from 85% in financial year '25 to 80% in financial year '26.

items.statement: Denave's Intellibank AI platform scaling across Demand Gen lifecycle; AI agents handle research, qualification, follow-up

items.statement: Global Flight Handling impacted by domestic passenger traffic decline in July-August due to airline capacity adjustments and West Asian airspace restrictions
items.quote: Domestic passenger traffic witnessed a year-on-year decline in July, August, primarily due to airline capacity adjustments, continued disruption arising from the West Asian airspace restrictions.

items.statement: Expect steadiness to return in Global Flight Handling in Q4 FY27; will update after Q3
items.quote: We expect steadiness to return in the fourth quarter, but we'll be able to update better when we look at the end of the third quarter.

items.statement: Total workforce 77,157 as of H1 FY27: 60,152 in IFM, 17,005 in BSS
items.quote: On headcount, our total workforce stands at 77,157, with 60,152 in the IFM segment and 17,005 in the BSS segment.

items.statement: H1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin 5.4% vs 5.0% in H1 FY26; IFM stable, BSS improved
items.quote: EBITDA for H1 stood at INR85.5 crores compared to INR70.9 crores during last year, a growth of 21%, with a margin improving to 5.4% from 5%.

items.statement: Headwinds expected in Denave (global environment) and Global Flight Handling in H2 FY27
items.quote: We believe these margins are sustainable, as I had mentioned when I briefed and as Sunil also talked about, there are some headwinds that we are seeing in Denave in the global environment and in global, which is our ground handling business.

items.statement: Long-term: expect growth rate of 11-12% to accelerate; at current rate would double in 5-6 years
items.quote: Our growth rate of 11%, 12%, which is what we have talked about in the past should accelerate. So if that accelerates, then we will more than double. Even at the current rate, we will approximately double in around 5, 6 years.

items.statement: IFM priorities: improve client-level profitability, shift mix to higher-margin technical services (MEP, energy management, technical AMCs), win integrated outcome-linked mandates
items.quote: We aim to improve client-level profitability, shift the mix towards higher-margin technical services such as MEP, energy management and technical AMCs, and continue to win integrated outcome-linked mandates.

items.statement: BSS sector mix: IT/ITeS 31%, BFSI 12%, rest across retail, consumer, manufacturing, aviation, others
items.quote: By sector; IT, IT-enabled services contribute to about 31% of BSS revenue and BFSI about 12%, with the rest spread across many other segments such as retail, consumer, manufacturing, aviation and other industries.

items.statement: GCC count in India ~2,400-2,500; projected to double in 4-5 years; UDS has exposure through IFM, seeking direct GCC exposure

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected to remain in current range; benefit from 80JJAA employment incentives but reliance decreasing
items.quote: The effective tax rate will largely remain in the same range because we have estimated what will be the full-year effective tax rate and accordingly have worked out for respective quarters. So, we don't see a much swing in that rate on a full-year basis.

items.statement: Guided consolidated sales growth of 18% to 20% for FY27
items.quote: As we look ahead, we remain encouraged by the positive demand environment across our key categories and markets, reinforcing our confidence in delivering our guided consolidated sales growth of 18% to 20% for the year.

items.statement: Targeted EBITDA margin range of 16% to 17%
items.quote: Our targeted EBITDA margin range continues to be 16% to 17%. However, we will evaluate -- we have to be patient for a couple of quarters.

items.statement: Volume growth contributed over 80% of the 18% revenue growth in Q2 FY27
items.quote: So, Sneha, volume growth has been close to about -- out of the 18%-odd growth that we've done, more than 80% growth comes from volume-based growth and 20%-odd comes from realization growth.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin at 12.4%, flat sequentially despite raw material volatility
items.quote: EBITDA for Q2 FY27 stood at INR82.8 crores and H1 FY27 EBITDA stood at INR165.3 crores with margins during both the periods at 12.4%.

items.statement: Uniclan baby hygiene EBITDA margin declined to 6.4% from 8.1% YoY due to raw material inflation
items.quote: Hence, we've seen the EBITDA margins come down from 8.1% in the previous year quarter to 6.4%. This is primarily on account of increase in the consumption or increase because of the raw material prices.

items.statement: Long-term target for Uniclan baby hygiene EBITDA margin is 8% to 10%
items.quote: We'll want to have margins of around 8% to 10% for this business segment in the longer term.

items.statement: Raw material inflation at ~15% in Q2 FY27; consumption impact ~9% after price hikes and mix
items.quote: So the inflation is around 15%. What we mentioned in Q1, Bhavin bhai, was when you compare it with the consumption, the impact was about 10%. So I'm saying inflation is about 15% with the consumption level of about 60%. So on consumption, the impact is around 9%.

items.statement: Raw material prices increased further in October, changing once or twice weekly
items.quote: Yes, absolutely. They are higher. And like I said, it's probably price increases are happening like once or twice every week now

items.statement: Taking calibrated price increases at granular product level to protect volume growth
items.quote: Wherever we believe that there is any room for increasing the selling prices at the MRP level or at the channel level or reducing the schemes and margins, we are taking those steps.

items.statement: Invested over INR200 crores in H1 FY27; expect further INR100-125 crores in H2 FY27
items.quote: During H1 FY27, we invested over INR200 crores in capital expenditure and expect to invest a further INR100 crores to INR125 crores during the remainder part of the year.

items.statement: Commissioned first building at 50-acre greenfield facility (~170,000 sq ft) for Reynolds pen manufacturing; revenue from Q3 FY27

items.statement: Second and third buildings at greenfield site have machinery installation underway for wooden pencils and office supplies
items.quote: Second building, machineries are being installed. Third building also machineries have been installed. And three other buildings, out of which one is relatively very small, they are at the finishing stage.

items.statement: Reynolds brand revenue contribution expected from Q3 FY27, gaining momentum in Q4 FY27
items.quote: But we'll see revenues from Reynolds brand from the goods manufactured by us flowing in from third quarter FY27 and gaining momentum in fourth quarter FY27.

items.statement: Working capital cycle maintained within guided 55-60 days despite volume growth and floods
items.quote: On the working capital front, despite strong volume-led growth and a challenging market environment, we have maintained our working capital cycle within the guided range of 55 to 60 days.

items.quote: The increase in debt is primarily attributable to our ongoing capacity expansion program. Post utilization of the IPO funds, which happened in April of this year, a large portion of the incremental capex has been funded through debt.

items.statement: Expect additional INR100-120 crores debt in midterm to fund ongoing capex
items.quote: But yes, I think we will require at least about INR100 crores to INR120 crores of debt in the midterm to fund the ongoing capex.

items.statement: Trade channel excited about Reynolds manufacturing under DOMS; anticipation high for sales launch
items.quote: The trade is very excited that now a brand like Reynolds being manufactured and sold through DOMS - this synergy itself is keeping the trade very excited. A lot of channel partners are waiting with in anticipation for sales to start as soon as possible.

items.statement: Measured pricing approach historically yields sustained volume growth and higher long-term margins
items.quote: In the past, in case of DOMS only, we've seen that whenever such significant price increases have happened, we've always taken measured approach. In the interim, it has impacted our margin. But in the long term, it has resulted into sustained volume growth backed by higher margins.

items.statement: Gross product sales schemes and discounts reduced YoY, indicating ASP improvement
items.quote: You would have seen that our margin -- our schemes and discounts that we give have actually come down when compared to previous year. This automatically shows that there have been some increases in our ASPs and this benefit is seen also in our consumption.

items.quote: Timeline target is June -July next year and we are targeting INR 1,000 crores of revenue from that business per year.

items.statement: Aspiration to triple or quadruple domestic revenue from INR 500 cr in next 1-2 years
items.quote: So, definitely we are quite positive that the numbers where they are today, from a INR 500 crores domestic revenue, we are hopeful that this should triple or quadruple in the next one or two years.

items.statement: INR 3,000 cr pipeline for India AI infrastructure from defense PSUs and government
items.quote: I can tell you that we have a pipeline of INR 3,000 crores for India. And from our IPO proceeds plus customer advance, we will be doing capex of INR 1,500 crores.

items.statement: Domestic PAT margin 26-27%; AI factory PAT margin 16-18%; India AI factory to have higher margin
items.quote: Yes. So domestic PAT margin would be like in the range of 26%- 27%, and this one AI factory PAT margin would be in the range of 16% to 18%. And once our AI also goes live in India, then that will have a higher margin.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA INR 1,137.5 million (12.3% YoY growth); PAT INR 603.7 million (26.3% YoY growth)
items.value: EBITDA INR 1,137.5 million, PAT INR 603.7 million
items.quote: EBITDA margin for H1 FY27 is INR 1,137.5 million, whereas for H1 FY26 is INR 1,012.7 million. So we again see a growth of 12.3% there. Similarly, PAT has also increased to INR 603.7 million in H1 FY27 against INR 477.9 million in H1 FY26. Thereby we see a growth of 26.3%.

items.statement: IPO proceeds INR 7,200 million raised; INR 469.13 million utilized; INR 6,730.87 million unutilized (INR 6,500 million in FDs)
items.value: INR 7,200 million raised, INR 469.13 million utilized
items.quote: So total amount raised through IPO issue is INR 7,200 million. Utilized out of the same is INR 469.13 million. The unutilized amount stands at INR 6,730.87 million as of date. We see most of them, we have close to INR 6,500 million, we have put that in fixed deposit and remaining amount has been there in the monitoring account.

items.statement: Advance of USD 140 million paid to Sharon AI; 50% amortized over 3 months from go-live, 50% in months 34-36
items.quote: Yes, so, we have paid an advance to Sharon AI of USD 140 million, out of which the 50% will be amortized over a period of three months from go -live, and the remaining 50% will be amortized in the month of 34, 35, 36.

items.statement: Existing data centers at 85% utilization; capacity additions in three data centers coming up in 2-3 months
items.quote: Yes, so currently we are utilizing close to 85% of our existing data centers and we are also increasing capacity in other three data centers which should be up and running in next two to three months.

items.statement: Targeting 1 GW power under control; acquiring powered land (50-100 MW) globally where hydro/wind/geothermal available
items.quote: So, Shiv, obviously we have put up our strategy in place that how we want to bring 1 gigawatt of power under our captivity, under our control. So, we have put up a strategy in place and we are targeting all those countries where hydropower is available, wind power is available, or geothermal power is available

items.statement: Consolidating customer base from 2,500 to top 400-500; moved smaller customers to internal virtual subsidiary; asked 50-60 customers to exit
items.quote: And all the small customers that we had, we are transferring those. So, we are trying to keep only 400 -500 customers in ESDS, not more than that. And all the smaller customers go to a Internal subsidiary, they sit in a separate office, they have their own operation.

items.statement: Sharon AI 8,200 GPUs fully contracted to ESDS on take-or-pay basis; no sharing with other customers
items.quote: This is a committed AI factory and private dedicated AI factory for us. It is not shared with anyone else. So, in this AI factory, there is no competition. This 8,200 GPUs are fully contracted to ESDS.

items.statement: Connected to top 17-18 global AI labs and banks; AI labs are primary consumers of AI factories
items.quote: This kind of AI factories are consumed by AI labs only at the moment. So , majority of the consumption of AI compute, AI factories, is being done by AI labs. So , we are now connected to the top 17-18 AI labs across the world and also the banks that are consuming AI.

items.statement: Sharon AI locked B300 GPU rate at $3.50/hr vs current market $7/hr; cannot increase prices due to 5-year client commitments
items.quote: We are lucky that we identified them as our partner very early because now the same B300 rates are being quoted at $7 an hour. What we got at $3.50 an hour from them, now the market is demanding $7 for the same B300s.

items.statement: India AI factory will command higher pricing than Sharon AI due to no legacy commitments
items.quote: Correct. In India what we are building, so there we will be able to charge higher price.

items.statement: Customer advances replicating Sharon AI advance structure sitting in current and non-current liabilities
items.quote: An exact similar arrangement we have done with our customer. So, customer have given us the advance which is sitting in the liability. You can see the exact replicating amount in the non-current asset and current assets.

items.quote: So, a year back we initiated a concept of CAIO, so Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer and Chief Product Officer. So, what happened was that the young people were brought to this position. So, for a CAIO role, we found someone internally. For CPO, we got a person from outside. We did not have a clue that the CAIO would eat up the role of the CIO and CTO.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue INR 2,719 million (24.6% YoY); total income INR 2,788 million (25.6% YoY)

And the total revenue in, H1 FY27 is INR 2,788 million, which includes INR 68 million of other income against a total income in H1 FY26 of INR 2,219 million. So thereby we see a growth of 25.6%.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue INR 1,383.4 million (3.5% QoQ growth from Q1 INR 1,336.6 million)
items.quote: Revenue from operation in Q2 is INR 1,383.4 million whereas for Q1 it was INR 1,336.6 million, so resulting in a growth of 3.5%.

items.statement: India has 40-50 GW surplus power for AI factories over 4-5 years; US and Europe have no power left
items.quote: So, Europe is left with no power, Australia is left with no power. So, every country which has power GPU, AI factories are there now and they don't have enough power left. So , India is the only country which has got 40 gigawatt 50 gigawatt surplus to be given for AI factories over the next 4 years-5 years.

items.statement: AI infrastructure funnel strongest; Managed Services and SaaS funnel less promising currently
items.quote: Managed Services and SaaS funnel is not as promising as the AI infra funnel is at the moment.

items.statement: 5-year revenue target INR2,800-3,000 crore supported by expansions and new R&D products

items.statement: Net working capital cycle increased from 63 days (Q1) to 76 days (Q2) due to lower creditor days from new suppliers with shorter credit periods; target to return to 60-70 days range
