items.statement: MDF overcapacity situation with new capacities from Action and Elixrr; margins under pressure till excess capacity absorbed by FY29
items.quote: I was saying we're in a typical overcapacity situation here, where till the excess capacity is absorbed, it's very difficult to margins to go back to the erstwhile 20% range. Currently, we're looking at further capacity addition, which has happened already in the quarter with Action coming up with the new capacity, as well as one capacity addition from Elixrr. I think the next two quarters will be

items.statement: Plywood growth driven by brand, distribution, stakeholder engagement; gaining share from unorganized players
items.quote: We have been very big on brand, so we always build on two, three fundamentals: our distribution, our brand, and we really work on our various stakeholders. We have been doing that consistently. We keep experimenting various things, and I think that is what has led to success, and we are happy about it.

items.statement: Laminates exports growing well; new Andhra capacity dedicated to large formats (more export-oriented); domestic also picking up
items.quote: Exports is growing quite well, and after the addition of our new capacity in Andhra Pradesh, which is dedicated towards large sizes. Large sizes historically have been more export-oriented than domestic, even though domestic is picking up in traction now. But we are seeing a good traction as far as export markets are concerned, and we are expanding.

items.statement: Management expects FY27 performance to be better than H1 FY27
items.quote: I think the way we are placed as of H1, you can definitely extrapolate the number, but it will be better than this. That is for sure.

items.statement: Management will not give FY28 guidance at this time
items.quote: I would not like to give any guidance for FY28 as of now, but so far as current financial year is concerned, it will be definitely better than H1, that is for sure.

items.statement: FY27 capex limited to Rs 15-20 crore for normal operational needs from internal accruals
items.quote: Amount can be in the range of Rs. 15 crores to Rs. 20 crores in max which will be from internal accruals only.

items.statement: Jumbo Laminates capacity utilization reached 41% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Capacity utilization in the jumbo laminate business reached to 41% during the quarter.

items.statement: Management targets 80-85% Jumbo Laminates utilization by March 2027
items.quote: We are striving for it. So, I would say, March, we will be at level of utilizing somewhere around 80%, 85%.

items.statement: MDF capacity utilization target for FY27 is 82-85%
items.quote: So, we will be utilizing the capacity somewhere around 82% to 85% across the year.

items.statement: Jumbo Laminates has signed orders for Q3 and Q4 FY27
items.quote: Yes. So we have already signed a few of the upcoming businesses for Q3 and Q4 as well. So we see a good amount of jumbo business coming into the action.

items.statement: Laminate business overall margin target 12-14%
items.quote: The margin as a whole business would be 12% to 14%. And we will make sure that we achieve those numbers what we are committing of 12% to 14% margin for the laminate business as a whole.

items.statement: Jumbo Laminates EBITDA margin 19.4% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA increased to Rs. 42 million from Rs. 23 million in Q1 FY27 with an EBITDA margin of 19.4%.

items.statement: MDF EBITDA margin 9.9% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: MDF EBITDA increased by 6% YoY to Rs. 194 million, with an EBITDA margin of 9.9%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 9.5% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA increased by 24.5% YoY to Rs. 280 million with an EBITDA margin of 9.5%.

items.statement: Strong domestic MDF demand drove 41% YoY revenue growth in Q2 FY27
items.quote: The growth was driven by domestic MDF business with India revenue increasing by 41% YoY.

items.statement: Laminate domestic revenue grew 82.1% YoY in Q2 FY27
items.quote: India laminates revenue increased by 82.1% YoY to Rs. 404 million while export revenue grew by 47.7% to Rs. 480 million.

items.statement: MDF domestic realizations fell 7% QoQ due to chemical price volatility and 5-10% competition pressure
items.quote: So, the current raw material scenario is also very skeptical like the chemical prices have been very volatile and there has also been price pressure, and there was competition of 5% to 10%.

items.statement: Laminate price hike taken after October 10, 2026, to reflect in Q3 FY27
items.quote: the price hike in laminate has just happened in the month of October, maybe I would say after 10th of October, because of which the price hike has been taken in Q3.

items.statement: Value-added MDF products contributed 44% of volumes and 55% of revenues in H1 FY27
items.quote: Value-added products contributed 44% of MDF volumes and 55% of MDF revenues.

items.statement: Target 50% MDF volumes and 60% MDF revenues from value-added products in FY27
items.quote: We are making progress towards our target of achieving 50% of MDF volumes and 60% of MDF revenues from value-added products during FY27.

items.statement: Added 8 new direct distributors and 27 dealers in MDF business in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Furthermore, during the quarter, we continued to strengthen our domestic distribution network by adding 8 new direct distributors and 27 dealers.

items.statement: Zero MDF exports in Q2 FY27 due to global trade uncertainties and elevated freight costs
items.quote: During the quarter, we continued to adopt a calibrated approach towards exports amid global trade uncertainties and elevated freight costs. Accordingly, we did not undertake any MDF exports during the quarter.

items.statement: Jumbo Laminates exports now to 63 countries, targeting 7 more by H2 FY27
items.quote: Before jumbo, our export was somewhere around 52 or 54 countries. Now we have expanded to 63 countries. So that's how we are growing. And the dream is by H2 we should at least add 7 more countries in our portfolio.

items.statement: Jumbo Laminates shipments mainly FOB basis; regular laminate exports 60-65% CIF basis
items.quote: if we look at all the shipments of Jumbo, they are majorly on the FOB basis, while when we talk about the regular laminate business, the 60% to 65% export is done on CIF basis.

items.statement: Inventory days reduced to 146 from 195; receivable days improved to 78 from 81; payable days reduced to 157 from 189 in H1 FY27 vs FY26
items.quote: Inventory days reduced to 146 from 195 in FY26 while receivable days improved to 78 from 81. Payable days also reduced to 157 from 189 d uring the same period

items.statement: Net debt increased to Rs 2,715 million as of Sep 2026 from Rs 2,546 million as of Mar 2026; net debt/equity 0.41 vs 0.39
items.quote: Net debt as of 30th September, 2026 was Rs. 2,715 million compared to Rs. 2,546 million as of 31st March 2026. The net debt equity ratio was 0.41 compared to 0.39 at the end of March 2026.

items.statement: BIS standards in place for MDF imports; only 2-3 foreign companies have BIS certification
items.quote: Out of, 52-53 companies, only 2 has the BIS. So that are the only 2-3 companies who are allowed to export their products in India.

items.statement: BIS on furniture expected to boost domestic MDF demand
items.quote: Once the BIS is done in the furniture industry that will give us boost for sure.

items.statement: Domestic MDF pricing pressure expected for one more quarter then stabilization
items.quote: I think this one more quarter is going to be the pressure, and it would be more on the stable side rather.

items.statement: Blended laminate realization improved 21.7% YoY to Rs 847 per sheet in Q2 FY27
items.quote: blended realization increased by 21.7% YoY to 847 per sheet, reflecting an improved product mix and higher contribution from premium laminate products

items.statement: MDF volume 76,000 CBM in Q2 FY27
items.quote: So, we have done very healthy volumes of 76,000 CBM.

items.statement: Freight costs for Jumbo Laminates exports surged from USD 800-900 to USD 8,000 per container
items.quote: The freight charges which were supposed to be at USD 800 or USD 900 are at USD 8,000. So, that is the main reason for this kind of variabl e charges

items.statement: Chemical raw material prices volatile due to ongoing war in the West
items.quote: there are also some raw material price hikes in the terms of chemical because of the ongoing war in the West.

items.statement: Brownfield Jumbo Laminates expansion would take ~8 months for main machinery lead time
items.quote: So, if we see it is a brownfield, supposing, then the lead time from the machinery, which is the most important part, and it takes generally 8 months for the main machine to get ready.

items.statement: Management reviewing capacity expansion plans for MDF and Jumbo Laminates for FY28-29; decision expected by end of Q3 FY27
items.quote: as of now, we will take this quarter to review everything and after which we would like to come to a conclusion. There are few other like few of the t hings internally getting discussed over. So, we will make an announcement once it is internally decided

items.statement: Targets 22-23% restaurant-level EBITDA margin post-Ind AS and 20-22% revenue growth from new store expansion
items.quote: See, the target, what we look at is from an EBITDA perspective, we should be having -- post Ind AS, I'm talking about, we should be between 22% to 23% of EBITDA at restaurant level.

items.statement: Plans to reach 200 outlets by FY30 with focus on Oriental, Italian cafe and QSR brands
items.quote: So we as a company have taken our strategy focused brand expansions, which I may reiterate, which will be Oriental and in Oriental, we have our mother brand Mainland China, Asia Kitchen thereafter, which is our mall format.

items.statement: Capex per restaurant INR 4-5 crores; annual capex ~INR 50 crores; 4-year plan ~INR 200-250 crores
items.quote: See, your point is well taken. Sir, what has -- let's say, when we talk in terms of a capex plan, which have been just detailed by Mr. Avik for the next 3 years, what we are looking at is for a restaurant, let's say, we spend between INR 4.5 crores to or INR 4 crores, INR 5 crores.

items.statement: 125 outlets as of Sep 30, 2026 (118 company-owned, 7 franchise); 2-3 new openings in Q3 FY27 including 2 Gong, 3 Walters, 1 Siciliana
items.quote: As of September 30, 2026, our network comprised 125 outlets, including 118 company-owned and operated outlets and 7 franchise-owned company-operated outlets, including a restaurant under our subsidiary.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth 8.1% in Q2 FY27, 11.32% in Q1 FY27, 9.8% in H1 FY27; optimistic on Q3 seasonality
items.quote: What we have witnessed during this particular quarter is the same-store sales growth which had been 8.1% in the quarter 2, which was 11.32% in quarter 1 and is 9.8% in H1 of FY27.

items.statement: Delivery mix 32% in Q2 FY27 vs 27.4% in Q2 FY26; expects 30-35% long-term; dine-in 68%
items.quote: This Q2 FY27 had 32% delivery and 68% dine-in, which was 27.4% on delivery and 72.6% Q2 FY26 of last year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 8.03% in Q2 FY27 vs 6.81% YoY; pre-Ind AS EBITDA 7.90% vs 6.52% YoY; restaurant-level EBITDA ~22% for Asia Kitchen
items.quote: Operational EBITDA grew by 39.44% to INR 10.242 crores against INR 7.47 crores in the corresponding quarter last year, with the EBITDA margin improving to 8.03% from 6.81%.

items.statement: No major price hikes taken; managing input cost inflation via vendor renegotiation and scale buying power
items.quote: So we haven't really taken a very big jump in price h ike. What we have managed to do is because of economies of scale having such a large operations, our vendors have been very supportive

items.statement: Asia Kitchen monthly throughput INR 60-75 lakhs (INR 2-2.5 lakhs/day); gross margin 76%; staff cost 20-22%; rental 18%; opex 11%; restaurant EBITDA ~22%
items.quote: On an Asia kitchen basis, we have a throughput almost like INR 60 lakhs to INR 75 lakhs in a month depending upon the size and location. This has a gross margins of almost like 76%.

items.statement: 75% of delivery customers are new; 25% loyal per aggregator data
items.quote: See, we don't get the delivery customer data point, but what we gather from aggregators is that 25% of our -- these are loyal customers and 75% of the guests who get into delivery are the newcomers.

items.statement: Operating cash flow ~INR 50 crores; expects to fund capex from internal cash generation
items.quote: And going forward, we will be able to generate this kind of revenues, and we should be cash flow positive in years to come.

items.statement: Kitchen-within-kitchen model enables multi-brand delivery from same kitchen without extra capex; leveraging aggregator platforms for visibility and deals
items.quote: So the best plan that has worked magically for us is kitchen within kitchen concepts, where, for example, if we have an Asian kitch en, we also do deliver our other Asian brands from the very same kitchen without having any extra capex or staff costs or any other costs added to it

items.statement: Liquor revenue 8-9% of total revenue
items.quote: We operate at around 8% to 9% of our total revenues as liquor.

items.statement: Chennai Park expected to take 2-3 years to achieve optimal utilization and sustainable profitability
items.quote: It'll take 2 years, 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margins for Chennai Park expected to stabilize at levels of established parks like Hyderabad, Bangalore and Kochi after 2-3 years
items.quote: Long-term margin, it will become like our established parks like Hyderabad, Bangalore and Kochi. So its margins will continue to expand, but this is the first year, so it's very erratic. It might move up and down in different, different quarters. After 2 to 3 years, it will stabilize.

items.statement: Company looking at 2-3 new locations for expansion, hopes to conclude deals before end of current financial year
items.quote: Yes, we are looking at 2 to 3 new locations, but no final call has been taken. We hope to conclude some of these deals before the end of this financial year, and we'll keep you updated.

items.statement: Typical capital for a large park in a city like Bombay might be close to INR 200 crores for land, last Chennai land purchase was roughly INR 100 crores
items.quote: So land parcel, the last time we bought was roughly INR100 crores for Chennai. For a city like Bombay, we might have to spend maybe close to INR 200 crores.

items.statement: Company plans at least 1 big project in next 1-2 years and maybe 1 Tier 2 city, possibly 2 large cities
items.quote: We are looking at least 1 big project in the next 1 or 2 years, and maybe 1 Tier 2 city. Maybe 2 large cities also is possible, but we will keep you updated.

items.statement: Substantial investments made over last 2 years in flagship global rides for capacity addition at Bangalore park
items.quote: One is capex investments, which you would have seen over the last 2 years, we've done some substantial investments, bringing some flagship global rides.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization across parks at 30-40% occupancy for whole year, considered normal for amusement parks
items.quote: So if you look at a whole year perspective, I think we are -- we'll be at a 30% or 40% occupancy, but that is normal for these kind of parks.

items.statement: Chennai Park expected to reach Bangalore-level footfall in about 3 years, will know more after second or third year
items.quote: It should take about 3 years from what we see. But I think we will only know, we can only comment on this maybe after second or third year because it's just our first year.

items.statement: Existing parks Bengaluru, Kochi, Hyderabad, Bhubaneswar grew revenue 8% YoY in Q2 with footfalls up 6%, and 13% revenue growth with 7% footfall growth in H1
items.quote: Together, our parks Bengaluru, Kochi, Hyderabad, Bhubaneswar grew revenue by 8% year -on-year in the quarter, with footfalls up 6%. For the half year, they grew revenue by 13% with footfalls up by 7%.

items.statement: Resorts business delivered best ever Q2 with 57% YoY growth, hospitality becoming increasingly meaningful contributor
items.quote: Our resorts business delivered their best ever Q2, with the resorts growing 57% year -on-year. Hospitality is becoming increasingly meaningful contributor to our business.

items.statement: Bengaluru and Kochi delivered best ever Q2 performance, Hyderabad delivered best ever H1
items.quote: Second, our existing parks, Bengaluru and Kochi, delivered their best ever Q2, and Hyderabad delivered best ever H1.

items.statement: Bhubaneswar park footfall down 20% YoY in Q2 due to extreme weather with 900% growth in rains affecting 20 out of 30 districts
items.quote: On the Bhubaneswar park, it was completely weather -led. There was a 900% growth in rains with about 20 out of 30 districts affected with extreme cyclones. And because of those weather disruptions, consumer sentiment was poor to drive footfall.

items.statement: Cochin not a weak quarter in Q3 due to group business and Christmas season, company bullish on Cochin Q3 performance
items.quote: In fact, it's not a weak quarter for Cochin because this is a big quarter for Cochin in terms of group business. And a lot of effort has been done in terms of revamping our GTM sales strategies. And we've seen some good signs in Quarter 2, as you would have seen the results. And we continue to stay bullish that Quarter 3 will be a good quarter for Cochin, led by groups and then ending with Christm

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded to 24% from 18% YoY, H1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 40%
items.quote: The EBITDA margin expanded to 24% from 18%. We also moved from a loss in Q2 last year to profit in this quarter. For the first half, the income grew 41% to INR378 crores and EBITDA grew 47% to INR150 crores at a margin of 40%.

items.statement: Chennai Park contributed INR 10.37 crores (73%) of EBITDA increase in Q2, existing parks contributed INR 1.83 crores (13%), resorts contributed INR 2.06 crores (14%)
items.quote: The INR14.26 crores increase in EBITDA was led by Chennai. And Chennai Park contributed about INR10.37 crores, accounting for about 73% of the EBITDA increase. Our existing parks contributed about INR1.83 crores, representing 13%. Our resort business contributed INR2.06 crores, accounting for the remaining 14 percentage.

items.statement: Average ticket price declined 3% YoY to INR 983 in Q2, offset by 11% increase in non-ticket revenue per guest to INR 510, ARPU up 1% to INR 1,491
items.quote: The average ticket price declined by 3% Y-o-Y to INR983. This was offset by an 11% increase in non-ticket revenue per guest to INR510, supported by our in-park spending initiatives. Consequently, average revenue per unit increased by 1% Y -o-Y to INR 1,491

items.statement: H1 FY27 average ticket price INR 1,192, non-ticket spend per guest up 16% to INR 559, ARPU up 5% to INR 1,750
items.quote: Our average ticket price for the half year stood at INR1,192. The non -ticket spend per guest increased by 16% to INR559, taking an average revenue per user up by 5% to INR1,750.

items.statement: Chennai Park ticket price 10% lower than Bangalore due to higher group footfall mix which is more discounted versus retail
items.quote: Chennai was 10% lesser than Bangalore because of just the pricing. Bangalore is priced at a higher point versus Chennai because it is our largest park. Now, if you compare it versus the previous quarters, it's just a matter of the skew of footfall we got. So we have 2 channels: one is the retail channel and the groups channel. Q2 predominantly in Chennai had a lot more groups versus retail footfal

items.statement: Non-ticket revenue grown at early double digits CAGR over 4-5 years, now at 30%+ of ARPU, company continues to build on retail and F&B product assortments
items.quote: I think we've been able to substantially grow our non -ticket revenue, and just not quarter -on-quarter, but I think across the 4 to 5-year CAGR, we've been able to grow at early double digits. So we've been able to kind of come to the global trends of almost having 30%-plus of non-ticket part of the entire ARPU.

items.statement: Company focusing on price-led, cohort-led interventions and bringing larger groups in lean seasons to improve weekday footfall and reduce seasonality
items.quote: So I think we are focusing on price -led, cohort-led interventions. And I think we've seen some good results in this lean season of quarter 2. And during these lean seasons, we also work on bringing larger groups that otherwise cannot afford our parks in the holiday season. And I think these are 2 initiatives that we continue to build on to increase our footfall in the lean seasons.

items.statement: Flexi tickets already implemented on online booking portal allowing customers to change dates based on weather or emergencies
items.quote: We have flexi tickets which anyways allow customers to change based on weather or any other emergency conditions that they have. So that's already implemented on our online booking portal.

items.statement: Chennai Park Q2 footfall skewed towards groups channel versus retail, groups more discounted impacting ATP
items.quote: Q2 predominantly in Chennai had a lot more groups versus retail footfall, and groups are obviously a little bit more discounted versus retail, and that's why you see the change in ATP.

items.statement: EsselWorld not up for sale, company prefers greenfield development over acquiring existing parks
items.quote: EsselWorld, I don't think is up for sale. I think they have some other issues. So they are not really looking to sell it. I think they have shut the operations. But we prefer to do on our own in a separate location. It's not that difficult. I mean, for us it doesn't make any difference whether we get an existing park or we start from scratch. It might take 1 or 2 years more. But other than that, I

items.statement: No further equity dilution planned, company can fund most capex from internal cash flows, may take some debt at some point
items.quote: We are not -- whatever equity dilution we had to do, we're already done. Now we are not looking to do any further equity dilution. I think we can with our own cash flows, we can fund most of the capex. Maybe some debt we might take at some point. But as of now, we don't need to dilute equity anymore.

items.statement: Spend per guest grew 11% in Q2 and 16% in H1 as more guests take up value-added and premium offerings
items.quote: Spend per guest also moving in the right direction. It's grown 11% in Q2 and 16% in H1 as more guests take up our value-added and premium offerings.

items.statement: Chennai Park first monsoon season (mid-October to end-November) will impact footfall, full year impact to be assessed
items.quote: So in Chennai, this is actually in sense our first ever monsoon, as Chennai monsoons happen between mid-October to end-November. We are also kind of understanding the overall consumer trends and patterns. But yes, the monsoons will have an impact on the footfall as we've seen, but we will only be able to get a better sense once we finish the whole year.

items.statement: Land prices fluctuating with uncertainty, may go up or down, making capital planning speculative
items.quote: Also land prices keep fluctuating, and this year, as there are a lot of -- there is a lot of uncertainty. Land prices may go down, it may go up. We don't know what is going to happen.

items.statement: Roughly 40-50% land still available across parks for future development, Hyderabad has less available land
items.quote: We have roughly 40% to 50% land is still available. Some parks like Hyderabad, it'll be less.

items.statement: Management maintains low double-digit revenue growth guidance for FY27, 20% home textile growth, and 40-45 new EBOs focused on West and South
items.value: low double-digit revenue growth; 20% home textile growth; 40-45 new EBOs
items.quote: We continue to maintain our guidance for low double-digit revenue growth, 20% home textile growth and 40-45 new EBOs focused on West and South also.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to be within plus/minus 100 basis points of FY26 level depending on Q3 performance
items.quote: So, as far as margins are concerned, we are into third quarter and this quarter is very important for us. So, we see plus-minus 100 basis point margin as compared to last financial year, depending on how this quarter goes.

items.statement: Price hike of 8-9% taken in winter wear to offset raw material cost increases
items.quote: We have taken a price rise of around 8% to 9% in this winter and I think that will suffice whatever raw material cost increased we have in the winter wear category.

items.statement: Pure wool raw material prices increased ~20% YoY, cotton cost of goods increased only 3%
items.quote: Also, if you look at our quarter 3 products, which supplies woolen products, the raw material price for pure wool has grown by almost 20% over the last year. This year also, we expect the same increase in the raw material price.

items.statement: Later festive season shifted consumer demand and winter sell-through from Q2 to Q3; macro inflation reducing discretionary spending but economy growing at 7%
items.quote: This year, the later festive season shifted a meaningful part of consumer demand and winter sell-through towards Q3.

items.statement: Cotton largest category at 63% of gross product sales in H1 FY27; home textiles, kids wear, footwear growing; woolen declining
items.quote: Cotton has been our largest reported product category since FY '22 and contributed approximately 63% of gross product sales in H1 FY '27.

items.statement: Gross sales increased across cotton (Rs 390 cr), home textiles (Rs 91.6 cr), kids wear (Rs 34.5 cr), footwear (Rs 9.3 cr); woolen declined to Rs 94 cr
items.value: cotton Rs 390 cr; home textiles Rs 91.6 cr; kids wear Rs 34.5 cr; footwear Rs 9.3 cr; woolen Rs 94 cr
items.quote: Cotton sales increased from Rs. 326 crores in H1 to Rs. 390 crores in H1 FY '27. Home textiles sales increased from Rs. 83 crores to Rs. 91.6 crores. Kids wear sales increased from Rs. 30 crores to Rs. 34.5 crores. Footwear increased from Rs. 4.9 crores to Rs. 9.3 crores. Woolen gross sales declined from approximately Rs. 106 crores to Rs. 94 crores.

items.statement: EBO count 506 (vs 497), shop-in-shop 632 (vs 578), MBO 1,413 (vs 1,615), National Chain Stores 846 (vs 891) as of Sep 26
items.quote: As on September 26, we reported 506 EBOs compared with 497 EBOs a year earlier. Our shop-in-shop network increased to 632 from 578. MBO declined to 1,413 from 1,615 while National Chain Stores declined to 846 from 891.

items.statement: Like-to-like (SSSG) growth 10% in FY26, 9% in H1 FY27; targeting 9-10% for FY27
items.quote: Last year, we grew at around 10% in like-to-like growth. And this year in first 6 months, we have grew by 9% in like-to-like growth. So, it is not that like-to-like growth has not been happening. It is there in last year also and we are confident that we should be growing around 9%-10% in this financial year also as far as like-to-like growth is concerned.

items.statement: Net working capital days improved from 176 in FY25 to 146 in FY26; seasonal funding requirement high in H1
items.quote: Reported and working capital days improved from 176 in FY '25 to 146 in FY '26.

items.statement: Net debt ~Rs 300 cr as of Sep 30 due to seasonal inventory build; permanent working capital debt ~Rs 200 cr as of Mar 31
items.quote: So, as far as the debt is concerned, this is just the working capital requirement being our accumulation model. We have to accumulate all the inventories. So, the working capital requirement as on 30th September is always high. So, you kind of look at our debt position as on 31st March only, which will be for this year around Rs. 200 crores, which is our permanent working capital requirement.

items.statement: 35 MW solar plant in Madhya Pradesh with PPAs signed; land identified; COD 31 Mar 2027; expected ROI 17-18%
items.quote: So, for the solar bid, I would like to mention that the PPAs for all these three sites have already been signed. It is a 35-megawatt plant that we are putting in Madhya Pradesh. The land has been identified, land aggregation is in place and all the three sites are supposed to go live on 31st March 2027 and we are on track to achieve that.

items.statement: Solar subsidiary expected revenue Rs 17-18 cr in FY28 with EBITDA margins 80%+
items.quote: Sorry, Diwakar ji, it will be around anywhere between Rs. 17 and Rs. 18 odd crores of revenue. And the EBITDA margins are upwards of 80% in a solar project.

items.statement: No buyback discussions held; management will inform exchanges if any
items.quote: We didn't have any discussion as far as any buyback is concerned in the management. As and when we have any discussion, we will definitely let the exchanges know about that.

items.statement: Rebates and discounts increased to 12% of revenue in H1 (vs 9% YoY) due to early end-of-season sales and old inventory liquidation; full-year expected 3-4%
items.quote: Compare it with the revenue in proportion to revenue. In proportion to revenue, it is 12%. As against last year, it was 9%. So, we have to see every percentage in relation to revenue only.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions and macro inflation impacting material costs and discretionary spending; later festive season shifted demand to Q3
items.quote: But unfortunately, this year, we got interruption by the material cost rise because of geopolitical tensions and all. So, that has hurt us in this quarter.

items.statement: Store economics target: increase revenue per sq ft from Rs 12,000 to Rs 15,000 in 2-3 years; long-term EBO expansion 40-45 per year
items.value: Rs 12,000 to Rs 15,000 per sq ft
items.quote: And yes, as far as store economics are concerned, we are right now at around Rs. 12,000 per square feet. And we have aspiration to increase it to Rs. 15,000 per square feet in next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Non-Monte Carlo brands (Rock.it, Cloak & Decker, Monte Carlo Home) contribute ~8% of revenue but growing faster than parent brand; Home growing ~20% CAGR
items.quote: Then if you talk about Cloak & Decker which is an economy segment, again it cannot be clubbed into Monte Carlo because Monte Carlo is a premium brand. So, both these brands if you see in last 2-3 years, they have been grown handsomely and they will have substantial revenue going forward.

items.statement: Export not a priority; tried white-labelling but margins insufficient; focusing on West and South India expansion instead
items.quote: A couple of years back, we tried working for an export order. But we realized there are not enough margin in exporting and doing white labelling for other brands. And we are a branded retail player. So, we do not want to get into doing white labelling for other players.

items.statement: No manufacturing expansion planned for cotton; 80% outsourced; focus on marketing over manufacturing
items.quote: No, we don't have such plans. We believe that outsourcing we have to make it more efficient. So, we are believing in that model only.

items.statement: Priority on cash conversion, consumer sell-through, and productive retail expansion for remainder of FY27
items.quote: For the remainder of FY '27, our priorities are consumer sell-through, productive retail expansion and cash conversion.

items.statement: Eligible for NSE listing after March 2027 audited balance sheet; net worth must exceed INR75 crores for three consecutive years
items.quote: We'll be eligible for listing on NSE after March '27 balance sheet. So once the March '27 balance sheet is audited, we will be audited before the 30th of May, then we have to submit to NSE, and we are eligible for listing over there.

items.statement: Target 120 corporate clients by end of FY27; currently at 54 sourced in H1
items.quote: See we have already sourced 54 and I think we should be able to source 120 clients by the year-end.

items.statement: MSME loan book target minimum INR150 crores-plus by March 2027 from current INR131 crores
items.quote: So as of today, it's INR131 crores MSME loan book, and minimum what we are targeting is INR150 crores-plus by end of the year.

items.statement: Expect quarter-on-quarter EWA disbursement growth of 15-20% in H2 FY27
items.quote: We are expecting quarter-on-quarter to grow by at least 15% to 20% on a Q-on-Q basis.

items.statement: Gold loan syndication annual target of INR1,300 crores will be achieved easily
items.quote: That we will achieve. That we will achieve. We will achieve that easily.

items.statement: Second half typically stronger due to festive season EWA demand and March quarter activity
items.quote: The second half is typically stronger for our business, supported by a festive season EWA demand and activity towards the March quarter.

items.statement: Gold loan demand down 30-35% due to falling gold prices and reduced balance transfer cases
items.quote: With the decrease in prices, you know, the demand for balance transfer has also decreased. But to counter that, we are tying up with two new banks.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 54% YoY due to operating leverage from technology-driven model with minimal manual intervention
items.quote: Sir, it's all operating leverage. The entire system is technology-driven. There is minimum manual intervention in the entire system.

items.statement: Current margin levels sustainable as technology handles growth without increasing employee strength or overheads
items.quote: We are using so much technology that the current expenses take care of the growth in business, so that is why our margins are improving.

items.statement: Onboarded 24 new corporate partners in Q2 FY27 across manufacturing, hospitality, education, apparel, technology and financial services
items.quote: During Q2 FY27, we continue to expand our partnerships network across the Earned Wage Access segment. We have onboarded 24 new corporate partners across manufacturing, hospitality, education, apparel, technology and financial services.

items.statement: Total corporate partners now 270; employee base 40,000-42,000 with 5,500 monthly transacting (12-13% engagement)
items.quote: So as now we have 270 corporates. Slowly and steadily, we are onboarding all these corporates migrating all these corporates to the Emerald Ekam platform.

items.statement: MSME loan book AUM at INR131 crores as of Q2 FY27, up from INR125 crores in June 2026
items.quote: See as on date our current AUM is INR131 crores.

items.statement: Launched Emerald Ekam integrated financial wellness platform combining salary access, loans, investments, insurance and employee benefits
items.quote: I'm very glad to announce the launch of Emerald Ekam. It's an integrated financial wellness platform that brings salary access, loans, investments, insurance and the employee benefits together under one digital roof.

items.statement: Revenue mix in Q2 FY27: 49% interest income, 39.2% distribution, 11.8% EWA business
items.quote: This quarter of the total INR100 what we have earned, 49% is from the interest income and 39.2% is from the distribution business and 11.8% from the EWA business.

items.statement: Tied up with SafeGold for digital gold offering on Emerald Ekam platform; silver not yet available
items.quote: Look we have already tied up with SafeGold. We are selling digital gold through them in Emerald Ekam. If you go to the Emerald Ekam site, there is a digital gold tab.

items.statement: EWA retention rate 90%; users transact until they leave organization; challenge is getting first transaction
items.quote: Our retention rate in EWA is 90%. So once a user/customer transacts once, they will keep transacting until they leave the organization.

items.statement: MSME loans average ticket INR40 lakhs at ~18% yield; EWA max limit INR1 lakh at 30-36% IRR
items.quote: So MSME loans average ticket is about INR40 lakhs, and yield is around 18%. For EWA, about INR1 lakh is the maximum limit. There is no downward limit. Minimum is INR100, and maximum is up to INR1 lakh for the EWA program, and IRR over there is around 30% to 36%.

items.statement: Bank funding costs unchanged so far; may increase if RBI hikes repo by another 25bps
items.quote: As of now, both the State Bank and the ICICI have not increased our rate of interest. But if another quarter RBI increases, I think they might increase it.

items.statement: Gold loan business under stress due to RBI tightening gold loan distribution policy and bank appraisal/sourcing practices
items.quote: During this quarter, the gold loan business has been under a little stress. That's basically DSA business because of certain regulatory requirements, which has influenced bank appraisals and the sourcing practices.

items.statement: Technology and AI adoption across departments eliminates need for additional headcount to support growth
items.quote: Talin is very good in adoption of technology, and we have put artificial intelligence in a number of our departments. So the need for more employees was not required.

items.statement: Signed Unity Small Finance Bank as lead facilitator for bank transfers; second pan-India partnership for Unity; another private sector bank tie-up imminent
items.quote: However, we have recently signed with Unity Small Finance Bank as the lead facilitator for funding of the bank transfers. This is the second partnership they have signed pan-India. We are in the process of signing off with another private sector bank, which we should be announcing shortly.

items.statement: Impairment loss on financial assets INR21.2 lakhs in Q1 FY27 and INR28.8 lakhs in Q2 FY27 including standard provisioning, default provisioning and recoveries
items.quote: And this quarter, it is about INR28.8 lakhs. So this includes the standard provisioning coupled with a provisioning towards the default assets and then minus the recovery that was done from the asset written off in the previous quarter.

items.statement: EWA monthly disbursement run rate INR14 crores in Q2 FY27 plus INR16 crores cross-sell; Q1 was INR12.5 crores
items.quote: See currently, if you talk about only the EWA, we are doing on an average about INR14 crores, and rest is what INR16 crores is from cross-selling on a monthly basis.

items.statement: MSME loan average duration 2 years (minimum 3 months); gold loan syndication Q4 FY26 INR125 crores, current run rate INR80 crores with HDFC/ICICI
items.quote: See it depends. Normally, you can say about 2 years. Rohitash Arora: And these loans are? Sanjay Aggarwal: Minimum we do it for 3 months and average duration is about 2

items.statement: Existing bankers (SBI, ICICI) have not increased credit costs despite RBI repo at 5.50%
items.quote: Yes, bankers have not -- our existing bankers have not increased the credit cost.

items.statement: NSE listing planned after March 2027 audited balance sheet; requires net worth >INR75 crores for 3 consecutive years
items.quote: NSE listing requirement is for 3 consecutive years, our net worth should be more than INR75 crores. And for the last 2 years in the '25 year, sorry -- so the net was more than INR75 crores.

items.statement: Management emphasizes steady, collection-focused growth over aggressive disbursement; cites 30 years experience and Aditya Puri/Tushar Chopra philosophy
items.quote: Now ramping up the NBFC business much easy, if we have a today top line of INR10 crores we can make INR20 crores in six months. But then it's not a disbursement business, it's a collection business.

items.statement: Gold loan volumes may recover in next 2 quarters if gold prices stabilize; new bank partnerships to offset decline
items.quote: I think gold loan business should -- if the gold prices stabilize, I think we should pick up in the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 consolidated total income INR10.07 crores (+45.81% YoY), PAT INR5.30 crores (+47.14% YoY); H1 FY27 total income INR19.51 crores (+42.94% YoY), PAT INR10.18 crores (+49.80% YoY)
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, Q2 FY27 total income stood at INR10.07 crores, registering year-on-year growth of 45.81% while PAT stood at INR5.30 crores, growing at 47.14% over the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Expects 9%-10% tonnage growth in H2 FY27 and medium term
items.quote: The similar growth we are expecting even in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin of 21%-22% going forward
items.quote: Yes, around 21%-22% is a sustainable EBITDA margin even going forward.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 10%-12% for next year assuming no realization change
items.quote: Overall, assume that if there is no change in the realization from now onward, for the next year at least, the guidance will be the revenue will increase at least around 10%-12%.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded to 23.3% from 19.7% YoY
items.quote: Correspondingly, the EBITDA margin expanded to 23.3% from 19.7% in the corresponding quarter last year, an improvement of 367 basis points.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin to sustain at 23%+ in near term, 21%-22% long term
items.quote: But as of now, considering these volumes and the current cost structure, whatever it is there, the 23% plus margin is sustainable.

items.statement: October tonnage growth ~20% YoY driven by festival demand and own fleet advantage
items.quote: Our tonnage growth in the month of October is around 20% plus compared to year-on-year.

items.statement: Volume growth across all industries; FMCG and textile stronger during festival season
items.quote: No, across all industry, because it is a widespread operations what we are having. Considering these festival seasons and all, now FMCG and textile, there is a good growth compared to the industrial and other segments.

items.statement: Freight rate hikes of ~5% in April and ~4% in May drove 9% realization improvement
items.quote: We did an increase at the beginning of the year from April 1st around 5% and in mid of May, we increased around 4%. There is a 9% increase in the freight rates.

items.statement: Fuel cost per litre rose from ~INR85 to INR97, pressuring operating costs
items.quote: The cost per litre increased significantly from approximately INR 85- INR 97, putting pressure on our operating cost structure.

items.statement: Fuel escalation clauses in contractual agreements (17%-18% of revenue) pass through fuel price changes
items.quote: With the contractual customers, most of the agreements as of today, we are having a fuel escalation clause. So based on that formula, whatever changes will happen, either it is increase or decrease, accordingly, we have to pass it on to the customers.

items.statement: If fuel price falls >5%, will reduce freight rates ~2.5% for every 5% fuel drop, margins maintained
items.quote: See, margin will be again at an optimum level. Margin, it will support further, little bit we can add to the margin. Always, how the maths will work, for every INR2 change in the fuel rate, there is a 1% change in the freight rates.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex INR158 cr (INR76 cr Q1, INR82 cr Q2) for vehicles and land/buildings
items.quote: Our capital expenditure for the first half stood at around INR158 crores, comprising around INR76 crores in quarter one and INR82 crores in quarter two.

items.statement: H2 FY27 capex expected INR150-160 cr; annual run-rate INR250-300 cr for vehicles and selective properties
items.quote: in the second half, again, we are expecting a capital expenditure of around INR150 crores, INR160 crores, which is including the vehicl es as well as some of the one or two properties what we are planning

items.statement: Added 51 branches in Q2, 67 in H1 FY27; new branches contributed ~2% of 10% volume growth
items.quote: During this quarter, we added 51 branches, taking the total number of new branches added during the first half to 67 numbers.

items.statement: Fleet at 5,941 vehicles end-H1; 76% debt-free, 11% fully depreciated; shifting to higher capacity vehicles
items.quote: As of the end of H1 FY27, our fleet comprised 5,941 vehicles. We continue to follow a disciplined fleet rationalization program involving the replacement and scrapping of older vehicles while improving the utilization of our existing owned fleet.

items.statement: Trade receivable cycle healthy at ~10-11 days due to paid/to-pay LTL model
items.quote: Consequently, our trade receivable cycle remains very healthy at approximately hardly around 10 - 11 days.

items.statement: H1 FY27 operating cash flow before WC changes INR415 cr; net operating cash flow INR363 cr
items.quote: The cash generated from operations before working capital changes is around INR415 crores, compared with around INR314 crores in the last first half year. Net cash generated from operating activities increased to INR363 crores from INR334 crores.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR337 cr (Sep 30) from INR440 cr (Mar 31); net debt/EBITDA 0.3x from 0.4x
items.quote: Despite these investments, we have successfully reduced our n et debt to INR337 crores as of September 30, compared with INR440 crores as on March 31, 2026. Our net debt -to-EBITDA ratio has consequently improved to 0.3 x from 0.4x at the end of FY 2026

items.statement: Buyback of up to INR280 cr at INR320/share (87.5 lakh shares, ~5% equity) approved; promoters not participating; tender window closed Nov 2, settlement Nov 9
items.quote: The board had recommended a share buyback program aggregating up to INR280 crores at a price of INR320 per equity share. The proposed buyback covers up to 87.5 lakh equity shares, representing approximately 5% of the company's paid-up equity share capital.

items.statement: ROCE ~25% last year; expects 30%+ this year after buyback and capital reduction
items.quote: If you see in the last year, we did almost around 25%. Considering the buyback and reduction in the capital, this year we are expecting our ROCE will be at least around 30% plus.

items.statement: Regained business from customers who left after freight rationalization; pursuing all-India contracts with corporate clients
items.quote: We have successfully regained business and tonnage from certain customers who had earlier discontinued services following our freight rate rationalization and strategic withdrawal from low-margin contracts.

items.statement: Service differentiation (own fleet, network, 10L+ customers, low claims) enables pricing power and volume growth despite rate hikes
items.quote: Because of this, whatever demand actually we made, we are in a position to give the service. Our tonnage growth in the month of October is around 20% plus compared to year-on-year.

items.statement: Bulk fuel procurement currently uneconomical (INR120-125 vs spot INR98-100); will resume if fuel prices fall
items.quote: The fuel what we are getting from the outside, if it is, say, INR100 as of today, INR98, INR100, the bulk purchase, it is in the range of around INR120, INR125.

items.statement: If fuel price drops >5%, will cut freight rates ~2.5% but maintain margins via selective route pricing and bulk procurement savings
items.quote: If tomorrow, assume that the scenario changes, definitely that option will be always open with us. Whatever savings we will do out of the bulk purchase, that is again will benefit to improve in the margins and no need to pass on that benefit to the customers.

items.statement: Employee increment process under review; no specific timeline yet
items.quote: Yes, we are examining again to consider the increment process. But shortly we will inform about it. As of today, there is no specific timeline as such, but definitely we are working around it.

items.statement: Realization improvement driven by freight rate hikes, not route mix; intra-state and inter-state margins similar
items.quote: Going forward, because of addition of new branches and new routes, that is not a significant contribution to the realization. The realization is directly related to the freight rates.

items.statement: Claim ratio negligible (decimals) vs industry 10%-12%; supports customer retention and pricing
items.quote: See, our claim ratio is hardly in decimal as compared to the other operator. If you compare, it is at least in the range of around 10%-12% claim ratio. But in our case, it is hardly any decimals.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 India hospital EBITDA margin exceeded 26%, among industry best, despite ARPOB well below peers
items.quote: And on the margin side, yes, it has gone up to more than 26%, which is now among the best in the industry, even though our ARPOB remains well below peers.

items.statement: Doctors and nursing costs fell 1.9% QoQ due to operating leverage on largely fixed clinical cost base
items.quote: Along with better realizations, we've also had the benefit of operating leverage on the costs where our doctors and nursing costs have come down by 1.9% QoQ, which has added to the margin.

items.statement: Management does not target specific margins; focus is on volume growth and affordable pricing
items.quote: Just to clarify, we don't target any specific margins. The margins you see, which are best-in-class despite an ARPOB that is significantly lower than peers, are a reflection of the huge amount of effort we've put in over the past 10 years in digitization, process improvement, supply chain and addressing every single driver of unnecessary cost in the company.

items.statement: Oncology drugs under price cap are only part of 15% oncology revenue; caps effective Nov 9; company supports transparent affordable pricing
items.quote: Oncology is about 15% of India hospital revenue, and the drugs that have come under the cap are only a part of it. I think the caps will go live from 9th of November, and we'll have a better idea at that point in time.

items.statement: Insurance combined loss reduced from INR33 crore to INR22 crore QoQ; Cayman insurance loss fell from $3.7M to $1.1M
items.quote: Nishant Singh: Prithvi, just to correct, the numbers have not worsened. The combined loss of the 2 businesses was around INR33 crores last quarter, and this quarter it is INR22 crores. So the losses have come down actually. Even for Cayman, if you look at the insurance losses, the number is down from $3.7 million to $1.1 million

items.statement: Insurance claims ratio trending down quarter-to-quarter; retail and SME book growing; break-even timeline not given
items.quote: The claims ratios themselves, if you look at quarter-to-quarter, that has come down significantly and it is trending -- continues to trend in the right direction.

items.statement: Will not give up on insurance nor pursue at any cost; adapting strategy, keeping spend low; clinics proven valuable and will continue
items.quote: Prithvi, neither we will give up on insurance nor we will pursue this at any cost. There were a set of strategies we had in mind when we first started out, and some did not work as well as expected. We are adapting and pivoting, and we're keeping the amount of money spent as low as possibly we can.

items.statement: Insurance loss INR14 crore, clinic loss INR8 crore in Q2 FY27; clinic business merging into hospital reporting
items.quote: Health insurance is around INR14 crores and clinics around INR8 crores. Last quarter, insurance was INR19 crores, which has now come down to INR14 crores, and clinics from INR14 crores to INR8 crores.

items.statement: UK business evaluated over 5-7 year horizon; insurance not measured on standalone ROCE; target is zero cash burn in insurance
items.quote: For the U.K. business, I think a 5 to 7-year time horizon is a good way of looking at the business because we have just entered and there is a journey that we have to achieve on that business. As far as the insurance business is concerned, we are not running a stand-alone health insurance company. It's part of the continuum of care.

items.statement: Group ROCE 15-16%; UK dilutes ROCE by 4-5%; expected to bridge over 5 years as India capex cycle ends
items.quote: So at a group level, our ROCE is between 15% to 16%. That's because we've come off a huge investment in Cayman as well as the investment we've made in U.K. and India entering the capex phase. But the dilution, which is coming purely because of U.K. is about 4% to 5% that we will want to bridge over the next 5 years or so.

items.statement: IP volumes up 4% YoY, OP footfall up 12.5% YoY; ARPOB rose from INR17.5M to INR19.5M annualised YoY
items.quote: So on IP volumes, we've seen 4% increase year-on-year. OP footfall, we've seen around 12.5% growth. ARPOB, as you said, has increased from INR17.5 million to INR19.5 million (annualised) year-on-year, as we focus more on high-end procedures and greater use of robotics.

items.statement: IP footfalls grew 6% QoQ and ~4% YoY; Eastern cluster transition issue settling; expect stronger footfall growth in Q3 and Q4
items.quote: Our IP footfalls have actually grown 6% quarter-on-quarter and almost 4% year-on-year. So we have been seeing IP growth on a continued basis between quarter.

items.statement: International patients 6-7% of hospital revenue, mainly from Bangladesh; growth organic, not targeted; subject to macro fluctuations
items.quote: International patients contribute around 6% to 7% of hospital revenue, but it is not something we specifically target. And when it comes to the volume, it is subject to a lot of these macro issues, which can fluctuate quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Occupancy 60-65% traditionally calculated; focus on throughput not occupancy; no bed additions currently
items.quote: Typically, it's 60% to 65%, but we follow the throughput model because occupancy usually is calculated on midnight beds. And when you're doing more and more efficient turnaround on care, that gets distorted if you only look at occupancy.

items.statement: Adding ~635 beds in FY28; quarterly addition guidance given 1 quarter in advance as facilities commission
items.quote: As and when our facilities are ready to be commissioned, we will share that guidance 1 quarter in advance.

items.statement: ALOS target 4-4.1 days over next 4-6 quarters from current 4.3-4.5; high-acuity cases keep ALOS elevated
items.quote: Like I mentioned even the last quarter, we want to -- over the next 4 to 6 quarters, we want to come closer towards 4 or 4.1 because we have a higher mix of certain very high ALOS procedures, the transplants, the bone marrow transplants and certain very high-end medical admission patients.

items.statement: UK acquisition on track for cost synergies; GCC rolled out; digital platform certification in 4-5 months; revenue side slower due to NHS seasonality and private channel building
items.quote: We have made progress on the building blocks. But as you rightly identified, it's not yet translating into additional revenue into the business, but we hope that will change fairly soon. On the cost side, we have seen good changes.

items.statement: Cayman insurance loss dropped from $5.4M to $3.7M to $1.1M over three quarters; July 2027 major repricing; aim negligible losses before then
items.quote: If you look at the quarterly trend of insurance losses, approximately, it was $5.4 million 2 quarters ago, $3.7 million in the previous quarter and $1.1 million this quarter. The reduction from $3.7 million to $1.1 million is a huge one.

items.statement: Cayman hospital growth driven by integrated care strategy and cost reduction; best growth days behind due to island size; focus on securing patient base
items.quote: We've always maintained the best days of growth for Cayman are behind it. Our size is a limiting factor and an anchor on our growth in that small island.

items.statement: H1 cash conversion ~88% vs historical 93%; shortfall from India and Cayman collection delays; UK cash conversion fine; expect normalization full year
items.quote: The reason you have seen a slightly lesser cash conversion in H1 is coming from India and Cayman. There has been a slight delay in both India and Cayman in terms of collections. Typically, Q2 is a

items.statement: UK separation costs from vendor renegotiations after carve-out; diseconomies of scale; costs known now and being mitigated; annualized benefits flowing over quarters
items.quote: Therefore, all our external vendors, for example, Microsoft or any and every kind of vendor had to -- we had to novate agreements and have essentially fresh agreements with these people. And naturally, as you can expect, there are certain diseconomies of scale when we went from a larger group to a smaller company.

items.statement: Cybersecurity a huge concern; cannot revert to pen-and-paper; must spend more on better systems; recent vulnerability patched quickly
items.quote: The wrong response to AI-powered attacks on critical infrastructure is to say, okay, let's go back to pen and paper. We cannot go back to those days. We've seen so much efficiency gain. Our patients move through the system much faster. Our nurses are less hassled at work. There's so much information flowing in our systems that going back to pen and paper is impossible for us. We just need to spend

items.statement: AI used in radiology (proven), voice bots, data interpretation for patient lists and OT scheduling; no decision-making errors; focused on low-hanging efficiency fruit
items.quote: AI in radiology predates LLMs. This is a technology that's fairly proven and is not prone towards making mistakes. AI-based radiology interpretation is now the gold standard the world over. We've been using it with great success. The rest of our applications use voice bots or just simple data interpretations from the information that we have to generate, say, for example, a set of patients with ou

items.statement: Building large integrated healthcare system across 2-3 geographies; leverage cross-country learnings; GCC in Bangalore drives cost savings across India, UK, Cayman
items.quote: So the thing we're trying to build is a very large integrated health care system across at least 2 or 3 geographies so that we're not exposed to any one country's, let's say, vagaries of whether it is currency depreciation or any sort of macroeconomic risk or be able to cater to different patient profiles across countries and leverage cross-country learnings from one country and then apply it to a

items.statement: Welcome IRDAI regulations; hospital channel for insurance distribution reduces cost; no significant strategy change anticipated
items.quote: We do welcome the IRDAI regulations. I think any move that adds value for the customer is welcome for us. We are the first hospital group to directly promote a health insurer. So we agree that, for example, hospitals are a good channel to offer health insurance to customers, which is one of the distribution channels to approach to make the process simpler for the customer, reduce cost.

items.statement: Insurance sold to employers/employee groups and retail to NH patients; group heavy initially, moderating over time; focus on loss ratios and network service
items.quote: We sell to employers and employee groups. On a retail basis, we sell largely, though not exclusively, to people who have a relationship with NH. And that -- hopefully that will continue.

items.statement: UK private (non-NHS) revenue share increasing from ~7%; not disclosing exact percentage; NHS contracting seasonal, reset April 1
items.quote: On the last part of your question, on private, that is non-NHS revenue, we are seeing an increase. We are not disclosing the exact percentage, but we are seeing small steps towards growing the non-NHS books of business.

items.statement: UK revenue recovery of 3-4 million additional per quarter would start showing cost benefits; annualized effects over several quarters
items.quote: So even if you go 1 or 2 quarters back, which is just 3 million, 4 million additional revenue for the quarter, we will start seeing these benefits flow in. But more significantly, once -- with time because these are changes we've made very recently. So the effect of them will flow in over a few quarters.

items.statement: Q2 margin uplift seasonal; Q3 typically muted; do not guide margins; follow industry trend for forecasting
items.quote: We do not guide on margins, but as you know, quarters are seasonal in health care. Q2 is a higher margin quarter. Q3 is slightly muted. So you should go with the trend you've seen in health care rather than extrapolate the current quarter.

items.statement: UK and Cayman revenue and costs in local currency; India bills in corresponding currency per transfer pricing; OCI shows positive currency conversion impact
items.quote: Revenue, cost, everything is in local currency terms. And even when we are billing from India, we bill in the corresponding currency as per the transfer pricing guidelines of India. So therefore, it is kind of BAU and you don't have to factor anything exceptionally for that.

items.statement: Revenue target of Rs 1,000 crores by FY28
items.quote: Our ambition is to achieve Rs. 1,000 crores in annual revenue by FY '28.

items.statement: Fully automated Khalapur facility for 1,000-liter IBC containers expected operational by Q3 FY27
items.quote: Our fully automated Khalapur facility for 1,000-liter IBC container is expected to be operational by Q3 FY 2027.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization around 64% last year, practical maximum 85-90%
items.quote: Yes, around 64%, yes. So, the last year, it was 64% approximately.

items.statement: Current capacity can support revenue of approximately Rs 425 crores without additional capex
items.quote: So, approximately Rs. 425 crores you can reach easily.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 12.41%, H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 14.34%
items.quote: EBITDA stood at Rs. 1,188.55 lakhs up by Rs. 101.97% year-on-year with a margin of 12.41%.

items.statement: Management targets sustainable double-digit EBITDA margins, aims for improvement
items.quote: I think double digit EBITDA is a good in this kind of market scenario. And we are trying to get over those things.

items.statement: Overall demand very good across most industries, positive outlook for future
items.quote: Overall demand is very good in the market. As we already said, we are supplying to many of the industries. So, I think one or two industries is down, but otherwise many industries are doing really good and the demand is very good.

items.statement: Exports currently ~1.5% of revenue, major markets USA, Canada, Europe, expecting growth after approvals
items.quote: So, the export yet not grown up good, but yes, in 6 months, around 1.5% of the total growth.

items.statement: Industrial packaging 81.88%, hospital furniture parts 16.27%, infrastructure furniture 1.86% of Q1 FY27 revenue
items.quote: Industrial packaging revenue stood at approximately 81.88%, hospital furniture parts revenue approximately 16.27%, infrastructure furniture and other recorded revenue of approximately 1.86% of total revenue for Q1 FY '26-27.

items.statement: Focusing on higher margin products, niche items share increased to 16%+ from 13-15%
items.quote: We were at around 13%, 14%, 15%. And now it is around 16% plus. So, I think, we consider this is a good and you will see a good progress, as like you can see 30% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: No hedging of polymer prices, 90-95% sourced domestically
items.quote: In India, polymers have not been hedged officially. So, definitely, we are also not doing the same thing. And we are buying 90% or 95% from India.

items.statement: H1 revenue split typically 40-60 between H1 and H2
items.quote: So, generally, 40-60 is the ratio.

items.statement: Total borrowing Rs 9,648.44 lakhs, cash balance Rs 6.07 lakhs, debt-to-equity 0.76x as of September 2026
items.quote: Our total borrowing stood at around Rs. 9,648.44 lakhs with cash and bank balance of Rs. 6.07 lakhs as of September 2026. Our debt-to-equity ratio stood at 0.76x in H1 FY '27.

items.statement: No inorganic growth announcements currently, things to be announced later
items.quote: Sir, I think, things to be announced very well. Right now, there is no announcement yet.

items.statement: IBC vertical offers capital turnover of approximately 15 times vs 8-10 times for other products
items.quote: The vertical offers attractive potential with capital turnover of approximately 15 times, compared with around 8-10 times for other products.

items.statement: Raw material prices have gone up but market prices also increased; pass-through effect observed
items.quote: The raw material prices have gone up. The raw material prices have gone up. Everybody knows that. Every raw material after the oil issues and all, every prices there is there. But the prices of the market has also gone up. So it is kind of a pass-through.

items.statement: Value-added share to reach 70-80% in next 2 years from ~20% currently; HR, stainless, auto steel, specialty driving mix shift
