items.statement: International constant currency growth estimated at 8-10% YoY range; majority of exports shipped by air
items.quote: I would say, Sanjay-ji, it's in the range of maybe say 8% to 10%, depends on which month or the realization comes in. Like dollar is fluctuating a lot, But I would say that could be the range.

items.statement: Management confident of being among top 1-4 aligner players in 2-5 years; trust factor and 36-year track record as key differentiators
items.quote: There are going to be top 1, 2, 3, 4 players and we are definitely going to be among them. What number it will be, time will tell. Our aspiration is always to be the number one, but we feel that the trust factor on an aligner case for a dentist is very, very important.

items.statement: Received tariff refund of approximately INR5.5 crores excluding interest, to reflect in Q3 FY27 results
items.quote: Additionally, I would like to highlight that we have recently received a tariff refund of approximately INR5.5 crores excluding interest, which will be reflected in our Q3 FY27 results.

items.statement: Scanner subscription model carries balance sheet risk if deployment scales significantly; laptop cost inflation doubled to ~INR2 lakhs
items.quote: So from that perspective, if you could show in terms of like how many scanners you intend to put up on the subscription basis, and what happens to someone who have recently bought, is there a flexibility for him to get into subscription? Because the word will spread, and so the other dentist would also demand a similar model from you. Then how, how are you going to look for that factor?

items.statement: QIP of INR700 crores planned for November; INR175 crores for debt repayment and WS promoter payout, INR50-70 crores for WS capacity expansion, INR300 crores for working capital, remainder for US office and Class B manufacturing setup
items.quote: We are progressing with preparations for the proposed QIP and are targeting November, subject to regulatory approvals, market conditions, and other applicable requirements.

items.statement: QIP proceeds allocation: INR175 crores for debt repayment and WS promoter payout, INR50-70 crores for WS insulator capacity expansion, INR300 crores for working capital, significant amount for US office and Class B manufacturing
items.quote: Out of the INR700 crores, about INR175 crores is for repaying the debt and the promoters of the company, WS. We are expanding in that organization another INR50 crores to INR70 crores to increase our capacity across porcelain and composite insulators.

items.statement: Consolidated order book crossed INR2,000 crores excluding Win-Win Specialty Insulators
items.quote: Our consolidated order book for the first time crossed INR2,000 crores, excluding the order book of Winwin Specialty Insulators.

items.statement: Quality Power coil division order book INR600 crores with anticipated INR200-500 crores intake in coming months; Mehru instrument transformers at INR600+ crores with L1 tenders pending; Endoks power electronics stable awaiting PCS shipments
items.quote: Quality Power, last year we did about INR220 crores, give and take, revenue. Our current order book is about INR600 crores. We anticipate anywhere between INR200 crores to INR500 crores of an order intake in the next few months.

items.statement: Turkey PCS factory for BESS at Nigde commenced full manufacturing operations; billing may commence current quarter subject to contractual milestones and customer acceptance
items.quote: In Turkey, our new PCS factory for BESS applications at Nigde has also commenced manufacturing operations. The facility is already operating in full manufacturing mode, with production activities aligned to customer projects.

items.statement: Win-Win Specialty Insulators completed type tests per American and European standards for porcelain insulators up to 400 kV; secured orders for 800 kV HVDC, 765 kV AC and 400 kV AC from major Indian utilities including Power Grid
items.quote: The team has successfully completed type tests in accordance with applicable American and European standards for porcelain insulators up to 400 kV within the last 2 months. At the same time, Win-Win has also secured orders for 800 kV HVDC porcelain insulators and also 765 kV AC and 400 kV AC applications from all the large Indian utilities and equipment manufacturers, including Power Grid.

items.statement: Guidance unchanged; revision expected end of Q3 if execution goes per plan; Q3 may be tough due to factory transitions and low-margin BESS billing, but numbers not expected to decline much
items.quote: The guidance is still not changed at this moment. We normally change guidances in end of Q3. I believe we are halfway there. I think it's too early to start celebrating if you really ask me.

items.statement: INR300 crores of QIP proceeds earmarked for working capital due to elongated cycle from reverse integration into HVDC CTC cable manufacturing (4 months extra working capital per project) and large order pipeline
items.quote: We are also earmarking about INR300 crores for working capital requirements. We have large order pipeline coming in with our new facilities getting qualified in the next couple of months. We would see a huge input requirement from customers, and we've also reverse integrated in the cable manufacturing business.

items.statement: Q3 may see subdued margins due to factory transitions and low-margin BESS project billing; Quality Power and Mehru expected to have good revenue and profit, Endoks could have blockbuster revenue from PCS factory
items.quote: Next quarter could be high in sales for us because it's Q4 for Endoks, but also a lot of BESS projects are being billed in, which means these are low-margin businesses. So, I believe from Quality Power and Mehru, we have good news with regards to revenue and profits.

items.statement: WS Insulators targeting US market directly with own brand for 765 kV insulators after Chinese equipment ban above 69 kV; currently one of only two global suppliers with two-part 765 kV design alongside PPC Insulators
items.quote: We are trying to push that advantage over the next two quarters. We will translate it into orders in the American market at much higher margins, unlike other peers who white-label the insulators. We intend to go directly with our brand inside the US.

items.statement: Endoks PCS factory in Turkey built at ~$2.5 million on existing 45-acre land; R&D spend ~$2 million over 2020-2025 expensed through P&L (not capitalized)
items.quote: The new factory that came in, I think, came in at about $2.5 million, that's it. The land, we already have about 45 acres of land in Turkey, so the land cost was not a big botheration.

items.statement: Win-Win Specialty Insulators acquisition process underway; integration of teams, customer relationships, technical capabilities and operational systems beginning; preserving WS manufacturing strengths and customer relationships while levera
items.quote: We are now beginning the process of integrating the teams and aligning customer relationships, technical capabilities, and operational systems. Our approach is -- our approach will be to preserve the manufacturing strengths and customer relationships established at WS, while leveraging the broader market presence of Quality Power

items.statement: Demand across reactors, instrument transformers, insulators, power conversion equipment, FACTS; driven by transmission infrastructure, HVDC, FACTS, renewable integration, grid stability, energy storage; global supply chain constrained with
items.quote: We continue to witness demand across reactors, instrument transformers, insulators, power conversion equipment's, and FACTS equipment. Investments in transmission infrastructure, HVDC, FACTS, renewable integration, grid stability, and energy storage continue to remain opportunities across our product portfolio.

items.statement: GE Vernova acquired Trench Group (largest competitor) for $9B; Trench has coil, instrument transformer, bushing lines overlapping Quality Power; Quality Power has advantage in FACTS/BESS which Trench lacks; expects sourcing volume increase
items.quote: I believe the sourcing volume from Quality Power can go up drastically over the next 2, 3 years, primarily because nobody would like to buy from the competition if option is given. So, I would say in the short term, we will have some synergies coming with GE, but on the medium term, I think we will stand to gain a lot more from Hitachi and Siemens.

items.statement: WS Insulators resolving LPG gas constraint: new PNG pipeline from GAIL commissioned next Monday enabling cheaper gas and full production ramp-up over next quarter
items.quote: The factory earlier had fallen into trouble because of want of LPG gases. Now, we've got a new PNG pipeline coming in. Next Monday, we will get a cheaper gas coming in, flowing in through GAIL pipelines.

items.statement: CTC magnetic wire facility at Sangli: machines installed, trials started; customer qualification needed; 4-5 months timeline; Q4 FY27 expected to discuss commercial use; currently using vendor capacity
items.quote: We have started trial, but I don't think we will use the cables immediately. We will need to qualify it with customers. We are giving ourselves about 4, 5 months on that project. Maybe Q4 this year is when you will hear us talk about it.

items.statement: Hyperinflation accounting (Ind AS 29) impact: Q1 FY27 INR8 crore debit to P&L; Q2 FY27 INR4 crore profit; net INR4 crore credit to P&L in Q2
items.quote: The hyperinflation for this first quarter was around INR8 crores debited to P&L. And in the second quarter, it was a profit of around INR4 crores. So, the net credit to P&L was INR4 crores as debit as loss.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue INR285.45 crores, PAT INR63.33 crores (80.10% YoY growth)
items.quote: For the quarter, our consolidated revenue from operations stood at INR285.45 crores, while profit after tax reached INR63.33 crore, representing a year-on-year growth of 80.10%.

items.statement: Focus on working capital management, procurement planning, customer collections, capex monitoring; reviewing subsidiary financials for margins, inventory, receivables, cash flow
items.quote: Working capital management, procurement planning, customer collections, and monitoring capital expenditure. We continue to review the financial performance of our subsidiaries, with particular attention to margins, inventory, receivables, and cash flow.

items.statement: Acknowledged team efforts across engineering, manufacturing, quality, procurement, finance, project execution for commissioning two facilities, regulatory approvals, audits, customer commitments; shop floor employees worked through operatio
items.quote: I would like to acknowledge the efforts of our teams across engineering, manufacturing, quality, procurement, finance and project execution, who have managed these responsibilities alongside our ongoing operations.

items.statement: US regulation banning Chinese equipment above 69 kV transmission category creates opportunity for WS Insulators as one of only two global suppliers (with PPC) of two-part 765 kV design with approvals
items.quote: The new act in US, which has come up recently in the last 2 months, where all Chinese equipment's are banned after 69 kV, that's a transmission category, which means that Europeans are already booked out.

items.statement: Global supply chain for specialized electrical equipment remains constrained; geopolitical developments, changing trade conditions, logistics disruptions, extended procurement lead times pressure manufacturers and project schedules
items.quote: The global supply chain for specialized electrical equipment remains constrained. Geopolitical developments, changing trade conditions, logistics disruptions and extended procurement lead times are placing additional pressure on manufacturers and project schedules.

items.statement: WS Insulators targeting higher margins in US market by selling directly under own brand vs white-labeling; taking delta on profits from 6-9 month lead time vs industry 18 months
items.quote: We will translate it into orders in the American market at much higher margins, unlike other peers who white-label the insulators. We intend to go directly with our brand inside the US.

items.statement: WS Insulators secured orders from all large Indian utilities and equipment manufacturers including Power Grid for 800 kV HVDC, 765 kV AC, 400 kV AC applications
items.quote: Win-Win has also secured orders for 800 kV HVDC porcelain insulators and also 765 kV AC and 400 kV AC applications from all the large Indian utilities and equipment manufacturers, including Power Grid.

items.statement: Quality Power has relationships with Hitachi, Siemens, GE (90% of world HVDC/FACTS business); expects increased sourcing from Hitachi and Siemens as they avoid GE-owned Trench
items.quote: Hitachi, Siemens, and GE own about 90% of the world business on HVDC and FACTS, and 70%, 75% is the other two. So, I wouldn't say too much negative. I would just say that we have a lot of things to work with the other two for increasing our volumes.

items.statement: Guided for at least 50% revenue growth in FY28
items.quote: With regards to next year, we have given a public guidance that we intend to grow at least around 50%, 5-0.

items.statement: Insulator orders booked at 20-25% EBIT; could be north of 30% without duty; US integration could reach 40%+
items.quote: At this moment, being in SEZ, when we come into India, we have about 8.25% duty. But in spite of that, I think the orders are being booked between 20% and 25% EBIT. If we didn't have to pay the duty, I think it would have been north of 30%.

items.statement: Group stable margin guided at about 25%; Quality Power >25%, Mehru 22-23%, Insulators ~25%, Power electronics 25%, PCS 10-12%
items.quote: So, I believe I can talk to you as a group. Quality Power will be always higher than 25%. Mehru, they would have delivered 22%, 23%, if not for the copper and oil hit that has happened. Insulators, our orders are being booked at about 25%. Power electronics, our traditional business, even if you look at this quarter, they've got 25%, but the PCS, as I said, about 10% or 12%.

items.statement: Order book execution timeline 15-18 months for 95%+ of orders; 99% fixed-price contracts
items.quote: So, we've always guided that we would be happy between 15 and 18 months. I would say 95% plus of the order book would be between 15 and 18 months. That's where we are.

items.statement: Near-term pipeline: INR500-600 cr reactor orders, INR400 cr instrument transformers, INR400-500 cr insulator orders
items.quote: I would say in the immediate future, you can see about INR500 crores to INR600 crores of reactor orders, about INR400 crores of instrument transformers, and another INR400 crores, INR500 crores of insulator orders, just to give an idea.

items.statement: INR25 cr capex for facility shift consolidating reactor/coil products; old factory kept for PCS/group businesses for at least a year
items.quote: So, it will not be additional. We will be shifting all of our reactor manufacturing into that facility, consolidating all coil products into that facility. The current facility, we are keeping it open for either bringing in the PCS business or any of the group businesses that we get into.

items.statement: 60 customer audits pending for Sangli plant; 1-2 audits per week; initial set expected in ~6 months
items.quote: So, we have got 60 audits, sir. 6-0 audits from different customers. So, let's say, Railway is one of the customer, Power Grid is one, Adani is one, you know, Sterlite is another. So, like that, let's say PG&E in America is a customer, ConEd is a customer. So, each customer has its own audit.

items.statement: Peak capacity utilization takes 3-4 years to train 400+ people per reactor; not machinery-driven; guidance given annually
items.quote: I would say factory's peak utilization don't come overnight. It takes a lot of people. None of our products are made by machinery, everything is handmade. So, before a reactor goes out of the factory, right from the supply chain, the cable, the painting, the winding, the assembly, I would say at least 400 people touch the equipment.

items.statement: Global transmission insulator demand-supply gap: demand ~4x supply; 18-month delivery lead times for 765kV/HVDC porcelain
items.quote: I believe the current demand-supply is demand may be about four, supply may be about one. And no capacity is coming up, which means that today if you buy a switchgear or anything on 765 kV, the delivery is 18 months, not because of switchgear, because of the porcelain.

items.statement: Data center reactor orders await financial closure; HVDC pipeline strong domestically (Make in India) and globally (Australia, Abu Dhabi, Korea, UK, US)
items.quote: For the data center business, we have shaken hands with multiple customers in the US. They are awaiting their financial closure before giving in an LOA. But also we have capacity constraints coming in already, because we have multiple FACTS orders that we are seeing coming in, some HVDC orders.

items.statement: Fixed-price contracts with raw material buffers; cannot pass on cost increases mid-contract; new contracts signed at higher prices
items.quote: We cannot pass on. These are fixed-price contracts. But the new contracts are signed at higher prices. So, if the prices of these raw materials or oil falls after a few months, we would stick to the same old prices. The customer does not negotiate after that.

items.statement: Inventory buildup from Turkey (INR20 cr chipsets/IGBTs) and insulator/bushing stocking; prefer inventory over stockouts given near-zero debt
items.quote: So, because Endoks had to take in the chipsets and IGBT, I think there's about INR20 crores of inventory coming in from Turkey. From Quality Power and Mehru, we have been stocking up on insulators and bushings and whatever is a long lead-time item, because we have to also match quarterly numbers.

items.statement: QIP of INR300 cr for working capital to fund 4-month cable manufacturing cycle (aluminum, components); expected to recoup in 24-36 months
items.quote: So, we are foreseeing that, even in Mehru, we see that there can be a working capital issue going forward if we keep on expanding the order book. So, this is a pre-emptive that we are doing internally before what we say before we get into a trouble later because just because of order book.

items.statement: QIP targeted around Nov 15-30 after preferential issue listing; EGM done, awaiting regulatory approvals
items.quote: So, we are waiting so we are waiting for the pref to complete. The pref have to get listed. The EGM was done. The pref listing is expected sometime this week before we open the QIP, but being a holiday season, I think if all the regulatory approvals come in time and everything is in order, I think around November 15th to 30th is what we are targeting.

items.statement: Turkey fully hedged; India uses plain vanilla options, active tracking; not covering USD currently due to rupee pressure; mostly domestic content
items.quote: So, we have a active tracking on -- in Turkey, everything is hedged. Nothing is left unhedged. In India, we have an active tracking. We normally do a plain vanilla option. We do not do anything what we say forwards. It's a plain vanilla option.

items.statement: Winwin (WS) has 70-year legacy, supplied Vizag HVDC 25 years ago; 800kV HVDC order secured post-ownership change; packaging insulators with reactors, instrument transformers, voltage dividers
items.quote: WS is a 70-year-old company. It has supplied multiple HVDCs in the country. So, we have a legacy. Actually, in Vizag, where we make it, the Vizag HVDC is being supplied by WS, and it has commissioned 25 years ago, and successfully operated without failures.

items.statement: PCS (power converter) booked at 10-12% margin; battery pass-through; domestic BESS not viable due to regulatory contingent liabilities; focus on export from India
items.quote: We booked the PCS at about 10% to 12%. The battery was a pass-through. But I will have to really push it through the factory to be able to tell you. It's a new product, new factory. Give us some time. About a quarter, I think we will have the published numbers this quarter.

items.statement: Making capacitor and GIS bushings; working with global vendors; will be in both composite and porcelain; not limited to transformer bushings
items.quote: I would rest it at that point. But I can already say that we are making capacitor bushings now, GIS bushings. GIS, we're already started delivering. Capacitors, we're working with a few vendors, global vendors, to be able to deliver. So, bushing does not mean only transformer bushing. Bushing is a very wide category.

items.statement: HVDC orders typically INR100-200 cr each; Barmer HVDC not expected before Q2 next year (engineering takes 1-1.5 years)
items.quote: For HVDC, it's a bulk order where any order goes between INR100 crores and INR200 crores. So, when an HVDC order comes, you will have to plan the capacity, too.

items.statement: Insulator demand sustainable for 5-7 years; Quality Power focused on 400kV, 765kV, HVDC transmission segment only
items.quote: I believe that demand can sustain for at least five to seven years.

items.statement: No territorial allocation unlike MNCs (Hitachi, Siemens, GE restricted to India/Asia); can sell to highest-paying customer globally
items.quote: Whereas, we are not bound by that. So, if there's a pricing pressure in India, we would go to some parts of the world. So, we will sell to the highest-paying customer at that month. So, that is not, I would say, a problem to Indian origin manufacturers, because we do not have territorial allocation.

items.statement: Put/call option for Mehru after 7 years; Endoks stake increase deemed capital misallocation (1% royalty gives tech access); prefer building over buying for next 6-9 months
items.quote: So, for Mehru, we have a put and call option after 7 years. With Endoks, we can do it, but I would say that at this moment, it's a capital misallocation, primarily because we have for 1% royalty bring the same technologies to India. And for the money that we need to pay the remaining 49%, I would say we could get another three or four Mehru kind of companies.

items.statement: Sukrut JV: H1 grew ~40% YoY, profitable; team turnaround from 10 years of losses to monthly profitability achieved; next focus is growth
items.quote: I think they have grown H1 was, I think, almost 40% growth over last year. They have been profitable. We are stabilizing the division. It's obviously a small division. The sales is managed through Yash. We are managing the operational portion of it.

items.statement: Cable business requires 4 months cash flow for manufacturing (100-200 tons aluminum, components); working capital negative impact before margin improvement
items.quote: And the cable business is going to take us about 4 months of cash flow in manufacturing timelines, where we end the vendor credit periods. Obviously, it will improve the margins, but initially you will see a working capital negative impact before it improves.

items.statement: Indian BESS regulations not conducive (decade-long guarantees/warranties, contingent liabilities); NTPC encashed GR Infra bank guarantee; need regulatory change for domestic entry
items.quote: Anything on domestic, you would read about GR Infra's bank guarantee being encashed last quarter by a biggest NTPC. The regulations in India are not conducive for us to get into India. There are too much of contingent liabilities to be able to sell the BESS in India, where the guarantees and warranties goes for more than a decade.

items.statement: Raw material cost pressure: aluminum, resin (petrochemical), copper, oil rose significantly; Q1 margin had Q4 shipments and vendor drawbacks not sustainable
items.quote: B, plus also aluminum price rose quite significantly, along with resin prices. Resin is a petrochemical product, along with paints. So, I think this was expected. The guidance was about 25%, and I'm and I'm happy that my organization teams were able to deliver much higher than that.

items.statement: Land bank: 40 acres free in Vizag, 40 acres in Turkey; Delhi and Pune facilities need capex for capacity; Sangli and Turkey have enough capacity for 2-3 years
items.quote: Fortunately, we sit on a large piece of landholdings now in Vizag, where we have about 40 acres free. And in Turkey also, we have about 40 acres, so land is not a big worry at this moment.

items.statement: Order inflow Q2 INR350 cr vs Q1 INR770 cr; coil/instrument transformer orders expected next quarter; PCS orders from Q4 this year
items.quote: As I said, we would like all our orders to be between 15 and 18 months. These are all fixed-price contracts. If you are not able to put across a capacity faster, then you will end up losing margins if you book on orders. At this moment, I think from the coil and instrument transform business, you will hear some good numbers in the next quarter. From the PCS, you would hear numbers from Q1 -- Q4 th

items.statement: Q2 FY27 was challenging due to below-normal monsoon, drought in parts of India, and weak pest pressure reducing herbicide, insecticide, and fungicide offtake
items.quote: The second quarter of FY '27 was challenging for the domestic agrochemical industry, primarily due to below normal and uneven Southwest monsoons.

items.statement: Expect Q3 FY27 to remain challenging; industry analysts expect agri input earnings to bottom out between October and December 2026 with recovery from Q1 FY28
items.quote: We, therefore, expect Q3 FY '27 to remain a challenging quarter. Industry analysts currently expect Agri input earnings to bottom between -- bottom out between October and December 2026 with a recovery from first quarter of FY '28 as weather conditions normalize.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 16% from 13% YoY; gross margin improved to 30% from 29% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 16% from 13%.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 12% from 10% YoY; gross margin improved to 29% from 26% YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA and EBITDA margin stood at INR50.1 crores and 12% in H1 FY '27 compared with INR41.9 crores and 10% in H1 FY '26.

items.statement: H1 FY27 channel mix: B2C 59%, B2B 35%, exports 6%; Crop Protection 85%, Plant Nutrients 5%, Biologicals 6%
items.quote: Our H1 FY '27 channel mix comprised B2C at 59%, B2B at 35% and exports at 6% of the revenue. During H1 FY '27, Crop Protection contributed 85% of revenue, while Plant Nutrients and biological contributed 5% and 6%, respectively, with the balance from other products.

items.statement: Key product growth in H1 FY27: Nova King 25x (INR9L to INR2.23Cr), Spine 76% (INR2.84Cr to INR5Cr), Fire 31% (INR7.74Cr to INR9.73Cr), Indo Apache 7% (INR10.77Cr to INR11.50Cr)
items.quote: I would also like to highlight the exceptional growth momentum de monstrated by our few products in H1 FY '27, such as Nova King, which surged from INR9 lak hs to INR2.23 crores on Y-to-Y basis, nearly 25x growth. Spine grew from INR2.84 crores to INR5 crores, a robust jump of 76% and growth of our brand Fire was from INR7.74 crores to INR9.73 crores, that is healthy 31% growth on year-to-year bas

items.statement: Export market developments: Egypt +129% YoY, reactivated Sudan, entered Taiwan, new orders via Germany for LatAm, entered Israel for plant nutrition, field trials for Empire and Indo Apache in Brazil
items.quote: Egypt emerged as the strongest export market, recording an impressive growth of 129% year- over-year. We successfully reactivated sales in Sudan, establishing a re newed revenue stream in that market. We successfully entered the Taiwan market, strengthening Indo Gulf's presence across Asia

items.statement: Board proposed reallocating INR8.34Cr unutilized IPO proceeds from in-house DF plant to specialty machinery and dedicated facility for climate stress management and PGR products at Barwasni (9,000 sq ft); expect facility operational by Q4 F
items.quote: As set out in the notice of our AGM, the Board has proposed reallocati on of INR8.34 crores of unutilized IPO proceeds originally earmarked for an in-house DF plant towards specialty machinery and a dedicated production facility for climate stress manag ement and plant growth regulators product at our Barwasni facility in Sonipat on an area of 9,000 square

items.statement: Inventory elevated at INR349.6Cr end-Sept vs INR343.5Cr end-Mar; debtors increased due to low rainfall; working capital cycle increased; expect operating cash flow to turn positive in H2 FY27
items.quote: Inventory stood INR349.6 crores at the end of the September compa red with INR343.5 crores at the end of March '26. Finance cost for H1 FY '27 was INR8.6 crores, 3% higher year-on-year basis. We will continue to manage working capital closely through the se cond half

items.statement: Negative operating cash flow in H1 FY27 due to increased debtors and inventory; expect positive operating cash flow in H2 FY27
items.quote: We are expecting in the second half, we will be in the positive position.

items.statement: Finance cost Q2 FY27 INR4.1Cr, 11% lower YoY; H1 FY27 finance cost INR8.6Cr, 3% higher YoY
items.quote: Finance cost for the quarter was INR4.1 crores, 11% lower than Q2 FY '26. Profit after tax stood at INR25.7 crores as compared with INR20.7 crores in Q2 FY '26, a growth of 24% wit h PAT margin at 10% compared with 8% in Q2 FY '26

items.statement: Three customer bases: B2C brand business domestic, B2B institutional/technicals, overseas customers; legacy distributor loyalty with some doing 60-100% Indogulf sales
items.quote: No. Like we have three kind of customers base. One is B2C, which is b asically brand business domestic. One is B2C -- sorry, B2B, which is basically institutional customers where we sell our technicals, they are basically the big corporates working in India. And then we have overseas customers

items.statement: Subsidiary Abhiprakash Globus revenue grew 58% sequentially to INR33.35Cr in Q2 FY27; entered Chhattisgarh and Odisha
items.quote: Our revenue from the operation grew 58% on a sequential basis, and we clocked at INR33.35 crores. We have entered two new states in this quarter, Chhattisgarh and Orissa, an d we are seeing good initial response for our products

items.statement: Generic agrochemical prices rose 15-20% Mar-May due to Middle East conflict, rupee depreciation, freight, packaging, solvent costs; since June prices corrected to pre-conflict levels; elevated channel inventory and weak demand constrained p
items.quote: In the preceding months, the Middle East conflict and related supply chain disruption pushed generic agrochemical prices up by roughly 15% to 20% between March and May, alongside rupee depreciation and higher freight, packaging and solvent costs. Since June, prices of several generic products have corrected to pre-co nflict levels, while elevated channel inventory and weak demand constrained the i

items.statement: 3 new specialty products commercialized in H1 FY27; one launched in September quarter received positive response; 3 products (Shaan, Polgar, another) sold ~INR11-12Cr in H1
items.quote: Our 3 products has given us good sales in this first half and this one particular product Shaan has already sold in the last six months of around INR4.5 crores and P olgar is around INR4.25 crores. Sanjay Aggarwal: Means almost another Company also, we have sold the products. So almost INR11 crores, INR12 crores we have done maybe means we are quite hopeful for H2 also for these 3

items.statement: Priorities for rest of FY27: deepen farmer engagements, expand differentiated portfolio across specialties and biologicals, pursue selective international opportunities, maintain discipline in procurement, inventory, manufacturing
items.quote: Our priorities for rest of FY '27 are to deepen farmer enga gements, expand our differentiated product portfolio across specialty products and biologicals, pursu e selective international opportunities and maintain discipline in procurement, inventor y and manufacturing

items.statement: DF line facing pricing pressure and shrinking margins; climate stress management emerging as fastest-growing category driven by heat waves, droughts, erratic rainfall
items.quote: After a dedicated commercial and market assessment, the Board and man agement concluded that the DF line was facing pricing pressure and shrinking margins, while climate stress management has emerged as one of the fastest-growing categories in ag ricultural input driven by heat waves, prolonged droughts, erratic rainfall and other abiotic stress that are increasingly affecting crop productivity ac

items.statement: Working with ICAR for 3 years on stress management products; collaborating with Pusa Institute for product development
items.quote: Also in the long term, we have been in the agreement with ICAR for three years where we are developing some stress management products for long term, and we are working closely with the Pusa Institute for the development of a few products in the times to come in this category.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY27 reiterated at INR3,200-3,500 crores, representing 60% growth over FY26
items.quote: We had a guidance to revenue of approximately INR3,200 crores to INR3,500 crores for the full financial year FY27. This would represent growth of 60% compared with FY26

items.statement: Healthy demand from retail partners driving 25.4% volume growth in Q2 and 41% in H1 FY27
items.quote: Our volume has also increased by 25.4% in the quarter and 41.0%in the first half, reflecting healthy demand from all our retail partners and our ability to scale up execution

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin guidance of 5-7% given evolving product mix and growth phase
items.quote: Broadly speaking, we should be in the range of 5 to 7% EBITDA looking at the current dynamics, current market situation

items.statement: Marol facility operational, Jaipur facility interior work ongoing targeting Jan-Feb commissioning
items.quote: Jaipur facility. The furniture means the interior work and, things are going on. Very soon we should be starting once it's finished, maybe Jan or Feb or something

items.statement: Targeting 75-80% manufacturing capacity utilization in coming years as new facilities ramp up
items.quote: And once if our Jaipur facility and all the facilities start, we should be lik e at around 75% to 80% of the manufacturing capacity we should be utilized in coming years

items.statement: Expanding product portfolio across designer, Turkish jewelry, plain gold, CZ and advanced gold categories
items.quote: We have been expanding our offering across categories including designer and Turkish jewelry while deeply deepening engagement with existing customers and onboarding new retail clients

items.statement: Deepening engagement with existing retail partners and onboarding new retail clients across South, West, North and East India
items.quote: We are expanding in new geographies, initially we were present only in South India, then we reached out to West Market. Now we have increased our presence in North India and also in East India

items.statement: Export share doubled to INR82 crores (6-7% of revenue), targeting 6-7% for FY27 with Dubai office approvals in place
items.quote: See, as of now you can always already see that the export has already doubled. We are at INR82 crores. Going forward, once this Dubai office is also in place, we are expecting a large chunk of the business coming from that market also

items.statement: Working capital intensive business requiring inventory buildup for new product launches and facility ramp-ups
items.quote: We are in a growing phase. We are in a consolidating phase. We need more inventory, more the gold, more product launches are there. So, my money will get, stuck in the inventory for some time till, till we find our feet on the ground

items.statement: Rights issue of INR99.83 crores fully utilized for working capital requirements
items.quote: During the quarter, we also successfully raised approximately INR99.83 crores through a rights issue. The proceeds are being deployed towards meeting the Company's working capital requirement

items.statement: Gold metal loans (GML) at 15-20% of stock profile, comfortable increasing to 30% for hedging
items.quote: As of now it's still, at 15%-20% of the stock profile, but we are comfortable going up to 30% looking at the current market dynamics and all

items.statement: Volume CAGR of 43% historically, targeting 25-30% volume growth in near term
items.quote: We have been historically growing at a CAGR of 43% for the past few years. So that's, one thing I can tell you, because that's something we have been achieving it and it will push the momentum

items.statement: Investment in Ratnaveer and Lalithaa Jewellery described as treasury deployment, not strategic diversification
items.quote: Yes, see, basically that needs to be taken as something in the context of treasury management rather than a strategic diversification of our core business

items.statement: Gold price volatility not seen as structural risk due to natural hedging and inventory discipline
items.quote: Our risk management policy is centered around natural hedging and inventory discipline. That's number one. Having said that, gold has historically demonstrated resilience across economic cycles

items.statement: No immediate plans for equity dilution or merger with Utssav; 3-5 year roadmap to be shared in next con call
items.quote: At present we have not decided on diluting any equity or raise now debts and all. Once the facility Jaipur starts and all, and how the demands and all we get it from our customer, on that basis, because see, we are looking out for advanced gold and a ll also from our customers. So, after once the facility has started, the management will take a call how to increase the debt or how to raise it thro

items.statement: Setting up wholly-owned subsidiary with initial investment of INR 2-5 crores for new jewellery categories
items.quote: we have thought that first we open a subsidiary with a very minimal fund, like INR2 crores, INR4 crores, INRS crores at most, since it is a new venture

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity increased from 2.5 to 4 tonnes; bridal segment started with 20 karigars, scaled to 40
items.quote: We have already increased our capacity from 2.5 to 4 tonnes; consequently, we will need to increase our headcount.

items.statement: Massive order volume from corporates with pipeline of 80 showrooms in 2 years; all major corporates associated
items.quote: Today we have a massive volume of orders. Corporates are expanding rapidly in India. I cannot name some corporates, but they have pipeline programs for 80 showrooms within two years.

items.statement: Profitability improves with rising gold prices due to percentage-based charging model; volumes remain intact
items.quote: If gold prices increase, our profitability actually improves. The reason is that we charge on a percentage basis. If I charge 6% on a product worth INR1,00,000, I earn INR6,000. If that same product becomes worth INR1,50,000, manufacturing it earns me INR9,000.

items.statement: Bridal jewellery reached ~10% of business volume in 6 months; target to match core business in 2-2.5 years
items.quote: in just the last six months, bridal jewelry has grown to account for approximately 10% of our business. This share s expected to continue growing; in fact, within two to two-and-a-half years, it could potentially reach a level comparable to our core business

items.statement: Corporate chain stores (Titan, Malabar, etc.) now 51% of business vs 35% at IPO; relationships evolved to strategic vendor status
items.quote: As you have seen, we have reached around 51% business share with major corporate chain stores in India, such as Titan and others. Our primary focus now is to increase our business with these corporate clients.

items.statement: Cash flow turned positive in 6 months; focus on reducing inventory, accelerating payments, increasing advance gold and cash mode
items.quote: That is precisely the point, to make the cash flow positive. For that, there are just two things: how much can we reduce this stock, the ready inventory? And since we are into B2B, supplying to stores, how fast can we get the payment cycle accelerated?

items.statement: Mangalsutra category growing at 30% CAGR; bridal segment addresses 60% of total market
items.quote: Furthermore, our mangalsutra category is performing exceptionally well, growing at a CAGR of 30%. The mangalsutra is also a part of bridal jewelry.

items.statement: Employee cost up 67% YoY due to capacity expansion, bridal entry, new segments; headcount growing with designers and karigars
items.quote: Sir, as I mentioned, we have already increased our capacity from 2.5 to 4 tonnes; consequently, we will need to increase our headcount. We will need to hire more designers, as we are focused on developing new designs.

items.statement: Board approved wholly-owned subsidiary for diversified jewellery manufacturing, design, trading, distribution across B2B/B2C
items.quote: Regarding the timeline, we just received board approval for this yesterday. Now, the company will be incorporated, its portals will be developed, designs will be created, and all new brand names will be registered.

items.statement: Gold price volatility makes consumers cautious; recycling model (old gold exchange) limits 100% outright sales
items.quote: If the price of gold were to reach, say, $5,000 US dollars per ounce, which translates to roughly INR1,70,000 to INR1,80,000, customers looking to purchase 100 grams of gold might choose to bring in 60 grams of their existing gold and pay for only the remaining 40 grams.

items.statement: Maintains FY27 revenue guidance of INR1900 crores with 10-10.5% EBITDA margin
items.quote: On guidance, we are maintaining our FY27 outlook of INR1900 crores of revenue with a 10 % to 10.5% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Targets 25-30% revenue CAGR for next couple of years
items.quote: And going forward also, like, we are doing this here, we are growing at 25% to 30% CAGR, and going forward also, that will be our endeavor to grow at 25% to 30%.

items.statement: No new capex needed in FY27-28; focus on utilizing new plants at Ghiloth and Gujarat
items.quote: For '27, '28, actually we won't need any capex, new capex. The idea on 20 of '27, '28 would be to do the utilization of the new plants that we have set up.

items.statement: Commissioned 13,000 tons steel processing capacity and sandwich panel line at Ghiloth Unit 5
items.quote: On 30th of October, about 3, 4 last week only, we have added 13,000 tons of steel capacity, processing capacity at our Ghiloth Greenfield project that is Unit 5, and we also commissioned our sandwich panel line in Ghiloth, Rajasthan.

items.statement: Gujarat greenfield plant to be commissioned in Q4 FY27 with 50,000 tons initial capacity (80,000 tons design)
items.quote: As conveyed earlier, we plan to get this new plant in Gujarat commissioned in the fourth quarter of the current financial year.

items.statement: Peak revenue potential at current capacity is INR2,800-3,000 crores
items.quote: With this plant that we have just commissioned at Ghiloth for the sandwich panels, plus the one which is coming up in Gujarat, with that, the total capacity of the company would be to do a revenue of close to INR2,800 crores to INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: Gross margin fell 2.3% in H1 due to steel cost rising faster than pass-through on existing orders
items.quote: First is, the steel and other input cost rose faster than we could pass them through on orders already being executed. So, our gross margin fell by almost 2.3%.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin recovered to 10.1% from 9.4% in Q1; expects H2 margins to improve further
items.quote: Our Q2 margin already recovered to 10.1% from 9.4% in quarter one, and H2 will see more of our orders priced at curre nt input price, as well as the inventory built up has given us a lot of confidence that we will be able to improve upon our gross margin in this quarter and the quarter next to this

items.statement: Raw material prices rose 17-18% in Q2 but margins still improved due to price escalations on existing orders
items.quote: Although at the same time in this quarter itself, the raw material prices have gone up by as much as 17% to 18%, but still the margins of the company improved.

items.statement: New orders priced at current input cost; pushing for escalation clauses but not yet standard practice
items.quote: Every new order is now priced on current input cost, and we have long-term sourcing arrangements in place. We're also pushing for price escalation clauses with our large customers. Yes, some of the customers have agreed, but it hasn't become a standard practice yet.

items.statement: Working capital increased to ~60 days vs 40-55 day guidance; receivables up INR144 crores (LC-backed) and inventory up INR92 crores (deliberate steel build)
items.quote: The second was the working capital went up by 60 -- went up to almost 60 days. Our guidance has always been around 40 days to 55 days would be the working capital. So, there is a slippage of almost 15 days to 18 days there.

items.statement: Expects working capital to normalize in Q3 as LC-backed receivables collect; collections are top priority for H2
items.quote: So, in this, the LC process is linked to the milestone billing, and there has been certain delays in that. So, due to that, the receivables went up by almost INR144 crores. But the good thing is, since they are backed by LC, so we expect this to normalize in this quarter three.

items.statement: Actively negotiating better payment terms on new contracts; aims to front-load payments in first two stages
items.quote: So, yes, in the last few mont hs, you know, we have started to focus on getting better payment terms from our customers, so I think, over a period of next 2 quarters to 3 quarters, we will start to see the changes as well

items.statement: Top 5 customers contribute 28-30% of order book; added 100+ new customers in H1; new customers account for 60% of order book
items.quote: Our top five customers contribute around 28% to 30% of our existing order book. The concentration risk is not there. And in terms of new customers, typically over the last 3 to 4 years, our new customers account for 60% of the order book and 40% comes from the existing customers.

items.statement: Sandwich panel capacity utilization rose from 35% in Q1 to 47-48% in Q2; pending order book above 5 lakh sqm
items.quote: In Q1, our capacity utilization for Mambattu was around 35%, which rose to aro und 47%, 48% in Q2. And current order book is also above 5 lakh square meters pending order book in hand for sandwich

items.statement: Hedges 48-50% of steel exposure covering 3-4 months; new orders provide natural hedge; seeks price increases for safeguard duty impact
items.quote: First is typically our steel exposure, we cover almost 48% to 50% of our steel exposure. So, since the pending order book is spread over the next 8 to 9 months, we are covered for the next 3 to 4 months.

items.statement: Remains net cash positive; ICRA reaffirmed A+ rating; deploying IPO proceeds with discipline
items.quote: We remain cash net cash positive. ICRA has reaffirmed our A+ rating, and we will continue to deploy our IPO proceeds with discipline.

items.statement: Received first data center structural steel order in Q3; existing capacity handles heavy structures up to 2m web width; no additional capex needed
items.quote: we are getting our fi rst order of structural steel supplying to the data center in this quarter and it is a heavy structure but in effect, the best part is whatever investment we have done in the past, a lot of investment, accommodates both heavy struct ure as well as the PEB building

items.statement: Data center subsidiary under discussion for DFMA products with one large customer; timeline uncertain
items.quote: This data center company which we floated in the last quarter, is related to one of the opportunities that has come our way. So, it is still under discussions. It is one big large customer to whom we are talking to, like make some DFM products for them, DFMA products for them.

items.statement: NCR GRAP restrictions post-Diwali may disrupt execution but not supply; civil front readiness determines impact
items.quote: NCR typically post-Diwali the GRAP starts and the delays in construction do happen. But the best part of pre-engineered buildings is the construction of pre-engineered buildings can carry on during this time if the civil works or the civil front of the customer is ready.

items.statement: Not aware of any clients setting up own PEB facilities; no competitive threat from backward integration
items.quote: As far as clients putting their own facilities, I am not aware of any of our clients putting up a PEB facility. So, I won't be able to answer that.

items.statement: Steel prices at peak (HR ~INR70,000/ton); no further near-term increase expected; margins recovered in Q2 despite 17-18% input cost rise
items.quote: The steel prices now, HR price is almost INR70,000 a ton, and they are at their peak level. So, I do not foresee any more increase in steel prices to happen in the near future.

items.statement: Targets 25% average revenue growth and 20% profit growth for FY27 over FY26; EBITDA growth not quantified
items.quote: We hope that this year we will see an average growth of 25% from the last year. We will also see a 20% increase in profit from the last year.

items.statement: Aims for fabrication business to contribute 5-7% of revenue and 10% of EBITDA by FY28
items.quote: By FY28, we aim to derive 5% to 7% of revenue and 10% of EBITDA from the fabrication business.

items.statement: Targets fabrication revenue contribution up to 10% of total revenue from PEB and railway segments
items.quote: Our goal is to scale the fabrication revenue contribution up to 10% of total revenue from PEB and railway segments.

items.statement: Fabrication order book stands at ₹76.5 crore as of September 30, split ₹50.8 crore PEB/railway and ₹25.7 crore Bihar Railway RDSO-approved orders
items.quote: As of September 30, our fabrication order book stands at a healthy ₹76.5 crore, which includes ₹50.8 crore from PEB and railway orders, and ₹25.7 crore from the Bihar Railway RDSO-approved unit orders.

items.statement: Fabrication EBITDA margin expected at 9-11% (Neeraj) and 10-12% (Chairman); distribution blended margin healthy with flat products better than long
items.quote: We believe EBITDA margins in the fabrication business range between 9% to 11%, which will play a critical role in enhancing overall company profitability going forward.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 gross margin 8.8%, EBITDA margin declined due to ₹2 crore loss on sold machines; pre-tax and post-tax margins grew 25-30 bps
items.quote: Sir, we bought some machines and gave them to Uttarakhand for fabrication. And those machines used to remain empty for 6 months, and closed for 3 months. In the first year, the work was going well. And then we sold those machines. In that, there was a l oss of Rs.2 crore. Because of that, our margin has

items.statement: Steel demand in Bihar very strong due to massive infrastructure growth; prices rising ₹2,500/ton monthly with no near-term correction expected
items.quote: Demand, especially in Bihar, remains very strong due to massive infrastructure growth. We don't see any price drops expected i n the near future; in fact, prices are being increased by ₹ 2,500 per ton monthly by manufacturers, and demand remains strong supported by recent government funding

items.statement: 66% revenue via dealer retail where Tata Steel fixes prices; project sales priced competitively; HR/CR/GP sheets follow Tata Steel structured pricing with premiums over other brands
items.quote: Around 66% of our revenue comes through direct dealer retail sales where Tata Steel fixes the prices, and we supply accordingly while maintaining our warehouse margins. For project sales, we price competitively based on demand and project scale.

items.statement: Installed fabrication capacity 24,000 MT (12,000 MT railway, 12,000 MT PEB) with 87,000 sq ft operational area; currently utilizing ~25% (500 MT/month of 2,000 MT capacity)
items.quote: we have an installed fabrication capacity of 24,000 metric tons in Purn ea—split equally into 12,000 tons for railway applications and 12,000 tons for PEB structures. We have an operational fabrication area of around 87,000 square feet

items.statement: Welding electrode plant in Purnea built, commercial production starts November; fabrication capex ~₹5 crore for machines when utilization reaches 60-70%; land parcels (43 acres Purnea, 15 acres Kolkata) available for future expansion
items.quote: Around 5 crore, because we already have land parcel available. So if there is a requirement, it will be for the machines.

items.statement: Expanding into value-added: tailor-made re-bars, PEB fabrication, railway structures, welding electrodes (own brand), nails (own brand), profiling GC sheets, brackets for Tata Steel
items.quote: We are setting up a welding electrode plant in Purne a. Th e plant is built, and commercial production will start this November. We will manufacture and sell under our own brand using our existing network

items.statement: Dealer network of ~1,200 across Bihar built over 25-30 years; top-2 Tata Steel distributor in India by volume; relationships strengthened by incentives, support, and full product range
items.quote: Tata Steel started the distribution system in 2000. Earlier, they used to do trading and in the last 20 -25 years, all the cream dealer s in Bihar are connected to me

items.statement: Competitive moat: 25-30 year dealer relationships, full Tata Steel product portfolio, integrated services (cut-to-length, profiling, engineering support), on-time delivery vs peers
items.quote: To make a network, we tell you to make 50 stores. It will take 5 years to make a network. The backbone of BMW is this network. The network of the dealer is the backbone.

items.statement: Working capital limit ₹350 crore (rated A- by CRISIL, upgraded from BBB-); inventory ~45 days, receivables ~45 days; 6x turnover on working capital
items.quote: As of now, our rating is working capital is 400 crore minus AIV. We have made a working capital limit of 350 crore. Government loans are also included. You are using 350 crore. In that 350 crore, you have 1300 crore. We are giving more than 6 times.

items.statement: CRISIL rating upgraded to A- from BBB-; focus on reducing inventory days, cash conversion cycle, and interest costs
items.quote: I would like to tell you that the BBB minus that we got from CRISIL has been upgraded to A minus this year.

items.statement: Interim dividend ₹1.5/share declared for current year; paid ₹1.5/share last year; aims to reward shareholders consistently as profits grow
items.quote: We also distributed an interim dividend of ₹1.5 per share last year, and our board has announced another interim dividend of ₹1.5 per share. We aim to reward our shareholders consistently as profits grow.

items.statement: Appointed engineer (Mr. Ganesh) at ₹21 lakh/annum for Karnataka fabrication orders; divisional business managers for Tiscon, flat products, districts; 8-10 people per division; Chairman's son full-time in distribution, grandson (MBA London)
items.quote: We have appointed a person yesterday. He is an engineer. We have posted his order in Karnataka. And we have appointed him at Rs. 21 lakh annually. And we will bring the orders there.

items.statement: Q2 FY27: Revenue ₹731 crore (+46% YoY), Gross Profit ₹64.6 crore (+24%), EBITDA ₹22.1 crore (+11%), PBT ₹15 crore (+50%), PAT ₹10.5 crore (+48%), PAT margin 1.4%
items.quote: During Q2 FY27, the company's revenue stood at ₹731 crore, compared to ₹502 crore in Q2 FY26, marking an impressive revenue growth of approximately 46%.

items.statement: Benefiting from government infrastructure push (PM Gati Shakti, central govt projects in East India, Bihar/Northeast focus on railways, airports, industrial parks)
items.quote: Supported by gove rnment initiatives like PM Gati Shakti and massive infrastructure development by Central Government across Eastern India, demand for steel fabrication is robust

items.statement: Railway fabrication subcontracted (not prime contractor), reducing payment risk; machines sold after underutilization caused ₹2 crore loss; capex timed to 60-70% utilization to avoid idle capacity
items.quote: In the railway, when contractors take orders to build the entire bridge, the steel fabrication can be made by m e. The design approved by the RDSO , I don't have any direct interaction with the

items.statement: Land bank: 16 acres + 43 acres in Purnea (housing + industrial park), 15 acres in Kolkata (registered), 1 acre recently purchased; housing plots and industrial plots planned for monetization
items.quote: We own two plots of land in Purnea - one measuring 16 acres and the other 43 acres. On the 16 acre plot, we plan to develop a housing project after acquiring a small adjoining piece of land.

items.statement: Medium-term revenue aspiration of INR 1,000 crores with exports contributing 25-30%
items.quote: Our medium-term aspiration is to scale our overall revenue to INR1,000 crores with exports contributing approximately 25% to 30%.

items.statement: FY27 volume growth guidance maintained at 8-10% with pickup expected in H2
items.quote: Yes, I think my guidance would be we still remain in line with the volume growth that we had given the guidance on earlier, which is about 8% to 10% and I think you will see that pick up in H2 this year because of the capacity increase.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at high teens 15-19%
items.quote: I think on the growth side, I had earlier given my guidance on high teens, so anywhere between 15% to 19%. So we are in line.

items.statement: Export growth guidance: short-term 30-35%, long-term sustainable 20-25%
items.quote: My guidance has always been sustainable over the long-term period is more on exports more like 20%, 25%. When I say long term is more like 5 years. But I think short-term growth, we had given a guidance of about 30% to 35%.

items.statement: FY27 total capex INR 84.7 crores including INR 58.22 crores for new plant
items.quote: So, our capex spend for FY27 is going to be INR 58.22 crores for the new plant and including the regular capex, the total capex is going to be INR 84.7 crores.

items.statement: New plant commenced commercial production 30 Oct 2026 adding 1.5M units; total installed capacity now 11M units; planning additional 1.5M units over 18-24 months to reach 12.5M units
items.quote: We commenced commercial production at our new plant on 30th October 2026, adding 1.5 million units of annual helmet and boxes manufacturing capacity. With this addition, our total installed capacity now stands at approximately 11.5 million units (Please note 11.5 million was mentioned erroneously, it should be read as 11 million) per annum.

items.statement: Capacity utilization for helmets and boxes at 83% as of Sep 30 2026; Q2 FY27 utilization 85% for helmets and boxes, 88% for EPS, 64% for water decals
items.quote: Our existing manufacturing capacity was operating at a relatively high utilization level of approximately 83% as of September 30, 2026.

items.statement: Export revenue grew from INR 53.2 crores in FY24 to INR 127.6 crores; H1 FY27 export revenue INR 79.4 crores, up nearly 50% YoY
items.quote: In H1 FY27, we recorded export revenue of INR79.4 crores. That's growth of nearly 50% over H1 FY26, reflecting the growing scale of international operations.

items.statement: SMK premium brand contribution increased from 13% in Q2 FY26 to 20% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: We are encouraged by the progress so far with SMK's contribution to overall sales increasing from approximately 13% in Q2 FY26 to 20% in Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Entered riding jackets under SMK brand via in-house manufacturing; target 10,000 units by Mar 27 and 40,000 units next fiscal; launching Bluetooth rider communication system Nov 2026
items.quote: We commenced production in September 2026. We are progressively scaling up this capability with plan of producing 10,000 units by March '27 and 40,000 units by next fiscal year.

items.statement: SMK margins 70-80% higher than Studds margins; new accessories margins in line with respective brand margins
items.quote: So I would say SMK margins are about close to 70% higher than Studds margins, depending on what kind of times. But if I was to talk about percentage, that will be typically the ballpark we are anywhere between 70% to 80% depending on product to product.

items.statement: Implemented 9% calibrated price increase (6.5-7% in Q1, balance in Q2); further price hike decision in Q4 depending on raw material prices
items.quote: So, the price increase that we've taken is 9%, which was slightly calibrated because about 7% -- 6.5% to 7% price increase we got during the Q1 and the balance we got in the Q2 because there were some older orders, which were committed at the older prices, export especially.

items.statement: Styrene-based raw material prices remain elevated in Q3; Q2 slightly better than Q1 but no softening yet; previous cycle lasted 2 years, this one expected slightly smaller
items.quote: In Q3, we were expecting styrenics to soften, but they haven't softened yet. They're still elevated. So as I said, we will wait for this quarter before we take a call for price increase.

items.statement: Presence in 70+ countries; incorporated wholly-owned subsidiary in Italy as warehousing and distribution hub for Europe
items.quote: An important step in this direction has been the incorporation of our wholly-owned subsidiary in Italy, which will function as a warehousing and distribution hub for Europe.

items.statement: Key growth geographies: Latin America (volume-driven, less price-sensitive), Europe and US (premium, higher margins)
items.quote: I would place the opportunity in 2 baskets. One is the Latin American market, where it's more of a quantity-driven, it's not as price-sensitive as India, and it's a quantitative driven market because it's a larger motorcycle market. Second, I would see Europe and U.S. as a more of a premium market where you have good margins and higher revenues.

items.statement: No inorganic plans in helmet space; manufacturing concentrated in Indonesia, India, China, Vietnam; would consider historic legendary brand if available
items.quote: I don't think so we're looking at an inorganic opportunity in the same space as helmets because we feel all the manufacturing of helmets is happening mainly in Indonesia, India and China and Vietnam, I would say.

items.statement: Biggest execution risk in foreign markets is ramp-up speed due to high fixed costs; subsidiaries may show losses initially until scale achieved
items.quote: I think the biggest risk on execution on the foreign markets is the speed at which we actually ramp up operations, and we're able to scale up sales because in these foreign markets, the fixed costs are very high.

items.statement: Q2 FY27: 2-wheeler helmet and boxes volumes 2.04M units, revenue INR 183.1 crores (+18.6% YoY), EBITDA INR 22.8 crores (-23.7% YoY), PAT INR 14.7 crores (-28% YoY)
items.quote: Our 2-wheeler helmet and boxes volumes stood at 2.04 million. Consolidated revenue stood at INR 183.1 crores, which grew by 18.6% year-on-year. EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 22.8 crores, decreased by about 23.7% year-on-year.

items.statement: H1 FY27: 2-wheeler helmet and boxes volumes 3.99M units, revenue INR 352.8 crores (+16.2% YoY), EBITDA INR 42.3 crores (-29.6% YoY), PAT INR 27 crores (-33.8% YoY)
items.quote: H1 FY27 performance, our 2-wheeler helmet and boxes volumes stood at 3.99 million. Consolidated revenue stood at INR 352.8 crores grew by 16.2% year-on-year. EBITDA stood at INR 42.3 crores, which decreased by 29.6% year-on-year.

items.statement: Domestic volume ~35 lakh, export volume ~4 lakh in H1 FY27; no demand issues currently; winter seasonality not flagged as concern
items.quote: So domestic volume is approx 35 lakh and export volume is about 4 lakh.

items.statement: Bluetooth products for both domestic and export; apparel focused on India first, exports later; accessories sold through same point-of-sale as helmets
items.quote: So Bluetooth will be both domestic and exports, but I think for the apparels, we are more focused on India right now. For exports, we need to build products which we are building through this year now.

items.statement: Accessories manufactured 70-75% in-house: hard luggage, helmet locks, cable locks, Bluetooth, jackets, gloves, goggles, rainwear, balaclavas, sleeves
items.quote: So we are doing motorcycle hard luggage. We are doing helmet locks, cable locks. We're doing, as we said, Bluetooth accessories. Bluetooth is what we're launching. We're doing jackets, we're doing gloves, we're doing motorcycle goggles, we're doing some rainwear. So everything related to motorcycle accessories. We're doing balaclavas, we're doing sleeves I would say about 70% to 75%, we are manufa

items.statement: First-year revenue target for jackets INR 15-20 crores; Bluetooth capacity >2 lakh units/year; accessories margins in line with respective brand helmet margins
items.quote: Starting off, I think the revenue potential from accessories because I said 40,000 jackets. So that's close to about anywhere between INR 15 crores to INR 20 crores.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA per kg to reach Rs.60-65 in FY2028
items.quote: Hopefully, we expect that maybe around 60 to 65.

items.statement: ALCU installed capacity currently 10,000-11,000 metric tons; full 18,000 tons expected by mid-December
items.quote: We have not been able to install the entire capacity, so, we are progressing and currently, we believe around 10,000 to 11,000 metric tons have been already installed and by January or somewhere close to that we will be able to do the remaining one.

items.statement: IPO funds for ALCU capex being used as planned; unspent amount in fixed deposits; capex largely complete by end of Q3
items.quote: The IPO funds set aside for the ALCU capex are being used as planned. The amount not yet spent is kept in fixed deposits. We expect the capex to be largely complete by the end of the third quarter in line with the planned completion Shailesh ji spoke about it.

items.statement: Inventory management improved via FIFO controls and new ERP; inventory levels brought down materially; controls remain in place
items.quote: During Q2, we worked through a major higher-cost inventory, introduced strict first-in-first-out controls and implemented a new ERP system which has brought inventory levels down materially. items.statement: Forward bookings for India leisure travel trending at 30% value growth YoY for OND quarter (Q3 FY27)
