items.statement: Expect double-digit growth in Financial Services segment for some time to come
items.quote: I believe the business will continue to deliver double -digit growth.

items.statement: Financial Services EBIT margin expected in 40% to 45% range
items.quote: From a margin perspective, we already guided the market before. We are expecting the range between that 40% to 45%.

items.statement: Sterling expects healthy EBITDA margin range of 32% to 37% depending on seasonality
items.quote: a healthy EBITDA margin that we will maintain depending on the seasonality is between 32% to 37%.

items.statement: Sterling demerger NCLT approval expected by end of March or early April FY27
items.quote: We are expecting this entire process to get over that is, in other words, get the NCLT approval by end of March or early April.

items.statement: India travel business saw recovery with momentum picking up sharply in September 2026
items.quote: Our India travel business saw a pace recovery through July and August with momentum picking up more sharply in September 2026.

items.statement: Domestic leisure business grew 8% led by Ladakh, Kerala, Sri Lanka, Bhutan and Bhakti portfolio
items.quote: Our domestic business grew by 8% during the quarter, led by destinations such as Ladakh, Kerala, Sri Lanka, Bhutan and the Bhakti & Darshan portfolio, especially Char Dham.

items.statement: Education forex business grew 33% despite industry outbound remittances declining 34%
items.quote: Against this backdrop, our education forex business grew by 33% .

items.statement: Corporate travel air transaction volume grew 18% with India and international volumes up 23% and 15%
items.quote: Air transaction volume grew 18% with India and international air volumes increasing by 23% and 15%, respectively.

items.statement: Sterling room nights sold increased 23% and occupancy improved 300 bps in Q2 FY27
items.quote: The room nights sold increased by approximately 23% while occupancy improved by about 300 basis points.

items.statement: Sterling H1 FY27 room nights sold up 24%, occupancy up 500 bps, ARR up 11%, RevPAR up 15%
items.quote: The room nights sold increased by approximately 24% . Our occupancy improved by 500 basis points, while the average room rates increased approximately 11%. This resulted in a total RevPAR of H1 growing a little over 15% year-on-year.

items.statement: Consolidated PBT before exceptional items at INR 848 million, flat YoY despite 5% income decline
items.quote: Our consolidated PBT before exceptional item stood at INR 848 million, which was broadly at the same level as last year despite the reduction in overall income.

items.statement: Consolidated PBT margin improved to 4.2% from 4% YoY
items.quote: What is also encouraging is that we have actually managed to improve our PBT margin to 4.2% compared to 4% last year despite the pressure on top line.

items.statement: Travel segment EBIT margin improved sequentially from 2.4% to 2.9%
items.quote: Overall, EBIT margins for the Travel segment have shown an improvement on a sequential basis from 2.4% to 2.9% in Q2 of FY 2027.

items.statement: India Travel EBIT margin held at healthy 3.8%, EBIT deficit narrowed from 31% to 22%
items.quote: We ended the quarter just 6% below last year with EBIT margins holding healthy at 3.8%. Due to the agility in our cost functions, we were able to narrow the EBIT deficit in the India business from 31% to 22%.

items.statement: Financial Services EBIT margin at 44.1% in Q2 and 44.7% in H1 FY27
items.quote: Our EBIT for the segment in Q2 improved by 10% Y-o-Y to INR 452 million and margins are at a very healthy percentage of 44.1%.

items.statement: Sterling Q2 EBITDA grew 4-5% reported, but 19-20% excluding INR 40 million GST input tax credit cost
items.quote: Excluding this incremental GST cost for analytical comparison, EBITDA would have actually been approximately INR 329 million, representing a growth of around 19% to 20% over the corresponding quarter last year compared to a reported growth of approximately 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Sterling H1 EBITDA grew 15% to INR 910 million, PBT grew 22% to INR 623 million
items.quote: For H1 FY27, the revenues grew approximately 19% to INR 2,971 million. EBITDA increased 15% to approximately INR 910 million, while PBT grew 22% to approximately INR 623 million.

items.statement: Sterling opened 7 resorts in Q2 FY27, highest ever quarterly expansion, portfolio now 83 properties and 4,000+ keys
items.quote: Q2 saw the highest ever quarterly expansion in Sterling's history as well with 7 resorts opened during the quarter to increase the portfolio to 83 properties and having crossed a key milestone of 4,000 keys as on 30th of September 2026.

items.statement: Sterling added 6 management contracts and 1 revenue share property in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our portfolio continued to grow duri ng the quarter with 7 new resorts opening, the highest number of openings we've done in a single quarter, comprising 6 management contracts and 1 revenue share property

items.statement: DEI signed 5 new partnerships in Malaysia, Maldives, Singapore, India; renewed 20+ partnerships; launched 3 in Indonesia, China, Maldives
items.quote: We had 5 new partnerships in the quarter signed up in Malaysia, Maldives , Singapore and India. We renewed most of our key partnerships, over 20 partnerships were renewed during this quarter. And we have launched 3 new partnerships in Indonesia, China and Maldives.

items.statement: DEI signed Warner Bros Harry Potter exhibit in Shanghai; anticipating Hong Kong Disney and Petronas Malaysia partnerships
items.quote: We just signed up the Warner Bros. Harry Potter exhibit in Shanghai, and we're very optimistic that it will bring us a sizable recovery on our revenue in the coming quarters. We are also anticipating partnerships with Hong Kong, Disney and Petronas Malaysia to begin soon.

items.statement: Sterling follows asset-light capital-light approach with management contracts and revenue share properties
items.quote: This is consistent with our asset-light capital-light approach to growth, allowing us to expand our network while maintaining capital discipline.

items.statement: Thomas Cook branch network grew 7% YoY to 310 branches via franchisee route
items.quote: On the distribution front, we continue to expand our reach with the branch network growing by 7% year -on-year via the franchisee route to 310 branches at the end of September 2026 compared to 289 branches.

items.statement: Sterling average room rates in owned/lease portfolio increased ~12% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Average room rates in our owned lease portfolio also increased by 12% approximately.

items.statement: Sterling H1 average room rates increased ~11%, RevPAR grew ~15%
items.quote: Our occupancy improved by 500 basis points, while the average room rates increased approximately 11%. This resulted in a total RevPAR of H1 growing a little over 15% year-on-year.

items.statement: Thomas Cook expanded experiential offerings with luxury rail journeys and cruise portfolio across multiple destinations
items.quote: We expanded our experiential offerings to include iconic luxury rail journeys across South Africa, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Egypt. We also added our luxury cruise portfolio with curated experiences across Antarctica, the Arctic, the Mediterranean and Europe.

items.statement: Sterling broadening beyond leisure into business and mixed-use destinations while strengthening spiritual, wildlife, destination-led hospitality
items.quote: At the same time, Sterling is progressively broadening its presence through beyond traditional leisure destinations into other travel occasions, including business destinations and destinations having a flavor of both business and leisure apart from contin uing to strengthen our leisure DNA, including spiritual, wildlife and destination-led hospitality

items.statement: Corporate travel added new accounts across pharmaceuticals, healthcare, auto components, fintech, digital payments
items.quote: We continue to expand our client base during the quarter, adding new accounts across pharmaceuticals, health care, auto components, fintech and digital payments.

items.statement: Financial Services digital adoption increased to 22.4% from 21.5% YoY; WhatsApp channel grew fourfold
items.quote: Our digital channels kept gaining ground during the quarter with overall digital adoption increasing to 22.4% compared to 21.5% in the corresponding period last year. This was supported by strong customer engagement across our app, WhatsApp channel, which grew fourfold and 3% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Forex cards sold via Blinkit quick commerce platform grew 96% vs Q3 FY26
items.quote: The number of forex cards sold through this platform grew 96% as compared to Q3 FY26, not an entirely like -to-like comparison, but it gives you a sense of the growth.

items.statement: Education forex grew 33% while industry outbound remittances fell 34%, indicating market share gains
items.quote: RBI data for April to August 2026 shows that outbound remittances under the education category declined by 34%, while travel -related foreign exchange remittance declined by 1%. Against this backdrop, our education forex business grew by 33% .

items.statement: Sterling impacted by GST input tax credit rule change: no ITC for rates INR 7,500 and under effective Sept 23, 2025
items.quote: Now, you cannot take the input tax credit for all the rates that are sold INR 7,500 and under. And if you know, in the seasonally weak quarter, you don't tend to sell more rates above INR 7,500, least you go actually empty or you go vacant.

items.statement: International DMS: Desert Adventures sales down 67% (improved from 89% decline in Q1), AlliedTPro down 22% (from 40%), Asian Trails up 9%
items.quote: The Middle East remains the most impacted market with Desert Adventures recording a 67% decline in sales as geographical uncertainty continued to weigh on the travel demand and travel confidence. However, this marks an improvement from the 89% decline we recorded in Q1, indicating a gradual recovery.

items.statement: Private Safari business: South Africa up 31%, East Africa up 14%
items.quote: On a more positive note, our private Safari business in South and East Africa continued to perform well with South Africa growing by 31% and East Africa by 14%.

items.statement: Group net debt INR 316 crores; cash includes float from prepaid forex cards
items.quote: So, we have a net debt of about INR 316 crores on a gross basis. And only the balance is really available as a sort of completely free cash.

items.statement: Sterling remains debt-free with net cash reserves of ~INR 3,805 million
items.quote: Sterling remains debt -free with net cash reserves of approximately INR 3,805 million at the end of the quarter.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; Sterling demerger expected to reward shareholders
items.quote: The fact that we are demerging Sterling, which is also holding INR 380 crores of cash is one of the ways of rewarding the shareholder.

items.statement: Group looking at acquisitions in line of business if price vs returns make sense
items.quote: We are also looking at possible acquisitions, which are the right fit. We don't want to go out and buy something which is completely different from what we do, but something in our line of business, we are willing to look at only if it makes sense in terms of the price vis -a-vis the returns.

items.statement: Sterling RevPAR grew 12% in Q2 FY27 and ~15% in H1 FY27
items.quote: This has resulted in a total RevPAR growth of 12%, demonstrating an improved revenue productivity.

items.statement: Corporate travel online booking tool adoption at 32%
items.quote: Also, the adoption of our online booking tool was a healthy 32%.

items.statement: DEI post-visit sales activated across 45% of sites by count, 35% by revenue; 1,200+ transactions in quarter
items.quote: We've activated post visit sales across 45% of our portfolio in terms of the number of sites. In terms of revenue, we've implemented the post visit sales across 35% probably of the portfolio. The good news is within this last quarter itself, we've seen 1,200 + transactions.

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions in West Asia/Middle East impacting Desert Adventures, DEI, AlliedTPro; recovery gradual but uncertain
items.quote: The external environment continues to be uncertain, and some of our international operations are still working throu gh the effects of the geopolitical disruptions

items.statement: Target 500 MW operating renewable portfolio by March 2027
items.quote: We have set out a target of reaching a 500 MW operating portfolio by March ‘27.

items.statement: 231.10 MW renewable projects under construction with land acquired and PPA signed
items.quote: 231.10 MW projects are under construction. Most of the cases, the land is already acquired. PPA is already signed

items.statement: Expect 200-220 MW renewable capacity addition in FY27
items.quote: Overall, it should be between 200 and 220 MW.

items.statement: Expect operating renewable capacity of 300 MW in Q3 FY27 and 400 MW in Q4 FY27
items.quote: Once fully operational, basically for Q3 we would basically have an operating capacity of about 300 MW, and in Q4, we basically will have an operating capacity of about 400 MW.

items.statement: EPC revenue guidance of INR 600 crores for full year FY27 based on 200 MW capacity addition
items.quote: we potentially look ed at EPC revenue of close to about maybe INR 600 crores for the full year, of which INR 200 crores has been booked now for H1

items.statement: Electricity generation revenue expected at INR 141-150 crores for FY27 vs INR 89 crores last year
items.quote: On the electricity generation, basically we expect that against basically the overall electricity sales of INR 89 crores last year, we should be close to about INR 141 -150 crores for the full year.

items.statement: EIM losses expected to narrow significantly in Q3 and Q4 FY27
items.quote: On the IEM we would not like to guide on the specific numbers, but in broader trend that the Q3, Q4 losses we are expecting to narrow significantly.

items.statement: EIM target to turn profitable in next financial year (FY28)
items.quote: The company's target is to turn positive in the next financial year.

items.statement: EIM manufacturing facility designed for 5,000 vehicles/year; battery plant similar capacity
items.quote: So, we have designed it for a capacity of 5,000 vehicles a year. We do not expect to fully fill that capacity immediately, obviously. The battery plan is a similar capacity.

items.statement: EIM full-scale production from January 2027 at run rate of 200 vehicles/month
items.quote: We will start actual full-scale production from January. The plant is ready. We are doing trial production of a few things, CKD kits, and we will start actual production at the run rate of about 200 basis per month from January.

items.statement: EIM charging network expansion from 8 to 15 stations by December 2026 and 40 by March 2027
items.quote: We expect to go from the current eight charging stations to 15 by December ‘26 and to 40 by March ‘27.

items.statement: Signed MOUs totaling almost 1,500 vehicles with large transporters for phased delivery
items.quote: We signed MOUs totaling almost 1500 vehicles, which will be delivered in part as a network is commissioned, and people can actually operate the trust from those corridors, and this will be done in phases.

items.statement: EIM contribution margin currently ~6%, down from 8% due to rupee weakness
items.quote: Our contribution margin right now is about 6%. It was earlier in the 8% range . The weakness of the rupee has had a small effect on it.

items.statement: EIM breakeven expected at annual run rate of 2,000 vehicles
items.quote: I think an annual run rate of 2,000 vehicles should be very positive for the business.

items.statement: EIM average truck selling price INR 60 lakhs (without battery); battery-as-a-service packages INR 14-33 lakhs/year for 7-year contract
items.quote: So, our average price is around INR 60 lakhs. 95% of our sales are without the batteries. So these are trucks without the battery.

items.statement: Over 10 banks and major NBFCs now financing EIM vehicles without battery, indicating lender confidence
items.quote: I can tell you we have more than 10 banks now lending to our customers for our vehicle without battery, which itself is a major breakthrough.

items.statement: Merger with Ravindra Energy filed with exchanges; expect legal completion by September 2027 (Q2 FY28)
items.quote: Overall, we are looking at something like September ‘27 as a likely completion timeline. Of course, it is subject to the various approvals that I mentioned just now.

items.statement: EIM paid-up equity INR 400 crores plus additional INR 100 crores shareholder funds
items.quote: The paid-up equity is now INR 400 crores. We've also got another additional INR 100 crores of shareholder funds.

items.statement: Incorporated EIM Megaplex subsidiary to hold charging assets, renewable energy assets, and battery-as-a-service
items.quote: We incorporated a step-down subsidiary for EIM Megaplex, which will be the network company, hold all the charging assets, any renewable energy assets that are required to support the charging infrastructure, and the batteries that we provide as a service.

items.statement: Post-merger combined network equity expected ~INR 900 crores
items.quote: From a network point of view post-merger, we're looking at about INR 900 crores of network post-merger.

items.statement: EIM vehicle uptime >99% vs ~90% for diesel trucks; 50% of Q2 sales were repeat orders
items.quote: The vehicle that we have launched has very strong customer satisfaction levels, uptime above 99% for most customers, and a significant number of the vehicles sold, for example, this quarter are repeat orders.

items.statement: Two EIM charging stations operating at >75% daily capacity; largest single-location charging sites in India by electricity volume
items.quote: Out of our eight charge stations, we now have two charge stations which are working at more than 75% of capacity on a daily basis. These are in fact, by volume of electricity, the largest or heaviest charging sites in the current single location sites in the country already.

items.statement: EIM charging network utilization currently <30% swaps/station; expected to improve with volume growth
items.quote: We are currently tracking in overall capacity utilization in terms of swaps per station at around less than 30%.

items.statement: EIM developing two new products for launch in next 12 months, including heavy-duty vehicle
items.quote: We ourselves are working on two other products, which we expect to launch in the next 12 months. Of which, the first one will be a heavy-duty vehicle.

items.statement: EIM aggressive indigenization plan; battery cells and critical motor parts to remain import-dependent medium-term
items.quote: However, there are two, three critical things for which India will be dependent on import for some time. For example, the battery cell and some critical parts of t he electric motor

items.statement: Merger scheme filed with stock exchange; 21-day public review underway; then SEBI review; NCLT approval expected
items.quote: We filed the merger scheme with the stock exchange last month. I think as a process, there is a 21-day window where the scheme is put up for publics review. We are currently undergoing review as well as some queries on the overall scheme.

items.statement: Plan to monetize existing solar assets (operating and under construction) to fund EIM network growth without external capital
items.quote: We believe there is a strong market for monetization of our existing projects, both operating and under construction. The equity that it would yield would help us grow the EIM network manifold from where we are, without having to raise any external capital.

items.statement: New renewable projects to be built for charging network; 100 swap stations over 18 months could require 200-300 MW solar
items.quote: If we were to basically add another 100 swap stations over the next 18 months, that is something that we are talking about 200-300 MW of solar capacity addition.

items.statement: EIM electricity trading book of ~120 MW/month to source lower-cost energy for charging network
items.quote: We have a large electricity trading book in Ravindra Energy this year. We are doing close to about 120 MW of electricity trading every month, something which would also enable us to source lower cost energy for our charging network.

items.statement: China technology export restrictions may affect battery supply; EIM has acquired tech from China/Korea and pursuing indigenization
items.quote: We've already acquired new technology from China and Korea and other countries. I have no doubt, personally, that as volumes grow in the sector, we will be able to source a lot of the components in India.

items.statement: EIM to organize analyst/investor day at Pune factory next quarter (Q4 FY27) when battery plant commissioned
items.quote: We expect to be in full scale production from January, so next quarter. I think, it's a very good suggestion. We'll organize an analyst and investor day at the factory.

items.statement: Warehousing revenue contribution targeted to reach 17-18% in coming quarters and ~20% in next 3-5 years
items.quote: Our aim is to gradually increase the contribution to 17% to 18% over the coming quarters and eventually to around 20% of our total turnover.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 10.21% from 7.24% YoY, up ~296 bps
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin improved to 10.21% from 7.24%, an approximation of approximately 296 basis points growth.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded to 10.88% from 7.84% YoY, up ~300 bps
items.quote: EBITDA margin also improved to 10.88% as compared to last year Q2 number of 7.84%, which is an expansion of almost 300 basis points.

items.statement: Freight rates surged significantly in H1 FY27, e.g., India-US 40-ft container rate rose from ~$2,800 to ~$9,600
items.quote: For example, the freight rate from India to US for a 40-footer at the beginning of the year or at the end of February/March was around $2,800, while the same was approximately up to $9,600 during August/September period.

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions causing longer lead times but cargo still moving via alternative routings
items.quote: There are a little bit of challenges which do come up. Currently, there are a lot of challenges in the Gulf, but still there are ways to move cargo, and maybe the lead times and transit times have increased a little bit, but eventually getting there and we are moving out.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue mix: sea export 33%, air & sea import 31%, air export 16%, warehousing 14%, clearance 6%
items.quote: Similarly, for half-year of FY2026-'27, the respective contributions for this segment were 33%, 31%, 16%, 14%, and 6% respectively.

items.statement: FY26 repeat customers 51% of business; top 15 customers >20% of turnover; focus on mid-sized customers for margins and payment discipline
items.quote: In FY26, repeat customers accounted for 51% of business, while our top 15 customers contributed more than 20% of turnover. We continue to focus on building long-term customer relationships and increasing repeat business across our service portfolio.

items.statement: New branch locations driven by manufacturing sector potential and import-export activity in the geography
items.quote: And the basis and the study of opening a new branch or office in that part of India would be on the manufacturing sector and the potential of import and export in that particular geography of India.

items.statement: Overall warehouse capacity utilization ~97.5%
items.quote: Currently, we are operating at almost 97.5% capacity utilization in terms of our overall utilization of the space.

items.statement: Bhiwandi expansion expected to add ~INR1 cr annual revenue at full utilization (INR50L from 15k sq ft + INR40-50L from pallets)
items.quote: With these two developments, if they operate at 100% capacity, then we may see additional INR1 crores revenue per year.

items.statement: GP margin percentage stable despite revenue surge; higher turnover drives absolute profit
items.quote: we operate almost at the same level of GP margin. Though, of course, with the increase in turnover, GP margin goes down, which we have seen in our results also, but the overall higher turnover helps us deliver the better result.

items.statement: Higher turnover increases working capital investment and interest cost, but EBITDA growth outweighs it
items.quote: when the turnover goes up, we have to basically invest more in working capital, but that goes in the interest. If the operating margin -- if the turnover goes up, our margin automatically goes up, and then that helps to increase the PAT, or maybe EBITDA -- rather EBITDA.

items.statement: Ind AS 116 shifts warehouse rent to interest and depreciation, inflating reported warehousing gross margin
items.quote: The gross margin reported for warehousing appears high because under Ind AS 116, rent on leased premises is not reflected in the cost, rather it is shown in our interest and depreciation.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation unpredictable; challenges in Gulf region increasing lead times but cargo still moving
items.quote: With the current geopolitical situation, it is a little unpredictable. We do not know how this current situation will be next week or in the next month, but as our business is such that we keep things moving and keep goods moving from one place to another, we definitely find solutions and new routings, and that is how we are catering and providing our customer solutions.

items.statement: Air freight expansion supported by contractual space agreements with carriers; focus on US, South America, Africa corridors
items.quote: We have contractual space agreements with many carriers. Our destinations mainly focus on the US, South America, as well as many parts of Africa as well.

items.statement: Global presence expansion planned in corridors where Flomic controls cargo (origin/destination)
items.quote: In terms of establishing our global presence, yes, it is there in our future plans, and predominantly in the sectors where we have our own controlled cargo, wherein cargo is either coming into India or going out from India to that particular origin or destination.

items.statement: New software implementation underway to optimize costs; tight control on employment and operating expenses
items.quote: we are working on new software, which is helping us to optimize our costs. We are working in that direction, and we have a tight control on our operating costs, be it employment cost or be it other operating expenses.

items.statement: Management expects strong second half and full FY27 for India business; Parador H2 EBITDA positive target
items.quote: These risks, notwithstanding our strong performance in the first half, gives us good solid confidence for the second half of the year. With a stronger portfolio, a richer product mix and new capacity BIRLANU LTD’S Q2 & H1 FY27 EARNINGS CALL TRANSCRIPT coming on stream and an unwavering focus on execution, we are well placed to sustain that momentum and deliver a strong second half of the year and

items.statement: Parador H2 FY27 EBITDA positive milestone; aim to cut into H1 losses
items.quote: So, at the moment, the first milestone for us to ensure is as we are out of the summer months, to ensure that in this remaining part of the year, which is H2, we should be positive. How much are we able to cut into the losses of the first half of the year, th at I think is something that we should see how that situation works out

items.statement: Nellore greenfield boards plant on track for commercial production in Q4 FY27; Hyderabad project groundbreaking by December
items.quote: On the capacity front, our greenfield boards plant at Nellore is on track to begin commercial production in the fourth quarter of this financial year. We also expect to break ground on our second new project in Hyderabad by December.

items.statement: Both Nellore and Hyderabad projects on track per plan; monitoring execution and capital deployment
items.quote: As mentioned by Akshat, both the Nellore and Hyderabad, both projects are on track as per our plan. We are closely monitoring project execution and capital deployment to ensure timely completion within the planned investment outlay.

items.statement: Walls segment capacity utilization around 85% across Boards, Blocks, Panels
items.quote: And capacity utilizations are depending on which product segment are in the vicinity of about 85%.

items.statement: India business EBITDA margin expanded over 400 bps YoY to 6.8% in Q2; fifth consecutive quarter of expansion
items.quote: EBITDA increased to Rs. 40 crores from Rs. 12 crores in the corresponding quarter last year, while EBITDA margin expanded by over 400 basis points to 6.8%.

items.statement: Roofs EBITDA margin improved 320 bps YoY to 11.5%; Walls margin up 120 bps YoY to 12.3%; Pipes margin up 630 bps YoY to nearly 5%
items.quote: The Roofs segment delivered a strong performance with revenue growing 28% year -on-year to Rs. 244 crores. EBITDA margin improved by 320 basis points to 11.5% compared to 8.3% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: BCG cost restructuring at Parador identified value envelope of EUR 9-14 million annual EBITDA savings; implementation started, results visible in 3-4 months
items.quote: The team, overall, the initiative has identified a value envelope of additional about 9 million to 14 million at an EBITDA line level, and that is what we are pressing on.

items.statement: Parador breakeven could reduce by EUR 1 million monthly (EUR 9-10 million annually) if BCG savings land
items.quote: Correct. I mean if these numbers land where they are supposed to, we would be shaving off the monthly breakeven by at least EUR1 million, annually at EUR9 million to EUR10 million is what we are looking at.

items.statement: Clean Coats built strong order pipeline for rest of year and beyond
items.quote: The foundational work at Clean Coats is now in place, and it has built a strong order pipeline for the rest of the year and beyond.

items.statement: India business revenue grew 17% YoY to Rs 588 cr in Q2; third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth
items.quote: The revenue for our India business grew by 17% to Rs. 588 crores, and this is now the third consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth.

items.statement: Roofs volume up 21% YoY; value-added share 35% higher; market share gains
items.quote: Our Roofs business continued to be the strong growth engine for the company with revenue up 28% over last year and a volume growth of 21%.

items.statement: Pipes revenue up ~20% YoY; value-added fittings now 47% of portfolio; priority markets growing faster
items.quote: Pipes has delivered a strong turnaround this quarter with revenue growing at nearly 20% over last year and also sequentially, while margins improved by 630 basis points.

items.statement: Construction Chemicals revenue up ~35% YoY; Clean Coats revenue up ~50% YoY
items.quote: Construction Chemicals grew by about 35% despite severe cost and pricing pressure arising from the ongoing geopolitical situation.

items.statement: Parador revenue declined 4.4% YoY in INR (11% in local currency); European demand weak
items.quote: I am now turning to Parador, for which it was a challenging quarter. Demand in key European markets remained weak, compounded by broader global sluggishness and revenue declined about 4.4% over last year.

items.statement: Parador North America revenue on track for 4-5x previous year; already 2x full prior year in first 6 months
items.quote: For instance, in the U.S., already in these 6 months, we have almost twice as more as what we did in full financial year last year. We are on track to finish in North America for this financial year at nearly 4 to 5x of previous year's performance.

items.statement: Germany new house permits and constructions increased over last 12-15 months; flooring demand uptick expected with 12-18 month lag
items.quote: In Germany and in other markets in Europe, this is probably now, for the last 12 to 15 months, there has been an increase in the number of new house permits and new house constructions that have happened, which is a significant change in trend from what we have seen in the previous 3 -year period.

items.statement: Roofs benefited from pent-up price correction and steel roofing price surge driving volume shift
items.quote: One, there was almost a pent-up requirement for price correction in the market over the last 2, 3 years because if you look closely at our numbers or any of our industry peers, the cost increase was much more than what we could pass on to the market.

items.statement: Pipes revenue growth: 4% volume, 15% pricing and mix; inventory gains marginal
items.quote: Overall, the revenue growth was about 20%, of which about 4% was the volume growth, and the rest was from a pricing and mix perspective, so 15% was pricing and mix related.

items.statement: Walls revenue growth 5.5%: volume 1-2%, realization 5-9% depending on product
items.quote: Overall, the growth in revenue is about 5.5%. The volume growth is in the vicinity of about 1% to 2% at an aggregate level. The realization growth is depending on which product is anywhere between 5% to 9%.

items.statement: Rooftop solar commissioned at Golan and Chennai; approved at 2 more units; green power to exceed 20-25% of energy mix in 2 years
items.quote: During the quarter, we commissioned rooftop solar at our Golan and Chennai units and have also approved solar capacity at 2 more manufacturing units. We expect green power to exceed 20% to 25% of our energy mix within the next 2 years, reducing both our energy cost and our carbon footprint.

items.statement: Solar projects to yield Rs 4-5 cr annual savings; new plants target 40-50% renewable energy, ~30-35% cost savings per location
items.quote: So, the solar projects, it is in a phased manner. It will take around 6 to 9 months' time at different locations. So overall, the annual cost savings will be in the range of Rs. 4 crores to Rs. 5 crores in annual business.

items.statement: Roofs value-added share 35% higher YoY; Pipes fittings now 47% of portfolio; Walls retail presence broad-based
items.quote: We are also selling a richer mix with the share of value-added products 35% higher than last year.

items.statement: Walls expanded retail presence alongside institutional channels for wider demand base
items.quote: We are also broad basing our growth. Alongside our traditional institutional channels, we have significantly increased our retail presence, giving the business a wider and more resilient demand base.

items.statement: Parador gaining shelf space in DIY chains (Bauhaus etc.) and share in high-street retail via product differentiation
items.quote: First and foremost, as a consumer preference, people are moving from high street retail to DIY, where today, we stand on more shelves. So, you visited OB and DM, but the Bauhaus and other big DIY chains, we have increased our shelf presence space, and the idea is that we are gaining share on the expense of other competitors.

items.statement: Parador added commercial sales layer targeting specifiers; good traction in commercial segment
items.quote: We have also added a layer of commercial sales on top of it. Now commercial, growing in the commercial segment meant building relationships with the specifier community and product differentiation, which we have done over the last 2 years, and there is a good traction coming in on the commercial side of the business.

items.statement: Roofs gained market share at expense of steel roofing due to steel price surge
items.quote: The second thing that is also held is one of our close competitor products, which is steel roofing. There has been a massive run on the prices of those products, which has also opened a bigger demand market for us as an industry.

items.statement: Parador gaining share as competitors fold or restrict activity; staying power a USP
items.quote: It is essentially coming from the fact that a lot of our competitors are also falling by the wayside, either they are holding up or they are restricting their areas of activity, and which is also somewhere helping us.

items.statement: Working capital position strengthened significantly vs prior year and corresponding period
items.quote: Our working capital position has strengthened significantly compared to both previous year and the corresponding period of last year.

items.statement: Total debt Rs 896 cr as of Sep 30 vs Rs 852 cr Mar 31; increase driven by greenfield projects and capacity expansion
items.quote: Our total debt stood at Rs. 896 crores as on September 30, as compared to Rs. 852 crores as of March 31. The increase was primarily driven by investment in ongoing greenfield projects and other capacity expansion initiatives to support future growth.

items.statement: Parador exposure EUR 40 million (EUR 20m SBLC + EUR 20m corporate guarantee)
items.quote: Yes. So as on today, our exposure is EUR40 million, EUR20 million, as you mentioned, is SBLC, and against corporate guarantee, it is EUR20 million.

items.statement: Clean Coats integration expected to complete by year-end subject to statutory approvals; synergies across operations, procurement
items.quote: The integration of Clean Coats with BirlaNu is expected to be completed by end of this year, subject to the requisite statutory approvals. We believe this integration will create further opport unities to realize synergies across operations, procurement, and other business functions while further strengthening our portfolio

items.statement: Parador impairment provision Rs 90 cr added in Q2; cumulative provisions Rs 164 cr as of Sep 30, 2026
items.quote: In view of the operating losses at Parador, we have recognized an additional provision of Rs. 90 crores towards diminution in the value of our investment in BirlaNu International GmbH, taking the cumulative provisions to Rs. 164 crores as of September 30, 2026.

items.statement: India business H1 revenue Rs 1,422 cr (+13.8% YoY); EBITDA Rs 138 cr (2x YoY); margin ~10% (+400 bps)
items.quote: Our India business sustained its strong momentum with revenue growing 13.8% year -on-year to Rs. 1,422 crores. EBITDA doubled to Rs. 138 crores from Rs. 69 crores in the corresponding period last year with margins expanding by over 400 basis points to approximately 10%.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties, supply disruptions driving raw material, energy, freight, currency inflation; high inflation and tight liquidity may weigh on near-term demand; El Nino risk to rural demand
items.quote: Geopolitical uncertainties and global supply disruptions continue to drive inflation in key raw materials, energy, freight, and currency. High inflation and tight liquidity are likely to weigh in on near-term demand, and the El Nino effect poses a risk to farm output and, therefore, rural demand.

items.statement: AI-enabled materials discovery platform approved; Rs 5 cr budget over 12-18 months; asset-light, not material to financials
items.quote: The first approval we have taken is to the tune of about Rs. 5 crores, which will be consumed over the next 12 to 18 months. The line to breaking even is not a long gestation time. So, this is not an asset -intensive, Capex-intensive business model that we are going after.

items.statement: India retailer engagement via WhatsApp-based AI-driven tool deployed 6 months ago; captures demand, enables fulfillment, cross-sell
items.quote: In the India business, a lot of our retailer demand and retailer engagement is being driven by a WhatsApp -based AI-driven tool, which is allowing us to capture the demand at a retailer level, process the demand at a distributor level for them and ensure fulfilment, and allows us direct access to this retailer community, including our ability to drive customized promotions and cross -selling, upse

items.statement: FY27 capex expected around INR 13,000 crores; FY28 capex around INR 10,000 crores or more
items.quote: We did around INR 6,000 crores in the first half. We should be doing a similar or a little bit -- not less, but something more in the second half. So it should be around INR 13,000-odd crores in this whole year. We look at a similar figure in the next year also. And then we -- as Rajesh ji had mentioned about the steel plant, what is the figure of steel plant coming up, then the majority would acc

items.statement: Stand-alone net debt target within 1-1.5x next 12 months EBITDA
items.quote: So we keep our debts accordingly, and that's our plan. We don't -- and yes, once the projects start coming up, and then, once the repayments are starting, then obviously, the debt reduces as per the repayment.

items.statement: Chemaf debt restructuring targeted to close within 3-4 months (by end FY27)
items.quote: So we are looking to close it within the next 3 to 4 months. So before the end of this financial year, it will be done.

items.statement: Chemaf long-term net debt expected around $500 million (from current ~$800 million) including plant completion capex
items.quote: So net debt in the longer run in the asset will be somewhere around $500 million from the current levels of around $800 million. And this includes the capex incurred for the plants because we are also spending money to complete the plants.

items.statement: Chemaf copper-cobalt complexes (Etoile & Mutoshi) targeted for completion by end FY27 and production in FY28
items.quote: We are confident of completing them by the end of this financial year and have them in production in FY28.

items.statement: Wire rod plant blast furnace and coke oven start Q4 FY27; steel plant and wire rod mill start Q1 2027 (FY28)
items.quote: Blast furnace and coke oven should get started in Q4. And steel plant and wire rod mill should get started in Q1 2027.

items.statement: Beneficiation (BHQ) volumes expected to start FY29
items.quote: FY29. Volumes of iron ore remains at 26 million tons throughout the period. Relevant or usable iron ore will remain at 26 million. The benefits should start in '29.

items.statement: FY27 copper production target revised to 5,850 tons (from earlier 8,000 tons) due to Surya Mines challenges
items.quote: So I think 5,850 is the target that we are looking for the full year. So in fact, earlier when we had disclosed in the last quarter, the target was higher at 8,000 tons. But given the challenges that we are having in Surya, a large part of the effort is going towards completing the Chemaf plant.

items.statement: Iron ore volume FY27 ~8 million tons; FY28 ~9.5 million tons (after 20% debottlenecking to 9.6 mtpa)
items.quote: This year, our volume should touch about 8 million tons. And next year, it should be around 9.5 million tons.

items.statement: Stand-alone H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 38.33%, up 542 bps YoY; Q2 margin 37.22%, up 419 bps YoY
items.quote: Our H1 EBITDA margin came in at 38.33%, the best half-year margin the company has ever reported and an expansion of 542 basis points year -on-year. Our Q2 margin stood at 37.22%, up 419 basis p oints year-on

items.statement: Value-added products contribute 61% of stand-alone revenue and 67% of EBIT in Q2 vs 43% and 49% a year ago
items.quote: Value-added products now contribute 61% of stand-alone revenue and 67% of EBIT in quarter 2 versus 43% and 49% a year ago. This is a structural re-rating of the earnings base, not a cyclical spike.

items.statement: Thriveni H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 19.18%, up 436 bps YoY; Q2 weaker due to monsoon and higher HSD/explosives costs
items.quote: EBITDA for H1 came at INR 884 crores, up 85% year-on-year with margins at 19.18%, an expansion of 436 basis points over the last year.

items.statement: Thriveni pursuing pass-through of higher input costs (HSD, explosives) to clients; negotiations underway
items.quote: We are actively pursuing pass-through of these higher input costs to our clients, and those negotiations are currently underway.

items.statement: Iron ore resource 26 million tons per year available till 2051; monthly run rate upward of 2 million tons
items.quote: With 26 million tons of iron ore available for -- till 2051, we think we are quite well placed in terms of balancing.

items.statement: Thriveni expects 12-14 million tons iron ore and 1.5-1.8 million tons manganese from Tata Steel JV mines from next year
items.quote: And we are expecting that at equipment contracting would help 12 million to 14 million tons of iron ore and around 1.5 million to 1.8 million tons of manganese from next year onwards.

items.statement: H1 FY27 stand-alone capex INR 6,052 crores on downstream steel and beneficiation projects
items.quote: The company incurred capex of INR6,052 crores in H1 FY2 7, as we continue to build out our downstream steel and beneficiation projects

items.statement: $300 million NCD enabling resolution passed for potential capex funding
items.quote: That's an enabling resolution what we have taken. So we just wanted to keep ourselves ready if such an opportunity arises. And we already have this resolution in place, and we can go ahead with it. And everything obviously will be used more and more for capex or that's what the intention is.

items.statement: Two 4 mtpa pellet plants running above rated capacity; debottlenecking underway; third pellet plant being added
items.quote: On pellets, both our plants of 4 million tons each capacity are running in excess of the rated capacity, and we are debottlenecking towards higher output while adding a third pellet plant as well.

items.statement: Slurry pipeline 1 running at full capacity; extending to longer, larger network to eliminate truck movement of fines
items.quote: The first pipeline is already running at full capacity and has actually lowered our freight cost for iron ore. And we are now extending this to a much longer and larger pipeline network, which will carry our beneficiated materials over long distances, eliminating the movement of fine iron ore by truck almost entirely.

items.statement: 1.2 mtpa integrated steel plant (wire rod) progressing; blast furnace and coke oven Q4 FY27, steel plant and wire rod mill Q1 FY28
items.quote: 1.2-million-ton integrated steel plant producing wire rod is progressing well and moving steadily towards commissioning.

items.statement: Chemaf Etoile and Mutoshi: 74,000 tpa copper and 20,000 tpa cobalt at full potential; captive ore, sulphuric acid, power locked in
items.quote: At full potential, these operations will produce 74,000 tons of copper and 20,000 tons of cobalt a year.

items.statement: Surya Mines targeted ~12,000 tpa copper; JORC resource estimation ongoing, will take time
items.quote: The Surya Mines is around 12,000 tons targeted production, whereas the Etoile and Mutoshi Mines are around 75,000 tons of production targeted in copper plus 20,000 tons of cobalt.

items.statement: Iron ore realization ~INR 6,700/ton (INR 670/ton in transcript appears to be a typo for INR 6,700); pricing based on quality, stocks, order book; considered sustainable
items.quote: Our price of INR6,700 reflects the quality. It's one of the best iron ores available, except maybe one company. And it reflects that pricing. It's a market which is quite open, and I wouldn't say -- I mean, it's a good market. So we are having a pricing system of our own.

items.statement: Pellet realization INR 11,348/ton (Q2) and INR 11,520/ton (H1); EBITDA INR 4,604/ton (Q2) and INR 4,988/ton (H1)
items.quote: Realization stood at INR 11,348 per ton in quarter Q2 and INR 11,520 for H1 with EBITDA of INR 4,604 and INR 4,988 per ton, respectively.

items.statement: DRI realization INR 31,040/ton (Q2); EBITDA INR 9,231/ton
items.quote: DRI realization stood at INR31,040 per ton in quarter 2 with an EBITDA of INR9,231 per ton.

items.quote: And in terms of coal also, due to these geopolitical issues for the pricing of HSD and explosives, we had to suffer a little bit. So that has also affected a little bit of our profitability and EBITDA margins. But now, those things -- as I told in my speech, that now we are having the pass-on mechanism with the mine owner, NTPC.

items.statement: Surya Mines: sulphuric acid shortage and high cost (no captive plant); diesel cost in DRC ~$3.2/litre (3x India) due to West Asia crisis and landlocked logistics
items.quote: Third, because the mines are far away from the plant, it is around 70, 75 kilometers, so -- and diesel cost in DRC has been very high. It is like $3.2 per liter, which is, I mean, almost 3x of what we see in India.

items.statement: Pellet sales mix 71% domestic, 29% export in Q2
items.quote: Our sales mix was 71% domestic and 29% export.

items.statement: Thriveni: equipment rental started at Tata Joda West Manganese Mine; DC Jain Dalpahar Mines production commenced Oct 2026; discussions for Tata Joda West Iron & Manganese, Vijay-II, Tiringpahar, Bamebari, Khondbond
items.quote: Also, production at DC Jain Dalpahar Mines, which commenced in October this year, and rental equipment for few other mines of Tata are also under discussion, namely Tata Joda West Iron and Manganese Ore Mines, Vijay-II iron ore mines, Tata Tiringpahar Iron and Manganese Mines, Bamebari Iron Ore and Manganese Mines and Khondbond manganese.

items.quote: I guess, you missed on the opening balances of the ore what we had as the closing balance last year. So that, I think, is not taken into consideration that's why you -- that material balance does not mean -- I think your numbers are not getting matched.

items.statement: Stand-alone net debt INR 9,316 crores (30 Sep 2026); consolidated net debt below INR 20,000 crores (includes Chemaf acquisition debt)
items.quote: Stand-alone net debt as on 30th September 2026 stood at INR9,316 crores, comfortable relative to the EBITDA the business is now generating, even through an intensive capex cycle. items.statement: Debt-equity for projects planned at 60-65% debt (less than 75%)

items.quote: The name of which has been changed to Thriveni Lloyds Swarnagiri Private Limited, has been approved for opencast and underground operations for 1.5 million tons per annum with a processing capacity of 1.5 million tons per annum.

items.statement: Iron ore production Q2: 3.95 mt (+15.5% YoY); H1: 10 mt (+35% YoY); sales Q2: 2.12 mt, H1: 7.59 mt
items.quote: Iron ore production for quarter 2 was 3.95 million tons, up 15.5% year-on-year with H1 production at 10 million tons, up 35% year-on-year. Sales were 2.12 million tons in quarter 2 and 7.59 million tons in H1.

items.statement: Pellet production Q2: 2.11 mt; H1: 3.81 mt (after 2nd plant commissioning in May)
items.quote: Pellets. Pellets Lloyds Metals and production was 2.11 million tons in quarter 2 and 3.81 million tons in H1 following the commissioning of our second pellet plant in May

items.statement: DRI sales Q2: 160.6 kt (+81% YoY); H1: 343.1 kt (+104% YoY)
items.quote: DRI sales volumes were 160.6 kilotons in quarter 2 and 343.1 kilotons in H1, up 81% and 104% year-on-year, respectively.

items.statement: Thriveni iron ore volumes (incl. BHQ) Q2: 11.22 mt; H1: 30.31 mt; coal volumes Q2: 18.82 mcm; H1: 44.84 mcm
items.value: 11.22 mt (Q2), 30.31 mt (H1) iron ore; 18.82 mcm (Q2), 44.84 mcm (H1) coal
items.quote: Iron ore volumes, including BHQ, stood at 11.22 million tons in Q2 and 30.31 million tons in H1. Coal volumes from our Indian operations, including overburden, were 18.82 million cubic meters in Q2 and 44.84 million cubic meters in H1.

items.statement: Thriveni: 88 electric equipment units operational at mine, 20 at railway siding; 14 mobile crushers, 26 HEMM for BHQ; 100T dumper converted to LNG hybrid
items.value: 88 electric units, 20 at siding, 14 crushers, 26 HEMM
items.quote: We now have 88 electric equipment units operational at the mine and a further 20 are at the railway siding. We have also mobilized 14 mobile crushers and 26 heavy earthmoving equipments for BHQ crushing and are mobilizing higher capacity equipment, including EH5000 Ultra Class dumpers Lloyds Metals and and large excavators to support the enhanced production. A 100-ton diesel dumper has already bee

items.statement: Thriveni Q2 margins hit by heavy monsoon in Odisha/Jharkhand and higher HSD/explosives costs; pass-through negotiations underway
items.quote: Due to rains, all the iron ore production as well as coal productions are badly hampered. And this year, particularly in Odisha and Jharkhand, both the places, there were heavy rains. And in terms of coal also, due to these geopolitical issues for the pricing of HSD and explosives, we had to suffer a little bit.

items.statement: Consolidated order book crossed INR1,000 crore for the first time, reaching INR1,087.3 crore as of September 30, 2026, up 51% YoY and 64% QoQ.
items.quote: As of September 30, 2026, the consolidated order book stood at INR1,087.3 crores, registering a growth of 51% year -on-year and 64% quarter -on-quarter compared to INR662 crores as of June 30, 2026.

items.statement: Order book accretion of INR425 crore in Q2 FY27; total new orders including execution of INR350 crore reached INR775 crore.
items.quote: Add to that about INR350 crores of order execution, which means the total order book or total of new orders during this period is close to about INR775 crores.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR2,000 crore by FY28 remains on track.
items.quote: Yes. I think we are on track for that, yes.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 15% by FY28 reiterated; management expects to achieve it earlier rather than later.
items.quote: I think the numbers that you stated and what we had also discussed previously, I think we stand by those numbers. items.statement: Consolidated Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin at 11.2%; H1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 9.5%.
items.quote: During quarter 2, the company reported consolidated revenue from operations of approximately INR346.7 crores with a growth of 15.3% compared to Q1 FY27 with EBITDA of INR39 crores and EBITDA margin of 11.2%.

items.statement: India glass-lined equipment business at high single-digit EBITDA margin in H1 FY27; expects 16-18% at INR300 crore revenue.
items.quote: We believe that even at current levels of operation, current levels of expenditure, even with a INR300-odd crores revenue, we could still be between 16% and 18% kind of EBITDA levels going forward.

items.statement: THALETEC Germany H1 FY27 revenue INR192 crore with EBITDA margin a little over 11.5%.
items.quote: So the revenue for the first half from THALETEC Germany is about INR192 crores. And the EBITDA margin was roughly about a little over 11.5%.

items.statement: Omeras (HLE Surface Technologies) achieved EBITDA breakeven in H1 FY27; targets double-digit EBITDA margins at EUR25-30 million revenue.
items.quote: We think that once we cross the EUR20 million revenue per annum, the company should get back to serious profitability and maybe between EUR25 million and EUR30 million, we could even be as high as double-digit EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Heavy engineering segment expected EBITDA margins 15-18% initially, maturing to ~22%.
items.quote: In the initial periods, the margins could be in the range of between 15% to 18%. Going forward, on a more mature basis, this business should deliver EBITDA margins of close to about 22%.

items.statement: New heavy engineering plant near Anand (Adas) for equipment >100-150 tons, up to 4.5-5m diameter and 15-20m length, targeting energy, oil & gas, petrochemicals, renewables.
items.quote: Yes. So as you rightly said, we are putting up a new plant at the site, which is called Adas close to Anand. This will be largely focused on heavy equipment. So these will be equipment's which are in excess of 100, 150 tons large diameters and length, so maybe up to 4.5 to 5 meters in diameter, 15, 20 meters in length.

items.statement: India demand optimistic in API and specialty chemicals; US demand high; Europe slightly subdued.
items.quote: So the demand scenario in India is quite optimistic. We have very high demand in, as I explained in my speech, in the API sector and the specialty chemical sector. So overall demand is quite good. Europe, the demand in Europe is slightly subdued, but it is not really subdued, but the demand from U.S. is quite high.

items.statement: THALETEC products now ~22% of India glass-lined product business, up from earlier quarters.
items.quote: We are now seeing this transition gaining momentum with THALETEC products contributing approximately 22% of our overall glass lined product businesses in India during the current quarter.

items.statement: India glass-lined equipment revenue expected INR260-280 crore in FY27 based on current order book visibility.
items.quote: We expect the revenue this year to be anywhere between INR260 crores and INR280 crores.

items.statement: Omeras H1 FY27 turnover slightly above EUR8.5 million, EBITDA breakeven achieved.
items.quote: during this entire half year, Omeras has achieved a turnover in a little excess of about EUR8.5 million and has touched EBITDA breakeven during the first half.

items.statement: Net working capital days increased to 102 days in H1 FY27 from 80 days in FY26 due to order book expansion; focus on improving efficiency.
items.quote: Net working capital days increased to 102 days in line with the order book expansion from 80 days in FY26.

items.statement: Debt ~INR350 crore, described as very manageable and not a concern; focus on consolidation over acquisitions.
items.quote: The debt on an overall basis is very manageable and not an area of concern at all.

items.statement: Management focused on consolidating existing businesses after Omeras acquisition; open to strategic opportunities in core area if digestible.
items.quote: I think the management is driven by consolidation at this point of time. All our businesses are looking promising and encouraging. We just completed the acquisition of Omeras just about a year back. I think it's a good time for us to sit back and consolidate it, sort of consolidate the operations.

items.statement: Omeras strengthened with new COO from large US multinational, new CFO, expanded design and sales teams across Europe.

Then we have a new CFO, who is on board since a couple of quarters. We have enhanced our design team. We have added new people in the sales teams across various geographies in Europe.

items.statement: Competitive intensity in India glass-lined and filtration & drying easing as demand picks up; booking orders at improving margins month after month.
items.quote: With the market demand picking up, I think obviously, that competitive intensity has gone down. We are able to not only book orders, we are able to book orders at improving margins month after month.

items.statement: Landmark EUR20.56 million order for vitreous enamel cladding panels for Fehmarnbelt tunnel (Germany-Denmark); delivery over 3-3.5 years starting early/mid next year.
items.quote: A key highlight during the quarter was the landmark order worth approximately EUR20.56 million secured by our step-down subsidiary, HLE Surface Technologies GmbH, Germany, for vitreous enamel cladding panels for the common wealth channel connecting Germany and Denmark.

items.statement: Omeras India plant likely to be commissioned in next 2 quarters, adding another moving part to the business.
items.quote: In fact, maybe at this time next year, we may have another moving part, as you said, of the Omeras India business, which is also likely to get commissioned in the next 2 quarters or so.

items.statement: Customer delivery acceptances delayed by 1-2 months due to geopolitical disturbances, impacting dispatches and revenue recognition.
items.quote: delivery acceptance by customers gets postponed simply because of Let's say, things like geopolitical disturbances and stuff like that due to which their own project execution or their own project implementation gets delayed by a month or even a couple of months here and there

items.statement: Guided 15-20% growth for corporate advisory and capital markets over next 3-5 years
items.quote: We've guided that corporate advisory and capital markets will see anywhere between a 15%-20% growth over the next couple of years, three to five years.

items.statement: Guided private markets loan book growth around 20% and investment side around 15%
items.quote: We've guided private markets will see a similar number, around 20% increase on the loan book and around 15% increase on the investment side.

items.statement: Guided wealth management AUM growth 20-25% subject to mark-to-market
items.quote: Wealth management, we've maintained 20% -25% growth in AUM, subject to mark-to-market.

items.statement: Guided asset management growth 15-20%
items.quote: Asset management, again, we expect to have 15%-20% growth.

items.statement: Guided affordable home loans AUM growth 25-30%
items.quote: On the home loan side, we've talked about 25% -30% growth in AUM, and we've already hit INR4,000 crores of AUM there.

items.statement: Guided blended 20% growth across businesses for next five years
items.quote: Overall, I think if you were to sort of weighted average this number, we're looking at 20% growth, at least for the next five years, year-on-year.

items.statement: Guided mid-teens ROE target in 3-4 years as investment cycle ends
items.quote: I think we will be targeting a return on equity in the mid-teens. That would be the endeavor towards the end of the investment cycle of many of our businesses.

items.statement: Guided profit growth 20-25% if revenue grows 15-20% due to operating scale
items.quote: If the revenue growth is between 15% and 20%, then the profit growth should be between 20% and 25% as we achieve more and more operating scale.

items.statement: INR130,000 crores of transactions filed with regulator for execution over next 12 months
items.quote: We still have INR130,000 crores worth of transactions, which are already filed with the regulator for execution over the next 12 months, and many more to be filed this quarter and next quarter.

items.statement: Closed INR83,000 crores transactions in Q2 FY27, ranked #1 in IPOs and QIPs
items.quote: Pleased to report that we were ranked #1 across IPOs and QIPs and closed transactions of INR83,000 crores in Q2.

items.statement: Primary markets revival from June with strong FPI and domestic participation

items.statement: October deal activity decent, expecting November-December to be decent

items.statement: Corporate advisory and capital markets annualized ROE ~36% for Q2 FY27

items.statement: Wealth recurring gross yield ~51 bps, net yield ~35 bps; new assets at north of 60 bps
items.quote: On the yields front, we have roughly gross yields of around 50 basis points on the recurring side, and we have net yields of around 35 basis points on the recurring business. It is actually 51 basis points on gross and roughly 35 basis points on net.

items.statement: ARC returns modeled at 16-18% on SR investments

items.statement: Real estate pricing needs 200-300 bps above corporate, pricing is a challenge

items.statement: Adding infrastructure and technology spend continuously in broking business
items.quote: We are adding infrastructure and spending on technology on a continuous basis in the broking business, and that growth will continue.

items.statement: 2-year filter life products now contribute a large share of revenue and mix, growing healthily.
items.quote: These products have done very well for us. And then now they contribute to a large share of our overall revenues and overall mix and growing healthily as well.

items.statement: Launched 6 new SKUs under Aeroguard brand in air purifiers, materially strengthening portfolio.
items.quote: We launched 6 new SKUs under the Aeroguard brand, materially strengthening our portfolio and positioning us well for the opportunity in the second half.

items.statement: Commodity inflation intensified, creating pressure on gross margins; no pricing actions taken during festive period to prioritize growth.
items.quote: At the same time, commodity inflation has intensified in recent months and is beginning to create pressure on gross margins. We deliberately refrained from taking pricing a ctions during the festive period, choosing instead to prioritize growth, customer acquisition and category expansion

items.statement: Price hikes taken in April: Water purifiers 5-6%, AMC 3-10%; no further hikes until planned mid-November increase.
items.quote: The price hikes that we have taken was in April. After that, we've not taken any price hikes since then. I think just to give you a broad sense, water was in the range of around 5% to 6%. That was the range in which price increase was taken.

items.statement: Stepped up advertising and sales promotion investments in Q2 and H1, focused on in-store visibility, new launches and consumer campaigns.
items.quote: We also stepped up our advertising and sales promotion investments during the quarter, particularly behind in-store visibility, new product launches and consumer campaigns.

items.statement: A&SP spends grew ahead of revenue in H1 with higher proportion towards sales promotions and in-store promoters.
items.quote: Overall, between A&SP in the first half of the year, our spends have grown ahead of our revenue. And like I said, the bias has been more towards SP expenses because we've chosen to increase our deployment of in-store promoters and our point-of-sale visibility.

items.statement: Rolling out Eureka Forbes branded fixtures across large retail stores to improve point-of-sale visibility and conversion.
items.quote: We are currently rolling out Eureka Forbes branded fixtures across large retail stores, improving the visibility of the point of sale, and strengthening customer engagement and conversion.

items.statement: Launched nationwide pre-filter check campaign and new customer connect point at 6-month post-AMC mark for free servicing and conversion.
items.quote: One is that we have launched a nationwide pre-filter check campaign, which allowed our customers to reach out to us and for our technicians to go and ensure that the customers' filters are genuine and if they need to be replaced, offer them that replacement opportunity.

items.statement: Introduced Aquaguard Express Care with same-day (4-hour) service promise for out-of-warranty/AMC customers.
items.quote: we've launched, a s you may have seen in investor deck also, the Aquaguard Express Care campaign and Express Care proposition, where we give customers who are out of our AMCs or out of our warranty same day, in fact, 4-hour service

items.statement: H1 working capital deployment higher due to festive inventory build-up, modern trade/e-com credit terms, and proactive BIS transition inventory; unwinding expected in H2.
items.quote: The first half typically involves higher working capital deployment due to 2 reasons. There is an inventory build-up ahead of the festive season and there is a higher share of modern trade and e-commerce sales, which are on standard credit terms.

items.statement: Net cash surplus of INR 304 crores at quarter end; H1 cash from operations negative historically, full year cash flow generated in H2.
items.quote: We ended the quarter with a net cash surplus of INR 304 crores. Cash balance in H1 was impacted due to working capital deployment.

items.statement: In FY26, entire operating cash flow generated in H2 alone; similar trend expected in FY27.
items.quote: Historically, a significant proportion of annual operating cash flow has been generated during the second half of the year as inventory levels normalize and receivables are collected. To illustrate, in FY '26, the entire operating cash flow for the year was generated in H2 alone.

items.statement: Company is net cash positive with INR 304 crores surplus; no borrowings mentioned.
items.quote: We ended the quarter with a net cash surplus of INR 304 crores.

items.statement: Promoter pledge activity has no bearing on company operations, governance, or financial obligations; company is professionally run with independent Board.
items.quote: See, as far as Eureka Forbes is concerned, this has no bearing on any of our operations. That is something which is between the promoter and whatever funding arrangement that they would have had with the financial institution for the acquisition.

items.statement: Competitive intensity increasing across segments but company gaining market share with comprehensive playbook across all price points.
items.quote: In this growing market with more competition as India's largest and strongest consumer brand, we have a right to win and to gain disproportionately in this growing market as the last quarter's performance demonstrates.

items.statement: Filter business growth accelerated in Q2 supported by stronger customer engagement and awareness.
items.quote: Encouragingly, growth in our Filter business accelerated during the quarter, supported by stronger customer engagement and awareness.

items.statement: Service revenue (AMC) remained steady in line with Q1 trends; focus on driving filter sales and newer AMC propositions.
items.quote: On the service business side, growth in filter sales acc elerated and AMCs remained steady in line with Q1 trends

items.statement: Commodity environment remains challenging with inflation persisting and worsening across key input categories.
items.quote: The commodity environment continues to remain challenging with inflation persisting across several key input categories and in some cases, are, in fact, worsening.

items.statement: Grey market for 2-year filters currently absent due to recency and longer life breaking parallel market's high-frequency renewal model.
items.quote: The unit price that they sell at is low, but the frequency of contact is high and the frequency of change is high. This 2-year filter life, given the longer life, breaks that relationship and breaks the equation fundamentally.

items.statement: Revised FY27 revenue guidance to INR 800 crore and PAT to INR 125 crore due to TLS incident impact
items.quote: At the start of the year , we guided a revenue of about INR 825 crores and PAT of about INR 137 crores, about 25% PAT growth. We now expect our revenue to be about INR 800 crore and PAT of around INR 125 crore.

items.statement: TLS incident expected to reduce FY27 total income by INR 20-23 crore and PAT by INR 10-12 crore, largely in H2
items.quote: We expect the incident to reduce our FY27 total income by about INR 20 crores to INR 23 crores and our PAT by about INR 10 crores to INR 12 crores, largely in the second half.

items.statement: Incident impact expected to last only next two quarters, then business as usual
items.quote: In our opinion, the impact of the incident may only last for next two quarters, after which it will be business as usual.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target maintained at around 25% consolidated level going forward
items.quote: EBITDA margins are around the 25%. That we will try and maintain because, obviously, our focus is more on the solutions business, which is anyway slightly high gross margins.

items.statement: Enterprise solutions on own five-product platform grew 36% YoY, now two-thirds of revenue; international markets also two-thirds of revenue
items.quote: The growth is coming from enterprise solutions built on our own five product platform that grew 36% and now makes up two -thirds of our revenue. International markets also contribute two -thirds of our revenue.

items.statement: Post-quantum migration, machine/AI agent identity, and data privacy are now board-level topics driving demand
items.quote: Customers now face fixed deadlines on post -quantum migration, on identity for machines and AI agents, and on data privacy. These are now board level topics, especially in banking and regulated industries.

items.statement: Won national PKI for Nigeria's certifying authority regulator; first Kazakhstan win with defense entity; pipeline growing in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan
items.quote: In Africa, we won the national PK I for Nigeria's certifying authority regulator; our entry into that market. In CAS, we secured our first win in Kazakhstan with a defense entity and our pipeline in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan is growing.

items.statement: Added significant clients in Indonesia, Philippines, Germany, Qatar, Abu Dhabi; cross-selling with Cryptas brought 3-4 large enterprise clients in Europe
items.quote: We added significant clients in Indonesia, The Philippines, Germany, Qatar , and Abu Dhabi. Cross selling with cryptos brought in three 4 eMudhra Limited Q2 FY27 Earning Call 05.11.2026 more large enterprise clients in

items.statement: UAE trust services pipeline building while awaiting license
items.quote: And in the UAE, our trust services pipeline keeps building as we await our license.

items.statement: Won DPDP deal for an NBFC in Q1; momentum continuing in Q2 with B2C banks, NBFCs, private sector; expect more traction next year as DPDP enforced
items.quote: We already won a deal in the last quarter itself for DPDP. This is for a NBFC. There is quite a bit of momentum in the current quarter. We should be winning many more deals for the data privacy.

items.statement: Target 40-50 DPDP clients in first year at INR 40-50 lakh to INR 1-2 crore per deal
items.quote: The idea is next year, how do we capture, let's say, 40 to 50 clients with the kind of value that we had, you know, ascribed earlier? That's the immediate scope because typically, the first phase will largely look at entities that are, you know, somewhat, you know, focused on customer data and meaningful scale and give some kind of a value of, let's say, INR 40-50 lakhs, INR 1 crore.

items.statement: Receivables grown in line with business, days stable; creditors declined despite revenue increase, weighing on H1 operating cash flow
items.quote: As our scale has increased, so have our working capital needs. Receivables have grown in line with the business; however, in terms of the number of days, it remains around the same level. Though the revenue has increased, we have paid the creditors without delay resulting in decline in creditors in spite of the increase in revenue. And this has weighed on the operating cash flow in the first half.

items.statement: CertiNext platform independent of TLS; can connect any SSL vendor; sold standalone in many cases; TLS not bundled requirement
items.quote: CertiNext is a neutral product. With CertiNext, we can connect any SSL given by any vendor. So, in lot of cases, it is sold standalone. It is not sold along with the TLS.

items.statement: Only directly affected customer is US University Federation; they continue with CertiNext and asked for TLS subcontract model; no existing contract terminations
items.quote: In the US, the only customer, University Federation, who will be directly affected was using our CertiN ext product and TLS certificate. They have decided to continue to work with us and asked us to provide the TLS certificate to any other TLS vendor on a subcontract model.

items.statement: Reputation risk contained to US and Middle East; India, Europe (Cryptas/Primesign brands), Africa, Far East largely unaffected
items.quote: So , that's where, the reputation risk is contained to US and a little bit of Middle East. That's where we estimate only instead of INR 823 crore, INR 800 crore could be there for the year as a whole.

items.statement: DPDP stack comprehensive across consent, data discovery, classification, protection, retention, governance, vendor management, DSAR; few competitors cover full stack; data protection expertise a strength
items.quote: There are quite a few companies that are building various capabilities, but many of them are focused on only one or two layers. There are a very few select names that are focused on the entire DPDP stack, and our whole expertise has been on data protection, which is where we score very strong.

items.statement: eSign volumes grown from 1-2 lakh to 7-8 lakh per day in one year
items.quote: Almost one year back, we were doing one lakh, two lakh eSign. Now, we are doing 10 eMudhra Limited Q2 FY27 Earning Call 05.11.2026 almost seven to eight lakh eSign per day

items.statement: TLS incident: weak keys in 8 intermediate certificates from April 2025 ceremony; revoked next day; none issued to end customers; root keys unaffected; browser programs distrusted related root; KPMG appointed for independent review
items.quote: On October 17 th, an independent researcher reported weak keys in eight intermediate certificates within one of our public TLS hierarchies created during a key -generation ceremony in April 2025. We revoked all eight the very next day. None of them had been used to issue any certificate to end customers and our root keys were not affected.

items.statement: AI used to analyze and improve security across technology; other business segments not affected as they don't store data like TLS
items.quote: But from a technology perspective, whatever possible, we are tracking to analyze with the help of the AI and see what are the further securities to put in place. That work is parallelly going on.

items.statement: Post-quantum migration deadlines (2029) driving POCs and planning; some PQC POCs already materialized into orders
items.quote: PQC adoption and migration. Basically, 2029. So many companies are kind of planning. They will start planning from next year onwards.

items.statement: Management reiterates long-term CAGR target of 30%+ but declines to give specific FY28 revenue guidance
items.quote: We would want to give it a pass for the moment. I think the only guidance that we want to talk as of now is a consistent CAGR of 30 plus.

items.statement: Compressor capacity expansion of 60 lakh units (INR 120-130 crore) targeted for completion by end of FY27
items.quote: The highest CapEx that was required was for compressors, about INR 120 crores, INR 130 crores, and I think a large portion of that has already been invested.

items.statement: EMS facility under commissioning, expected to go live by December 2026 for captive consumption
items.quote: EMS this year, I think by December it should be live, the additional capacity, although it will not contribute to the top line, as I said earlier as well.

items.statement: AC indoor unit expansion 70% complete, balance 30% to be done in 1-1.5 months; ODU expansion to follow
items.quote: AC indoor is ongoing, and I said 70% of that has already been done. There's another 30% that should happen over the next 1, 1.5 months.

items.statement: Compressor capacity expansion to 60 lakh units targeted for completion by end of FY27 (Q4)
items.quote: Hopefully by the end of this financial year, Q4, mid of Q4, end of Q4.

items.statement: Deep freezer capacity to increase from 1.5 lakh to 2.5 lakh by June-July 2027
items.quote: Deep freezers, we are at 1.5 this year, and hopefully before the end of -- before the start of the next season, we should have the additional capacity of 1 lakh.

items.statement: AC IDU capacity to reach 14-15 lakh units (1.5-1.6 million) after expansion
