items.statement: Long-term sustainable EBITDA per ton of ~Rs 85,000 post Phase-3 at optimal utilization; 26% volume growth seen sustainable for FY27
items.quote: we believe post Phase-3 expansion, a long-term EBITDA per ton of approximately Rs. 85,000 per ton should be sustainable

items.statement: No specific quarterly or next-year EBITDA per ton guidance given; 75k-85k is long-term sustainable range not quarterly guidance
items.quote: the 75,000 -85,000 is a long -term sustainable rate, we believe, given the overall mix of the business. It is not intended to be a guidance for any quarter or specific year

items.statement: Sustained growth across power generation, transmission, renewables, electrification, industrial and digital infrastructure; OEMs expanding capacity
items.quote: We see sustained growth and investments across power generation, transmission and related equipment driven by grid infrastructure development, renewable energy integration, electrification and growth , electricity requirements from industrial and digital infrastructure

items.statement: India CTC demand expected ~120k-130k tons by FY30 excluding exports; HVDC and 765kV add incremental demand
items.quote: by FY '30, we expect the overall CTC, the demand to be approximately around 120,000 tons to 130,000 tons in India

items.statement: Export revenue grew 108% YoY and 44% QoQ in Q2; exports now 32% of revenue vs 26% in Q1
items.quote: Export revenue in Q2 grew 108% year -over-year and 44% higher than last quarter. As a result, exports represented almost 32% of our revenue in Q2, up from 26% in Q1

items.statement: Target to return exports to historical ~40% of revenue over next 1-2 years on expanded capacity
items.quote: our objective over the next few years is to return exports to its historical average of around 40% of total revenue

items.statement: Received trial order for 2 HVDC transformers overseas; Power Grid approved Supa facility for up to 765kV transformers and reactors
items.quote: Last quarter, we received a trial order to supply specialized wires for 2 HVDC transformers overseas, which demonstrates that our HVDC opportunity is not just confined to India alone

items.statement: Phase-2 expansion 96% complete as of Sep 9, 2026; installed capacity 57,845 MT available for H2 FY27
items.quote: We are very pleased to have completed 96% of both Phase -1 and Phase-2 of our capacity expansion as on September 9th, 2026, roughly 6 months ahead of schedule. Period end capacity stood at 57,845 metric tons and is now available for H2 of FY ' 27

items.statement: Board approved Phase-3 to add specialized wire capacity targeting ~72,200 MT total by Q1 FY29; includes 10 acres land purchase
items.quote: The board has approved a new Phase -3 expansion to add specialized Magnet Winding Wires manufacturing capacity, and which is expected to increase the company's total installed capacity to approximately 72,200 metric tons by Q1 of FY 2029

items.statement: Phase-3 capex up to Rs 185 cr over next 18 months funded by internal accruals and long-term debt; majority spend in FY28

items.quote: What excites us most about this is that this is more like a storage asset -- is more like -- sorry, more than a storage asset. Much like our LPG business, it does allow us to participate in the distribution of ammonia to industrial customers, moving further along the value chain and capturing margin significantly higher than traditional -- just traditional storage revenues.

items.statement: LPG distribution margin of INR7,000 per ton achieved through procurement efficiencies from large capacities, VLGC-compliant jetties, low freight, minimal demurrage, and integrated supply chain
items.quote: What has happened is that over the last 1.5 years, we have improved our cost efficiency by having larger capacities where we can unload from largest of the ships.

items.statement: Tristar acquisition subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions; expected completion in Q4 FY27
items.quote: Subject to regulatory approvals and the customary closing conditions, we expect to complete this transaction in Q4 of FY27.

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions affected Q1 logistics volumes; global supply conditions largely normalized but growth driven by capacity additions and structural strengths
items.quote: This also shows the resilience of our infrastructure platform and the reliability of our operations.

items.statement: Tristar management to continue in place for 30-year operating history; no management changes expected post-acquisition
items.quote: This company has been operating for the last 30 years. And the entire management is in place and will carry on. We don't expect to change the management and the continuity will ensure that there is no disturbance in the operations and performance of the company.

items.statement: Welcome new LPG infrastructure investments (Petronet LNG, IOCL, BPCL, JSW) as India has only ~1 million metric tons static storage (~10 days) vs ideal 90 days; competitive advantage from world-scale terminals, low-cost construction, rail/pi
items.quote: We have around 1 million metric tons of static storage capacity as far as I know in India. That is not even equivalent to 10-day storage. Every -- most of the countries, I may not say every, most of the countries in the world would ideally like 90 days storage capacity and infrastructure.

items.statement: Tristar acquisition brings global operations headquartered in Dubai with international network, diversified service offerings, and established global customer relationships including Shell, Glencore, BP, Total, Saudi Aramco
items.quote: They have -- as we mentioned, the customer partnerships that they have with Shell, with Glencore, with so many other BP, Total and so on, Saudi Aramco, so many different partnerships that they have, long-term business relationships.

items.statement: Record-breaking profit in H1 FY27: revenue INR4,570 crores, EBITDA INR1,184 crores, PAT INR866 crores (doubled year-on-year); EPS INR21.23 up 140%
items.quote: I'm pleased to report a record-breaking profit in the first half of this Aegis Logistics & year, FY27. We had a revenue of INR4,570 crores, generating an EBITDA of INR1,184 crores and a profit after tax of INR866 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin corridor of 12%-12.5% for next two quarters
items.quote: we have decided that we will try to remain within our corridor of 12% -12.5%. In some quarters, it will be at lower end of corridor, some quarters it will be at higher end of the corridor. This will remain for the next two quarters, so it will not be impacted.

items.statement: Core business capex of INR400-500 crore annually
items.quote: Every year, we invest close to our depreciation, which is about INR400 crore-INR500 crores every year on our core business.

items.statement: Lithium-ion plant to be cash neutral in 2-3 years
items.quote: our plan is we have to make it cash neutral in two to three years' t ime, which is, I think, a very fair ask by global standards

items.statement: Phase 2 lithium capex decision at 80% utilization of 6 GWh
items.quote: we should be waiting for about, let's say, 80% utilization level. At that point, we should make a decision.

items.statement: Phase 2 lead time lower due to existing utilities and land for 12 GWh
items.quote: we have bought the land for 12 GWh. We have put up all the utilities, the power substations, the boilers, chillers, everything for 12 GW h. We have everything in the same campus, our giga campus. Our lead time for phase two will be much lower than phase one, because phase one, it started from greenfield

items.statement: Cumulative equity investment in EESL INR5,352 crore including INR550 crore in current FY
items.quote: As of today, Exide's cumulative equity investment in EESL stands at INR5,352 crore s, including INR550 crores invested in the current financial year

items.statement: 6 GWh lithium-ion cell plant commissioned in Bengaluru on 23rd September
items.quote: 23rd September was a milestone for us. Exide Energy completed commissioning of 6 GWh of lithium-ion cell plant in Bengaluru.

items.statement: Two NMC lines of 1.5 GWh each commissioned; will utilize first line then shift to second
items.quote: We have commissioned two lines of NMC. First line is 1.5 GW h, and the second line is also 1.5 GW h. First we will utilize the first line. Once we reach our 1.5 GW h, then we will shift to the second line.

items.statement: Debottlenecking lead-acid factories to meet concurrent OEM and aftermarket growth
items.quote: we are investing capital in debottlenecking each of our factory. Thankfully, we have multiple factories where brownfield expansion and brownfield debottlenecking is possible. So we are doing that. Substantial capital has been allocated to squeeze out every line, every asset.

items.statement: Automotive OEM business grew over 25% for fourth consecutive quarter
items.quote: The automotive OEM business grew by over 25% for the fourth consecutive quarter, as vehicle makers stepped up production and dispatches.

items.statement: Two-wheeler and four-wheeler replacement business delivered fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth
items.quote: The two-wheeler and four-wheeler replacement business delivered its fourth consecutive quarter of double -digit growth, helped by a steadily expanding vehicle par c and the reach of our distribution network

items.statement: Home inverters grew 20% YoY; solar grew 40%+ YoY supported by PM Surya Ghar Yojana
items.quote: Home inverters grew by 20% year -on-year, while solar grew by 40%+, supported by the favo urable seasonal demand as well as the government initiatives, including the PM Surya Ghar Yojana

items.statement: Exports grew over 20% YoY for second consecutive quarter on low base
items.quote: Exports grew by over 20% year-on-year for the second consecutive quarter on a low base.

items.statement: Electric two-wheelers reached 11.6% of two-wheeler retail in September; Vahan registrations ~2 lakh/month
items.quote: Electric two -wheelers reached 11.6% of the two -wheeler retail in September, which is directly relevant for our lithium-ion business.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA INR606 crore, up 53.6% YoY; margin 12.1% vs 9.4% YoY (+270 bps)
items.quote: EBITDA came in at INR606 crores, up 53.6% year-on-year, and EBITDA margin improved to 12.1% from 9.4% in the quarter two, resulting in an expansion of about 270 basis points on a low base.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA margin 12.2%, up 130 bps YoY; H1 pre-tax profit up 46.5% YoY
items.quote: For half year, EBITDA margin was 12.2%, up 130 basis points year -on-year. Half year pre-tax profits grew by 46.5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Calibrated price increases of ~9-10% on four-wheeler and ~5% on two-wheeler since January
items.quote: I think between January and October, I would say, because in October also we have taken one round. In January and October, we have taken about more than 10%, I would say. items.statement: Input costs elevated due to geopolitical challenges and weaker rupee; lead/LME benefit offset by rupee depreciation
items.quote: Input costs remained elevated vs last year due to prolonged geopolitical challenges, especially across West Asia, as well as a weaker rupee. Crude oil prices went up significantly, resulting in an overall inflationary environment. On a sequential quarter basis, the full benefits of softer lead or softer LME for lead and antimony prices could not be fully realized due to continuous weakening of rup

items.statement: Automotive technology shifting from standard flooded to EFB and AGM batteries
items.quote: Because more and more we see trend on enhanced flooded battery, EFB battery as we call it, as well as the AGM batteries, which is absorbent glass mat. So we have both, we have this portfolio. We are exporting it, we are selling this to our OEMs big time. Even in aftermarket, the EFB sales have picked up big time. So the technology in automotive will shift, I believe, from the standard flat plate f

items.statement: Tubular lead-acid to remain dominant for inverter/solar in Indian conditions
items.quote: On the inverter side, tubular, you know, we are the largest tubular battery manufacturer. Tubular does not only go to inverter, it also goes to solar, multiple applications. It is a seasonal business , but the technology will stay like this, because India is the largest tubular manufacturer in the world. Nobody else uses tubular. But in our kinds of use cases, in Indian conditions, where you need

items.statement: Gained high share in key OEM launches including MG Hector Tomahawk and Tata Aeris
items.quote: We gained high share across key upcoming OEM launches, the new launches, for example, MG Hector Tomahawk, and Tata Aeris.

items.statement: Signed long-term strategic cooperation agreement with ExCom Energy Solutions GmbH for European industrial battery and energy storage
items.quote: In September, we signed a long -term strategic cooperation agreement with the ExCom Energy Solutions GmbH, Germany. This is to expand our industrial battery and energy storage business across the European Economic Area.

items.statement: NMC performance testing satisfactory for leading two-wheeler OEMs; lifecycle testing underway
items.quote: As we speak, for some of the lead ing two -wheeler OEMs, the performance testing is over. Now they are doing the lifecycle testing. There is a process, there is a sequence. Lifecycle testing takes time, and once lifecycle testing is over, they will do the pack and the vehicle level testing. That is the next phase. So far, the performance testing has been very satisfactory. We got positive feedback

items.statement: LFP 102 Ah cells supplied to telecom operators for validation and used in own e-rickshaw packs with positive response
items.quote: On the LFP side, the 102 Ah LFP cells we are already making. We have given it to some telecom operators for validation, as well as we have started using it in our e-rickshaw packs, which is our own pack. These packs have been delivered to the market, they are running, and we have got quite positive response on the performance of the LFP cell as well.

items.statement: Major OEM revenue expected from beginning of Q4 or February; small OEM NMC revenue may start next month
items.quote: I think the major OEMs, we are hoping will start in from beginning of quarter four or maybe February. Pravin Saraf: Yes. Avik Roy: But surely this fiscal year

items.statement: Lithium-ion cells still have 5-10% cost gap vs imported Chinese cells on landed basis
items.quote: We still have a 5% -10% cost gap with imported Chinese on landed basis, based on the form factor and chemistry. That's a very high-level statement. We still have that gap on a landed basis.

items.statement: BESS cell manufacturing dependent on PLI scheme clarity; will apply for PLI
items.quote: For BESS cell, we have the possibility to make the cell, but as you all know that we have the PLI scheme announced. We are waiting for the PLI, we will of course apply for the PLI. As under the PLI scheme, we will need to wait, and once the clarity is there, then we can g o ahead with the manufacturing of the cell

items.statement: Raw materials 100% from SVOLT-approved vendors; no independent low-cost vendor development
items.quote: these materials are 100% from the approved vendors of our technical partner, SVOLT. We have not ventured out and tried to develop our own low-cost vendors.

items.statement: Three months inventory holding planned for raw materials due to potential China export restrictions
items.quote: we are looking for three months inventory holding, because of the increase in maybe the because of the restriction, it will take some time.

items.statement: Working capital requirement for lithium ramp-up factored into approved annual capital allocation budget
items.quote: the working capital, whatever is required, has already been factored in our annual capital allocation budget, which we already declared officially. Our board has approved for that amount already. So in terms of working capital requirement, we are well covered within our approved limit.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with healthy operating cash flows
items.quote: The balance sheet remains strong. We continue to be debt-free and generate healthy operating cash flows.

items.statement: No fresh equity raise planned for lithium phase 2; funding from internal accruals and working capital
items.quote: going forward, it will be mostly for the working capital, land, loss funding, things like that. Not so much for capital equipment.

items.statement: Standalone revenue INR5,026 crore, up 20.3% YoY; H1 revenue INR10,331 crore, up 18.9% YoY (first time above INR10,000 crore half-year)
items.quote: Standalone revenue for quarter two was INR5,026 crores, which is up 20.3% year-on-year. The growth momentum of quarter one carried into quarter two, taking our half -yearly revenue to INR10,331 crores, up by 18.9% year-on-year. This is the first time we have crossed INR10,000 crores revenue milestone in half year.

items.statement: Phase 2 lithium capex per kWh could be higher due to rupee depreciation unless equipment prices fall
items.quote: Could be, could be. Because we already see this happening at the tail end of our capex phase one also, because dollar has appreciated by 10%. So the first one year, two year, whatever our capex was, at the tail end of the capex, we found that weak rupee hitting us. So in phase two, we do not know at what level the exchange rate will be. But yes, it can work negatively regarding our capex per kilow

items.statement: Mark-to-market loss of ~INR600 crore on HDFC Life investment in H1
items.quote: there is a mark -to- market loss on HDFC Life in this six months of around INR600 crore. That may be the reason you are talking about the base of the investment, which has changed from X to X minus. This is only mark-to-market.

items.statement: Reiterated full-year double-digit revenue growth guidance
items.quote: With this, we are reiterating our guidance for the full year to remain at double-digit. We'd call that out at the start of the year. We've managed to deliver that a little ahead of that, in the first two quarters, and we look to maintain that momentum going forward for the remainder of the year as well.

items.statement: India standalone margin dilution only 10 bps in Q2 FY27 despite inflation
items.quote: On a margin lens, our dilution was only 10 basis points. We mitigated a huge amount of inflation that has happened.

items.statement: India FMCG grew 10.7% with 5.5% volume and 5.2% pricing growth in Q2 FY27
items.quote: India FMCG grew 10.7%, coming on the back of decent volume growth at 5.5%, and pricing at 5.2%.

items.statement: Premium portfolio contribution increased from 17% to 20% over 18 months, growing at 4x overall rate
items.quote: Our premium portfolio used to contribute 17%. It has now gone up during these 18 months from 17% to 20%, and this premium portfolio is growing at 4X our overall rate and is margin accretive.

items.statement: Target to increase premium portfolio contribution to 23% over next 18 months
items.quote: We want to take our premiumization up to 23% over the next 18 months. Maybe even sooner.

items.statement: Plan to invest additional 150-200 bps in advertising and promotion for core brands
items.quote: We're going to look to invest 150 to 200 basis points of advertising and promotion extra, or media investments that go further in those areas.

items.statement: Distributor count reduced by 43% under Project Saksham, throughput up 2x, ROI up 30%
items.quote: We've carried out a very massive consolidation exercise over the last year. It's resulted in a reduction in our distributors by about 43%. And honestly, it was the need of the hour, and I'm glad the teams have done such a strong job of it, because that has resulted in lower distributor attrition by almost 80%. It has resulted in their throughput going up by 2X. It has resulted in their ROI going u

items.statement: Target direct reach to over 100,000 villages with geotagging
items.quote: So the idea is to get over 100,000 villages where we go directly, and each of these is going to be geotagged so that it's very clear what is being sold, so that we can really enhance the quality of this coverage.

items.statement: Operating efficiency savings target increased to INR 170-200 crore (1.5x previous INR 115 crore)
items.quote: The focus is the savings tha t we generated: INR 115 crores, we need to deliver 1.5x of those savings. The way I see it, I take the number as INR 170 to 200 crore, so the aim is to generate the savings that we can then look to plough back into the business

items.statement: Strategic M&A rated red; no new category entry, focus on adjacency, scalability, synergies and right valuation
items.quote: We're looking at M&A in two parts. One is in the area of taking a minority stake in D2C companies, which allows us to learn, understand trends, and engage and play a role in how these companies evolve with the founders. We got RAS as part of Dabur Ventures. Dabur Ventures was formed on October 2025, and RAS was the first investment that was done earlier this year. So that's one aspect of it. And t

items.statement: Strong balance sheet with INR 6,000 crore war chest in India for acquisitions
items.quote: And point number two was more for your capital allocation for inorganic opportunities, which I think we have a strong balance sheet, a strong war chest with us, almost 6,000 crores in India itself. So those funds are always available for us, provided there's the right acquisition, you know, at the right valuation, which is more synergistic.

items.statement: Portfolio rationalization: 6 brands and 350 SKUs removed, rated green
items.quote: So, 6 brands, 350 SKUs, are gone. I've given us a rating of green in this space, but I promise you this is going to be a big area of focus as we look to our future as well, because this is where we will be able to ensure that we focus our energies on the few big priorities that we are going to be focused on.

items.statement: Healthcare segment grew 6.9% in Q2 FY27, OTC and digestives growing at strong double-digits
items.quote: Now, a lot of people ask me about healthcare performance. To me, 6.9% performance is a strong recovery. We had a recovery that started last quarter as well. If I look at it, it's not where we need it to be, but if you look at it from the context of where this business was, we are beginning to see a good recovery, and the team has strong plans to take this forward.

items.statement: International business growing at 20% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: International business continues strong growth momentum; it's growing at 20%.

items.statement: No new global CEO; Herjit Bhalla inducted on board, international business runs independently under Mr. Narang oversight
items.quote: There is not going to be a new global CEO. The board and the management very strongly feel that what we have right now is what we need in the business at this stage. So, I have been inducted onto the board. I will continue to be focused on the India business, the SAARC business, and the duties that come to me as being part of the board. The international business, even today, runs independently, w

items.statement: Mid-term strategic vision exercise initiated, to be shared in 6-8 months with 2031 plan
items.quote: We believe that the time is right for us to get into a strategic midterm exercise that we will initiate now, right? So, I look forward to coming back to you all in the next 6 to 8 months with a medium-term vision that talks about a 2031 plan and sharing with you what things we will continue to keep doing.

items.statement: Challenging macro environment with Middle East conflict, crude price rise, elevated inflation impacting consumption
items.quote: The environment has been challenging, given the Middle East conflict, resulting in crude prices going up and higher inflation. But for us, within FMCG across the board, it's been a challenging environment in order to drive consumption. It's been an environment where inflation has been elevated, and we've had to calibrate what we are doing.

items.statement: General trade growth returned to mid-single digits for 2 consecutive quarters, highest in 19 quarters
items.quote: We've now delivered two quarters where our growth on GT has been mid-single digit growth. This quarter, we've delivered our highest growth in the last many quarters, I think 19 quarters or so, in GT.

items.statement: Alternate channels sustaining strong double-digit growth
items.quote: Alternate channels have been growing at a fast clip for us: strong double-digit performance in this space, and for me, the way I see it, they are going to play a key role in the evolution.

items.statement: Focus on health and wellness: OTC, digestives, functional beverages, strength and vitality identified as growth areas
items.quote: We've identified health and wellness. It's clearly what I've been hearing ever since I've come. We need to evolve our play and strengthen our play, and actually claim our right to win in this segment, so that's an opportunity.

items.statement: Retail Next program rolling out across 40,000 stores targeting 1.5x GT growth
items.quote: We are ramping up our channel program. And that is something that we're now building across 40,000 stores. We call it the Retail Next program. Within that, we are very clear that we want to deliver growth that is 1.5 times the growth of the rest of GT.

items.statement: New initiative IRIS launched for continuous replenishment and forecasting accuracy
items.quote: We recently launched an initiative called IRIS, which is really about continuous replenishment, or CRS, and forecasting accuracy, to be able to take more value out of that space and to drive further efficiencies in that aspect of our business

items.statement: Consolidated revenue grew 11.6% in Q2 FY27, second consecutive quarter of double-digit growth
items.quote: We've delivered 11.6% growth at our consolidated level. We did have some impact on our operating profit, and that's largely been on account of higher inflation from the supply chain and freight and logistics at the international business level. But we've still managed to ensure we deliver a strong PAT. Now, you would see that this is the second consecutive quarter of double-digit growth at the rev

items.statement: Food & Beverage segment continues accelerated growth momentum with strong double digits
items.quote: F&B, the food business, continues its accelerated growth momentum, strong double digits. The beverages business bounced back on the back of a good season, but more importantly, what we are doing on the premium end of the portfolio with Real Activ Coconut and Real Activ, which is growing strongly, and the additional incremental investments that we put behind Real in this quarter.

items.statement: Quick commerce viewed as complementary, enables premium portfolio placement and innovation
items.quote: A lot of people ask me that: for a company like Dabur, where distribution has been a moat, how does growth in quick commerce impact us? You know, the honest truth is: it's fantastic, because what quick commerce is allowing me to do is innovate better; it's allowing me to ensure my premium portfolio goes there; it's allowing me to get more lines in than a classic, traditional GT system cannot do be

items.statement: Commercial capability rated best-in-class, execution strong, no major structural changes needed
items.quote: I can tell you one thing that really stands out for me, having now spent 6 months at Dabur, having also worked at MNCs all my life prior to that, the commercial capability that I see at Dabur is best in class, is brilliant. The ability to drive execution is absolutely fantastic, because decisions get taken, and once a decision is taken, the call to action is strong; the execution is brilliant.

items.statement: Honey strategy: purity traceability to beekeeper, premium monofloral/organic/regional variants, sampling for penetration
items.quote: There is also traceability that we are working on, and we'll start talking about it soon- where we are now being able to trace the honey back to the beekeeper; that's going to be made available to consumers. So, as far as honey is concerned, that's going to be big work that's happening on the core. In addition to this, we are also focused on driving usage, occasion-based usage, which is important

items.statement: Chyawanprash strategy: new TVC, gummies format, winter loading strong, focus on relevance and usage occasions
items.quote: What we need to do is make it more relevant for consumers today, so that they understand what it does for us, and hence we're talking to them in a different form, in a different manner. That's one aspect of it. The other aspect of it is we also realise that the format in which it comes today could be a little challenging for, let's say, the younger consumers, and hence, we have the gummies. That i

items.statement: McKinsey consultant engagement under review, decision expected in next month
items.quote: So we're going to figure that out over the course of the next month. We haven't taken a final decision on that. But yes, McKinsey has been part of the journey with us as part of Vision 7.

items.statement: Chemist channel program critical for OTC and digestives, part of Project Saksham focus
items.quote: The chemist program, and within that, the chemist channel program, is a key aspect of Project Saksham as well. I think for us, it's really about- and I go back to how we're going to use MSL and digitisation to enable us to ensure we get the right portfolio in the right store. The chemist program is critical for us from an OTC or a digestive lens, and that is part of the focus that is being driven.

items.statement: Capex for FY26-27 expected in range of Rs 1,200 crore to Rs 1,500 crore, mostly revamping and retail expansion
items.quote: The capex for financial year 2026-27 is expected to be in the range of %1,200 crore to 21,500 crore, which includes refinery maintenance, revamping, and small-value IRR projects including retail projects.

items.statement: Targeting retail presence of about 500 outlets by end of FY2028
items.quote: We are targeting a retail presence of about 500 retail outlets by the end of FY 2028.

items.statement: Next maintenance shutdown expected early next financial year, around April
items.quote: The next one is expected early next financial year, maybe around April.

items.statement: Grid power project expected to be fully available by financial year end, targeting fuel and loss around 9.5%
items.quote: If you remember, last time we said that we are targeting about 9.5. Dhaval Popat: Agreed. Devendra Kumar: Let it stabilise, and then we should be closer to that number

items.statement: Retail sales grew ~50% YoY in Q2 due to private OMCs curtailing operations; direct marketing grew 30-40% YoY
items.quote: Q2 has seen very high sales of retail products, primarily because of the curtailment of retail operations by the private OMCs. We are seeing a year-on-year growth of almost 50% from the last quarter.

items.statement: Solvents business (xylol, MTO, toluene) grew nearly 100% YoY, touching 10 TMT per month
items.quote: We have also strongly entered the solvents business, primarily xylol, MTO and toluene, and we are quite strong there. Compared to last year, we have grown significantly, by nearly 100% in this space, and we are touching 10 TMT per month in the solvents segment.

items.statement: Diesel direct marketing volumes doubled to ~40 TMT in Q2 from 20 TMT in Q1
items.quote: We are seeing total sales of almost 40 TMT, as opposed to 20 TMT in quarter one. TMT is thousand metric tonnes.

items.statement: Net cracks available around $20 above average landed cost; GRM not published quarterly due to methodology differences
items.quote: Based on the current systemic arrangements, we see movement in SAED that is more in line with the international market, but the net cracks available are more or less around $20 above the average landed cost.

items.statement: Conscious decision not to publish quarterly GRM numbers due to methodology differences across companies
items.quote: we had taken a conscious decision not to publish quarterly GRM numbers. The reason was that there is a huge difference in the way, or the methodology, GRM is computed by different companies, and some other PSUs have also taken that approach.

items.statement: Devanagonthi to Bengaluru Airport ATF pipeline authorised by PNGRB, completion by 2029-30 at cost of Rs 200 crore plus
items.quote: PNGRB has granted authorisation to MRPL for laying, building, operating or expanding a petroleum and petroleum products (ATF) pipeline from Devanagonthi to Bengaluru airport. This is expected to be completed by the year 2029-30 at a cost of ¥200 crore plus.

items.statement: Capex for FY26-27 expected Rs 1,200-1,500 crore, mostly revamping and retail expansion; Devanagonthi-Bengaluru pipeline a major upcoming project
items.quote: our capex remains in the modest range. Again, sticking to my opening statement, it is ¥1,200 crore to %1,500 crore, and that is mostly revamping and, to some extent, our retail expansion.

items.statement: Q2 crude mix: domestic ~25%, term contracts ~20%, spot balance from West Africa, Americas, Middle East, Russia; Russian barrels ~32% vs 28% in Q1
items.quote: In Q2, domestic crude made up about a quarter of our intake, term contracts about a fifth, and spot purchases the balance, drawn mainly from West Africa, the Americas, the Middle East and Russia. Russian barrels made up about 32% of our Q2 basket, against approximately 28% in Q1.

items.statement: No VGO or high sulphur fuel oil processed as intermediates in past six months; constantly evaluating market offers
items.quote: In the past six months, we have not had any requirement of taking in VGO or high sulphur fuel oil as intermediate products for processing. However, we are constantly evaluating market offers, and we are in touch with other refineries within India on the available intermediate feedstocks, to see if we can maximise our secondary processing units.

items.statement: Product mix slightly impacted by CHTU fire (designed for heavier crudes); distillate impact less than couple of percentage points
items.quote: As DF said, it is a very marginal impact. If | had to put a number to it, the impact on total production could be less than a couple of percentage points of the distillates.

items.statement: Swing capability between ATF and diesel exists on monthly basis depending on crude availability
items.quote: The swing capability exists. We can swing between products quite quickly, even ona monthly basis, depending on the right type of crude. The constraint would be the sourcing of crude; as long as we have the right crude for doing that, we should be able to swing pretty fast.

items.statement: Retail network 257 outlets across Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh; half-yearly retail margin marginally negative
items.quote: Our retail network has 257 retail outlets across Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and, lately, Andhra Pradesh. The half-yearly retail margin continued to be marginally negative.

items.statement: Gained market share as private OMCs curtailed retail and direct marketing; expect some customer stickiness when situation normalises
items.quote: We are seeing a year-on-year growth of almost 50% from the last quarter. While this is not a structural change — it has to do with the fact that some of the private OMCs have curtailed sales due to lower margins — as DF said, we are a public sector company, and being a responsible public sector company, we have not curtailed operations.

items.statement: Borrowings fell over Rs 35,000 crore in six months to Rs 9,245 crore at end Sep 2026; debt-equity improved from 1.01 to 0.55
items.quote: Borrowings fell by over 35,000 crore in six months, reaching %9,245 crore at the end of September. This is, of course, variable and depends on working capital requirements. The debt-equity ratio has correspondingly improved from 1.01 as reported at the end of March 2026 to 0.55 at the end of September 2026.

items.statement: Interim dividend of Rs 33 per share declared, total Rs 3,526 crore
items.quote: Considering the positive performance for H1 ofthis year, the Board has declared an interim dividend of 33 per share, which works out to a total dividend of 3526 crore.

items.statement: Formed JV OPML (ONGC Petrochemicals Marketing Limited) with ONGC 50%, OPaL 25%, MRPL 25%; MRPL investment Rs 12.5 crore
items.quote: there was the formation ofa JV company, OPML, that is, ONGC Petrochemicals Marketing Limited, with a 50% stake held by ONGC, 25% by OPal and 25% by MRPL. MRPL's investment will be to the tune of %12.5 crore.

items.statement: Received international credit rating BBB- (Stable) from Fitch, at par with sovereign rating
items.quote: For the first time, MRPL has been able to obtain an international credit rating. Fitch International has assigned a rating of BBB- (Stable), which is at par with the sovereign rating and comparable with its peer companies and OMCs.

items.statement: Closed long-pending reformate classification tax dispute; received refund of Rs 212 crore
items.quote: There was a long-pending tax case, and we have been able to close that long-pending reformate classification dispute. We have received a refund of %212 crore.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict in West Asia squeezing assured Middle East supplies, longer voyages, steep freight and insurance cost increases
items.quote: As you all know, the industry, especially the refining industry, is going through challenging times due to geopolitical situations mainly arising out of the conflict in West Asia. This has resulted in a squeezing of assured supplies from the Middle East, longer voyage times and a steep increase in freight and insurance costs.

items.statement: Won two National Innovation Awards at ETM 2026 in Goa, reinforcing R&D commitment and Aatmanirbhar Bharat vision
items.quote: The company has won two National Innovation Awards at the recently concluded 29th Energy Technology and Innovation Meet, that is, ETM 2026, held at Goa. These achievements reinforce the company's commitment to R&D and innovation and support the Government of India's vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat.

items.statement: Overall FMCG consumption environment remains strong with stable improving trajectory despite inflationary headwinds
items.quote: The overall consumption environment, as we see it, remains strong. FMCG demand across various categories remains stable in the improving trajectory despite the inflationary headwinds.

items.statement: Edible oil volume growth ambition of 4% to 5% sustained
items.quote: We had also talked about that our ambition in the Edible Oil segment will be to sustain our volumes and grow at 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Peanut butter e-commerce growth target ahead of category within next 2 quarters; modern trade entry in FY28
items.quote: Our ambition will be within next 2 quarters to put it ahead of category growth in e-commerce channel. And while we achieve that, we will also then enter into these platforms in general trade and modern trade, especially modern trade where saliency of value-added offerings is relatively much higher. And that would be a task for FY '28.

items.statement: No anticipated cost-side impact requiring price increases in quarter ahead; stable consumer pricing environment foreseen
items.quote: And overall, I would say, in the quarter ahead, I do not anticipate any, let's say, impact on the cost side, which will impact margins or which will need us to do price increases.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margin expanded 240 bps YoY in Q2; adjusted expansion 370 bps
items.quote: Our normalized EBITDA margin has expanded by 240 basis points. However, if you look at because last year, you may recall, we had talked about certain expenses which are one-off and project expenses in nature. This year, virtually those expenses are negligible. So, if I do an unnormalized or an adjusted comparison, the growth would have been 370 basis points.

items.statement: Foods business margin improved 70 bps in inflationary environment; edible oil margin dilution but absolute margin protected
items.quote: Overall, if I look at, despite this inflationary cost environment, our gross margin has increased by about 19% to about INR107 crores, which is also driven very strongly by manufacturing and logistics efficiency and better cost absorption and disciplined management of our freight network. This, if I look at in the context of our food business, which is where our core is lying, there the improvemen

items.statement: Calibrated price increases taken in relevant categories; broad-based inflation in packaging and commodities passed through without volume impact
items.quote: We have been able to take price corrections, price increases in relevant categories where we have seen inflationary trends on certain commodities like packaging, et cetera, we have seen broad-based inflation. And these inflations, we have been able to calibrate in our pricing. And our brands have shown resilience and power so that our volume trajectory has not got impacted, while, of course, we ha

items.statement: Innovation contributing ~6% of sales from last 2 years' NPDs; 24 new products launched in Q2; premiumization adding 3-4% to growth
items.quote: Happy to share that today, roughly about 6% of our overall sales come through NPDs we have launched in last 2 years, and this is a very strong and sustainable growth engine we are building because today, these innovations dominantly sit in e-commerce or B2B business.

items.statement: Volume growth breakdown: ~10% volume, 3-4% premiumization, 6-7% price increases
items.quote: So I would say a real way to look is to read this number is about 10% volume, 3% premiumization and 6% to 7% impact is coming on account of price increases.

items.statement: E-commerce now 19% of sales at ~INR90 crores; growing 43% YoY in Q2 vs 38% in H1
items.quote: This business has scaled up significantly over the last 2 years. It is now close to INR90 crores of our business with 19% of our sales at a company level coming from this channel alone.

items.statement: B2B culinary portfolio growing with export expansion in Southeast Asia and key account penetration
items.quote: In B2B, we continue to focus on increasing penetration across domestic key accounts. We are building our export business stronger in Southeast Asia, driven also by new product introductions.

items.statement: Manufacturing footprint combined with third-party capabilities; expanded 3P network for capacity and innovation
items.quote: Our growth model is now becoming increasingly capital efficient, combining our existing manufacturing footprint with third-party capabilities, and we have expanded a mix of networks in 3P sites, driving some of our capacity requirements as also some of our innovations in the journey in the last few months.

items.statement: Negative operating cash flow ~INR49-50 crores in H1 due to strategic inventory build in corn/oats and receivables increase in line with sales momentum; DSOs constant
items.quote: In inventory, we have taken certain structural calls because of the uncertainty in the environment we faced. We have looked at areas where volatility could impact availability, and we have consciously taken our inventories up. And some of these areas are in corn, some of our products like oats, where we are consciously trying to build inventory. That is one. Second, if you look at overall finished

items.statement: Inventory and receivables levels expected to normalize in Q3 as environment stabilizes
items.quote: We are seeing signs of stabilization. So you would also see as we get into Q3, this level will come back.

items.statement: Popcorn corn secured via contract farming in Andhra and Chhattisgarh; diversified sourcing; no significant inflation expected next year
items.quote: We have a very secure contract for next year. We do not see any significant inflationary trend on the popping corn.

items.statement: Core portfolio volume growth doubled to 10-12% vs historical 10%; non-core edible oil volume growth turned positive at 5%
items.quote: Our volume growth in core portfolio used to be about 10%, which has expanded to about 12%. Part of it could be about the GST benefit. So I would still say we are at a 10% to 11% volume growth sustained level in the business. If you look at noncore, oil used to be historically declining. We did some experiments, which gave us a confidence that we could target 4% to 5% volume growth in oils, and tha

items.statement: ACT II ready-to-eat popcorn volume growth 23%, value growth 38% in Q2; ready-to-cook volume growth 5-6%
items.quote: Our Q2 growth was 38% in value terms, 23% in volume terms, and this is really one of the fastest-growing businesses for us, driving our performance and efficiency. Ready-to-cook business is also growing at about 12% in value and 5% in volume terms.

items.statement: Culinary portfolio (ketchups, mayo, sauces) volume growth 13% in Q2 vs 11% H1; value growth 21% Q2, 18% H1
items.quote: Again, very strong performance in this portfolio, Q2 volume growth of 13%, ahead of overall H1 volume growth of 11%, indicating acceleration in volumes and value growth, of course, again, reflects a very similar trend, growing at 18% in H1 and 21% in Q2.

items.statement: Edible oil volume growth 5% in Q2; value growth 19%; premium staple pricing kept stable
items.quote: In Q2 also, we have maintained a volume growth of 5%, which means we would have gained significant share in the Premium Edible Oil segment and our value growth, of course, has been strong and healthy at 19%.

items.statement: Sales Force Automation completed covering 400,000 outlets; 80% outlets regularly billing in Q2; improving range, depth, route productivity
items.quote: So today, we have 400,000 outlets, which are on this platform directly covered where we get full visibility of our billing efficiency. We have seen marked improvement in our billing efficiencies as we moved along this journey and about 80% of our outlets are getting regularly in Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Edible oil duty reduction in September led to stable to marginal deflation; movements within +/-5% manageable
items.quote: In September, there was a structural duty reduction by the government. And post that, dominantly, we are seeing the movements have been in the range of plus/minus 5%. And that much, I think, is very easily manageable through price calls and price changes.

items.statement: Del Monte key account/export annual contracts up for revision Dec-Mar; price increases expected to improve margins in Q4
items.quote: Specifically, I would say the impact should come more in Q4 rather than in Q1 because general renewal of contracts will happen between December to March.

items.statement: Core categories marketing spend at ~9% A:S ratio; target 9-10%; sequentially increased vs Q1
items.quote: Second, on the core categories where we are investing, we have already reached the level of about 9% of A:S or advertising to sales ratio. And we have talked about that 9% to 10% is the benchmark we would really want to operate because that we believe is critical. So, we are already very close to the level we would want to operate on, on a going basis on investment in our core categories.

items.statement: Sundrop business grew 19% in Q2, 17% in H1; Del Monte grew 26% in Q2, 20% in H1
items.quote: We have Sundrop growing at 19% in Q2. In H1, the growth is 17%. In Del Monte in Q2, we have grown at 26%, H1 growth being 20%.

items.statement: Gained market shares across categories in e-commerce via focused investments, tech backbone, performance marketing ROI
items.quote: We have actually gained shares across categories, driven by the fundamental changes in the way organization was approaching the channel.

items.statement: Edible oil price volatility risk low for next 3-4 months post duty reduction; movements within +/-5%
items.quote: In terms of environment, what we are seeing in the more recent times, I do not think there is immediate concern about increasing or inflationary environment in the next 3 to 4 months.

items.statement: Inorganic opportunities continue to be evaluated to build on platform
items.quote: Alongside this organic growth, which we have been very strongly focused on, we, of course, continue to evaluate any opportunity which may come in the environment for us to add inorganic opportunities, which can build on the platform, we have been able to create.

items.statement: FY27 guidance retained: order inflow INR22,000-25,000 crore, revenue growth 8-10%, EBITDA margin 8.5-9%
items.value: INR22,000-25,000 crore order inflow; 8-10% revenue growth; 8.5-9% EBITDA margin
items.quote: On our last call, we have shared our guidance for FY27 , which is order inflow in a band of INR22,000 crores-INR25,000 crores, revenue growth of 8%, 10%, and EBITDA margin in the range of 8.5%-9%. We have decided to retain our guidance for FY27 .

items.statement: Order book INR80,167 crore as of Sep 2026, up 11% YoY; Q2 inflow INR4,838 crore; including Oct orders, FY27 inflow INR11,108 crore (50% of lower guidance band)
items.quote: As of 30th September 2026, our order book stands at INR80,167 crore s, which is 11% higher than a year ago. During the quarter, we have booked new orders worth INR4,838 crores, mainly from our buildings and water and railway divisions.

items.statement: Bid pipeline remains ~INR2.5 lakh crore; order book 3.5x trailing 12-month revenue giving multi-year visibility
items.quote: I think in the last call in May, I have already shared the prospective pipeline of projects that we get to see, which at this point of time, at that point of time was about INR2.5 lakh crore s.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 consol EBITDA margin 8.79% vs 8.66% YoY; H1 FY27 9.1% vs 8.7% YoY; standalone Q2 8.48% vs 7.45% YoY
items.quote: At consolidated level, EBITDA we achieved 8.79%, which is INR528.46 crore s, and PBT of 4.47%, which is INR269.85 crore s, that is before exceptional items.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex INR253 crore vs INR500 crore full-year budget; FY28 capex expected similar but may increase for mining project
items.quote: We have incurred a capex of INR83 crores in the Q2 FY27 and INR253 crores in the first six months, as against the budget of INR500 crores for the financial year '27.

items.statement: Working capital (excl. cash/margin money) INR5,532 crore (28% of turnover, 96 days); trade receivables down to INR2,697 crore (53 days) from INR3,055 crore (68 days) QoQ
items.quote: In respect of working capital, excluding cash and margin money deposits, at the end of Q2 FY27, it stands at INR5,532 crores, which is 28% of the turnover. In terms of days, it is 96 days.

items.statement: Standalone net debt INR2,293 crore (up from INR2,008 crore QoQ); consol net debt INR3,887 crore (up from INR3,513 crore QoQ); debt-equity 0.32
items.quote: At the end of Q2, it stood at INR2,471 crores and net debt of INR2,293 crores. At the end of Q2 FY26, the same is INR2,115 crores and net debt of INR1,890 crore s.

items.statement: Cash & equivalents INR178 crore (down from INR404 crore QoQ); margin money deposits INR740 crore; H1 JJM collections INR1,720 crore
items.quote: Cash and cash equivalents. It is INR178 crores as at the end of September '26 and INR404 crores as at the end of June, and INR584 crores as at the end of March '26.

items.statement: 81% of contracts have escalation clauses; raw material price increases largely offset via price variation clauses
items.quote: 81% of our contracts have got the escalation clauses. Any increase in the prices will majorly offset from the price variation clauses that are available.

items.statement: JJM order backlog INR5,412 crore (excl. O&M); UP JJM major portion to complete by Mar 2027; AP Capital City order book INR14,500 crore with 30-40 day collections
items.quote: Excluding O&M. Generally, O&M we consider when we started, but excluding O&M, the order backlog is, one minute. INR5,412 crores.

items.statement: Smart meter installation 51% complete, 49% outstanding; payments regular with no working capital challenges; first payment on installation, balance over 93 months
items.quote: Yes, it is almost like 51% we have completed installation, and 49% is outstanding.

items.statement: BharatNet execution 11% of contract in MP & Uttarakhand; ~INR1,000 crore spent; billing started; housed in Electrical T&D division
items.quote: We have done almost like 11% of the total contract we have executed in both MP and Uttarakhand. We have almost spent about INR1,000 crore s on its work, and we have started billing now.

items.statement: Loans to group companies INR306 crore (up from INR290 crore QoQ, INR295 crore Mar'26); Vizag land sale receivable INR270 crore expected recovery by Q4 FY27
items.quote: Loans to group companies, INR306 crores at the end of September, and INR290 crores at the end of June, and INR295 crores at the end of March 2026.

items.statement: Retention money INR2,547 crore (up from INR2,396 crore QoQ); 53% of mobilization advances interest-bearing at 9.07% avg rate (down from 60% QoQ)
items.quote: In respect of retention money, it stands at INR2,547 crores in Q2 FY27, as against INR2,396 crores at the end of June 26th, and INR2,250 crores as at the end of March 26th.

items.statement: Ken-Betwa project progressing reasonably; land acquisition issue 30-40km from site; contract value INR3,389 crore for NCC portion
items.quote: We are happy to share with you that we are mak ing reasonable progress on this project

items.quote: This INR107 crore s investment relates to a project in Hyderabad. We have invested in that project, and the project is in midway. It was stopped, and the developer is in a little problem.

items.quote: The TBM machine was capitalized and put to use in the month of September. From September, that means second quarter of this year. Definitely, the depreciation is going to go up in the third quarter and fourth quarter.

items.quote: When I made the last comment, the crude was hovering at about $95. The crude went up to $114. Today, it's at $105, $106. So it's still at elevated levels. items.quote: So if you look at the 400 bps drop in the gross margin, it's largely due to the industrial business, which we believe that in this quarter, we've announced our price increases on our industrial side of about 4%. We believe that we can recover. And we believe that, look, it's a bit of a short-term issue, which we start to correct, right?

We've seen mid-double-digit growth in our decorative business

items.quote: I think what you should be aware of is the fact that JSW Dulux, the composition of the decorative to industrial business is 60% -40%, right? In fact, 57%-43%, right, compared to some of our larger players, which are 90% -10% or 80%-20%. And hence, the gross margin dilution of the industrial business impact is significant more on Dulux, which is not structural, it's temporary.

items.quote: We have already started cross manufacturing. So across both our plants, JSW Dulux, 5 plants and the three plants of JSW Paints, we started cross manufacturing. items.quote: We've had capex -- a higher capex increase on the industrial side of the business early during the year because the capacity utilization in our industrial business, particularly in some of our verticals that touched close to 75%.

items.quote: Vehicle refinish, we believe that we've started gaining market share. In our Marine & Protective, we are holding in some segments, gaining but otherwise holding market share. items.quote: We've seen about INR 7.3 crores realized in Q2, which is driven by supply chain efficiencies. We've cross manufacturing and unified projects business. items.quote: So my answer is yes, competitive intensity in terms of market activation, discounting continues to run, maybe at slightly lower levels than it used to be a couple of years, but it's still the same. Look, I think we are working on a strategy, where I think our focus is in t

items.statement: Crude at $105-115 (up from $95) and USD/INR at 94.5-96 (up from 93-94) pressuring margins
items.quote: The entire AOP budget planning, etcetera, was done at a different crude and dollar to rupee. That no longer stands sort of there. In this quarter, we've seen elevated crude levels, and we've seen elevated the dollar to rupee conversions at INR 96. So obviously, those two variables have impacted the industry.

items.statement: Demand buoyancy may be tested by elevated price hikes (decorative ~13.5%) and rainfall deficiency lag effects
items.quote: We believe that the current price increases are already very at elevated levels. If you take decorative that you mentioned, it's already at about 13.5%, which is a lit tle high.
