items.quote: The interest expense is INR 9.6 crores compared to INR 9.5 crores last quarter.

items.statement: Second interim dividend of INR 96 crores declared late September 2026, paid October 16
items.quote: It's second interim dividend of INR 96 crores, which was declared during last week of September 2026 and deposited in separate bank account, The payment was done on October 16.

items.statement: Chief Revenue Officer hired 2 quarters ago; leadership stable; refreshing go-to-market feet for enterprise sales; RSU expense stable at INR 3.2 crores
items.quote: I just want to correct that there's not been a lot of churn or change. We hired a Chief Revenue Officer 2 quarters ago. And that is it, right?

items.statement: Revenue INR 615.2 crores ($64.4M), up 23.4% YoY, 2.2% QoQ; adjusted net profit INR 66.5 crores ($6.9M), up 53.1% YoY
items.quote: We closed with a strong revenue of INR 615.2 crores or $64.4 million, which reflects a 23.4% year over year increase or 2.2% quarter over quarter.

items.statement: Middle East geopolitical uncertainty persists; US midterm elections may stabilize or destabilize; high-tech clients in layoff mode but adopting AI PDLC
items.quote: I don't think the crisis is over yet because there is no certainty, and we believe that the midterm election results in the U.S. will have something to do with it, either it will stabilize or further destabilize the situation.

items.statement: Working capital at 35 days, at lower end of 35-40 day guidance range
items.quote: Working capital was at 35 days at the lower end of our 35- to 40-day guidance range that we provide every quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin excluding large deals ~5.13%, similar to last year same quarter
items.quote: if we eliminate the large deal, I mean, on account of large deals. This moves up to about some 5.13%, very similar to what it was in the last year , similar in same quarter.

items.statement: TSG large deals exceeded INR3,800 crores, ~9% of group revenue
items.quote: Large deals exceeded INR3,800 crores and accounted for roughly 9% of the group's revenue.

items.statement: India distribution grew 67% YoY; Middle East grew 41% despite geopolitical uncertainty
items.quote: India continued to lead growth with the distribution business growing 67% year-on-year during the quarter, while the rest of the world excluding Arena grew 38%.

items.statement: PC and smartphone price increases 30-50% YoY driving revenue growth
items.quote: The price increases have been anywhere between 30% to 50%. Yes.

items.statement: TSG revenue up 91% to 20% of mix driven by AI servers/GPUs with 4x ASPs
items.quote: On the Technology Solutions Group, it was a standout performance this quarter. Revenue increased 91%, taking TSG to 20% of the consolidated mix.

items.statement: Large TSG deals almost entirely from neo-cloud operators
items.quote: It's almost all neo cloud.

items.statement: Receivable provisioning INR213 crores (INR67 cr SISA, INR135 cr Arena); inventory provisioning not material
items.quote: It's about INR213 crores, which includes about INR67 crores in SISA and in Arena about INR135 crores.

items.statement: Debt-equity at 0.5-0.6x; comfortable up to 0.6-0.8x globally; may raise capital if growth sustains
items.quote: See, the distribution business, which is working capital intensive, you tend to have normally debt equity of beyond 1:1. And this is what we will see across many constituents. But globally, it's on -- I mean it would be about 0.6x to 0.8x.

items.statement: Capital investment on funded portion for large deals almost nil; non-funded portion utilized
items.quote: Capital investment on the funded portion is almost nil. We only have a non-funded portion being utilized for the purpose of large deal.

items.statement: ROE 21.6%, net ROCE 22.7% (ex-Arena 24.4% and 28%)
items.quote: Return on equity improved to 21.6% and net ROCE to 22.7%. Excluding Arena, these measures are even stronger at 24.4% and 28%, respectively.

items.statement: Sustainable quarterly opex expected between INR950-1,000 crores
items.quote: We should track anywhere between INR950 crores to INR1,000 crores a quarter.

items.statement: Consumer PC volumes declining; commercial PC flat to low single-digit growth; smartphone consumer volumes declining
items.quote: We can definitely see the volumes, as I said, the consumer volumes are declining, the unit volume shipments, and we can also see activations in PCs, Microsoft activation data is negative 20%, 30%.

items.statement: H2 FY27 growth expected north of 25% YoY barring demand contraction from price hikes or West Asia crisis escalation
items.quote: But otherwise, Yes, you're right. There is no reason to disbelieve that will be north of 25%.

items.statement: Arena Turkey turnaround uncertain due to unpredictable market curve balls despite new leadership and exited high-interest business
items.quote: we really cannot estimate all the new curve balls that are coming up in the Turkey market. That's the challenge.

items.statement: SSG gross margin >6% and profitability above Redington average; orchestration model expected to improve margins structurally over 3-5 years
items.quote: Clearly, if you see SSG gross margin this quarter, it's higher than 6% and the profitability from the SSG business is also higher than the average PAT compared to the overall Redington average.

items.statement: Neo-cloud data center opportunity in India estimated at INR150,000 crores over next 4 years; distribution role in hardware sourcing and ecosystem orchestration
items.quote: We see we talked about the next 4 years as INR150,000 crores opportunity.

items.statement: Large deal margins below normal 4.5-5% run-rate but meet ROCE targets with minimal incremental opex
items.quote: Definitely margins are not as interesting as normal business unit run rate margins that we have between 4.5 and 5. But the ROCE, we have been clear about picking up deals and partnering, especially on the hardware side, there is a ROCE target we have.

items.statement: Q2 FCF negative INR1,871 crores due to high growth; H1 FCF positive INR583 crores; working capital days controlled but quantum rises with growth
items.quote: See, the free cash flow may not be a right metric when you see a growth rate of this nature in a working capital intensive business. So it is purely to do with higher growth, and that's the trade-off that's being chosen.

items.statement: AI PC adoption >40% in commercial segment vs ~10% in consumer; enterprise refresh cycle supporting commercial PC demand
items.quote: the adoption of AI PCs is more than 40% in the commercial PC segment and bought by enterprises, whereas the consumer is still hovering around 10%.

items.statement: India, GCCL, Africa to remain strong growth drivers in H2; UAE/KSA dependent on geopolitics; TSG and SSG strongest segment drivers; ESG/MSG cautious on price-volume elasticity
items.quote: I think India, GGCL and Africa will continue to be very strong growth drivers. We still see growth in UAE and KSA come back, it will depend on the geopolitical disruption.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR43,002 crores (+48% YoY); PAT ex-exceptional INR581 crores (+50% YoY); ex-Arena revenue +54%, PAT +55% to INR657 crores
items.quote: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR43,002 crores, up 48% year -on-year. Profit after tax, excluding exceptional items, rose 50% to INR581 crores.

items.statement: H1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR77,967 crores (+41% YoY); PAT ex-exceptional INR1,067 crores (+61% YoY) - highest ever first half
items.quote: For the first half of '27, consolidated revenue reached INR77,967 crores, a growth of 41% year-on-year, while profit after tax, excluding exceptional items reached INR1,067 crores, growing at 61%.

items.statement: Market share flat to slight gain across brands; no significant loss
items.quote: largely, we are flat to a slight gain in market share is what we think in our markets we are in, not a whol e lot. And -- but we have not lost market share

items.statement: Strait of Hormuz closure increasing supply chain TAT and inventory in Middle East
items.quote: Strait of Hormuz is closed, and we need to find alternate routes of receiving the material. So everything has increased the TAT of doing the business and that's one of the -- I mean key reasons why inventory is on the high side.

items.statement: Arena has totally new management team steering restructuring and Turkey-specific dollar-denominated growth
items.quote: Arena has a totally new management team in place who is now steering the company through.

items.statement: AI Exchange platform launched, engaging hundreds of partners and ISVs; early traction in small bits with good funnel; long journey to scale
items.quote: We are engaging hundreds of our partners with this, talking to their customers. And we've had many ISVs engage this model. This is a completely change of the go -to-market model. We are seeing traction in small bits and bites and a good funnel.

items.statement: Google now top-5 vendor for Redington driven by smartphone and cloud/office growth; cloud partnership expanding in India
items.quote: Google for us has two parts to it, has got a smartphone piece and it's got an office and cloud piece. So put together, it's grown very well for us.

items.statement: CloudQuarks 2.0 rolled out across Middle East, Africa; TrackMyCloud and Reonix adoption improving partner stickiness
items.quote: Our new CloudQuarks 2.0 has been rolled out to all of Middle East, Africa and Information Classification: RL\Public Cycle management tools, which is TrackMyCloud and Reonix has become -- has found better adoption by

items.statement: Five AI learning centers established in India over last 2 quarters under CSR program
items.quote: We also rolled out five AI learning centers over the last 2 quarters now in place in India, executed as part of our CSR program.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15% and EBITDA margin of 20% expected to be exceeded
items.quote: For FY27, guidance was revenue growth of 15% with an EBITDA margin of 20% . With pricing in our key APIs expected to remain stable in the near term and on the back of a strong first half and the outlook for the rest of the year, we now expect to exceed both.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 30% YoY to INR316 crores driven by higher volumes and improved price realization
items.quote: Revenue grew 30% year -on-year to INR316 crores. This was driven by higher volumes, improved price realization and continued growth across our product portfolio.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 gross margin 35%, EBITDA margin 21%, PAT margin ~13%
items.quote: Gross profit, including manufacturing expenses, rose 41% to INR111 crores and gross margin expanded to 35%. EBITDA stood at INR68 crores, a growth of 40% with margins expanding 145 basis points to 21%, aided by operating leverage. PAT grew 57% to INR39.6 crores, a PAT margin of approximately 13%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 22-24% for next year
items.quote: So I think it will be around 22% to 24%.

items.statement: INR280 crore capex program, INR160 crore deployed, INR120 crore remaining for H2 FY27
items.value: INR280 crores total, INR160 crores deployed
items.quote: we have deployed INR160 crores of the INR280 crores program so far and the program remains on track for completion by FY27.

items.statement: Peak debt (long-term and short-term) expected around INR400 crores by end of FY27
items.quote: So both put together will be around INR400 crores by end of this year.

items.statement: Ibuprofen utilization at 90-95%, capacity expanding to 9,600 tons/year in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: So right now, the utilization level is at 90% right now, 90% to 95%. So, we are at full -- we are running at full capacity right now. Again, at the same time, we are doing another -- we are still continuing our existing capex to improve capacity further to 9,600 metric tons.

items.statement: Peptide pilot production targeted Q4 FY27, first CRO revenue Q2 FY28
items.value: pilot Q4 FY27, revenue Q2 FY28
items.quote: Pilot scale production is targeted for Q4 FY27 and we expect our first CRO revenue from it in Q2 FY28.

items.statement: 6-8 new molecules expected to start commercial production in FY28
items.quote: As a result of these APIs, we now expect 6 to 8 new molecules to sta rt commercial production in FY28.

items.statement: High-value APIs share increased to 49% in H1 FY27 from 47% in FY26
items.quote: Across the portfolio, high-value APIs continue to climb as a share of our revenue to 49% in the first half from 47% in FY26.

items.statement: Ibuprofen contribution to be kept below 30-35% of revenue
items.quote: So even with our increased capacity of ibuprofen, we think it will be below 30% or around that 30 %-35%. We will not -- we will make sure that, you know, it's not a single product company.

items.statement: Raw material price pressure expected to continue for 1-2 quarters
items.quote: Yes, there is pressure on the raw material prices, but also the global scenario. I mean, we've also increased our raw material prices. I think it will continue for the next 1 to 2 quarters, I believe.

items.statement: Ibuprofen EBITDA margins in teens, derivatives have much higher margins but lower volumes
items.quote: But definitely I think our EBITDA margins are in the teens. That much we can tell you on this particular product. And with respect to other products, we have a few other derivatives of ibuprofen , we have multiple salts of ibuprofen, everything that's available in the market. We are currently already validated in CEPs and DMFs already filed. And definitely margins on those are much, much higher co

items.statement: Board approved INR50 crore loan to SMS Peptides subsidiary
items.quote: To support its expansion, the Board recently approved a loan of INR50 crores to the subsidiary.

items.statement: R&D completed 19 DMF/CEP filings in last 24 months, 6 in H1 FY27, target 10 for FY27
items.quote: our team has over 200 professionals and has completed 19 DMF and CEP filings over the last 24 months. We continued that momentum into this quarter. So far we have completed 6 filings, 4 in the first half and 2 more in October, well on track for our FY27 target of 10.

items.statement: Asset turnover excluding CWIP is 1.72x, target 1.75x in 2-3 years
items.quote: Yes, the current fixed asset turnover excluding capital work -in-progress is 1.72. We definitely expect an improvement on that going forward.

items.statement: Peptide team has ~30 PhD chemists, recruiting ongoing, dedicated CEO for peptides
items.quote: Right now, we have around 30 chemists, most of them are PhDs. And definitely, I think there is a recruiting process still ongoing because also considering the fact that we just started our R&D a few months back. So the recruiting process is still ongoing. Again, it's fairly new. But again, we have a CEO for peptides, dedicated CEO for peptides and there is a different team and division that is wor

items.statement: Ibuprofen pricing is cyclical with up and down phases, shortages and overcapacity periods
items.quote: typically, see, for these commodity products, it's always cyclical. There will be a time in a year when you can -- the margins will really go up, but the remaining time, the margins will be slightly lower. But it's a cyclical product, and it goes through many phases. It's been since many years, right, the product in the market. So it goes through multiple phases. There will be up phases, there wil

items.statement: FY27 hospital EBITDA margin expected flattish around 22% post-ESOP; no FY28 margin guidance given due to drug price cap uncertainty
items.quote: So, we expect end of the current financial year, the EBITDA margin should be flattish, and future financial year, we would not like to comment on the margin in the present circumstances.

items.statement: Diagnostics FY27 revenue growth outlook 12-13%; expects mid-teens growth in few quarters then back to industry growth
items.quote: See, our FY '27 growth expectation remains in the 12% to 13% range as of now. We believe the impact of brand transition is largely behind us, and we expect growth to strengthen further as awareness is improving.

items.statement: Committed capex of INR 3,500 crore over next 3-3.5 years for 2,000 beds (brownfield expansions and completed acquisitions); greenfield projects additional
items.quote: As regards your other question on committed CAPEX, it is roughly around INR 3,500 crore, and it is spread over next, say, 3-3.5 years' time.

items.statement: Targeting ~600 bed additions in FY27 (100 from Suguna acquisition, rest brownfield); 200 beds/year for next 2 years from brownfield; major brownfield completions at Mohali and Shalimar Bagh by FY30
items.quote: This year we are targeting to achieve , add around 500 plus beds, plus there is one acquisition which Dr. Raghuvanshi has just mentioned about Suguna in Bangalore. With that, we will be adding around 600 beds in the current financial year itself.

items.statement: Bangalore cluster at ~1,000 beds after Suguna acquisition (110 beds, expandable to 150); 8 facilities total; further brownfield expansions at Yeshwanthpur, Suguna (+50 beds), BG Road
items.quote: Recently, we completed the acquisition of the 110 -bedded Suguna Hospital in Bangalore, taking our hospital bed capacity in the r egion to approximately 1,000 beds.

items.statement: Greenfield 400-bed super specialty hospital in Ashok Vihar, Delhi NCR via long-term services agreement with Seth Sunder Lal Jain Charitable Eye Hospital Society; completion in ~4 years
items.quote: In addition, we entered into a long -term healthcare services agreement for a 400 -bedded greenfield super specialty hospital to be developed in Ashok Vihar, New Delhi, by Seth Sunder Lal Jain Charitable Eye Hospital Society.

items.statement: Hospital occupied beds up 9% YoY to 3,616 in Q2 FY27; occupancy improved to 72% from 71%
items.quote: Occupancy improved to 72% in Q2 compared to 71% in the corresponding quarter last year. The number of occupied beds increased by 9% to 3,616 from 3,318 in Q2 of Financial Year '26.

items.statement: Consolidated operating EBITDA pre-ESOP margin 24.2% in Q2 FY27 vs 23.9% YoY; Hospital 23.3% vs 22.9%; Diagnostics 26.2% vs 26.1%
items.quote: Our consolidated operating EBITDA pre -ESOP expense grew by 19.2% over Q2 of Financial Year '26 to INR 663 crores, with operating EBITDA margins improving to 24.2% in Q 2 of Financial Year '27 from 23.9% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: ARPP grew 6.8% YoY to INR 2.1 lakh; driven mainly by case mix (complex cases, robotic surgeries); price increase contribution ~1.5 percentage points
items.quote: ARPP also grew by 6.8% to INR 2.1 lakh compared to INR 1.96 lakh in Q2 of Financial Year '26.

items.statement: Drug price cap on 137 oncology drugs (effective Nov) will negatively impact profitability; drugs ~1/3 of oncology revenue; exact impact being assessed
items.quote: Of course, it will be a negative impact on the profitability. The drugs generally contribute around one-third of the oncology revenue, and not all drugs are part of this, and there are certain packages also.

items.statement: Hospital key specialties growth: renal sciences 27%, neuro sciences 28%, orthopedics 30% YoY in Q2
items.quote: During the quarter, our key specialties, including renal sciences, neuro sciences, and orthopedics recorded a year -on-year revenue growth of 27%, 28%, and 30%, respectively.

items.statement: Diagnostics wellness revenue +28% YoY, specialized testing +14%; wellness contribution 15% vs 13% YoY; B2C revenue mix 54% vs 52%
items.quote: Within the portfolio, revenue from wellness and specialized testing in Q2 Financial Year '27 grew by 28% and 14%, respectively, compared to the corresponding previous period last year.

items.statement: International patient revenue +12.4% YoY to INR 190 crore (8% of hospital revenue); digital channel revenue +18.6% YoY (29.5% of hospital revenue)
items.quote: Our revenue from international business grew 12.4% compared to Q2 of Financial Year '26 to reach INR 190 crores and contributed approximately 8% to the overall revenues in Q2 Financial Year '27.

items.statement: Diagnostics patient volume +5.8% YoY, +9.9% QoQ; tests processed +7.2% YoY to 11.39 million; ~300 gross touch points added in Q2
items.quote: During the quarter, patient volume grew by 5.8% year -on-year and 9.9% quarter -on-quarter, demonstrating the strength of our network, brand, and customer engagement initiatives.

items.statement: Evaluating strategic M&A in Mumbai, Kolkata, Hyderabad including build-to-suit sale/lease models; also exploring Tier 2 city opportunities
items.quote: In addition to the above, it would also be pertinent to highlight that we are also making ve ry good progress in our other focus clusters such as Mumbai, Kolkata, and Hyderabad, evaluating strategic M&A opportunities including build -to-suit sale and build -to-suit lease models.

items.statement: Net debt INR 2,188 crore; net debt/EBITDA 0.87x (Sep 2026) vs 0.96x (Sep 2025); can repay in 2 years at steady state but may fluctuate with acquisitions
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, the company's net debt stands at INR 2,188 crore, with a healthy net debt-to-EBITDA of 0.87x as on September 30, 2026, as against 0.96x on September 30, 2025.

items.statement: IHH can increase stake above 50% (no legal constraint); could provide INR 10,000 crore over time at current market price; will approach when Fortis needs fresh capital
items.quote: Having said that, our parent IHH has expressed very openly that it wants to increase its stake to above 50%. At the current market price, this could provide us with additional capital of INR 10,000 crore over time.

items.statement: Added ~300 doctors in Q2 across network (new hospitals, capacity expansions, FMRI); hired in head & neck, rheumatology, neurology; no major attrition at FMRI
items.quote: Yes. So, we continuously try to keep on engaging more and more clinicians for our network. Some of the hiring has happened in the new hospitals which we have acquired.

items.statement: Forensic audit ordered by court underway; auditors appointed and information submitted; court indicated 6-month timeline; company awaiting completion
items.quote: Yes. So, as far as the forensic audit is concerned, the auditors have been appointed, as you are aware, and they have sent their requisition of our information to us. We have submitted the necessary information to them.

items.statement: Hospital IP volume growth 13% YoY in Q2; 15 facilities with EBITDA margin >20% (84% of revenue) vs 13 facilities (76%) in FY26
items.quote: So, volume growth in IP is around 13%, compared with the corresponding quarter previous year.

items.statement: Diagnostics H1 FY27: 21.85 million tests (+5.3% YoY); 500+ gross touch points added; B2C:B2B revenue mix 53:47 vs 52:48
items.quote: For the first half of FY '27, we conducted 21.85 million tests compared to 20.75 million tests in H1 FY '26, representing a growth of 5.3%.

items.statement: Drug price cap on oncology drugs creates near-term margin uncertainty; regulatory environment has "lot of noise"; industry expected to adapt over time
items.quote: there are a lot of noise going around about this industry, about the drug caps and other things. And a circular has been issued which will be effective in November, an d we are expecting some more turmoil may be

items.statement: Suguna Hospital total investment ~INR 410 crore (INR 270 crore acquisition + INR 140 crore expansion/renovation); expected to reach ~25% EBITDA margin over time, ARPOB ~INR 2 crore/bed
items.quote: Then we are planning to expand it by another 40 beds over time, plus the renovation of this facility to bring it at Fortis standard. All put together, it will be another INR 140-odd crore number.

items.statement: Internal IRR hurdle 15% and payback 8-10 years for acquisitions; sometimes overridden for strategic reasons
items.quote: Yes, we have an internal benchmark which has been approved by our Board. So, generally, we don't touch any project, with an IRR below 15% and a payback of exceeding 8 to 10 years.

items.statement: FMRI new block ready, awaiting final approvals (expected within month); Manesar radiation oncology commissioning by Feb (Q4); Manesar EBITDA low double-digits positive
items.quote: We are likely to receive those approvals within this month. All the final inspections, etc., have happened, and hopefully we should be able to commiss ion all those hospital beds pretty soon.

items.statement: Punjab cluster capacity constrained (occupancy >70-75%); 500+ bed brownfield expansion at Amritsar and Mohali underway
items.quote: The cluster you have particularly pointed out about Punjab, there we are actually facing a capacity constraint. As I mentioned in the earlier question, there is a big expansion going on in two of our big units, Amritsar, as well as in Mohali, which are underway.

items.statement: Gleneagles O&M (Hyderabad, Chennai) first year focused on stabilization; operations flat; improvement expected from next year
items.quote: I think next year onward we should be seeing some improvement in the operation. Right now operations are almost flat. There has not been much improvement in the operations in the O&M.

items.statement: Bangalore Bannerghatta hospital occupancy ~58% but improving; People Tree (Yeshwanthpur) and TMI in ramp-up; cluster occupancy lower but profitability good
items.quote: There is a big hospital at Bannerghatta Road which is operating at occupancy level around 58%, although occupancy level has gone up from the earlier one.

items.statement: Generating decent cash flow to support committed capex and further acquisitions through internal accruals; balance sheet well capitalized
items.quote: We are generating decent cash flow to support this type of CAPEX, plus there will be room for further acquisitions through internal accruals.

items.statement: Supreme Court clarified IHH can increase stake above 50% (no constraint); forensic audit only covers ex-promoter share dissipation period
items.quote: So, there is no constraint in IHH increasing its stake because that has been clarified right at the Supreme Court when the earlier decision came in FY'23.

name: Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd

items.quote: The guidance, as what we have said last year, was ₹37,000 crore, and we are moving up, and then we should be able to catch up with about ₹40,000 crore. So, ₹37,000 crore to ₹40,000 crore is the CapEx what we are looking at. And the capitalization guidance would be about ₹25,000 crore to ₹30,000 crore.

items.statement: Capex expected to continue well beyond ₹40,000 crore in FY28 and FY29 driven by order book and land compensation costs
items.quote: With the initial expenditures on the projects and all, they are very good, and the CapEx would be continuing to be in the range much beyond ₹40,000 Crore. It should continue to be.

items.statement: H1 FY27 execution: 2,616 ckm transmission lines and 25,100 MVA transformation capacity commissioned; two full TBCB SPV projects completed

items.statement: Consolidated PAT grew 8% YoY in Q2 FY27; operating income grew 7.7% but regulatory tariff trajectory reduced effective growth to ~3%

On the operating income, ₹887 crore on the operating income is the plus, that is more than 7%; 7.7% is the growth on the operating front for transmission.

items.statement: Receivable days reduced to 10.54 days; outstanding dues >45 days down significantly
items.quote: Robust collections revenue: We are very pleased to inform you that the billing and the realization is always one of the finest what we have been doing. The number of outstanding dues is also… more than 45 days has come down significantly. And the receivable dues, as you see from the graph, stands about 10.54 days.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio 59:41 (1:1.5); tied up JBIC green loan ¥80 billion, SBI ₹10,000 crore, UBI ₹5,000 crore, bonds ₹2,000 crore
items.quote: The gross fixed assets as on date about ₹2.8 lakh crore standalone and consolidated ₹3.29 lakh crore. The debt-equity is 59.41, which is having enough room for us to actually work upon the massive projects pipeline which we are envisaging, 1:1.5%.

items.statement: Raised JBIC green loan ¥80 billion, SBI term loan ₹10,000 crore, UBI ₹5,000 crore, bonds ₹2,000 crore; more funding in pipeline

items.quote: There is a definitive price variation formula, which is based upon certain indices which are predetermined. So, the movement of the indices, the quantum of that particular material and that equipment, the weightage which is given to it, that is the one which will dictate the price, the one which is already finalized or agreed upon. So, it may move up or down, but we have to accommodate or properly

items.statement: Land compensation guidelines notified by Centre; states adopting market-based rates; process digitized by POWERGRID
items.quote: The Ministry has come up with the guidelines for providing compensation to the landowners. This was the way how we had to go forward, which was the ask also by everyone. items.statement: Crude-related cost increases balanced by currency depreciation in Q2 FY27

items.statement: IT services hiring remains cautious, mostly replacement hiring; AI/ML, data engineering, cloud, DevOps, cybersecurity, SAP and composite skills drive demand
items.quote: Hiring across the IT service s companies in the last quarter has still stayed cautious. Most of it has been replacement hiring rather than new roles. However, the roles that have been hired were more skilled and of higher value

items.statement: Over 16,000 open positions at end of Q2 FY27 with healthy pipeline
items.quote: Looking ahead over the next three to six months, we enter Q3 with t he festive deployment in hand and a longer season behind it, over 16,000 open posit ions, and a healthy

items.quote: We are doing a lot of AI hiring, data engineering hiring, so they come at a higher value a nd a higher rate card, which is where our PAPM has gone up by 10

items.quote: To enable this, we are investing in sales productiv ity, hiring, AI and digital capability, our brand, and leadership depth. Our core team has grown to about 2,790 from about 2,500 in March

items.quote: Second, we divested our 30% stake in Crystal HR under the put option. We recovered our full original investment with no loss on capital invested.

items.quote: We are evaluatin g opportunities for M&A and have nothing at advanced level to disclose today. Anything material will be disclosed to the exchanges as and when required

items.quote: Yes, start with our tonnage for this quarter is 265,000 tons, and it is grown year -on-year basis 7.5% on volume side.

items.quote: Our strategy is always to keep high with the SMEs, but yes, in this quarter we also maintained 50/50, where 50% business is coming from the SME customer and 50% from the like to be build big customers.

items.quote: We created almost, I think, in 20 cities, which is really having more volumes on these cities. We already created that segment, and that is giving a good traction from the customer and resulting this good revenues coming.

items.quote: Many of the cases we have already taken up with our customers, and customers are evaluating that. items.quote: It was a year back that we have already entered into Honda business on the electronic LCD clusters and we have been continuously growing Honda business. items.quote: I think market share, definitely we have not lost. And we have gained some market share because of the new product, whatever we have launched during Q2, both on the driver information system and also on the plastics and also on the ACFMS.

items.quote: The second is coming from various export customers. As we mentioned in the previous earning call, Caterpillar is one of our largest customers in the U.S. where we export to the larger water pumps.

items.statement: Target loan book of INR 2 lakh crore by end of FY27 and INR 3 lakh crore by 2030

items.quote: We are targeting that during this year, this financial year, we will be around INR 2 lakh crores loan book. By 2030, we had given an initial guidance two years back that we will be achieving around INR3 lakh crores loan book.

items.quote: Regarding ROA, we are trying to maintain between 2% - 2.2%, and definitely we will be maintaining that kind of ROA.

items.quote: If you see, without this EBR of 20,000, presently also our spread is 1.96%, which is just around 2%, and our net interest margin is 2.93.

items.statement: No special dividend planned; cash corpus reserved for product development and capital investment toward INR1,000 crore target

items.quote: Secondly, finance cost is not increased, we are debt-free company till now.

items.quote: So, I think ballpark, I would say that around 85-15 would be the mix. 85% to 90% is domestic, 10% to 15% is imported. A majority of the roller press rolls raw materials are imported because these are heavy forgings and castings which are not made in India.

items.quote: I believe this year, we may realize INR3,000 per CBM as EBITDA. Mind you, earlier, we were talking about INR3,000 as per CBM for revenue. This may very well be the EBITDA realization from this year.

items.statement: LPG distribution EBITDA per ton at shade above INR7,000 in Q2 FY27, demonstrating structural cost efficiency gains from supply chain investments
items.quote: In fact, EBITDA per ton in distribution is a shade about INR7,000 in the current quarter Q2, which is you can regard as a normal quarter. So we have achieved INR7,000 plus.

items.statement: Aegis Vopak EBITDA margins expanded to 78.6% in Q2 FY27 from 74.7% year-on-year, improvement of approximately 372 basis points
items.quote: EBITDA also grew by 22.4% to INR212 crores compared with INR173 crores in the Q2 of FY26 with EBITDA margins also expanding to 78.6% from 74.7%, an improvement of approximately 372 basis points.

items.statement: Hold more than 30% of India's LPG static storage capacity across 6 terminals, with total capacity reaching ~29 million tons when JNPA commissioned
items.quote: So we hold more than 30% of the static capacity of LPG in the country.

items.statement: Aegis Vopak throughput for Q2 FY27 was 1.1 million tons
items.quote: That is 1.1 million tons.

items.statement: Passed resolution in EGM for funding of INR6,000 crores, with INR6,400 crores cash available on September balance sheet for Tristar acquisition
items.quote: So we have already passed a resolution in Extraordinary General Meeting to do a funding of INR6,000 crores. We have, if you see my September balance sheet, already INR6,400 crores available cash.

items.statement: Targeting gearing of no more than 0.6x for Aegis Vopak capex, with $2 billion equity requirement to be met through IPO proceeds and internal accruals
items.quote: We will pursue this growth with disciplined funding through a balanced mix of equity, internal accruals and debt, targeting a gearing of no more than 0.6x.

items.statement: Ammonia terminal enables vertical integration - sourcing, storage and distribution with distribution margin similar to LPG at INR7,000 per metric ton and storage charges ~INR2,750 per metric ton
items.quote: So this is what it brings to you. So, if you get around INR10,000 a metric ton and you have built a terminal capable to do 1 million tons, even if you Aegis Logistics & start at 25% capacity utilization as you begin, you have a huge payback because your cost is so low

items.statement: Tristar acquisition subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions, expected completion in Q4 FY27
items.quote: Subject to regulatory approvals and the customary closing conditions, we expect to complete this transaction in Q4 of FY27.

items.statement: Management constrained from discussing Tristar integration details and synergies until transaction completes in next few months
items.quote: We really are constrained to talk much on a transaction that has still not been completed. So pardon our constraint because we cannot really step out and put everything right across.

items.statement: Tristar management to remain in place post-acquisition, no management changes expected ensuring operational continuity
items.quote: We don't expect to change the management and the continuity will ensure that there is no disturbance in the operations and performance of the company.

items.statement: Tristar acquisition brings global operations headquartered in Dubai with international network, diversified service offerings and established global customer relationships
items.quote: Tristar is an integrated energy logistics company headquartered in Dubai, but with global operations.

items.statement: Aegis Logistics has INR6,400 crores free cash on September balance sheet, acquisition funding matches available cash without stretching balance sheet
items.quote: We have, if you see my September balance sheet, already INR6,400 crores available cash. So we are good. We don't need to stretch. We don't need to take crazy debt for the acquisition.

items.statement: 15-year take-or-pay agreement with Hindustan Zinc for ammonia terminal at Pipavav provides long-term revenue visibility and predictable cash flows
items.quote: We have signed a 15-year take-or-pay agreement with Hindustan Zinc, which gives us long-term revenue visibility and predictable cash flows and reinforces the commercial case for this investment.

items.statement: LPG distribution margin of INR7,000 per ton achieved through procurement efficiencies, large capacity terminals, VLGC-compliant jetties, and supply chain optimization, not price leadership
items.quote: What has happened is that over the last 1.5 years, we have improved our cost efficiency by having larger capacities where we can unload from largest of the ships.

items.statement: Welcome new LPG infrastructure investments in India (Petronet LNG, IOCL, BPCL, JSW) as country has only ~1 million metric tons static storage vs ideal 90-day requirement
items.quote: Infrastructure is always welcome. India is short on infrastructure. We have around 1 million metric tons of static storage capacity as far as I know in India. That is not even equivalent to 10-day storage.

items.statement: Second half of FY27 promises to be as good as or better than first half, with general tendency for stronger second half performance
items.quote: Otherwise, what I'd like to leave everybody with the message is that I think we've had an amazing first half of the year. The second half of the year promises to be as good, if not better.

items.statement: Revenue ambition of INR900-1,000 crores by FY30
items.quote: Our longer -term roadmap outlines a revenue ambition is INR900 crores to INR1,000 crore s by FY30, supported by geographical expansion, larger project opportunities, and growth in our operational business.

items.statement: Total work order book INR806.80 crores, unexecuted INR473.86 crores as of November 2026
items.quote: As of November 2026, our total work order book stood at INR806.80 crores, with an unexecuted order book of INR473.86 crores.

items.statement: Expecting INR100 crores orders by December and another INR100 crores by March 2027
items.quote: We are expecting at least INR100 crores in jobs by December. We will add another INR100 crores in jobs by March 2027.

items.statement: Bidded for approximately INR500 crores jobs, planning to bid another INR500 crores
items.quote: We have bidded for approximately INR500 crore jobs. We are expecting at least INR100 crores in jobs by December. We will add another INR100 crores in jobs by March 2027. So, for that, we are planning to bid another INR500 crores in jobs.

items.statement: Planning to add INR200 crores to order book this year, INR1,000 crores next year
items.quote: This year I am planning to add only INR200 crores. Next year definitely I will increase my book by INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Will raise debt and structured debt from market for future expansion beyond INR200 crores order book addition
items.quote: for further future expansion, since our order book is already expanded this year, so we will raise debt from the market. We are also thinking of structured debt from the market, and we will execute projects through our expansion, through our project cash

items.statement: 90% revenue from PSU/government customers, repeat order rate ~70%, in advanced talks with GFL, Chatterjee International, BCPL for private orders
items.quote: Importantly, approximately 90% of our rev enue comes from PSU and government customers, while our repeat order rate stands around 70%.

items.statement: Advanced discussions with GFL for 5 new plants in Gujarat/UP, Chatterjee International for southern expansion, BCPL for INR11,000 crores fertilizer expansion in Assam
items.quote: I am talking with GFL as well as Chatterjee International. For GFL, they are coming with 5 new plants in Gujarat and UP. GFL is a listed company. They are planning to expand because of this LiB expansion lithium-ion battery. So, they are planning to set up their electrolyzer plant in India. So, they are coming with 5 plants and we are in advanced discussions with them to get some jobs from there b

items.statement: EBITDA grew 10.29% to INR13.60 crores, PAT declined 1.71% to INR6.25 crores due to higher finance cost and WIP timing
items.quote: Our EBITDA grew 10.29% to INR13.60 crores compared with INR12.33 crores in the corresponding period last year. Profit after tax stood at INR6.25 crores compared with INR6.36 crores in H1 FY26, representing a marginal decline of 1.71%.

items.statement: Minor EBITDA margin drop ~0.1% due to WIP pause, upfront mobilization and higher finance cost impacting PAT
items.quote: Ma’am, i t is a minor drop around 0.1% or something. So, it is bec ause of operational performance. Right now, we have -- you see there is a UWIP in our book, so that is going to be taken second place in the month of February or March. That time the profitability can be booked. So right now, the WIP is on pause

items.statement: Negative operating cash flow (H1: -INR5.69 crores) due to seasonal revenue recognition in Feb-Mar, high inventory and vendor advances, receivables 90% from PSUs
items.quote: If you see, H1 is minus 5.69. It is because of inventory and short -term advances which we used to give to mechanical and other creditors, because for mechanical procurement and some electrical procurement we have to give advances to the vendors. Because of that, short-term advances are high.

items.statement: Positive cash generation expected in 1-2 years once stable sales achieved
items.quote: Cash collection is also on time, but cash operations will take more than a year or two to show a positive value once we are properly on stable sales.

items.statement: Only 8-9 players in sub-INR300 crores oil/gas/fertilizer projects; larger projects have 3-4 players (Kalpataru, L&T, KEC)
items.quote: If you go for more than INR300 crores or INR400 crores jobs, then you will find only Kalpataru, L&T, might be KEC in some cases. So, they are competing with us, 3 or 4 players. In below INR300 crores jobs, there are 8 to 9 players in the market only.

items.statement: India refining capacity 267.12 MMTPA (Apr 2026), projected 309.5 MMTPA by 2030; government investing INR84,390 crores in deep-sea exploration, INR23,770 crores in biogas
items.quote: The country's installed refining capacity stood at 267.12 MMTPA as of April 2026, with government projections indicating an increase to 309.5 MMTPA by 2030. Additionally, expansion in natural gas transmission networks and city gas distribution infrastructure is expected to create opportunities across pipeline construction, processing facilities, and maintenance services.

items.statement: Government allocated INR84,390 crores for Samudra Manthan deep-sea exploration and INR23,770 crores for biogas production; storage expansion expected in next budget
items.quote: One is the expansion of Samudra Manthan, an investment INR84,390 crores in the expansion of acreage, land, and water acreage in sea areas. So, they are going for deep -sea exploration activity, so the government is giving INR84,390 crore s in that activity. As well as the government has given INR23,770 crores in biogas production.

items.statement: Transitioning from regional specialist to PAN India platform; strengthening presence in Western India (Gujarat, MP, UP) during FY26-FY28
items.quote: During FY26 to FY28, we intend to strengthen our presence in Western India, particularly Gujarat, MP, and UP, while expanding our capabilities to undertake larger and more complex projects.

items.statement: Bidded for INR150 crores water supply project in Agartala, two ONGC projects (cathodic protection, firefighting), tracking INR100 crores ONGC tenders, IGDL second phase pipeline, ONGC RTP 500km pipeline
items.quote: So, ma'am, right now we have currently bidded in one, for water supply improvement works in Agartala, Tripura only. It is around approximately INR150 crores that we have bidded for. And 2 projects we have bidded in ONGC. One is for cathodic protection systems and another is for firefighting systems, bot h in ONGC, in different places. One is in Gujarat and another is in Andhra Pradesh right

items.statement: Working capital managed through reserves, surplus, project cash flows; will raise debt for expansion beyond INR200 crores order book addition
items.quote: For working capital presently, whatever debt we raised and equity we raised from the market, we have reserves and surplus. And for present execution of projects, we have working capital with us and from the present cash flow from the projects. And for further future expansion, since our order book is already expanded this year, so we will raise debt from the market.

items.statement: Strategic targets subject to project awards, execution progress, and market conditions
items.quote: These remain strategic targets subject to project awards, execution progress, and market conditions.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 20-22% for FY27
items.quote: So we earlier gave the guideline of around 20% to 22% in the growth of the top line, and we will stick to that guideline only.

items.statement: H1 FY27 gross margin expanded 405 bps to 30.2%, EBITDA margin up 240 bps to 17.7%, PAT margin up 178 bps to 11.5%
items.quote: Gross margin expanded by 405 basis points to 30.2%. EBITDA rose 40.1% to INR 32.34 crore, and the EBITDA margin improved by 240 basis points to 17.7%. Profit after tax grew 43.3% to INR 21.09 crore, with the PAT margin rising by 178 basis points to 11.5%.

items.statement: Ink and paper now 56.2% of revenue vs 48.7% year ago; recurring consumables largest revenue segment with better margins than machines
items.quote: In H1 FY '27, ink and paper contributed 56.2% of our revenue, which is up from 48.7% a year ago. Recurring revenue is now the largest part of our business, and it carries better margin than the machine sale.

items.statement: Operating cash flow turned positive INR 27.16 crore vs outflow INR 10.90 crore; trade receivables stable at INR 116.03 crore despite 20%+ revenue growth; payment cycle 90-120 days
items.quote: We generated operating cash flow of INR 27.16 crore in H1 FY '27 against an outflow of INR 10.90 crore in the same period last year. Trade receivables were broadly stable at INR 116.03 crore, even at revenue grew by more than 20%.

items.statement: Cash and bank balance rose to INR 21.64 crore at end September from INR 1.27 crore in March
items.quote: Cash and bank balance stood at INR 21.64 crore at the end of September, up from INR 1.27 crore in March.

items.statement: 50/50 JV with Swastik Strategic Ventures LLP to form True Colors Advanced Materials Private Limited for integrated coated media manufacturing from pulp
items.quote: We have entered into 50/50 joint venture with Swastik Strategic Ventures LLP to establish an integrated manufacturing platform for specialized lower GSM-coated media that is used into digital printing. The new company will be called True Colors Advanced Materials Private Limited.

items.statement: No restriction on funding routes; may use internal accruals, project debt, JV capital, and equity if it creates long-term shareholder value
items.quote: So, currently what we are looking is at the opportunity that is in front of us as a pool at the company level. So, eventually the mix could include internal accrual, project-level debt, strategic JV capital that what we did, and if it creates a long-term shareholder value, then equity, yes.

items.statement: India imports 70-75% of sublimation paper; base paper availability limited to 32-34 GSM vs China's 29 GSM; INKIA ink formulation capability developed over 3-4 years R&D
items.quote: China, is supplying around 29 GSM coated paper, and if you see the volume, then it is somewhere around 70% to 75% of the paper that India needs is being imported. So technology constraint is there, supply constraint is there, base paper availability is an issue to make the ultra-low GSM specialized paper which can withhold the coating chemistry is the challenge right now across the industry.

items.statement: INKIA ink formulation capability difficult to replicate due to particle size, chemistry parameters, and application knowledge; not easy for new entrants to produce digital textile printing ink
items.quote: So, answer to your question in a simple word, it is not easy, first of all to, produce the ink for the digital textile printing application or digital printing application. Second thing, now once you have the ink, you must have the knowledge of application as well, right? Because when you are applying to the different media, how the media will react is not only dependent on the type of the ink, it

items.statement: Ink revenue lagged volume growth due to global price correction; ink prices coming down globally as volumes rise
items.quote: So it is basically due to the global price correction into the ink prices. So globally price are coming down for the ink as the volume is rising.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by higher consumable mix; machine business has thin margins (~5% gross) while consumables drive profitability
items.quote: So the whatever margin that you are seeing now, it is because of the product mix. So once the consumable business goes up, every time you will see the margin in this direction.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin range historically 14-18%; currently around 17%
items.quote: So, at the consolidated level, if we see, we have reported this time the margin around 17%, but last year, when we put the margin number of around 15% EBITDA margin, so broadly, it is a range that is around, let's say, 14%-15% to let's say up to 18%, and in that range we get the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Paper JV capacity 8-10 crore meters/year integrated plant from pulp to coated sublimation paper; 25% capital subsidy under Viksit Gujarat policy
items.quote: So, number one is, it is a total coated paper capacity. It is starting from the pulp. Pulp works as the raw material. It makes the base paper and coat it on the same line. So it is more towards the integrated plant, which can produce the sublimation paper around 8 to 10 crore meters.

items.statement: Ink manufacturing plant getting 35% capital subsidy under Viksit Gujarat policy
items.quote: And in our ink manufacturing plant, it is 35% of the capital subsidy is there.

items.statement: Ink capacity expanding from 80 tons/month (INKIA) to 150 tons/month new facility by FY27 end; target 250-500 tons/month longer term
items.quote: So currently what we are manufacturing is through INKIA Inks Private Limited, which merger is being proposed and accepted by BSE, and it is under the NCLT process. So, once the merger is being happened, that 80 tons of capacity will be added into True Colors along with the new facility that we are putting of 150 tons.

items.statement: Paper coating capacity expanded from 1 crore to 2 crore meters/month in FY26; JV targets 8-10 crore meters/year
items.quote: We moved from 15 lakh meter to 30 lakh, then we extended to 1 crore meter, and currently we are producing 2 crore meter paper.

items.statement: Installed base ~956 machines with ~50 crore meters annual capacity at 100% utilization; current ecosystem paper requirement ~22-25 crore meters/year
items.quote: Currently, if you see, the number of machines that we have installed having the capacity of, let's say, around 50 crore meter, it can print at the 100% efficiency, for example.

items.statement: Machine mix 70-75% sublimation, 25-30% reactive; may shift to 60-40 over 4-5 years as viscose/cotton printing grows
items.quote: So currently, if you see, it is 70-75% is the sublimation, 25-30% is the reactive. And over the years, people are expanding in both the direction.

items.statement: Global digital textile printing volumes rising; India printing ~230-240 crore meters annually, targeting 500 crore meters in coming years
items.quote: And if India is moving in the direction from right now currently printing around 230-240 crore meter annually to, let's say, 500 crore meter in next few years, then the requirement will still be import dependent because we don't have the manufacturing capability.

items.statement: Receivables ~116 days due to Q2 volume concentration; payment cycle 90-120 days; exploring bill discounting, channel financing, distribution model
items.quote: The one thing that I would also like to mention is Quarter 2 is a much larger volume compared to Quarter 1. So that is why if we the number is still like 116, because majority of the business that we have generated is Quarter 2.

items.statement: INKIA merger approved by BSE, under NCLT process; valued at Rs 60 crore (15x PAT of Rs 4 crore) at Rs 240/share; will consolidate from April 2026
items.quote: So at that time considering the projected PAT numbers that was achieved into last financial year, around Rs. 4 crore PAT was achieved in last financial year at the revenue of Rs. 24 crore. And based on that PAT, it was given a multiplication of 15 and, valued at Rs. 60 crore at the share price of Rs. 240.

items.statement: INKIA was 50% owned by 4 directors individually, 50% by partners; merger involves promoter entities
items.quote: So currently what we are manufacturing is through INKIA Inks Private Limited, which merger is being proposed and accepted by BSE, and it is under the NCLT process.

items.statement: Global export opportunity for ink and paper as alternative to China; participating in exhibitions in Brazil, USA, UAE; margins potentially better in exports
items.quote: Like if you see our last year journey, we have put so many remarks by participating into exhibition into Brazil. We are participating into America. We have participated in exhibition into UAE and some of the other countries as well.

items.statement: Paper JV equity Rs 40 crore (50-50); open to internal accruals, bank debt, or equity raise depending on timing
items.quote: So as I mentioned now that can be done through the internal accrual right now, that can be done through the bank debt. And so, we are also open in the direction of the equity as well.

items.statement: Ink consumption averaging 115 tons/month over last 6 months; peak demand 140-150 tons/month
items.quote: If you see the averaging consumption in last 6 months, we have reported is 115 tons.

items.statement: INKIA produced ~80 tons/month; 35-40% supplied to True Colors ecosystem, rest to other distributors
items.quote: So generally, if we see last year total INKIA's production, almost 35% to 40% of ink was being used into True Colors' ecosystem and rest of the ink was supplied to the other distributor in India.

items.statement: Viksit Gujarat policy declared 2026 provides 25% capex subsidy for paper plant, 35% for ink plant
items.quote: Yes, so this CapEx is under Viksit Gujarat policy, which has been declared in 2026. So it is around 25% of the CapEx , total capital subsidy is there. And in our ink manufacturing plant, it is 35% of the capital subsidy is there.

items.statement: JV partner Swastik Strategic Ventures LLP is Surat-based group in weaving, infrastructure, construction; brings operational expertise
items.quote: Right. So they are basically a Surat-based group. Mainly their business is textile and the infrastructure and the construction business is what they were doing.

items.statement: Merger timeline uncertain - NCLT process ongoing, may complete before year-end; consolidation effective April 2026 regardless
items.quote: So, for the merger, we got the approval from the BSE before 3 to 4 months. Then we applied for the NCLT and the process of the NCLT is going on. So merger may happen maybe before the end of the year depending on the communication and depending on the approval.

items.statement: INKIA merger share swap at current market price at time of NCLT approval (not fixed Rs 240); originally valued at 15x PE vs company's 8x PE
items.quote: At the current price at the time of the approval.

items.statement: Focus on expanding installation base to grow recurring consumable revenue; ecosystem approach serving own machines plus broader India market
items.quote: So that is the fundamental of the business that more focus towards the recurring revenue, increasing the installation base. And that will increase the pool of the meter that India can print through our machine.

items.statement: Global digital ink market dependent on China; True Colors positioning as alternative supplier with manufacturing capability
items.quote: So, if we see the world's map for digital textile printing ink, or let's say digital printing ink, entire world is depending on our neighbor, that is China.

items.statement: Working capital and receivables focus area; improvement seen but still significant; exploring bill discounting and channel financing
items.quote: Going forward, working capital and the receivable is always the matter of focus for us. It was been a focus, and that is why you have also seen the improvement over there as well.

items.statement: Receivables >180 days data not disclosed on call; management to check and revert
items.quote: I just need to check the database once, and I will ask Abhishek to get back to you with that number as well.

items.statement: No specific FY27 numbers for INKIA until merger completes; consolidated reporting from April 2026
items.quote: So, let the approval come from the merger. Right now to put the numbers onto it will be little bit earlier. So once the merger is there, we will report that number into the consolidated balance sheet.

items.statement: Direct printing requires pre/post treatment infrastructure (stenter, steaming, washing) making it higher capex and cost vs sublimation
items.quote: In the direct printing, when we talk about the cotton or viscose which is being printed directly, it needs a pre- and post-treatment. So to make a pre- and post-treatment, you need the complete infrastructure just like the mill.

items.statement: Management expects year-on-year EBITDA margin expansion but urges focus on trailing 12-month volume growth rather than quarterly fluctuations; no specific timeline for 25% long-term margin target.
items.quote: Year-on-year margins should expand, but I would urge people to look at 12-month trailing versus quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Store addition pace for FY27 expected to be similar to FY26, prioritizing experience quality over speed.
items.quote: On the FY27, we continue to go with the same that we will try and deliver what we delivered last year.

items.statement: India eye tests grew 44% YoY to 70 lakh; global eye tests up 40% YoY to 80 lakh.
items.quote: India eye test grew 44% to 70 lakhs with remote optometry now live in 934 stores, up from 303 a year ago, powering the volume-led growth.

items.statement: Hustlr Club acquired lakhs of members this quarter, many buying glasses for the first time.
items.quote: Lakhs joined this quarter, many owning glasses for first time.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA Pre-Ind AS margin expanded from 11.1% to 13.8% YoY; India EBITDA Pre-Ind AS margin rose 2.6 pp to 16%; International margin rose to 10.6% from 7.3%.
items.quote: EBITDA Pre-Ind AS grew 65%, twice as fast as revenue, with margin expanding from 11.1% to 13.8%.

items.statement: India product margin improved to 64.0% from 63.4% YoY; gains from in-house manufacturing offset by rupee depreciation.
items.quote: Product margin was 64.0% against 63.4% last year, and most of the gains from in-house manufacturing were actually consumed by the rupee's depreciation this quarter.

items.statement: International product margin expanded to 77.1% from 75.5% YoY on deeper supply chain integration and higher sunglasses mix.
items.quote: Product margins expanded to 77.1% versus 75.5% last year on deeper supply chain integration of OWNDAYS and Meller and higher sunglasses mix.

items.statement: Global store count reached 3,624 with 165 net new stores added in Q2; India at 2,868 stores (143 net new, 94 in Tier 2+), International at 756 stores (22 net new).
items.quote: We added 165 net new stores globally, taking the network now to 3,624 stores.

items.statement: Hyderabad mega-factory built for 50 million pairs annually is around 12 months from commissioning; Bhiwadi facility runs at 75% automation.
items.quote: Hyderabad, built for 50 million pairs a year under one roof, and around 12 months from commissioning takes all of this to the next level.

items.statement: INR/RMB rate moved from ~₹11-12 to ₹14.2, pressuring India product margins; structural hedging via Thailand capacity, China JV stake increase, and India manufacturing.
items.quote: If you look a few quarters back, it used to be around ₹11 or ₹12 to RMB. Now it is ₹14.2 as of today.

items.statement: ASP increase driven by premium lens adoption (OWNDAYS progressives) and designer collaborations (John Jacobs with Masaba, Shantanu & Nikhil); units per customer rose from 1.8 to 1.9.
items.quote: ASP increase comes at the back of people choosing more progressive and premium lenses at Lenskart.

items.statement: Sunglasses grew strongly led by Meller; flat sequential revenue after Q1 seasonal peak is normal.
items.quote: Sunglasses grew strongly, led by M eller, and a flat sequential revenue after Q1 seasonal peak is the normal shape of the year

items.statement: Lenskart Gold active members crossed 1 crore in India, up 39% YoY; gold fees collected ₹73 crore, up 55% YoY.
items.quote: Lenskart Gold crossed 1 crore active members in India, up 39% year-on-year, with ₹73 crores of gold fees collected in the quarter, up 55% from last year.

items.statement: India NPS recovered to 79.6 from 77.6 in June quarter.
items.quote: India NPS, as you are aware, dipped to 77.6 in June, but we assured you that we have been working hard to get back to our NPS levels. I'm happy to share with you that in this quarter it is back at 79.6.

items.statement: H1 operating cash flow ₹388 crore after inventory rebuild for festive season; funded ₹187 crore store capex and ₹297 crore plant/other capex, leaving ₹12 crore net cash inflow before M&A.
items.quote: Operating cash flow was ₹388 crores for the first half of the year after working capital buildup as inventory was rebuilt ahead of the festive season.

items.statement: H1 store capex ₹187 crore for 297 net new stores; plant and other capex ₹297 crore including Hyderabad factory.
items.quote: This funded the store capex of ₹187 crores for the 297 net new stores that we added. And after including the ₹108 crores of other income and inflows, covered the plant and other capex of ₹297 crores.

items.statement: Trailing 12-month revenue crossed ₹10,000 crore, EBITDA ₹2,200 crore, Pre-Ind AS EBITDA ₹1,300 crore, PAT near ₹800 crore on 40 million eyewear units.
items.quote: On a trailing 12-month basis, we have now crossed ₹10,000 crores of revenue, ₹2,200 crores of EBITDA, ₹1,300 crores of Pre-Ind AS EBITDA, and close to ₹800 crores of PAT on 40 million eyewear units.

items.statement: India same-store sales growth 20.8% YoY; same pin code growth 27.1% YoY.
items.quote: In Q2, India delivered same-store sales growth of 20.8%. With same pin code growth of 27.1%.

items.statement: International eyewear units grew 29.7% YoY; transacting customers up 22.7% YoY.
items.quote: Eyewear units grew 29.7% and transacting customers were up 22.7%, with 22 net new stores added during the quarter.

items.statement: Remote optometry live in 934 India stores (up from 303); Drysh AI-assisted eye test in pilot, enabling 20x optometrist productivity.
items.quote: Remote optometry now in 934 stores, and also Drysh, the AI-assisted eye test, is in pilot.

items.statement: Smart glasses launched in April, now in 500 stores; 90% buyers take prescription with eye test; iterative software/firmware updates every two weeks.
items.quote: We have just now managed to put this in 500 of our stores. Maybe just a week or two back it started being available in all the stores.

items.statement: Currency volatility (INR/RMB) remains major headwind for India product margins; packaging, logistics, oil-price input inflation minimal impact.
items.quote: The challenge that we've been grappling with is largely around FX. The raw material on this is largely imported, right? So, if you see the INR versus RMB exchange rate, if you look a few quarters back, it used to be around ₹11 or ₹12 to RMB. Now it is ₹14.2 as of today.

items.statement: Global myopia rates rising rapidly, especially Southeast Asia; consumers seeking alternate D2C brands; Lenskart not yet pursuing market creation internationally.
