items.statement: Differentiating via outcome-based ResolX model vs competitors' license/per-seat SaaS; AI becoming competitive differentiator to win high-value mandates on outcomes not price
items.quote: Increasingly, AI is becoming more competitive differentiator in enabling us to compete for a larger high value mandate by offering customers, stronger outcomes and greater values rather than just competing on price alone.

items.statement: North America focus for Clariva and expansion; LATAM presence via Netcom (Costa Rica, Colombia); USD 10.8M Costa Rica contract; no specific hedging or FX details discussed
items.quote: As regards to geographies and domains, right now, we are continuing to keep North America as a focus area and try to build on to the business over there. As of now, the focus is purely on North America.

items.statement: Short-term borrowings rose to INR 54 crore from INR 11 crore; sole debt is USD 14.75M for Netcom acquisition at ~9% cost; company otherwise debt-free
items.quote: Company is debt free company. The company has only taken one debt for the acquisition of Netcom business. It's 14.75 million has disbursed from one of the banks. And debt cost is around 9% like that.

items.statement: Actively evaluating acquisitions; no fixed timeline (3-12 months); target companies to join growth journey; subsidiary stake increased by converting INR 25 crore receivables/advances into equity (2.75% additional stake)
items.quote: We are definitely looking at for acquisitions, and they are currently on the way. We don't really have a horizon whether we'll have it closed in next three months, six months, or twelve months because it's a long process. But, yes, they are on our radar, and we are evaluating various companies to really see how it can really join us in this growing journey.

items.statement: Business is annuity-based with long-term contracts (3-5 years); quarterly run-rates stable and sustainable; no project-based revenue fluctuation
items.quote: Our quarterly run rates for the last two quarters have absolutely been sustainable, and they are in line with all our projections. And we clearly see this happening for the next two quarters as well. Please keep in mind that our business is not a project-based business. It's an annuity-based business, and it's a month on month revenue generation.

items.statement: CWIP ~INR 80 crore for AI platform development; product near completion; depreciation to start once revenue line visible; capital allocation disciplined with focus on healthy balance sheet
items.quote: Currently we are under the development phase, and we require some further expenditure, which we are incurring this quarter and coming quarter. Once the development is completed and a revenue line is also visible, then depreciation will be charged. Currently, the product is under development.

items.statement: FY30 INR 2,000 crore revenue target remains on track based on current run rate and FY27 projections
items.quote: Based on our current run rate and FY27 projection, we are well on track.

items.statement: Revised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 40-45% from earlier 30%+
items.quote: On an overall basis, considering all positives, we revise our growth guidance for this year from 30% to more than 40%.

items.statement: Capex guidance increased to Rs 750 crore for FY27
items.quote: As a result, our new CAPEX guidance for the year would be around Rs. 750 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 15-16% for coming quarters
items.quote: The guidance going forward will remain between 15% and 16%, in the quarters to come.

items.statement: Five new plants to be added in next 12 months including two IPO-funded plants, two leased plants in Pune and Chennai, one rented plant in Jhajjar
items.quote: we are commencing additionally five plants in the next 12-month time period, which includes advancement of the CAPEX, which is to be incurred on the two IPO -funded plan ts, p lus additionally, we are leasing two new plants, one in Pune and one in Chennai and we are also building one additional, we are also renting one more additional plant in Jhajjar

items.statement: Electronics and battery component capex estimated at Rs 150-200 crore for FY27, may spill to Q1 FY28
items.quote: The CAPEX on the electronics and battery component both put together would be about Rs. 150 crores to Rs. 200 crores.

items.statement: All plants currently running at 75% peak capacity, hit 100% during festival months
items.quote: at this point of time, all our plants, we are running at 75% capacity. In fact, last two months, we were run ning at 100% capacity

items.statement: Three new wiring harness plants to become operational by mid-FY28
items.quote: And these plants will become, the next three plants will become operational in FY 2028 or… Rahul Dhoot: Yes, that is correct. Mid 2028

items.statement: Organic adjusted EBITDA margin maintained at 15.2% despite tough commodity cycle
items.quote: in spite of the hard cycle of commodities, our organic adjusted EBITDA margins remained consistent at 15.2%.

items.statement: Reported EBITDA margin 14.3% after 0.5% ESOP impact and Multilink consolidation
items.quote: Reported EBITDA margins after considering 0.5% ESOP impact and Multilink consolidation is 14.3%.

items.statement: Multilink margins expected to improve after integration completion and automation at new Hosur facility by April 30
items.quote: And by April 30th, we should be able to have 100% of those products move to the new facility with the new setup and with the automation involved. And that is where I believe that by April 30th, we will be able to be in line with what we have been discussing.

items.statement: Two-wheeler industry grew 16% YoY, domestic EV >100%, ICE >10%, exports 28% per CM data
items.quote: For the two-wheeler industry, the last quarter was one of the best quarters with 16% growth. Comparing Y-o-Y performance for the quarter, domestic EV industry grew in excess of 100% and ICE in excess of 10%. Export for two-wheeler grew about 28% as per CM data.

items.statement: Company revenue grew 60% YoY, wiring harness +44.6%, non-wiring harness +124%
items.quote: Against the same, Dhoot Transmission saw a very strong growth of 60% on Y-o-Y basis. Revenue from wiring harness grew 44.6% , Y-o-Y and from non -wiring harness business by 124%.

items.statement: EV revenue grew 108% YoY, now 31% of total sales vs 27% in Q1 and 24% in FY26
items.quote: EV revenue in the same quarter grew 108% for us and with this, the overall contribution of EV revenue has now reached 31% of our total sales, up from 27% in Q1 and from 24% of FY 2026.

items.statement: Export growth expected at 10-15% annually for next three years with three new customers
items.quote: I believe that we are looking at three new customers over there and we will be able to grow at the rate of 10% to 15% every year for the next three years.

items.statement: EV customers indicating 2x volumes in coming 2-3 years, two top customers building for global markets
items.quote: At this point of time, all our customers, all our EV cus tomers are talking of 2x volumes in the coming two, three years

items.statement: Multilink acquisition contributed Rs 160 crore in Q2, added Hero MotoCorp as new customer for non-wiring harness products
items.quote: Multilink acquisition contributed to about Rs. 160 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: Ramping up powertrain battery volumes with new South India-based customer
items.quote: We have started ramping up volume for the powertrain battery with our new South India-based customer.

items.statement: Two battery manufacturing plants (South and West) and new wiring harness plant at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar commenced production in H1
items.quote: During the first 6 months, we added two battery manufacturing plants, one in South and one in West. Both of them have commenced production. Our new wiring harness plant at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar got functional and we are already running at full capacity in that plant.

items.statement: RideVision ADAS system for 2W, 3W, CV is evolving business, currently imported from Europe
items.quote: So, this RideVision product which is an ADAS system for the 2, 3 and the commercial vehicle. So, this is an evolving business and right now whatever like you know, for some of the customers are using, they started to execute this production. So, these are all getting imported and these are mainly from the European side.

items.statement: Copper and commodity price increases passed through to customers quarterly, cycle expected to soften from current quarter
items.quote: the copper and the other commodity price increases are passed on to the customer quarter to quarter. And they hav e been going on in line with it. The only difference has been that the last quarter was also very hard on commodity. I believe from this quarter onwards, the commodity cycle will soften up

items.statement: Copper price inflation impact on topline estimated at 4-5% YoY
items.quote: Copper price inflation would be about 4% - 5%, not more than that.

items.statement: Receivables elevated due to festival season exit run rate, expected to normalize to 45-55 days
items.quote: Our sense is that the receivables should settle around 55/ 45 -50 to 55 days timeframe in the long term and as the year approaches and we stabilize the monthly sales run rate, they should look normal.

items.statement: Fully repaid debt from IPO proceeds, net cash/bank/FD balance at Rs 900 crore
items.quote: we have fully repaid the debt which was to be repaid out of IPO proceeds and our net cash, bank and FD balance is at Rs. 900 crores, which is in line with our expectations.

items.statement: IPO proceeds kept in FDs, will only be used for M&A or organic capex per IPO objectives
items.quote: Whatever will go in M&A will go in M&A. whatever will go in organic will go in organic. So, I mean, till the time that is not going to move in, you will see those FDs remaining in the company.

items.statement: Acquisition discussions ongoing but will comment only when matured
items.quote: Of course, there are areas and there are discussions going on, but we want to comment on it only when they are matured enough to be commented.

items.statement: Pre-exceptional PAT at Rs 162 crore, up 30% YoY
items.quote: Pre-exceptional PAT for the quarter is at Rs. 162 crores, which is an increase of 30% over the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Organic growth estimated at 41-42% YoY after adjusting for 4-5% copper inflation impact
items.quote: Correct. Yes, correct. 41%, 42%.

items.statement: Exceptional item was one-time payment done before IPO in public interest, no recurring monthly amount
items.quote: an old story. This is a one-time. This is never going to recur in the future. Manish Poddar: And what about the monthly amount also, Rahul? Rahul Dhoot: No, nothing. There is nothing. We do not pay any more, any amount

items.statement: No plans for EV charging infrastructure business, remain B2B supplier of on-board/off-board chargers
items.quote: For the EV charger infrastructure business, we do not have plans as of now.

items.statement: Hub motor vs mid-mounted motor change has no impact on wiring harness supply, content may slightly increase
items.quote: In fact, to the best of my knowledge, the length of the wiring harness will be slightly bigger, so the content will go up. But I am not very sure about that. But yes, talking about our products and all, it is not going to have any change in terms of the change from a mid-mounted motor to a hub motor.

items.statement: Order book Rs 6,500 crore as of Sep 30, up from Rs 6,000 crore on Jun 30
items.quote: As on 30th September, we have order book of Rs. 6,500 crores. On June 30th, it was about Rs. 6,000 crores.

items.statement: Fresh order intake Rs 2,100-2,200 crore in Q2 FY27
items.quote: So, during the quarter, we have secured about Rs. 2,100 and Rs. 2,200 crores of order book.

items.statement: ~60% of order book (Rs 4,000 crore) to be executed in FY27
items.quote: 60% of the order book position is going to be executed in the current financial year, which is about like Rs. 4,000 crores

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex Rs 370 crore; gross block Rs 2,411 crore
items.quote: On CAPEX , we have already done CAPEX about Rs. 370 crores Karamtara Engineering Limited November 06, 2026 6 as per the planned CAPEX in H1 and our g r oss block stood at Rs. 2,411

items.statement: H2 FY27 capex planned Rs 200-250 crore for Saudi plant, profile unit, PEB, tower testing facility
items.quote: This would be within the range of Rs. 200-250 crores.

items.statement: Aggregated installed capacity 8,79,800 MTPA (excl. rolling & galvanizing) at end of Q2 FY27
items.quote: At the end of the current quarter, our aggregated install ed capacity reached 8,79,800 metric tons per annum excluding rolling and galvanizing facilities used for captive

items.statement: Target capacity utilization 60-70% by FY27 end; optimum 85-90%
items.quote: This year, we expect to have capacity utilization within the range of 60% to 70% by the year end.

items.statement: Saudi plant trial production by Dec 2026, galvanizing by Mar 2027; full capacity utilization by FY29-30
items.quote: we are hopeful that by December end, we should have some trial production happening there . T he galvanizing plant is also being put up . T he material is reaching us and by March , we are hopeful that we will start doing some trials for galvanizing

items.statement: PEB facility at Bhachau 100,000 tonnes; trials by Mar-Apr 2027
items.quote: We are looking to start with 100,000 tonnes of capacity in our Bhachau plant and the team, our business head has already joined and so is the design team.

items.statement: Total sellable capacity ~1.4 million tonnes after all capex and Saudi ramp-up
items.quote: So, with all the CAPEX in place and once our Saudi is also up and running, and the capacity which we have said that which is going to come up in our Kutch area, this will become like 1.4 million tons, around 1.4 million tons of the sellable capacity.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 11.9% (+100 bps QoQ); freight cost pass-through to aid H2 margins
items.quote: EBITDA was Rs. 196 crores at a margin of 11.9%, a growth of 46% year-on-year basis. Of course, freight continued to remain high during the quarter.

items.statement: Freight cost pass-through in large US contracts; Middle East contracts partially absorbed
items.quote: Freight becomes a pass - through. In large contracts in North America, it's pass - through . Some contracts in the Middle East have been on actual s . Some places we have been able to pass through part of it, some we have had to absorb

items.statement: Raw material risk mitigated via back-to-back booking; commodity price risk contained
items.quote: As a policy, we mitigat e the risk of raw material fluctuations by booking material on a back - to - back basis. This discipline approach enables us to protect margins and keep commodity price risk contained

items.statement: Global renewable energy and power transmission supercycle; India 500 GW by 2030, $400 bn investment
items.quote: Currently, India has committed to Karamtara Engineering Limited November 06, 2026 3 achieving 500 gigawatts of non - fossil fuel capacity by 2030 and around 800 gigawatts by 2035 with incremental investments estimated at $ 400 billion by

items.statement: US demand robust driven by data centers, chips, aging transmission grids; Rs 550 crore order received yesterday
items.quote: We incidentally just one very large 550 crore order yesterday in the US, the order has just come in yesterday and we believe that it's going to be a large transmission market for us.

items.statement: International revenue 73% in Q2 FY27 (70% H1); US ~57% of order book; forex hedged via PCFC and natural hedge
items.quote: In Q2 '27 revenue from operations was Rs. 1,647 crores, a growth of 62% year-on-year basis. The international revenue stood at 73%.

items.statement: Tariffs pass-through; 30% price advantage vs US manufacturers even at 50% tariff
items.quote: tariffs , it really doesn't matter where the tariffs go because it's all a pass through to us . A s I have spoken in our last call , last quarter's call that the difference between our product that we are supplying out of I ndia and what is being sold by the US manufacturers , there's still a 30 % upside on that in the selling price and the tariffs get factored in

items.statement: Working capital cycle 37 days in H1 FY27; debtor days down QoQ from 100 to 94
items.quote: During H1, FY27 our working capital cycle reduced to 37 days.

items.statement: Debtor days increased YoY due to higher international mix (73% vs 45%) and Middle East transit delays
items.quote: Last year in the same quarter if you see our international sales were 45%, but in this quarter we have done 73% as international sales. So, in international sales, there is a longer working capital cycle as compared to the debtor days in the domestic market.

items.statement: Capex funded from internal accruals, IPO proceeds (Rs 200 cr in FD), and term debt if needed
items.quote: From the internal accruals, and to some extent from debt if required, then we will go for the term debt. But as of now, it looks like that we have sufficient cash flow available within the system because we haven't utilized the IPO money as of now ful ly. So, that is also there in the system. You have seen that in our balance sheet, Rs. 200 crores has already been parked in FD

items.statement: Historical revenue seasonality: 42-45% in H1, 55-58% in H2
items.quote: Historically we have been at about 42% to 58% revenue, that's how the revenue has been casted for us historically.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues (Middle East) impacting freight costs and dispatch; margins to improve if situation settles
items.quote: the freight impact if it continues , that will continue to impact us , but if things settle down completely that margin will also get passed back to profitability

items.statement: Defense/aerospace subsidiary under discussion; no guidance yet; team building in progress
items.quote: We have three or four possible scenarios that are playing out for us right now and we are trying to see which is the best way forward. So, it's all under discussion and deliberation. We are also trying to build out the team which is the core for building this business, so we are not wanting to give any guidance as of right now.

items.statement: US customers repeat orders due to quality, delivery reliability, backward integration; replacement cost high
items.quote: There's a lot of customer belief in us over the years. It's a very sensitive market where you need to have quality product, which you've delivered consistently over the years for people to have confidence in giving you those orders.

items.statement: Compete with Indian and Turkish firms; Chinese limited by national security and quality requirements in US/Europe
items.quote: Yes, so China is very limited in terms of because let's say in the US or in some of the countries in Europe, they don't want Chinese products because of national security. Some of them have regulations against and the kind of quality products that are required in some of the European countries, the Chinese manufacturers cannot match up to those.

items.statement: Saudi local content mandate requires in-kingdom manufacturing; cannot serve via exports
items.quote: Local manufacturing is a must in the kingdom of Saudi Arabia due to the preconditions of local content in all energy infrastructure projects. Therefore, the local requirements cannot be served through exports from India or other country.

items.statement: Normalized Titan Jewellery margin for Q2 FY27 is 11.1% after adjusting for ₹490 cr customs duty gain and ₹46 cr CaratLane gain; further normalizing for 60 bps MTM reversal gives 11.7%.
items.quote: Normalized margin, once you do adjustment for this, on Titan Jewellery business would be 11.1%.

items.statement: Management anchors FY27 jewellery margin target around 11% despite mix shifts and gold price volatility.
items.quote: I think we still, Mihir, would like to anchor our margin target at around 11%.

items.statement: CaratLane H1 margin remains healthy; EBIT margin expected to gradually inch up from 8% to 9% over next couple of years.
items.quote: But if you look at the entire H1 margin profile of CaratLane, still remains healthy, still remains as per our plan that gradually their EBIT margin should start inching up from 8% to 9%, and then further from there in next couple of years.

items.statement: Watch division margin improved in Q2 FY27 driven by Edge collection, Made in India campaign, and strong sales in ₹25,000–₹1 lakh price points.
items.quote: This quarter, we've had a really good story on Edge, driven partly by the Made in India: A Titan Story piece, as well as the launch of a good set of products that took price points up and therefore margins up.

items.statement: Festive season saw strong start during Navratri, mid-season softness due to gold price volatility, and strong recovery from Oct 31; studded jewellery sustained growth, investment buying soft.
items.quote: The first phase of Navratri, we saw good consumers, positive consumer sentiments and good traffic to our stores. Pretty much from the day of Vijayadashami for the next few days, there was some softness owing to gold rate volatility, which kept customers away. But pretty much from the last weekend, which was October 31, we have seen customers come back as we saw an al l- time low perhaps of the las

items.statement: CaratLane saw healthy revenue and buyer growth during 24-day festive period barring one weak week.
items.quote: During the 24 days of festive season, we, barring for one week, I think we have seen a very healthy growth in terms of both revenue as well as buyer growth.

items.statement: Watches posted better-than-Q2 growth in October, particularly in ₹25,000–₹1 lakh price points where share gains continue.
items.quote: Watches, generally festive doesn't really do that well, but this time around, in October, we had pretty good growth, better than Q2. The momentum looks good, and particularly in the price points of ₹25,000 to ₹1 lakh, which is an area that we have been gaining share, we have done really well.

items.statement: Studded jewellery growth is industry-wide, driven by secular trend toward natural diamonds since January; Diamond Expertise Centres at 250+ stores will play out longer term.
items.quote: It is a month-on-month sustainable kind of track. But we think it is an industry-wide thing. As far as the benefits of Diamond Expertise Centre, it will play out over time. We have now reached about 250+ stores.

items.statement: Lower caratage (18K, 14K, 9K) and lightweight jewellery gaining fast adoption, especially in North and West; strategy is long-term, not tied to short-term gold price moves.
items.quote: We have been working on 18-carat gold for core gold jewellery, both in wedding and daily wears, and also 14-carat in Tanishq studded jewellery and up to nine-carat in Mia. And so far, it has built a good catalogue and a good availability across stores in the last 9 to 10 months, and it is growing at a very fast clip, and we are seeing good adoption by customers.

items.statement: Buyer growth flat in Q2 due to festive shift and weak coin demand; recovery seen in late festive period but final outcome depends on last few days.
items.quote: Both of that, Nihal. Both the festive shift as well as the gold coin and investment buying, both have contributed.

items.statement: New buyers entering at sub-₹1 lakh price points across Mia, CaratLane, Tanishq; gold exchange programme, store upgrades and network expansion are key levers.
items.quote: For buyer growth to happen, we need buyer growth sub ₹1 lakh, and therefore, a lot of our efforts are to make jewellery accessible, give a lot of product choice, sub ₹1 lakh, sub ₹50,000.

items.statement: Domestic gold prices trading at discount to international since customs duty hike, creating realization pressure; customs duty gain of ₹490 cr (Titan Jewellery) and ₹46 cr (CaratLane) in Q2 fully normalized.
items.quote: Since increase in customs duty, the domestic market has been operating at a discount compared to international. I am talking about gold prices. That leads to the gold price realization pressure.

items.statement: Management expects government may reduce customs duty eventually, which would eliminate grey-channel attractiveness and improve operating environment.
items.quote: Our expectation is that at some point of time, government would also perhaps take a view on customs duty, and again, the way they have done, and they will hopefully reduce that, so that that grey channel attractiveness completely diminishes.

items.statement: Competitive intensity rising structurally as organized players expand geographies and smaller jewellers discount; management braces for continued increase and keeps margin guidance anchored at 11%.
items.quote: Competitive intensity, please expect it to continue to improve and increase all the time. More players will come, more people get capital, more people want to expand.

items.statement: Damas acquisition second-tranche liability revalued down by ₹671 cr to ₹1,668 cr under Ind AS 109; fair-value assessment each quarter may cause further pluses/minuses; long-term opportunity unchanged.
items.quote: This amount is ₹671 crores. As per Ind AS 109, any financial liability has to be fair val ued at every accounting period. And with the current environment, when we looked at our liability at the end of four years, which was accounted for in our books of accounts at ₹1,668 crores, the reassessed liability is less by ₹671 crores

items.statement: Board approved ₹2,500 cr fund raise to replenish existing borrowings, not additional debt.
items.quote: This is a replenishment of some of the existing borrowing. It is not additional borrowing.

items.statement: Non-jewellery businesses (Watches, EyeCare, Fragrances, Fashion Accessories, Taneira, TEAL, North America jewellery) delivered strong growth and higher operating leverage in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: Watch division, EyeCare division, our newer businesses, fragrances, fashion accessories, even Taneira has started showing some promising green shoots. TEAL on the other side, and international jewellery business on North America, they have been doing extremely well, and we believe that they will continue their growth trajectory, making a meaningful contribution to Titan consolidated performance.

items.statement: MTM volatility of 40-60 bps per quarter on gold forwards/futures is now a recurring P&L feature; management advises not to overreact to quarterly swings.
items.quote: With the current, the way gold price behaves, the way our volume and forwards, futures, etcetera, valuation happens, it has become part and parcel of our P&L that 40-50 basis point of MTM pluses, minuses will keep happening, and we need to live with this.

items.statement: FY27 jewellery margin guidance anchored at ~11%; no change despite gold price correction or competitive pressure.
items.quote: We would not, as far as FY27 is concerned, change our stance on margins.

items.statement: Expects modest second half FY27 due to high base, inflation, weak monsoon, and rate tightening
items.quote: We've already stated that the second half is going to be a bit modest. The primary reasons are what you already described. There is a lot of effect, inflation effect in the system. Monsoons have been weak. The interest rates are getting tightened.

items.statement: Expects flat to modest growth in Q3 FY27 relative to high prior-year base
items.quote: We expect flat to modest growth in Q3 FY27 relative to a high prior-year base.

items.statement: RBIC EBITDA margin declined due to raw material prices, forex, depreciation change, and capacity investments; expects recovery in subsequent quarters
items.quote: are some effects that we currently have in the short term, which is the forex effect, the increased investments that we've been doing to enhance capacities. So there's a lot of investment going in. There is a change of depreciation method and, of course, significant increase in raw material

items.statement: Bosch Limited margins on upward track despite transient forex and raw material impacts; endeavor to maintain and improve margins
items.quote: See, our endeavor is to maintain and even improve on the margin. Quarter-on-quarter, there could be some effects which we may encounter like currently we just talked about the forex impact or the raw material prices going up suddenly or some costs which have not yet been passed on to the OEMs or to our customers.

items.statement: Cost pass-through to customers has contractual time lag; may not recover 100% due to customer pushback
items.quote: There is a certain time lag in this as we are passing on to our customers, if we have a contractual base for this passing on. We have a time lag because of the occurrence of the increased cost and the point in time as this has been contractually agreed for recomposition or reimbursement by our customers.

items.statement: FX pass-through is contract-based for most customers, negotiation-based for some
items.quote: For most of the customers, it is contract based, but there is single customers where it is negotiation based.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex INR350 crores; annual spend focused on upgrading production lines for volume output
items.quote: Was a very high spend in the third quarter of the financial year. So most of the spending goes into plant and machinery, that's the lion's share of it. And in this year, it especially is the upgrading of existing production lines to facilitate the volume output so that we can deliver to our customers.

items.statement: RBIC Chakan plant surpassed 20 million active safety units cumulative across ESP, ABS, and two-wheeler ABS platforms
items.quote: During the quarter under review, our Chakan ma nufacturing facility scaled new milestone, officially surpassing a cumulative milestone of over 20 million active safety units manufactured across each of our four-wheeler ESP, ABS, and two-wheeler ABS platforms

items.statement: Chennai power tools plant surpassed 20 million power tools production milestone
items.quote: Our Chennai power tools plant surpassed a production milestone of 20 million power tools this quarter.

items.statement: RBIC commissioning additional line for ABS10M two-wheeler ABS capacity increase and new-generation ESP10 start of production
items.quote: The decline is again attributed mainly to increase in raw material prices and one-time costs incurred for start of production of new-generation ESPs like ESP10 and commissioning of additional line for increase in capacity of ABS, which is ABS10M for two-wheelers.

items.statement: Validated CNG direct injection on engine and vehicle benches for passenger car and LCV segments, achieving diesel-par performance
items.quote: In a world's first, Bosch Limited has successfully validated CNG direct injection on engine and vehicle benches for passenger car and light commercial vehicle segments, achieving performance and fuel efficiency on par with diesel, confirming technological leadership in alternate fuels.

items.statement: Launched first PPE safety helmets range, diversifying Power Tools beyond hand tools
items.quote: In a major strategic milestone, the division successfully diversified beyond hand tools into an adjacent market with the launch of our first ever range of PPE safety helmets.

items.statement: Launched PRO360 digital platform for professionals simplifying tool management, services, inventory, and rewards
items.quote: Also launched PRO360 platform for users and sub-dealers. PRO360 is Bosch's all-in-one digital platform that helps professionals work smarter by simplifying tool management, services, inventory, and rewards.

items.statement: Surpassed 5,000 Bosch Workshops benchmark in Mobility Aftermarket
items.quote: In a major milestone, we have surpassed the landmark 5,000 Bosch Workshops benchmark.

items.statement: Received Innovation and Technology Excellence Award at annual supplier conference; Bidadi plant honored with Automation and Operational Excellence; Jaipur plant awarded Customer-Centric Approach Award
items.quote: Recently, at the annual supplier conference, the company was recognized with Innovation and Technology Excellence Award. Further, our Bidadi plant was honored with Automation and Operational Excellence. Another OEM awarded our Jaipur plant with the Customer-Centric Approach and Looking Through the Lens of the Customer Award.

items.statement: RBIC received Super Platinum Quality Award from marquee OEM partner
items.quote: RBIC's relentless focus on operational excellence directly translates into deep customer trust, recently consolidated by the prestigious Super Platinum Quality Award conferred by one of our marquee OEM partners.

items.statement: CAFE Phase 3 effective April 2027; Bosch well positioned as core system and calibration partner with super credits for hybrids
items.quote: Following the final gazette notification for CAFE Phase 3 effe ctive April 2027, OEMs are actively aligning their platform road maps.
